# Leading-NUL node alias trimmed on storage, so relayed node_announcement signature covers different alias bytes

## Details
lnd verifies a node_announcement signature over the exact 32 alias bytes received (lnwire.ReadElement *NodeAlias keeps all 32 bytes; NodeAnnouncement1.DataToSign writes alias[:] via WriteNodeAlias), but stores the alias as the Go string returned by NodeAlias.String(), which is bytes.Trim(n[:], "\x00") and therefore removes leading as well as trailing NUL bytes (lnwire/node_announcement.go:60-63) even though its comment states it trims trailing padding only. When the announcement is later rebuilt from the graph store for gossip sync (models.Node.NodeAnnouncement(true) -> lnwire.NewNodeAlias(alias), which left-aligns the string and pads the end), an alias that began with one or more 0x00 bytes is re-encoded differently from what was signed, while the stored AuthSigBytes is attached verbatim. The re-emitted node_announcement thus carries a signature that no longer verifies.

This is the same defect class as the verified finding sql-store-address-type-regrouping-breaks-node-ann-signature (re-encoded bytes != signed bytes on DB-backed relay) but with a different source: the alias field rather than address ordering, and it is independent of the store backend. The kv store writes node.Alias via wire.WriteVarString (graph/db/kv_store.go:4692) and the SQL store writes the same string column, so the default bbolt deployment is affected.

Attack path: any gossip participant controlling a node with one announced public channel (graph/builder.go:931-950 requires the node to be in the channel graph) signs and broadcasts a node_announcement whose alias is e.g. "\x00\x00attacker" (valid UTF-8, <=32 bytes, so lnwire.NewNodeAlias accepts it on decode; BOLT 7 permits any valid UTF-8 alias). The victim lnd verifies it (netann.ValidateNodeAnn passes because DataToSign uses the untrimmed bytes), stores the trimmed alias, and relays the original wire message immediately. Every later store-backed re-encoding — ChanSeries.UpdatesInHorizon for gossip_timestamp_range syncs (discovery/chan_series.go:196-205, no check) and FetchChanAnns for query_short_channel_ids replies (:300-345, only ValidateNodeAnnFields) — emits "attacker\x00..." under the original signature. lnd peers reject the message (addNode -> ValidateNodeAnn fails, logged as an error and dropped; the ban manager scores only channel-announcement/update failures); how other implementations treat a peer repeatedly serving invalid-signature gossip (warning, error, disconnect) is dependency behaviour not verified here.

Consequence: the victim's stored alias differs from the one it verified, and it serves node_announcements with non-verifying signatures to every syncing peer, so the affected node's announcement does not propagate through the victim and the victim appears to its peers as a source of invalid gossip. No funds, confidentiality or availability impact on the vulnerable node itself; integrity of relayed signed gossip is degraded.

## Evidence
1. [lnwire/node\_announcement.go:59–63](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/node_announcement.go#L59-L63)
   NodeAlias.String() uses bytes.Trim(n[:], "\x00"), which strips NUL bytes from BOTH ends of the 32-byte alias although its own comment says it trims trailing padding only. An alias whose first bytes are 0x00 loses them here. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [graph/db/models/node.go:238–252](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/models/node.go#L238-L252)
   NodeFromWireAnnouncement stores Alias: msg.Alias.String() (the trimmed string) together with AuthSigBytes taken from the wire signature, after the gossiper has verified that signature over the untrimmed 32 bytes.
3. [graph/db/models/node.go:193–228](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/models/node.go#L193-L228)
   Node.NodeAnnouncement(true) rebuilds the wire alias with lnwire.NewNodeAlias(n.Alias), which copies the string to the front of a fresh [32]byte and pads the END with NULs. For an alias that began with NULs the rebuilt field differs from the signed one, yet the stored AuthSigBytes is attached unchanged.
4. [lnwire/node\_announcement.go:182–215](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/node_announcement.go#L182-L215)
   DataToSign serialises a.Alias via WriteNodeAlias (all 32 raw bytes), so netann.ValidateNodeAnnSignature verifies the received leading-NUL alias as-is; the signature is bound to the untrimmed bytes.
5. [lnwire/node\_announcement.go:43–56](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/node_announcement.go#L43-L56)
   NewNodeAlias only requires len<=32 and valid UTF-8; U+0000 is a valid UTF-8 code point, so an alias such as "\x00\x00abc" is accepted both at decode (lnwire.go:457-467 passes all 32 raw bytes to NewNodeAlias, preserving them) and at rebuild. BOLT 7 permits any valid UTF-8 alias, so the input is spec-compliant.
6. [discovery/gossiper.go:2191–2201](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2191-L2201)
   addNode verifies the signature over the wire struct (untrimmed alias) and then persists NodeFromWireAnnouncement(msg); the verified bytes and the stored/re-emitted bytes therefore diverge. handleNodeAnnouncement (:2611-2660) relays the original wire message immediately, so first-hop propagation succeeds and only store-backed re-encodings are broken.
7. [discovery/chan\_series.go:196–204](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/chan_series.go#L196-L204)
   UpdatesInHorizon (gossip_timestamp_range sync) re-encodes node announcements from the store via NodeAnnouncement(true) and yields them to the syncer with no signature re-check.
8. [discovery/chan\_series.go:300–344](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/chan_series.go#L300-L344)
   FetchChanAnns (query_short_channel_ids replies) sends the store-reconstructed node announcement after only netann.ValidateNodeAnnFields (DNS check); the mismatched alias bytes go out under the original signature.
9. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:4692–4695](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L4692-L4695)
   The default bbolt store persists node.Alias as the trimmed Go string (wire.WriteVarString) and reads it back the same way (deserializeLightningNode :4879-4885), so the defect is present on the default backend, not only native SQL (sql_store.go buildNodeWithBatchData :4407-4409 stores/reads the same string).
10. [graph/builder.go:931–949](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/builder.go#L931-L949)
   assertNodeAnnFreshness ignores announcements for nodes not already in the channel graph, so the attacker must control a node with one announced public channel (the only prerequisite).

## Impact
Integrity (low): the node persists an alias that differs from what it verified and relays node_announcements whose signature does not verify to peers that sync from it, so the announcement is blocked at this relay and the victim is logged by peers as a source of invalid gossip. lnd peers only log and drop such messages; no confidentiality or availability impact on the node itself.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any node with one public channel broadcasts a validly signed node_announcement whose 32-byte alias starts with 0x00 bytes. The victim lnd verifies it over the raw bytes, stores the NUL-trimmed string on either backend, and every subsequent DB-backed re-encoding (gossip_timestamp_range sync, query_short_channel_ids reply) carries a signature over different alias bytes. No authentication, interaction or special configuration is required.

## Recommended fix
1. The alias is canonicalised (leading NULs stripped by bytes.Trim in NodeAlias.String()) between signature verification and storage, so the stored representation cannot reproduce the signed bytes. Fix criteria: Storing and rebuilding a node announcement must reproduce the exact 32 alias bytes that were signed (e.g. trim only trailing padding with bytes.TrimRight, or persist the raw 32 bytes); a received announcement with a leading-NUL alias, when re-encoded via Node.NodeAnnouncement(true), must pass netann.ValidateNodeAnnSignature. Alternatively reject such aliases at netann.ValidateNodeAnnFields so nothing unreproducible is ever stored.
2. The DB-backed serving paths (ChanSeries.UpdatesInHorizon, FetchChanAnns) relay store-reconstructed node announcements with the stored signature attached but without confirming that the reconstruction still verifies. Fix criteria: Announcements reconstructed from the store are signature-checked before being sent to peers, and ones that fail are skipped and logged rather than relayed under a non-matching signature.

# Legacy v0 coop-close fee ratchet adopts remote sub-relay fee, persisting unbroadcastable close tx

## Details
For non-taproot (segwit v0) channels closed through the legacy closing_signed negotiation (the default path: protocol.rbf-coop-close is off, and the remote can simply not signal the RBF feature bit), lnd accepts whatever fee the remote eventually steers the negotiation to, with no lower bound.

`ReceiveClosingSigned` (lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:963-998) calls `calcCompromiseFee` for every remote offer that does not match one of ours. That function (:1324-1388) ratchets our previous offer down by 10% per round while the remote's fee is more than 30% below it, and as soon as the remote's fee is within 30% of our ratcheted offer it returns `remoteFee` unchanged, which the caller treats as agreement. The integer ratchet stops shrinking at 9 sat, so any remote fee >= 7 sat is adoptable; there is no comparison against the min relay fee, the channel's commitment fee rate, or any fee-rate floor. The only guard, `proposal > c.maxFee`, is an upper bound and applies only when we are the initiator. A remote in either role therefore drives our accepted fee to an unrelayable value: e.g. with our ideal fee I it repeats a 1-sat offer for ceil(ln(142/I)/ln(0.9)) rounds (about 20-50 messages), then offers 100 sat (~0.6 sat/vB on a ~170 vB close), which we accept.

On agreement the node signs via `CompleteCooperativeClose`, then `MarkCoopBroadcasted` (:1079) durably writes `ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted` and the tx before `BroadcastTx` (:1097). `BtcWallet.PublishTransaction` rejects the tx through TestMempoolAccept and `mapRpcclientError` returns `ErrMempoolFee` (btcwallet.go:1285-1308), so the error propagates to `negotiateCloseErrHandler` (peer/brontide.go:5582-5602), which only resets in-memory state, deletes the closer and disconnects. On every reconnect `loadActiveChannels` (brontide.go:1295-1339) withholds the channel from the switch, `restartCoopClose` (:3736-3748) returns nil because a close tx exists and RBF is not allowed, the chain arbitrator re-publishes the unrelayable tx forever (chain_arbitrator.go:894-950), and a non-force RPC close is refused (rpcserver.go:2904-2924). The remote never has to broadcast anything: it holds our signature for the low-fee tx but that tx is just as unrelayable for it, and the legacy close input is non-RBF (sequence 0xffffffff), so the only exit is a local force close.

This is a distinct reachable path into the persist-before-publish sink already recorded for taproot channels in `legacy-taproot-responder-accepts-arbitrary-fee-persists-close` (chancloser.go:920-944, which bypasses calcCompromiseFee entirely) and the RBF sibling `rbf-closee-unvalidated-remote-fee-locktime`; it affects the far more common segwit-v0/anchor channels and both negotiation roles. The earlier dismissal of the v0 branch (ledger dismissed-chancloser-1324-6b98) considered only zero/negative fees, not positive sub-relay fees. BOLT 2 asks the receiver to fail the connection when fee_satoshis is unreasonably low; lnd instead commits to it.

## Evidence
1. [lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:1324–1387](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go#L1324-L1387)
   calcCompromiseFee is the only fee-acceptance logic on the segwit-v0 path. When the remote's offer is out of the 30% window it ratchets our last offer down by 10% (ratchetFee, :1311-1319); once the remote's offer is within 30% of our ratcheted offer (feeInAcceptableRange, :1293-1305) it returns remoteFee verbatim. There is no absolute floor (min relay fee, dust-relative, or fee-rate) anywhere in this function; the ratchet only stops shrinking at 9 sat (9 - 9/10 = 9), so any remote fee >= 7 sat is eventually adoptable.
2. [lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:963–997](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go#L963-L997)
   ReceiveClosingSigned, case !feeMatchesOffer (non-taproot channels, both initiator and responder roles): proposal := calcCompromiseFee(...); only an upper bound (proposal > c.maxFee, initiator only) exists. When proposal == remoteProposedFee the function falls through to finalisation with the remote-chosen fee.
3. [lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:1067–1098](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go#L1067-L1098)
   On fee agreement CompleteCooperativeClose signs the tx, then MarkCoopBroadcasted (:1079) durably stores ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted plus the tx BEFORE BroadcastTx (:1097). A sub-relay-fee tx fails TestMempoolAccept and the error is returned, but the persisted status/tx are never reverted.
4. [peer/brontide.go:5582–5601](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L5582-L5601)
   negotiateCloseErrHandler handles the BroadcastTx error: ResetState on the in-memory channel, delete the closer, disconnect. Nothing clears the persisted ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted.
5. [peer/brontide.go:3736–3747](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L3736-L3747)
   restartCoopClose: because BroadcastedCooperative() now returns a tx and RBF close is not allowed for the channel, it returns (nil, nil) — the negotiation is never re-driven on reconnect, and loadActiveChannels (:1295-1339) keeps the channel out of the switch.
6. [lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go:1285–1307](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go#L1285-L1307)
   mapRpcclientError maps the backend's min-relay / mempool-min-fee rejection to lnwallet.ErrMempoolFee, which PublishTransaction returns to the chan closer (not an ignored reason), so the close is never published yet remains persisted.
7. [contractcourt/chain\_arbitrator.go:894–949](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/chain_arbitrator.go#L894-L949)
   republishClosingTxs/rebroadcast re-publish the stored unrelayable coop close tx on every start; this is the only automatic action taken for a CoopBroadcasted channel.
8. [rpcserver.go:2904–2923](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L2904-L2923)
   A non-force CloseChannel is refused because the link is no longer in the switch and no RBF closer exists; the operator's only exit is a unilateral force close.

## Impact
No confidentiality impact. Integrity LOW: channel.db durably records a cooperative close that can never relay, with the channel's status flipped to CoopBroadcasted; balances are unchanged so no funds move. Availability LOW: the channel is permanently parked in waiting-close, excluded from the switch on every reconnect, never re-negotiated, not coop-closable via RPC, with the chain arbitrator re-publishing a doomed tx; the operator must force close (CSV delay on their own funds plus on-chain fees that a cooperative close would have avoided). Scope is one channel per attack, repeatable across every channel the attacker shares with the victim.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any channel counterparty on a non-taproot channel (the default channel types) that does not negotiate RBF coop close. As initiator it sends shutdown then repeated closing_signed messages with a tiny fee until our ratcheted offer is within 30% of its target sub-relay fee, then offers that fee with a valid signature; as responder it does the same against our offers. Each round is one message pair and lnd never aborts on repeated unacceptable offers. The victim deterministically co-signs, persists ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted and fails broadcast. No credentials, no user interaction, no defence to defeat; default configuration suffices.

## Recommended fix
1. calcCompromiseFee/ReceiveClosingSigned accept any remote fee that is within the compromise window of our ratcheted offer, with no absolute lower bound relative to the backend's min relay fee or a configured floor; the ratchet itself has no floor other than integer arithmetic. Fix criteria: A remote closing_signed fee below a sane floor (at least the min relay fee for the estimated close tx weight, i.e. a fee rate not below chainfee.FeePerKwFloor/RelayFeePerKW) must never be adopted or ratcheted toward; such offers must be rejected (fail the negotiation/connection per BOLT 2) rather than signed. Verify by driving the negotiation with repeated 1-sat offers followed by a sub-relay offer and confirming no signature or persisted close tx is produced.
2. MarkCoopBroadcasted persists ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted and the close tx before BroadcastTx succeeds, and nothing reverts the status when broadcast fails, so a single rejected tx permanently disables the legacy close path for the channel. Fix criteria: A cooperative close that the backend refuses to relay must not leave the channel in a terminal CoopBroadcasted state: either validate relayability (e.g. TestMempoolAccept / fee-rate check) before persisting, or revert/clear the status and stored tx on broadcast failure so the channel is reloaded into the switch and negotiation can restart on reconnect. Verify by forcing a broadcast failure and confirming the channel is usable/coop-closable afterwards.

# Native-SQL graph store writes one row per channel_announcement feature bit and TLV record, persistently

## Details
When lnd runs with db.use-native-sql=true on sqlite or postgres (config_builder.go:1123-1330 wires graphdb.NewSQLStore, invoices and payments onto one native store; for sqlite this is the single file lnd.sqlite, lncfg/db.go:605-610), the graph SQL store persists a channel announcement's feature vector as one graph_channel_features row per set bit and its ExtraOpaqueData as one graph_channel_extra_types row per TLV record, each via a separate single-row statement executed sequentially inside the channel scheduler's shared write transaction (graph/db/sql_store.go insertChannel 5146-5182, reached from AddChannelEdge 895-944 through batch.TimeScheduler; batch/batch.go:56-78 runs every queued request's Do inside one ExecTx). It is the channel_announcement sibling of the verified record sql-store-node-features-row-per-bit-write-amplification (upsertNodeFeatures, node_announcement); the sink, tables, source message and gating differ.

The input is remote and bounded only by the 65,535-byte wire frame. ChannelAnnouncement1.Features is a RawFeatureVector whose Decode (lnwire/features.go:661-707) reads a uint16 length and calls Set for every set bit with no cap; FeatureBit is uint16 (features.go:34), so an 8,192-byte all-ones vector yields 65,536 distinct bits. After the fixed fields (~8.6 KB including that vector) the remaining ~56.9 KB of the frame can carry ExtraOpaqueData of ~14,000 zero-length odd-typed TLV records (a 3-byte BigSize type in 253..65535 plus a 1-byte zero length = 4 bytes each); tlv.Stream.decode (tlv/stream.go:168-290) stores every unknown odd type with its bytes in the parsed-types map with no record-count limit, marshalExtraOpaqueData (sql_store.go:5056-5085) turns each into a map entry, and insertChannel issues one UpsertChannelExtraType per entry. netann.ValidateChannelAnn (netann/channel_announcement.go:96-) checks only the four signatures, which the attacker produces with keys it controls; handleChanAnnouncement (gossiper.go:2700-2812) applies isPremature, IsKnownEdge, IsClosedScid and the signature check, then builds the edge with WithFeatures(ann.Features) and ExtraOpaqueData unmodified. There is no size bound on either field and no channel-announcement rate limiter (chanUpdateRateLimiter at gossiper.go:3413 covers channel_update only).

Gating: each announcement must name a fresh SCID with block height <= the node's best height (AddChannelEdge returns ErrEdgeAlreadyExist otherwise). Under neutrino, AssumeChannelValid is forced to !neutrino.validatechannels, i.e. true by default (config_builder.go:1741), and the funding check at gossiper.go:2856 is skipped, so the attacker can stream announcements for arbitrary fresh SCIDs with no on-chain cost. Under bitcoind/btcd validateFundingTransaction (gossiper.go:3989-4030) requires a confirmed P2WSH 2-of-2 output of the announced bitcoin keys per SCID; one transaction with many ~330-sat outputs supplies one valid announcement per output, so the per-message cost is dust plus fees.

Cost per accepted announcement: 65,536 InsertChannelFeature plus ~14,000 UpsertChannelExtraType single-row statements (~80k statement executions) in one write transaction. On sqlite this holds the single writer lock of the shared lnd.sqlite for the transaction's duration: invoice settlement and payment writes queued behind it wait on busy_timeout (default 5 s, sqldb/config.go:43) and ExecTx's 20 retries (sqldb/interfaces.go:25) before failing, and every other channel edge/policy write in the same batch waits for the whole batch. On postgres the lock is per row but the 80k round trips and rows remain. Per-statement latency is an assumption about modernc sqlite / pgx, not measured. Unlike the node case the rows are never replaced: each fake channel leaves ~80k rows that persist until the channel is removed, which for a policy-less channel happens only via pruneZombieChans after ChannelPruneExpiry (14 days, graph/builder.go:31,525-561), and batchLoadChannelData (sql_store.go:6413-6480) reloads every feature and extra-type row for each channel on ChannelView at startup, pathfinding, describegraph and gossip query replies, so DB size and read latency grow with each message.

Reachable only when db.use-native-sql=true on sqlite/postgres (a documented, supported, non-default option: sample-lnd.conf:1605, lncfg/db.go:86); bbolt and kvdb-emulated SQL store the vector as a single value (kv_store.go:4969-4977; their separate defect is the 900-byte read cap finding).

## Evidence
1. [graph/db/sql\_store.go:5146–5156](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/sql_store.go#L5146-L5156)
   insertChannel iterates edge.Features.Features() and executes one InsertChannelFeature statement per set bit with no cap on the number of bits; the feature vector comes unmodified from the remote ChannelAnnouncement1.
2. [graph/db/sql\_store.go:5159–5181](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/sql_store.go#L5159-L5181)
   The same function then executes one UpsertChannelExtraType statement per TLV record found in the announcement's ExtraOpaqueData (marshalExtraOpaqueData, 5056-5085, keeps every unknown odd type of any length, including zero-length records), with no cap on the record count. A zero-length record with a 3-byte BigSize type (253..65535) costs 4 bytes, so ~14,000 records fit beside an 8 KB feature vector in one 65,535-byte frame.
3. [graph/db/sql\_store.go:895–943](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/sql_store.go#L895-L943)
   AddChannelEdge runs insertChannel inside a chanScheduler batch request: every statement executes sequentially in one write transaction shared with every other channel edge/policy write queued in the same batch, so the attacker's statement storm stalls them all.
4. [lnwire/features.go:661–706](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/features.go#L661-L706)
   RawFeatureVector.Decode reads a uint16 length and calls Set(FeatureBit(i)) for every set bit with no cap. FeatureBit is uint16 (line 34), so an 8,192-byte all-ones vector sets all 65,536 distinct bits; the vector plus ~57 KB of ExtraOpaqueData fits one 65,535-byte wire message.
5. [lnwire/channel\_announcement.go:73–92](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/channel_announcement.go#L73-L92)
   ChannelAnnouncement1.Decode reads Features through ReadElements with no bound beyond the message frame and only ValidateTLV() (a P2P stream parse) on ExtraOpaqueData; both fields are covered by the four signatures the attacker produces with its own keys.
6. [discovery/gossiper.go:2795–2811](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2795-L2811)
   handleChanAnnouncement validates only the signatures (netann.ValidateChannelAnn) and builds the edge with models.WithFeatures(ann.Features) and ExtraOpaqueData unmodified; there is no size check and no channel-announcement rate limiter (the token bucket at 3413 applies to channel_update only).
7. [discovery/gossiper.go:2850–2857](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2850-L2857)
   The funding-output check is skipped entirely when AssumeChannelValid is set (forced to !neutrino.validatechannels, i.e. true by default under neutrino, config_builder.go:1741), so under neutrino every announcement with a fresh, non-premature SCID is accepted and inserted; under bitcoind/btcd validateFundingTransaction (3989-4030) requires one confirmed P2WSH 2-of-2 output of the announced keys per announcement, which a single transaction with many ~330-sat outputs supplies cheaply.
8. [discovery/gossiper.go:2955–2959](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2955-L2959)
   The edge is handed to Builder.AddEdge -> SQLStore.AddChannelEdge without any further bound on features or extra data.
9. [sqldb/sqlc/migrations/000008\_graph.up.sql:186–211](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/sqlc/migrations/000008_graph.up.sql#L186-L211)
   Schema: graph_channel_features holds one row per (channel_id, feature_bit) and graph_channel_extra_types one row per (channel_id, type); rows are removed only when the channel row is deleted (ON DELETE CASCADE), so they persist for the life of the (fake) channel.
10. [sqldb/sqlc/queries/graph.sql:1041–1070](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/sqlc/queries/graph.sql#L1041-L1070)
   InsertChannelFeature and UpsertChannelExtraType are single-row statements; there is no bulk insert, so cost is one round trip/parse per bit and per record.
11. [graph/db/sql\_store.go:6459–6479](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/sql_store.go#L6459-L6479)
   batchLoadChannelData reloads every feature row (GetChannelFeaturesBatch) for each channel whenever edges are read (ChannelView at startup, pathfinding, gossip query replies, describegraph), so the inserted rows are a persistent read cost as well.
12. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:4969–4976](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L4969-L4976)
   Sibling kv store writes the whole vector as one VarBytes value (its own defect is the 900-byte read cap, finding kvstore-chan-announcement-features-exceed-900-byte-read-cap); the row-per-bit expansion is specific to the SQL backend.

## Impact
Availability: on sqlite the single-writer lock of the shared lnd.sqlite is held for the transaction's duration per 65 KB received, so invoice/HTLC settlement and payment writes wait on the 5 s busy_timeout and 20 ExecTx retries and every other graph write in the batch stalls; a sustained stream keeps the writer saturated. On both backends ~80k rows per fake channel persist for at least the 14-day zombie horizon and are reloaded by batchLoadChannelData on startup ChannelView, pathfinding, describegraph and gossip replies, so storage and read latency grow without bound as the stream continues. Per-statement latency is an assumption about the modernc sqlite / pgx drivers (go.mod pins). No confidentiality impact; integrity limited to delayed graph updates.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any node that can deliver gossip to the victim (a direct brontide connection into a restricted inbound slot, or relay through the network). It signs channel_announcements with its own four keys, each carrying an 8,192-byte all-ones feature vector and ~57 KB of zero-length odd TLV records, one fresh SCID per message; the gossiper verifies only those signatures and applies no size bound or channel_announcement rate limit. Under neutrino (AssumeChannelValid forced on by default) no on-chain output is needed; under bitcoind/btcd one confirmed dust P2WSH 2-of-2 output per message, mass-produced in a single transaction. Each accepted message expands to ~80k sequential single-row statements in one write transaction. Requires the victim to run db.use-native-sql on sqlite/postgres, a supported, documented, non-default storage option rather than a disabled security control: attack_requirements PRESENT.

## Recommended fix
1. insertChannel expands a remote-supplied feature vector and TLV stream into one SQL statement per set bit and per record with no bound on their count, so a single 65 KB gossip message dictates ~80k sequential writes inside a shared transaction and leaves that many persistent rows. Fix criteria: An accepted channel_announcement's persistence cost must be bounded independently of its bit/record count: either reject announcements whose feature vector or ExtraOpaqueData exceed a fixed size (consistently with the kv store caps) before AddEdge, or store the vector/stream as a single value (or a bounded bulk insert). After the fix, an 8,192-byte all-ones feature vector with 14k extra records must not produce more than a small constant number of statements, and the write transaction duration must not scale with the message contents.
2. The gossiper admits channel announcements of any size and, under AssumeChannelValid, for any SCID, so there is no upstream limit on how many such messages reach the store. Fix criteria: Gossip-level validation should bound Features and ExtraOpaqueData sizes for ChannelAnnouncement1 before the edge is built (lead-gossiper-3442-23f2), so that both kv and SQL backends receive only announcements they can persist and reload within fixed cost.

# Remote-signer wallet builder omits Rebroadcaster; low-fee force closes never retried

## Details
lnd has two production wallet builders in config_builder.go. DefaultWalletImpl.BuildChainControl (797-826) attaches a pushtx.Broadcaster to lnwallet.Config for every non-neutrino backend so that each published transaction is re-sent on every new block until confirmed, specifically continuing when the backend answers 'mempool min fee not met' / 'min relay fee not met' or reports the tx already in the mempool (broadcastErrorMapper, 1946-1988; documented in release-notes-0.16.0 as per-block rebroadcast). RPCSignerWalletImpl.BuildChainControl (902-915), selected by ImplementationConfig whenever remotesigner.enable=true (config.go:1980-1996; the documented remote-signing deployment of a watch-only lnd over bitcoind/btcd, docs/remote-signing.md), builds lnwallet.Config without a Rebroadcaster and offers no option to add one. LightningWallet.PublishTransaction (lnwallet/wallet.go:546-548) then performs a single send.

On btcd/bitcoind the btcwallet wrapper runs TestMempoolAccept first (lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go:1331-1398); when the reject reason is a min-fee error it never calls the underlying wallet's PublishTransaction (so the tx is not even recorded as unmined for btcwallet's own startup resend) and returns lnwallet.ErrMempoolFee. ChannelArbitrator's StateBroadcastCommit (channel_arbitrator.go:1162-1181) deliberately swallows ErrMempoolFee and advances to StateCommitmentBroadcasted, commenting that the rebroadcaster will republish regularly; handleBlockbeat (3139-3147) only advances from StateDefault, so nothing re-publishes the stored commitment on later blocks; the only remaining re-publication is republishClosingTxs at ChainArbitrator start (chain_arbitrator.go:1406), i.e. a process restart. The utxonursery's legacy second-level timeout publish (utxonursery.go:1070-1080) makes the same assumption. Anchor CPFP cannot compensate: the anchor child alone fails TestMempoolAccept with missing-inputs when its parent is not in the mempool (fee_bumper.go:666-675) and lnd's sweeper never re-sends the parent nor uses SubmitPackage. Sweeper-managed transactions themselves are retried through per-block fee bumping and are not affected.

Result, reachable only in a remote-signing deployment (remotesigner.enable=true) with a bitcoind/btcd backend: when a force close is required (counterparty unresponsive with an HTLC that must be claimed or timed out on-chain) and the commitment fee rate is below the current mempool minimum, the commitment is published once, rejected, marked as broadcast, and never re-sent while mempool conditions change. The arbitrator waits in StateCommitmentBroadcasted for a confirmation that cannot come, so HTLC CLTV deadlines can elapse; the counterparty can then confirm its own commitment plus HTLC-timeout (or claim with the preimage after the upstream has timed out) and the node loses the in-flight HTLC value. The counterparty controls the precondition: as funder it sets the commitment fee rate via update_fee with no lower bound enforced (link.go:4584-4620; funding-time floor absent per fundee-no-commit-feerate-floor-unrelayable-commitment), so holding it at the relay floor makes any ordinary congestion sufficient; for victim-funded anchor channels lnd itself caps the commitment fee at 10 sat/vB (DefaultAnchorsCommitMaxFeeRateSatPerVByte, funding/manager.go:4991-4993), so congestion above that rate suffices without the attacker being funder. The default build recovers automatically once the mempool minimum drops; the remote-signer build recovers only on operator restart or manual republish.

Distinct from force-close-publish-insufficient-fee-stranded-no-anchor-cpfp (unmapped ErrInsufficientFee -> StateError in all deployments): here the error is correctly mapped and the arbitrator's chosen recovery path depends on a component that one production configuration never constructs. Dependency assumptions: btcwallet v0.16.20-pre's TestMempoolAccept/MapRPCErr surface bitcoind's 'mempool min fee not met' as chain.ErrMempoolMinFeeNotMet; neutrino's own SendTransaction rebroadcasts internally, so the neutrino backend is unaffected.

## Evidence
1. [config\_builder.go:902–915](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config_builder.go#L902-L915)
   RPCSignerWalletImpl.BuildChainControl builds lnwallet.Config without the Rebroadcaster field. This is the production ChainControlBuilder whenever remotesigner.enable=true (the watch-only node of a remote-signing deployment, docs/remote-signing.md, which the doc diagrams with a bitcoind/btcd backend).
2. [config\_builder.go:797–826](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config_builder.go#L797-L826)
   The default builder wires a pushtx.Broadcaster for every non-neutrino backend that re-sends each unconfirmed tx on every new block and keeps retrying on ErrMempoolMinFeeNotMet / ErrMinRelayFeeNotMet / ErrTxAlreadyInMempool (broadcastErrorMapper, 1946-1988). The remote-signer builder lacks it, so the two production modes differ in funds-safety behaviour.
3. [config.go:1980–1995](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config.go#L1980-L1995)
   ImplementationConfig selects RPCSignerWalletImpl as ChainControlBuilder when RemoteSigner.Enable is set; there is no option to add a rebroadcaster in that mode.
4. [lnwallet/wallet.go:546–548](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/wallet.go#L546-L548)
   LightningWallet.PublishTransaction: with Cfg.Rebroadcaster nil it calls the wallet controller once and returns; no background retry exists.
5. [lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go:1331–1398](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go#L1331-L1398)
   For btcd/bitcoind the wrapper runs TestMempoolAccept first; when the reject reason is a mempool/relay min-fee error it never calls the underlying wallet's PublishTransaction (so btcwallet never records the tx as unmined and will not resend it at startup either) and returns lnwallet.ErrMempoolFee via mapRpcclientError (1285-1309).
6. [contractcourt/channel\_arbitrator.go:1162–1181](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/channel_arbitrator.go#L1162-L1181)
   StateBroadcastCommit swallows ErrMempoolFee and advances to StateCommitmentBroadcasted, with the comment that 'The rebroadcaster makes sure this transaction is republished regularly until confirmed or replaced'. In remote-signer mode that component does not exist: the commitment is marked broadcast but is in no mempool.
7. [contractcourt/channel\_arbitrator.go:3139–3147](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/channel_arbitrator.go#L3139-L3147)
   handleBlockbeat only calls advanceState while in StateDefault; nothing in StateCommitmentBroadcasted re-publishes the stored commitment on later blocks.
8. [contractcourt/chain\_arbitrator.go:1405–1410](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/chain_arbitrator.go#L1405-L1410)
   republishClosingTxs (877-950) is invoked only here, while ChainArbitrator starts, i.e. on process restart. Between restarts a rejected commitment stays unbroadcast.
9. [contractcourt/utxonursery.go:1070–1080](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/utxonursery.go#L1070-L1080)
   The nursery's legacy second-level HTLC timeout publish tolerates ErrMempoolFee 'because the tx is rebroadcasted in the background', relying on the same absent component.
10. [htlcswitch/link.go:4584–4620](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L4584-L4620)
   processRemoteUpdateFee enforces only the upper fee-exposure limit; a funder counterparty may hold the commitment fee rate at (or below) the relay floor, so any ordinary mempool congestion puts the commitment below mempoolminfee at close time.
11. [sweep/fee\_bumper.go:666–675](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sweep/fee_bumper.go#L666-L675)
   Anchor CPFP cannot fill the gap: the anchor child alone fails TestMempoolAccept with missing-inputs when the parent commitment is absent from the mempool and is treated as spent by others (ErrInputMissing); the sweeper never re-sends the parent and no code in sweep/ or contractcourt/ uses SubmitPackage.

## Impact
A commitment that is marked broadcast but never re-sent lets on-chain HTLC deadlines pass, so the node loses the in-flight HTLC value in the affected channel(s) — a direct loss of funds, the primary asset in the threat model (integrity HIGH). Availability LOW: on-chain resolution of the affected channels stalls until an operator restart or manual republish. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: a channel counterparty (any remote peer that opens or accepts a channel with the node; no lnd privileges). Steps: as funder hold the commitment fee at the relay floor via update_fee (no lower bound enforced, link.go:4584-4620), or rely on lnd's own 10 sat/vB anchor commitment cap; go unresponsive with a pending HTLC while the mempool minimum exceeds the commitment fee rate, forcing the victim to force-close; the victim's single publish is rejected with ErrMempoolFee, the arbitrator marks the commitment broadcast and never retries it; after CLTV expiry the attacker confirms its own commitment and HTLC-timeout. Attack requirements PRESENT: the victim must run remotesigner.enable=true with a bitcoind/btcd backend and the mempool minimum must exceed the commitment fee at close time (trivially met when the attacker pins the fee at the floor). No user interaction; low complexity.

## Recommended fix
1. RPCSignerWalletImpl.BuildChainControl constructs lnwallet.Config without the Rebroadcaster that the default builder wires and that contractcourt/utxonursery assume is present. Fix criteria: Both production wallet builders must provide the same background rebroadcast behaviour for non-neutrino backends (or a shared helper must construct it), so a transaction rejected for low fee or evicted from the mempool is re-sent on subsequent blocks until confirmed or replaced in remote-signer mode too. Verification: in a remote-signing setup against bitcoind, a force close whose commitment fee is below the mempool minimum is re-published once the minimum drops, without restarting lnd.
2. contractcourt tolerates ErrMempoolFee on publish by relying on an optional component without checking it exists. Fix criteria: Code paths that swallow publish errors on the assumption of background rebroadcast must either verify a rebroadcaster is configured or schedule their own retry (e.g. re-attempt on each block beat while in StateCommitmentBroadcasted). Verification: with Rebroadcaster nil, a low-fee force close is retried on subsequent blocks.

# Gossip-planted undecodable KV graph records make the KV-to-SQL graph migration fail, bricking lnd startup

## Details
Condition: holds for a node whose operator enables db.use-native-sql (sqlite/postgres kvdb backend, docs/db_migration_guide.md Stage 2) at a time when global migration 10 (kv_graph_migration) has not yet been recorded. Under that setting config_builder.go:1169-1185 calls graphdbmig1.MigrateGraphToSQL on the node's own KV graph (the header comment in sql_migration.go claiming it is never called is stale).

The migration iterates the KV graph with the frozen forEachChannel in graph/db/migration1/kv_store.go. That reader has two read-side caps the live write side never enforced: channel features are read with wire.ReadVarBytes(r, 0, 900) (migration1/kv_store.go:1770) although the live putChanEdgeInfo (graph/db/kv_store.go:4969-4974) writes the encoded feature vector unbounded; and the policy blob is read with a 10000-byte cap (migration1/kv_store.go:2176) although the live serializeChanEdgePolicy (graph/db/kv_store.go:5473-5488) writes 8 bytes of max_htlc plus up to MaxAllowedExtraOpaqueBytes (10000) of ExtraOpaqueData into that one var-bytes blob. Both records are remotely plantable: the gossiper stores ann.Features verbatim (discovery/gossiper.go:2804-2811; lnwire RawFeatureVector.Decode accepts any uint16 length and makeFundingScript falls back to the legacy script for non-taproot bits), and ChanEdgePolicyFromWire copies upd.ExtraOpaqueData verbatim (graph/db/models/channel_edge_policy.go:123) while KVStore.UpdateEdgePolicy validates only TLV well-formedness, not length (graph/db/kv_store.go:3389-3393); max_htlc is mandatory (netann validateChannelUpdate1Fields). A ChannelAnnouncement1 with a feature bit >= 7184 (encoded vector >= 899 B, signed by the attacker's two nodes for a real funded channel) or a signed channel_update carrying 9993..10000 bytes of odd-type TLV data is therefore accepted, committed, and thereafter undecodable by the frozen reader.

The migration has no tolerance for such records. migrateChannelsAndPolicies (sql_migration.go:547-665) skips only records whose *decoded* ExtraOpaqueData fails TLV parsing (ErrParsingExtraTLVBytes); a record the KV reader cannot decode surfaces as a wire MessageError from forEachChannel (migration1/kv_store.go:396-398 for edge info; 256-257 via getChannelMap for policies, whose switch tolerates only ErrEdgePolicyOptionalFieldNotFound and ErrParsingExtraTLVBytes), is returned unchanged, and MigrateGraphToSQL fails (sql_migration.go:57-63). sqldb.ApplyMigrations (migrations.go:501-541) runs the MigrationFn in one write transaction and returns on error, so the graph migration is rolled back, version 10 is never recorded, and it re-fails identically on every start; config_builder.go:1238-1248 makes that fatal. Migration 7 (invoices) committed earlier in the same run and wrote the KV invoice-bucket tombstone (config_builder.go:1138-1167), so reverting to db.use-native-sql=false is refused (config_builder.go:1351-1373). The node starts in neither mode.

The only in-product escape, db.skip-native-sql-migration (lncfg/db.go:88), records versions 10 and 14 as applied without moving data: the node starts with an empty SQL graph (re-syncable) and an empty SQL payments store while the KV payments database, including in-flight attempt records, is abandoned. Otherwise the operator must restore a pre-migration backup (docs recommend one) and stay on KV, or hand-edit the KV graph; the planted record persists for as long as the attacker keeps the channel open, so every later migration attempt fails the same way.

The project's own tests (sql_migration_test.go 'channel policy with bad tlv data') establish the intent that one bad record must not fail the migration; undecodable records violate that intent. This is distinct from the live-store cap mismatch recorded at graph/db/kv_store.go: the migration1 reader is a frozen copy, so a fix to the live store does not repair this path, and already-planted records remain in operators' KV graphs. Assumption on dependency: btcd v0.25.1-pre wire.ReadVarBytes returns a *MessageError (not io.EOF/ErrUnexpectedEOF) when the declared count exceeds maxAllowed; its source is not in the checkout.

## Evidence
1. [graph/db/migration1/sql\_migration.go:547–665](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/migration1/sql_migration.go#L547-L665)
   migrateChannelsAndPolicies drives the whole channel migration through the frozen forEachChannel; the only skip logic (574-595) handles ErrParsingExtraTLVBytes raised after a record has been decoded, and every other error from the reader is returned unchanged at 662-665, which MigrateGraphToSQL (57-63) turns into a fatal migration error. This is the code the fix must change: an undecodable edge or policy must be skipped and counted like TLV-invalid records.
2. [graph/db/migration1/kv\_store.go:387–411](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/migration1/kv_store.go#L387-L411)
   forEachChannel aborts the iteration (return err at 396-398) on the first edge-index value deserializeChanEdgeInfo rejects; getChannelMap is called first (378) so a bad policy aborts before any channel is visited.
3. [graph/db/migration1/kv\_store.go:1770–1772](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/migration1/kv_store.go#L1770-L1772)
   deserializeChanEdgeInfo reads the channel features with wire.ReadVarBytes(r, 0, 900, ...); a stored feature vector of >= 899 encoded bytes (2-byte length + bitmap, i.e. any bit index >= 7184) produces a MessageError that is not EOF-tolerated.

   getChannelMap tolerates only ErrEdgePolicyOptionalFieldNotFound and ErrParsingExtraTLVBytes; any other deserializeChanEdgePolicyRaw error (256-257) aborts the whole map load and therefore forEachChannel.

   ApplyMigrations runs each custom MigrationFn in its own write transaction and returns on the first error; the graph migration (version 10) is rolled back in full and never recorded in migration_tracker, so it is re-attempted and re-fails on every start. 12. [config\_builder.go:1238–1247](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config_builder.go#L1238-L1247)
   Any ApplyAllMigrations error is fatal for lnd startup.
13. [config\_builder.go:1138–1166](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config_builder.go#L1138-L1166)
   The invoice migration (version 7) runs before the graph migration (version 10) and writes the KV invoice-bucket tombstone inside its committed transaction, so by the time version 10 fails KV mode has already been sealed.
14. [config\_builder.go:1351–1372](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config_builder.go#L1351-L1372)
   With db.use-native-sql=false lnd refuses to start once the tombstone exists ('invoices bucket tombstoned, please switch back to native SQL'), so the operator is locked out of both modes.
15. [lncfg/db.go:88](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lncfg/db.go#L88)
   The only in-product escape, db.skip-native-sql-migration, marks the graph and payments migrations as done without moving data: the KV graph and the KV payments database are abandoned.

## Impact
Availability: lnd cannot start under native SQL and cannot revert to kvdb; a node that cannot start cannot resolve HTLCs or punish breaches until the operator restores a pre-migration backup, hand-edits the KV graph, or sets skip-native-sql-migration. Integrity: that only in-product recovery path discards the KV graph and the KV payments store (including in-flight attempt records) without migrating them, so node state is degraded as a direct consequence of the attack. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any Lightning node that controls one public, funded channel the victim learns of through gossip (both endpoints may be attacker nodes; no relationship to the victim). It broadcasts one ChannelAnnouncement1 with a feature bit >= 7184 or one signed channel_update with 9993-10000 bytes of odd-type TLV extra data; the gossip network relays it or the attacker delivers it directly over 9735. The record is committed deterministically (gossiper.go:2804-2811 / models/channel_edge_policy.go:123 -> live kv_store.go:4969-4974 / 5473-5488). The victim's first start with db.use-native-sql=true after that point fails at migration 10 on every attempt, and KV mode is sealed by the migration-7 tombstone. Requires the victim to opt into native SQL (non-default, documented Stage 2 migration) after the plant, hence AT:PRESENT; no privileges, no interaction.

## Recommended fix
1. migrateChannelsAndPolicies/forEachChannel treat any undecodable edge-index or policy value as fatal for the entire migration, even though the live writer could persist records exceeding the frozen reader's caps and the migration already skips TLV-invalid records by design. Fix criteria: An edge-info or policy value the migration1 KV reader cannot decode must be skipped (counted and logged, like ErrParsingExtraTLVBytes today) rather than aborting MigrateGraphToSQL; alternatively the frozen reader's caps must accept every record the live writer could have produced (features unbounded by the writer; policy blob up to 8 + MaxAllowedExtraOpaqueBytes). Verify by inserting an edge-index value with a 901-byte features field and a policy value with a 10001-byte blob into a test KV graph and confirming MigrateGraphToSQL completes, migrates every other record, and lnd starts.
2. Startup sequencing seals KV mode (invoice tombstone at migration 7) before the graph migration has succeeded, so a failing migration 10 leaves no working mode. Fix criteria: A failure in a later custom migration must leave the node able to start in the previous mode, or all KV-to-SQL custom migrations must succeed atomically before any KV tombstone is written. Verify by making migration 10 fail and confirming lnd can still start with db.use-native-sql=false.

# Node alias with interior NUL byte aborts the graph SQL migration on PostgreSQL, bricking lnd startup

## Details
A remote gossip node whose public channel is already in the victim's graph can plant a node alias containing an interior 0x00 byte in the victim's bbolt graph; when the operator later enables db.use-native-sql on a PostgreSQL backend, the KV-to-SQL graph migration hands that alias verbatim to a TEXT column, PostgreSQL rejects it, the whole migration aborts, and lnd can no longer start in either storage mode.

Input path: lnwire decodes the 32-byte alias and validates it only through NewNodeAlias (lnwire/lnwire.go:457-467), which checks length and utf8.ValidString (lnwire/node_announcement.go:43-57); 0x00 is valid UTF-8. NodeAlias.String() trims NULs only at both ends (node_announcement.go:60-63), so "a\x00b" survives. The gossiper's addNode runs netann.ValidateNodeAnn, whose field check inspects only DNS addresses (netann/node_announcement.go:98-120), then calls Graph.AddNode(models.NodeFromWireAnnouncement(msg)) (discovery/gossiper.go:2191-2201), which copies msg.Alias.String() (graph/db/models/node.go:246). The builder only requires that the node already exist in the graph, i.e. that it is an endpoint of a known public channel (graph/builder.go:939-948); it never inspects the alias. The KV store writes the alias as raw bytes (graph/db/kv_store.go:4693, wire.WriteVarString) and the frozen migration reader returns it unchanged (graph/db/migration1/kv_store.go:1542-1546).

Sink: global migration 10 (sqldb/migrations.go:86-89) runs MigrateGraphToSQL. migrateNodes skips only ErrParsingExtraTLVBytes and address-parse errors (sql_migration.go:251-270); insertNodeSQLMig passes SQLStrValid(node.Alias) to InsertNodeMig for graph_nodes.alias TEXT (sql_migration.go:1453-1466; 000008_graph.up.sql:18-19) and any error is fatal ('could not persist node', 275-280) up through MigrateGraphToSQL (48-51). PostgreSQL rejects any text/varchar value containing byte 0x00 (SQLSTATE 22021, 'invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00').

Consequence: ApplyMigrations runs each migration in its own ExecTx and records the version only on success (sqldb/migrations.go:471-477, 501-541), so version 10 is rolled back and re-attempted on every start while version 7 (invoice migration), which already committed and wrote the KV invoice tombstone inside its callback (config_builder.go:1138-1167), stays applied. The ApplyAllMigrations error is fatal to startup (config_builder.go:1238-1248), and reverting to db.use-native-sql=false is refused because of the tombstone (config_builder.go:1351-1373). Recovery requires hand-editing channel.db, restoring a pre-migration backup, or db.skip-native-sql-migration, which abandons the KV graph and payments data (lncfg/db.go:88). docs/db_migration_guide.md lists the Postgres graph relational migration as 'Available with v0.20', so this is a supported shipped path; the kvdb_postgres backend is in RELEASE_TAGS (make/release_flags.mk:31) and the native store has no build tag.

The SQLite backend (modernc.org/sqlite) stores NUL-bearing strings, so only PostgreSQL deployments are affected. The live SQL store's own upsert (graph/db/sql_store.go:4683-4695) would merely reject the attacker's announcement; the difference here is that the record is already in the victim's KV database before the sink is reached.

Dependency assumptions: PostgreSQL (all supported versions) rejects 0x00 in text values; the native SQL store is opened with database/sql driver 'pgx' from github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 v5.11.0 (sqldb/postgres.go:12-14,104; sqldb/go.mod:9), which transmits Go string bytes to the server without stripping NUL.

## Evidence

   insertNodeSQLMig passes the KV alias verbatim (SQLStrValid(node.Alias.UnwrapOr(""))) into InsertNodeMig, which writes the graph_nodes.alias TEXT column; any database error is returned. This is where the alias must be sanitised or the failure tolerated.

8. [graph/db/models/node.go:238–252](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/models/node.go#L238-L252)
   NodeFromWireAnnouncement stores msg.Alias.String() on the node that is persisted.

   assertNodeAnnFreshness is the only gate: the announcing node must already be in the graph, i.e. be an endpoint of a known public channel. This is the attacker's sole precondition; the alias is never examined.

   The live KV store writes the alias as raw bytes (wire.WriteVarString), so the NUL-bearing alias is durably stored in channel.db.
11. [sqldb/sqlc/migrations/000008\_graph.up.sql:18](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/sqlc/migrations/000008_graph.up.sql#L18)
   graph_nodes.alias is a TEXT column; on PostgreSQL text values may not contain the byte 0x00.
12. [sqldb/migrations.go:471–540](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/migrations.go#L471-L540)
   Each migration is skipped only if its version is recorded (471-477) and runs in its own ExecTx that records the version only on success (501-541): version 7 stays committed while version 10 is rolled back and re-fails on every start.
13. [config\_builder.go:1138–1166](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config_builder.go#L1138-L1166)
   The version-7 invoice migration callback writes the KV invoice bucket tombstone before the later graph migration (version 10) runs.
14. [config\_builder.go:1238–1247](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config_builder.go#L1238-L1247)
   An ApplyAllMigrations error is fatal for startup.
15. [config\_builder.go:1351–1372](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config_builder.go#L1351-L1372)
   With the invoice tombstone set, starting with db.use-native-sql=false is refused, so the operator cannot fall back to KV mode.
16. [sqldb/postgres.go:104](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/postgres.go#L104)
   The native SQL store is opened with database/sql driver 'pgx' (github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 v5.11.0 per sqldb/go.mod:9), which sends Go string parameters to PostgreSQL unmodified; the server rejects 0x00 in text.

## Impact
Availability: lnd cannot start under native SQL (migration 10 re-fails every start) and cannot revert to kvdb (config_builder.go:1351-1373); the node is offline, unable to resolve HTLCs or punish breaches, until the operator performs manual DB surgery, restores a pre-migration backup, or sets db.skip-native-sql-migration. Integrity: that only in-product recovery abandons the KV graph and payments history (lncfg/db.go:88). No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any Lightning node that is an endpoint of a public channel present in the victim's graph (graph/builder.go:939-948 is the only gate). It signs and broadcasts one node_announcement whose 32-byte alias contains an interior 0x00 followed by a non-NUL byte; lnwire (NewNodeAlias) and netann accept it, the gossiper persists it in bbolt, and it stays until the attacker replaces it or its channel is pruned. The victim's first start with db.use-native-sql=true on a PostgreSQL backend then fails deterministically at migration 10, and KV mode is sealed by the version-7 invoice tombstone. The attack needs the victim's documented but non-default configuration (native SQL on postgres), hence AT:PRESENT; no privileges, no interaction, no timing.

## Recommended fix
1. insertNodeSQLMig/migrateNodes hand a remote-chosen alias to the SQL backend unneutralised and abort the whole migration on any per-node insert error, so a single string PostgreSQL refuses (interior NUL in a TEXT column) denies startup. Fix criteria: The migration must neutralise NUL bytes in the alias (strip or encode) before insert, or skip and log a node whose insert fails for data reasons like it does for TLV-invalid nodes (its channels then get a shell node). Verify by storing a node with alias "a\x00b" in a test bbolt graph and running MigrateGraphToSQL against PostgreSQL: it must complete and lnd must start.
2. Alias validation at the P2P boundary (lnwire.NewNodeAlias) accepts bytes that the SQL schema cannot store, so acceptance and storability diverge, and the live SQL store/KV store persist the alias without neutralising NUL. Fix criteria: Aliases accepted from gossip must be representable in every supported backend (reject or strip interior NUL at validation or before persistence). Verify that a node_announcement with an interior NUL alias is either rejected before persistence or round-trips through both the KV and SQL graph stores on PostgreSQL.

# ChannelReestablish for unknown channel ID scans every closed channel per message

## Details
ChannelStateDB.FetchClosedChannelForID (channeldb/db.go) is meant to find the close summary whose funding outpoint matches a 32-byte ChannelID by seeking to the shared 30-byte prefix and examining only the candidate keys with that prefix. The loop guard is written as `bytes.Compare(cid[:30], op[:30]) <= 0`. Because cursor.Seek(cid[:30]) positions on the first key >= cid[:30], every subsequent 36-byte outpoint key has op[:30] >= cid[:30], so the guard is always true and the loop runs until the cursor is exhausted. The lookup is therefore O(N) in the number of closed channels instead of the intended O(log N + candidates); a cid of all zero bytes selects the whole bucket, and even a legitimate cid scans from its prefix to the end.

This sink is reachable by any remote peer. peer/brontide.go readHandler calls resendChanSyncMsg for every ChannelReestablish whose ChanID is not an active channel of that peer; the peer needs no channel, only a completed brontide handshake (one of the default 100 restricted inbound slots, config.go DefaultNumRestrictedSlots). resendChanSyncMsg memoises only successful resends in p.resentChanSyncMsg; a lookup miss is not remembered, so each such message performs a fresh kvdb.View, Seek and full scan, decoding every closed-channel outpoint and deriving a ChannelID for comparison. No per-peer limiter covers this message type (only Ping and OnionMessage are limited in readHandler).

On bbolt (v1.4.3) the per-entry cost is a few hundred nanoseconds of in-memory cursor work, so a ~120-byte message costs on the order of a millisecond on a node with thousands of closed channels, and each attacker connection's readHandler can keep one core busy. On the sqlite/postgres kvdb backends (kvdb/sqlbase/readwrite_cursor.go) every cursor.Next() is a separate SQL query returning the full close-summary value, executed inside one read transaction that holds a pooled connection for the whole scan. The kvdb sqlite backend does not set WithTxLevelLock but defaults to a 2-connection pool (sqldb/config.go MaxConns, lncfg/db.go:208, kvdb/sqlbase/db_conn_set.go:56), so two concurrent scans occupy the whole channel.db pool and the node's own channel-state transactions wait behind them; on postgres the cost is one network round trip per closed channel per message (the optional --db.postgres.withgloballock additionally serialises writers behind the read, but is off by default and not relied on here).

The bound on a single scan is the victim's closed-channel count (victim state, not attacker-grown), so this is amplification rather than unbounded work: the attacker converts an intended logarithmic lookup into a linear one per message and can repeat it indefinitely. No data is disclosed, since the RemotePub check still gates the actual resend. This is distinct from the dismissed lead dismissed-brontide-5121-c908, which considered only the authorization check on the success path.

Assumption: bbolt v1.4.3 (go.mod) cursor Next/Seek are in-memory B+tree operations; database/sql holds one pool connection per open transaction; kvdb/sqlbase behaviour is read from the in-repo source.

## Evidence
1. [channeldb/db.go:1420–1446](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/db.go#L1420-L1446)
   FetchClosedChannelForID seeks the closed-channel cursor to cid[:30] and loops `for ; op != nil && bytes.Compare(cid[:30], op[:30]) <= 0; op, c = cursor.Next()`. Keys are 36-byte serialized funding outpoints (channel.go locateOpenChannel/putChannelCloseSummary). After Seek every key k satisfies k >= cid[:30], hence k[:30] >= cid[:30], so the guard is always true and the loop ends only at the end of the bucket. Each iteration decodes an outpoint and derives a ChannelID. The intended bound (stop when the 30-byte prefix differs) is never applied; an all-zero cid seeks to the first key and visits every closed channel.
2. [peer/brontide.go:2432–2449](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L2432-L2449)
   readHandler: for every lnwire.ChannelReestablish whose ChanID is not in p.activeChannels, resendChanSyncMsg(targetChan) is called inline on the read goroutine. Any peer that completed the brontide handshake (a restricted inbound slot, no channel needed) can send this message with any ChanID; only Ping and OnionMessage have per-peer limiters in this handler.
3. [peer/brontide.go:5124–5162](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L5124-L5162)
   resendChanSyncMsg consults p.resentChanSyncMsg first, but the memo is written only after a successful resend (line 5161). A miss (ErrClosedChannelNotFound) is never memoised, so every unknown-ChanID ChannelReestablish from the peer reaches FetchClosedChannelForID and pays the full scan.
4. [kvdb/sqlbase/readwrite\_cursor.go:88–108](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/kvdb/sqlbase/readwrite_cursor.go#L88-L108)
   On the sqlite/postgres kvdb backends each cursor.Next() is a separate `SELECT key, value ... WHERE key>$1 ORDER BY key LIMIT 1` executed inside the read transaction (which holds one pooled connection for its lifetime), so the scan costs one database round trip, returning the full close-summary value, per closed channel per message.
5. [sqldb/config.go:57–66](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/config.go#L57-L66)
   SqliteConfig.MaxConns defaults to 2; lncfg/db.go:208 passes it to sqlbase.Init and kvdb/sqlbase/db_conn_set.go:56 applies it via SetMaxOpenConns. Two concurrent attacker-triggered scans therefore occupy the whole channel.db connection pool and the node's own channel-state transactions queue behind them for the scan's duration.

## Impact
Pure resource consumption: each small message forces an O(closed channels) cursor scan on the channel-state database, and on sqlite/postgres kvdb one SQL query per entry inside a read transaction that holds one of the (default 2 on sqlite) pooled connections, delaying the node's own channel-state reads and writes while the attack is sustained. No confidentiality or integrity effect; the RemotePub check still gates the resend. Work per message is bounded by the victim's closed-channel count and stops when the attacker stops, so this is a sustained slowdown rather than a crash, hang or persistent outage: LOW.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any remote node able to complete the Noise handshake to port 9735 (knows the victim pubkey) and occupy a restricted inbound slot. Delivery: after init, repeatedly send ChannelReestablish with ChanID = 0x00..00 (or any value not among the attacker's active channels). Each message is dispatched on the read goroutine to resendChanSyncMsg, misses the memo, and calls FetchClosedChannelForID, which scans every closed-channel entry. No privileges, no user interaction, no non-default deployment state; impact scales with the victim's closed-channel count and is heaviest on the SQL kvdb backends.

## Recommended fix
1. FetchClosedChannelForID's loop guard compares in the wrong direction, so the scan never stops at the end of the matching 30-byte prefix range and degrades to a full-bucket scan whose extent is chosen by the caller-supplied ChannelID. Fix criteria: The lookup must visit only keys sharing the 30-byte prefix with the requested ChannelID (terminate as soon as op[:30] != cid[:30]), so cost is O(log N + candidates) independent of the remaining bucket contents. Verify by issuing a ChannelReestablish with an all-zero ChanID against a database with many closed channels and confirming the cursor visits at most the candidate keys.
2. resendChanSyncMsg memoises only successful resends, so a peer can repeat the same unknown-channel lookup indefinitely at full database cost. Fix criteria: Unknown-channel ChannelReestablish lookups from a peer should be bounded per connection (memoise misses or rate-limit/disconnect on repeated unknown ChanIDs) so that repeated messages do not each reach the database scan.
