# Native-SQL graph store writes one row per node feature bit; an 8 KB signed node_announcement forces ~65k-145k single-row statements in one write transaction, repeatable without rate limit

## Details
When lnd runs with db.use-native-sql=true on sqlite or postgres (default false; a supported backend documented in docs/db_migration_guide.md and listed in the threat model), the graph SQL store persists a node announcement's feature vector as one graph_node_features row per set bit, its addresses as one row per address and its ExtraOpaqueData as one row per TLV record, each via a separate single-row statement executed sequentially inside the node scheduler's write transaction (graph/db/sql_store.go upsertNodeFeatures 4719-4770, upsertNodeAddresses 4878-4917, upsertNodeExtraSignedFields 4954-5005, called from upsertNodeAncillaryData 4523-4557). The sibling kv store writes the same vector as a single value (kv_store.go:4698).

The input is remote and unbounded up to the wire limit: NodeAnnouncement1.Features is a RawFeatureVector whose Decode (lnwire/features.go:661-707) reads a uint16 length and calls Set(FeatureBit(i)) for every set bit with no cap. FeatureBit is uint16 (features.go:34), so distinct bits saturate at 65,536 (bits beyond 8,192 bytes alias onto lower indices): an 8,192-byte all-ones vector sets every one of them. netann.ValidateNodeAnn checks only DNS addresses and the signature; the gossiper (handleNodeAnnouncement 2577-2627) and builder (assertNodeAnnFreshness 931-961) accept the message if the node already exists in the graph (one announced channel, whose endpoints may both be the attacker's) and the attacker-chosen uint32 timestamp is newer than the stored one. There is no rate limiter for node announcements (only channel_update has the per-direction token bucket at gossiper.go:3413), so the attacker can stream accepted announcements for its own node indefinitely, several per 500 ms batch if desired (each passes the UpsertNode newer-timestamp check inside the same transaction).

Cost per accepted message: first acceptance of an all-ones vector costs 65,536 InsertNodeFeature statements; thereafter flipping between all-ones and empty costs 65,536 DeleteNodeFeature + 65,536 InsertNodeFeature (~131k), each preceded by a GetNodeFeatures read of up to 65,536 rows. The ~57 KB of the 65,535-byte message not used by the 8 KB vector can carry ~8,100 IPv4 addresses (one UpsertNodeAddress each, after DeleteNodeAddresses) or ~14,000 zero-length odd-typed TLV records (one UpsertNodeExtraType each; tlv P2P decode accepts any unknown odd type). All of it runs in one ExecTx (batch/batch.go:41-75); every other node announcement queued in that 500 ms batch waits for it, and the gossiper goroutines handling them block. No DB timeout applies on this path (no WithTimeout in graph/db, discovery or graph/builder). Per-statement cost is an assumption (modernc sqlite v1.x in-process parse+exec per ExecContext; pgx round trip per statement on postgres), not measured: seconds to tens of seconds per message on sqlite, longer on mobile/RPi, minutes on networked postgres.

Impact. On sqlite the invoice, graph and payments stores share the single lnd.sqlite base DB (config_builder.go:1253-1340) with DefaultSqliteMaxConns=2 and busy_timeout 5 s (sqldb/config.go:33-44); the attacker's transaction holds the WAL writer lock for its duration, so invoice settlement / exit-hop HTLC writes (invoiceregistry.go UpdateInvoice) wait, hit SQLITE_BUSY -> ErrSerializationError (sqlerrors.go:62-71) -> up to 20 retries, and fail with ErrRetriesExceeded under a sustained stream, causing the link to fail incoming HTLCs; payments to the node stop. On postgres the writer is not exclusive but the node scheduler batch and node-announcement processing for all peers stall for the transaction's duration, and the DB absorbs ~100k statements per 65 KB received. Rows persist: ~65k feature rows per attacker node are re-read on every FetchNodeFeatures during pathfinding (routing/pathfind.go:625,1025,1357), on NodeUpdatesInHorizon pages served to syncing peers, and in describegraph.

Reachable only when db.use-native-sql=true on sqlite/postgres; bbolt and kvdb-emulated SQL store the vector as one value and are unaffected.

## Evidence
1. [graph/db/sql\_store.go:4719–4770](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/sql_store.go#L4719-L4770)
   upsertNodeFeatures reads the node's existing feature rows then issues one DeleteNodeFeature per bit no longer set and one InsertNodeFeature per newly set bit; the loop is bounded only by the set bits in the remote feature vector (up to 65,536), with no cap or bulk form.
2. [graph/db/sql\_store.go:4523–4557](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/sql_store.go#L4523-L4557)
   upsertNodeAncillaryData is called by upsertNode for every accepted announcement and runs the per-feature, per-address and per-TLV loops sequentially inside the caller's write transaction.
3. [graph/db/sql\_store.go:4878–4917](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/sql_store.go#L4878-L4917)
   upsertNodeAddresses deletes all address rows then issues one UpsertNodeAddress per advertised address; ~8,100 IPv4 entries fit alongside an 8 KB feature vector in one message.
4. [graph/db/sql\_store.go:4954–5005](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/sql_store.go#L4954-L5005)
   upsertNodeExtraSignedFields issues one UpsertNodeExtraType per TLV record in ExtraOpaqueData (~14,000 zero-length odd-typed records fit in the remaining message space).
5. [graph/db/sql\_store.go:253–275](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/sql_store.go#L253-L275)
   AddNode submits upsertNode to the nodeScheduler batch; every node announcement queued in the 500 ms window shares one write transaction and waits for it.
6. [batch/batch.go:41–74](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/batch/batch.go#L41-L74)
   The batch runs all requests inside a single ExecTx; a slow request holds the transaction open and every other request's caller blocks on its errChan until the transaction finishes.
7. [sqldb/sqlc/queries/graph.sql:167–198](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/sqlc/queries/graph.sql#L167-L198)
   InsertNodeFeature / DeleteNodeFeature are single-row statements; there is no bulk form, so each feature bit is one driver execution.
8. [lnwire/features.go:661–706](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/features.go#L661-L706)
   RawFeatureVector.Decode reads a uint16 length and decode() calls Set(FeatureBit(i)) for every set bit; no upper bound on length or popcount. Because FeatureBit is uint16, bits beyond index 65535 alias onto lower ones, so an 8,192-byte all-ones vector sets all 65,536 distinct bits.
9. [lnwire/features.go:34](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/features.go#L34)
   type FeatureBit uint16 fixes the ceiling of distinct feature bits at 65,536 per announcement.
10. [netann/node\_announcement.go:98–122](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/netann/node_announcement.go#L98-L122)
   ValidateNodeAnnFields validates only DNS addresses; no bound is placed on the feature vector, address count or TLV record count before the announcement is persisted.
11. [discovery/gossiper.go:2577–2626](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2577-L2626)
   handleNodeAnnouncement gates only on non-zero timestamp, IsStaleNode (newer than stored) and addNode (signature + DNS checks). No per-node or per-peer rate limiter applies to node announcements (contrast the channel_update token bucket at gossiper.go:3413).
12. [graph/builder.go:931–960](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/builder.go#L931-L960)
   assertNodeAnnFreshness requires only that the node already exists in the graph (one announced channel) and that the attacker-chosen uint32 timestamp exceeds the stored one.
13. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:4695–4701](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L4695-L4701)
   The sibling kv store encodes the whole feature vector as one value in a single Put; the SQL store issues ~4-5 orders of magnitude more statements for the same input.
14. [sqldb/config.go:33–43](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/config.go#L33-L43)
   SQLite defaults: 2 connections and a 5 s busy_timeout. A multi-second write transaction holds the single writer lock; other writers time out with SQLITE_BUSY.
15. [sqldb/sqlerrors.go:62–70](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/sqlerrors.go#L62-L70)
   SQLITE_BUSY is mapped to ErrSerializationError, so blocked writers spin through the ExecTx retry loop (20 retries) and then fail with ErrRetriesExceeded.
16. [config\_builder.go:1253–1339](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config_builder.go#L1253-L1339)
   Invoices, graph and payments stores are all built on the same native-SQL base DB (one lnd.sqlite file / one postgres DB), so the stalled sqlite writer lock also blocks invoice and HTLC settlement writes.

## Impact
Availability: on sqlite the shared single-writer lock on lnd.sqlite is held for the transaction's duration per 65 KB received, so invoice/HTLC settlement writes wait, fail with SQLITE_BUSY -> ErrSerializationError -> ErrRetriesExceeded under a sustained stream, and the node stops accepting payments; on both backends node-announcement processing for all peers stalls behind the batch and ~65k persistent rows per attacker node inflate every later feature read (pathfinding, gossip sync). Per-statement latency figures are assumptions about the sqlite/pgx drivers, not measured. No confidentiality impact; integrity impact limited to delayed graph updates.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any gossip participant owning one announced channel (both endpoints may be theirs). It connects to the victim or any relaying peer and sends node_announcement for its own node with an 8,192-byte all-ones feature vector (65,536 bits), the rest of the 65,535-byte message filled with addresses or odd-typed TLV records, a valid signature and timestamp = previous+1; alternating with an empty vector doubles the per-message statement count via deletes. Each message is accepted (signature + newer timestamp only) and expands to ~65k-145k sequential single-row statements in one write transaction; no rate limiter applies, so the stream can continue indefinitely. Requires the victim to run db.use-native-sql on sqlite/postgres (a supported, documented, non-default backend) and the attacker to own one public channel: attack_requirements PRESENT.

## Recommended fix
1. The SQL store materialises a remote-controlled bit vector, address list and TLV set as one row and one statement per element, with no bound on how many elements a single announcement may carry. Fix criteria: Per-announcement persistence cost must be bounded independently of the attacker's element count: reject node announcements whose feature vector / address list / extra-TLV count exceeds a sane limit at ingestion (gossiper, netann or lnwire), and/or store the feature vector as a single serialised value or bulk-insert diffs in a bounded number of statements. Verify that an 8 KB all-ones feature vector is either rejected or persisted in a small constant number of statements and that invoice writes are not blocked beyond normal transaction time.
2. Node announcements have no rate limiting in the gossiper, so an attacker can replay the expensive write path as fast as timestamps allow. Fix criteria: Apply a per-node (and ideally per-peer) rate limit to accepted node announcements comparable to the channel_update token bucket, so repeated announcements for the same node are dropped beyond a burst.

# RegisterBlockEpochNtfn backlog from height 1 is computed inline, stalling the chain notifier dispatcher

## Details
chainrpc.ChainNotifier/RegisterBlockEpochNtfn (onchain:read, carried by the default readonly.macaroon: rpcserver.go:105-108, lnd.go:859) lets the caller supply a 'best known block' (hash + height) so the notifier replays the blocks the client missed. chain_server.go:612-628 forwards any non-zero hash/height pair unchanged; the only implicit checks are that GetBlockHash(height) succeeds (height must be 1..tip) and that the hash is a real block header, both public chain data.

In all three backend notifiers the registration is handled synchronously inside notificationDispatcher, the single goroutine that also connects new blocks into the TxNotifier (bitcoind.go:395 chainConn.Notifications(), btcd.go:449 chainUpdates) and services every registration and cancellation from every lnd subsystem over the unbuffered notificationRegistry/notificationCancels channels (bitcoind.go:100-101; sends at 768, 853, 949, 1037, 1047). For the registration the dispatcher calls chainntnfs.GetClientMissedBlocks inline (bitcoind.go:376-379, btcd.go:430-433, neutrino.go:502-505). GetClientMissedBlocks (interface.go:533-567) fetches the hash at the claimed height, runs GetCommonBlockAncestorHeight (zero iterations when the hash matches, otherwise two header fetches per step back to genesis when a real hash is paired with a different real height, interface.go:499-524), then getMissedBlocks(startingHeight+1, tip+1) (interface.go:670-703): one GetBlockHash plus one GetBlockHeader backend call per height and a BlockEpoch with header retained for every block. With mainnet block 1's hash and height 1 this is roughly 2 x tip (~1.8M) sequential backend RPCs to bitcoind/btcd and on the order of 100 MB of retained epochs before the dispatcher loop runs again; the epochs are then pushed into the client's unbounded epochQueue (queue.ConcurrentQueue) where they stay until the RPC stream drains them, so a client that does not read keeps the memory resident and can open further streams.

While the backlog is computed no new block is delivered to the TxNotifier, so every confirmation and spend notification in the node (contractcourt resolvers, breach arbiter, sweeper, funding manager, channel arbitrators) is frozen, and other subsystems' RegisterConfirmationsNtfn/RegisterSpendNtfn/RegisterBlockEpochNtfn/Cancel calls block on the unbuffered registry channel. The caller can queue further registrations (processed sequentially by the dispatcher) to extend the stall indefinitely. The threat model classes a hang that makes the node miss HTLC/CSV/breach timeout windows as loss of funds; this hang is reachable with the lowest-privilege standard macaroon via a single small request. On neutrino the per-block cost is a local header-store read (neutrino.go:1143) so the stall is shorter, but the O(tip) inline loop and allocation remain.

Assumption (dependency not in checkout): btcwallet v0.16.20-pre chain.BitcoindClient and chain.RPCClient implement GetBlockHash/GetBlockHeader as direct per-call backend RPCs with no header cache; neutrino's ChainService.GetBlockHeader reads the local header store.

This is distinct from the verified chainrpc-height-hint-one-unbounded-historical-rescan (chain_server.go:384): that record concerns conf/spend height hints driving historical rescans that run in their own goroutines; this one concerns the block-epoch backlog, which runs on the dispatcher goroutine itself and therefore blocks block processing and all registrations rather than merely consuming resources.

## Evidence
1. [lnrpc/chainrpc/chain\_server.go:612–628](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/chainrpc/chain_server.go#L612-L628)
   The RPC builds a chainntnfs.BlockEpoch from the caller's hash and height whenever both are non-zero and passes it as the client's 'best block' to ChainNotifier.RegisterBlockEpochNtfn. Any real block hash with its true height (e.g. block 1 on mainnet, public data) is accepted; nothing bounds how far below the tip it may be.
2. [lnrpc/chainrpc/chain\_server.go:70–74](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/chainrpc/chain_server.go#L70-L74)
   The RPC requires only onchain:read, which readPermissions (rpcserver.go:105-108) contains and lnd.go:859 bakes into the default readonly.macaroon.
3. [chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:354–392](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go#L354-L392)
   The blockEpochRegistration is handled synchronously inside the dispatcher: GetClientMissedBlocks is called inline (376-379) and then every missed block is pushed to the client's queue, before the loop can service anything else.
4. [chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:218–226](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go#L218-L226)
   notificationDispatcher is 'the primary goroutine which handles client notification registrations, as well as notification dispatches'; the same select consumes notificationCancels (226), notificationRegistry (253) and chainConn.Notifications() (395), so while the backlog is computed no block is connected to the TxNotifier and no registration/cancel from any subsystem is processed.
5. [chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:100–101](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go#L100-L101)
   notificationCancels and notificationRegistry are unbuffered channels; RegisterSpendNtfn (768, 853), RegisterConfirmationsNtfn (949), RegisterBlockEpochNtfn (1037) and epoch Cancel (1047) all block on them, so every subsystem registering or cancelling an on-chain watch stalls for the duration of the inline backlog.
6. [chainntnfs/interface.go:533–567](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/interface.go#L533-L567)
   GetClientMissedBlocks fetches the hash at the client's claimed height, walks GetCommonBlockAncestorHeight, then calls getMissedBlocks(startingHeight+1, notifierBestHeight+1), i.e. from the caller's height to the tip.
7. [chainntnfs/interface.go:670–703](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/interface.go#L670-L703)
   getMissedBlocks preallocates a slice of (tip - height) BlockEpochs and issues GetBlockHash and GetBlockHeader for every height in the range (about 1.8 million backend RPCs for height 1 on mainnet), retaining a hash and header per block, all before returning.
8. [chainntnfs/interface.go:499–524](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/interface.go#L499-L524)
   If the caller pairs a real hash with a different real height, GetCommonBlockAncestorHeight walks both chains back one header at a time (two GetBlockHeader calls per step) until they meet or genesis's zero PrevBlock errors out, a second caller-controlled inline loop bounded only by chain height.
9. [chainntnfs/btcdnotify/btcd.go:408–446](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/btcdnotify/btcd.go#L408-L446)
   Identical inline handling in the btcd notifier (chainConn is *chain.RPCClient, each call a btcd RPC); the chainUpdates case that connects new blocks is in the same select (449).
10. [chainntnfs/neutrinonotify/neutrino.go:474–516](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/neutrinonotify/neutrino.go#L474-L516)
   Identical inline handling in the neutrino notifier; NeutrinoChainConn.GetBlockHeader (1143) reads the local header store so each call is cheaper, but the O(tip) loop and allocation are the same and still block the dispatcher and the rescanFilterUpdate case (518) that other subsystems wait on.

## Impact
No disclosure or data modification. Availability: the chain notifier's single dispatcher goroutine is blocked for the whole backlog computation (roughly 2 x tip sequential backend RPCs per request against bitcoind/btcd, repeatable without limit), during which no block is connected to the TxNotifier, all on-chain confirmation/spend delivery in lnd halts, and every subsystem's register/cancel call blocks on the unbuffered registry channel; additionally on the order of 100 MB of epochs per request is retained in the client's unbounded epochQueue until the attacker's stream drains it. Sustained denial of the node's on-chain monitoring, which the threat model ties to missed HTLC/CSV/breach windows, is a high availability impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds any macaroon with onchain:read (the default readonly.macaroon) and can reach gRPC (10009) or REST (8080, /v2/chainnotifier/register/blocks). They call RegisterBlockEpochNtfn{hash: <mainnet block 1 hash>, height: 1}. The RPC forwards it; the notifier dispatcher synchronously fetches hash+header for every block up to the tip before servicing anything else. Repeating the call, or opening several streams, keeps the dispatcher busy continuously. Only public chain data is needed; no race, no configuration dependency, no user interaction. The gRPC server imposes no stream or rate limit (lnd.go:376 sets only MaxRecvMsgSize).

## Recommended fix
1. The RPC layer forwards an arbitrary caller-chosen best block, and the notifiers compute the full backlog from it synchronously on the single dispatcher goroutine that also processes new blocks. Fix criteria: A block-epoch registration must never block the notifier's block-processing loop: the backlog must be computed and delivered off the dispatcher goroutine (or incrementally), and the dispatcher must continue connecting blocks and servicing registrations while a backlog is produced. Verify by registering with height 1 and confirming new blocks are still delivered to other clients during the replay.
2. RPC-originated best-block heights are unbounded, so a single request can demand a replay of the entire chain. Fix criteria: RPC-supplied best blocks must be bounded to a reasonable window below the current tip (or rejected beyond it) and the resulting backlog bounded in memory; verify that a request far below the tip is rejected or streamed in bounded chunks rather than materialised at once.

# PruneGraph/DisconnectBlockAtHeight append nil edge on tolerated ErrEdgeNotFound, then dereference it

## Details
KVStore.PruneGraph (graph/db/kv_store.go:1576-1585) and KVStore.DisconnectBlockAtHeight (1841-1849) call delChannelEdgeUnsafe for each channel to remove and deliberately tolerate ErrEdgeNotFound, but they still append the returned *models.ChannelEdgeInfo, which is nil on every error path of delChannelEdgeUnsafe (3224-3240). After the write transaction commits, both functions iterate the collected slice and read channel.ChannelID to invalidate the reject and channel caches (1627-1631, 1894-1898). A nil entry is a nil-pointer dereference; PruneGraph runs in the Builder's networkHandler goroutine with no recover, so lnd panics and exits.

The tolerated path is reachable for a channel whose chan-index and edge-index entries exist: fetchChanEdgePolicies (5387-5418) maps every policy read failure onto ErrEdgeNotFound, and a policy can be stored in a form the reader rejects. serializeChanEdgePolicy (5481-5491) checks only that ExtraOpaqueData is <= MaxAllowedExtraOpaqueBytes (10000) and then writes max_htlc (8 bytes, mandatory per netann/channel_update.go:280) followed by ExtraOpaqueData as one VarBytes, while deserializeChanEdgePolicyRaw (5567-5575) reads that VarBytes with a 10000-byte cap. With 9993-10000 bytes of extra data the stored blob is 10001-10008 bytes, ReadVarBytes fails with a non-EOF error, fetchChanEdgePolicy returns it, fetchChanEdgePolicies converts it to ErrEdgeNotFound, delChannelEdgeUnsafe returns (nil, ErrEdgeNotFound) before deleting anything, and PruneGraph appends nil. The gossip path (discovery/gossiper.go:3442-3451 -> Builder.UpdateEdge -> KVStore.UpdateEdgePolicy, kv_store.go:3388) imposes no bound on ExtraOpaqueData beyond TLV validity, so a remote node can plant such a policy for its own public channel. The same write/read mismatch is the subject of the verified record kvstore-policy-extra-opaque-plus-maxhtlc-exceeds-read-cap; this record is the distinct crash it enables.

Because the prune-log entry for the block is committed before the panic, the block is not reprocessed on restart, and the undeletable channel and its undecodable policy remain in the graph. With the default in-memory graph cache, startup cache population (getChannelMap, which returns any non-tolerated policy decode error) then fails on the same entry, so the node does not come back without manual intervention.

Assumption: btcd v0.25.1-0.20260310163610 wire.ReadVarBytes returns a wire.MessageError (not io.EOF/io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) when the encoded length exceeds maxAllowed, per its documented contract.

## Evidence
1. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:1576–1584](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L1576-L1584)
   PruneGraph: for every spent outpoint that has a chan-index entry, delChannelEdgeUnsafe is called; ErrEdgeNotFound is tolerated but the returned *ChannelEdgeInfo, which is nil on every error path, is still appended to chansClosed. This is the line the fix must change.
2. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:1627–1630](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L1627-L1630)
   After the write transaction (including the prune-log Put) has committed, PruneGraph reads channel.ChannelID for every collected entry; a nil entry is a nil-pointer dereference that panics the process.
3. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:1841–1848](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L1841-L1848)
   DisconnectBlockAtHeight has the identical pattern: ErrEdgeNotFound tolerated, nil edgeInfo appended to removedChans.
4. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:1894–1897](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L1894-L1897)
   removedChans is dereferenced after commit; a nil entry panics during reorg handling (syncGraphWithChain or the staleBlocks path of networkHandler).
5. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:3224–3239](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L3224-L3239)
   delChannelEdgeUnsafe returns (nil, err) when fetchChanEdgeInfo or fetchChanEdgePolicies fails, before any Delete has run, so the channel stays in the graph while the caller receives ErrEdgeNotFound.
6. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:5387–5417](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L5387-L5417)
   fetchChanEdgePolicies rewrites every error from fetchChanEdgePolicy, including a decode failure of a present value, into ErrEdgeNotFound, steering delChannelEdgeUnsafe's callers into the tolerated path.
7. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:5481–5490](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L5481-L5490)
   serializeChanEdgePolicy bounds only len(ExtraOpaqueData) <= 10000 but writes max_htlc (8 B) || ExtraOpaqueData as a single VarBytes, so a stored blob can be 10001-10008 B.
8. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:5567–5574](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L5567-L5574)
   deserializeChanEdgePolicyRaw reads that blob with wire.ReadVarBytes(r, 0, 10000, ...); a length above the cap is a non-EOF error that is propagated, and fetchChanEdgePolicy (5349-5381, case err != nil) returns it, so the stored policy is undecodable.
9. [netann/channel\_update.go:280–283](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/netann/channel_update.go#L280-L283)
   The max_htlc flag is mandatory for every accepted channel_update, so the 8-byte prefix is always written and any 9993-10000 B ExtraOpaqueData yields an unreadable policy.
10. [discovery/gossiper.go:3442–3450](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L3442-L3450)
   A remote channel_update's ExtraOpaqueData is copied into the policy (ChanEdgePolicyFromWire) and handed to Builder.UpdateEdge -> KVStore.UpdateEdgePolicy, which only checks TLV validity (kv_store.go:3388); no size bound exists on the gossip path.
11. [graph/builder.go:1157–1165](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/builder.go#L1157-L1165)
   Every accepted public channel's funding outpoint is added to the ChainView filter, so the attacker's spend of its own funding output is returned by FilterBlock and reaches PruneGraph as a spent outpoint.
12. [graph/builder.go:905–918](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/builder.go#L905-L918)
   PruneGraph is invoked for each connected block from the Builder's networkHandler goroutine (started at builder.go:287); there is no recover() in graph/, so the panic terminates lnd.

## Impact
An unrecovered panic terminates lnd at a moment the attacker picks (for example while HTLCs are in flight or a breach must be punished). The prune-log entry is committed first, so the block is not reprocessed, and the poisoned policy remains; with the default graph cache, startup population returns the same decode error and the node stays down until the operator repairs the database. No data is disclosed; the only state change is the already-committed prune-log entry and the channel that should have been removed but was not.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any Lightning node that owns a public channel the victim has in its graph. It signs a channel_update for that channel with 9993-10000 bytes of valid odd-type TLV extra data (well within the 65535-byte wire limit); the gossiper verifies signature and fields only and the store persists it. The attacker then broadcasts the spend of its own funding output at a time of its choosing. When the block arrives, the chain filter matches the outpoint, PruneGraph tolerates the decode-derived ErrEdgeNotFound, appends nil, commits the prune log and panics. No victim configuration or interaction is needed; the default btcd/bitcoind backends validate and filter channel outpoints.

## Recommended fix
1. PruneGraph and DisconnectBlockAtHeight append delChannelEdgeUnsafe's return value even when the tolerated ErrEdgeNotFound is returned, and later dereference the nil pointer in the cache-invalidation loop after the transaction has committed. Fix criteria: Only successfully deleted edges may be collected into chansClosed/removedChans, and the post-commit loops must never dereference a nil entry. Verify by making delChannelEdgeUnsafe return ErrEdgeNotFound for a chan-index hit (e.g. a policy value the reader rejects) and confirming PruneGraph and DisconnectBlockAtHeight return normally without a panic.
2. fetchChanEdgePolicies converts every policy read error, including decode failures of a present value, into ErrEdgeNotFound, hiding corruption as absence and steering callers into tolerated-error paths that leave the channel in the graph. Fix criteria: A decode failure of a present policy value must be distinguishable from a missing policy so callers do not treat corruption as 'not found'; verify by storing an undecodable policy value and confirming delChannelEdgeUnsafe either deletes the channel or returns a non-ErrEdgeNotFound error.
3. The policy serializer and deserializer disagree on the bound of the stored blob (max_htlc prefix plus ExtraOpaqueData versus a 10000-byte read cap), so remotely supplied data can be persisted in a form the node cannot read back. Fix criteria: Every policy the store accepts must be readable by the store's own deserializer; verify by writing a policy with max_htlc set and 10000 bytes of ExtraOpaqueData and confirming fetchChanEdgePolicy decodes it or the write is rejected before persistence.

# DeriveSharedKey with an unknown raw pubkey runs a 100,000-key BIP32 scan inside the wallet DB write transaction, stalling onion processing, signing and wallet writes

## Details
signrpc.Signer/DeriveSharedKey lets the caller identify the local key by raw public key. When key_desc.raw_key_bytes is supplied the handler forces key_index to 0 and hands KeyDescriptor{Family, Index: 0, PubKey} to KeyRing.ECDH (lnrpc/signrpc/signer_server.go:819-847); any valid compressed secp256k1 point is accepted and nothing checks that it belongs to the wallet. BtcWalletKeyRing.ECDH -> DerivePrivKey then (a) skips the derivation cache because PubKey != nil, (b) opens a walletdb.Update transaction, (c) persists the caller-chosen key family as an account, and (d) because PubKey is set and Index == 0, linearly derives up to MaxKeyRangeScan = 100,000 children of that family, comparing each to the supplied point, inside that write transaction (keychain/btcwallet.go:273-372, keychain/derivation.go:46-50). For a point that is not a child of the family every one of the 100,000 BIP32 derivations (HMAC-SHA512 plus EC scalar multiplications to obtain each child pubkey) runs before ErrCannotDerivePrivKey is returned, so a ~100-byte request holds the wallet database's exclusive writer lock for the whole scan — on the order of seconds per request.

While the lock is held every wallet.db writer in the process waits: the sphinx router's onion decryption, because server.go:671 wraps the node key as NewPubKeyECDH(*nodeKeyDesc, cc.KeyRing) with PubKey set and Index 0 and therefore takes the same DerivePrivKey -> walletdb.Update path for every HTLC and onion message; commitment, HTLC and sweep signing via lnwallet/btcwallet fetchPrivKey -> deriveKeyByLocator -> DeriveFromKeyPathAddAccount; the wallet's block/transaction processing; address and key derivation; funding flows and transaction publishing. With the postgres kvdb backend WalletDBWithGlobalLock defaults to true (lncfg/db.go:124), so wallet reads block as well. A caller can keep several requests in flight so that legitimate writers are delayed by the sum of the queued scans, and sustain this for as long as it keeps sending, degrading HTLC forwarding/settlement and on-chain reaction for the duration. Since the request fails, no key material is returned. Account creation for the chosen family is already reachable by a signer:generate caller through SignMessage with any family and is not counted as a gain here.

Entry points verified: SignOutputRaw and ComputeInputScript go through BtcWallet.fetchPrivKey (locator derivation or PrivKeyForAddress lookup, no scan); SignMessage/SignMessageCompact/SignMessageSchnorr and MuSig2CreateSession pass a KeyLocator only. DeriveSharedKey is therefore the sole RPC entry to the scan branch and requires the signer:generate permission (signer.macaroon, or the custom macaroon docs/remote-signing.md tells operators to bake for the watch-only node). That permission grants signing and ECDH with wallet keys, not the node's wallet lock, and the threat model names limited-macaroon RPC callers reaching beyond their grant as in scope. In remote-signing deployments the watch-only node sends the same shape for legitimate index-0 keys (lnwallet/rpcwallet/rpcwallet.go:448-451), so the signer's wallet.db is the one locked and the watch-only node's requests fail on their 5 s rpcTimeout.

Dependency behaviour assumed (btcwallet v0.16.20-pre and walletdb v1.5.1, bbolt v1.4.3 per go.mod): ScopedKeyManager.DeriveFromKeyPath performs fresh BIP32 child derivations per call with no per-index cache; walletdb.Update on the bbolt backend holds bbolt's single writer lock for the whole closure (readers are not blocked); Wallet.DeriveFromKeyPathAddAccount uses a write transaction. If btcwallet caches per-index derivations the wall-clock cost per request drops, but the lock is still held for the full 100,000-iteration loop.

This resolves ledger lead lead-btcwallet-342-cd95.

## Evidence
1. [keychain/btcwallet.go:342–371](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/keychain/btcwallet.go#L342-L371)
   Scan branch of BtcWalletKeyRing.DerivePrivKey: with PubKey set and Index == 0 it performs up to MaxKeyRangeScan sequential scope.DeriveFromKeyPath calls, comparing each derived pubkey to the supplied point, all inside the enclosing walletdb.Update closure. For a point that is not a child of that family all 100,000 iterations run before ErrCannotDerivePrivKey is returned. This is the code the fix must change: the search must not run under the exclusive writer, or must resolve via an index rather than a linear scan.
2. [keychain/btcwallet.go:273–301](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/keychain/btcwallet.go#L273-L301)
   The DeriveFromKeyPathCache fast path is skipped whenever PubKey != nil (273-284); the request then opens walletdb.Update (exclusive writer on bbolt; on the postgres kvdb backend WalletDBWithGlobalLock defaults true, lncfg/db.go:124, so readers block too) and createAccountIfNotExists persists the caller-chosen family before the scan.
3. [lnrpc/signrpc/signer\_server.go:819–846](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/signrpc/signer_server.go#L819-L846)
   signrpc.Signer/DeriveSharedKey: when key_desc.raw_key_bytes is set the handler requires key_index == 0 (819-821), parses any valid compressed secp256k1 point (parseRawKeyBytes, 1250-1268) and calls cfg.KeyRing.ECDH with KeyDescriptor{Family: caller-chosen, Index: 0, PubKey: caller-chosen}. Nothing checks that the point belongs to the wallet, so the attacker chooses a point that forces the full scan.
4. [lnrpc/signrpc/signer\_server.go:73–76](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/signrpc/signer_server.go#L73-L76)
   DeriveSharedKey is gated only by the signer:generate macaroon permission; no rate limit or concurrency cap applies (lnd.go:376 sets only MaxRecvMsgSize). SignOutputRaw/ComputeInputScript use BtcWallet.fetchPrivKey (locator or PrivKeyForAddress lookup, no scan) and SignMessage*/MuSig2CreateSession pass a locator only, so this is the sole RPC entry to the scan branch.
5. [keychain/btcwallet.go:389–394](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/keychain/btcwallet.go#L389-L394)
   ECDH passes the full descriptor, including the caller's PubKey, straight to DerivePrivKey.
6. [keychain/derivation.go:46–49](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/keychain/derivation.go#L46-L49)
   MaxKeyRangeScan = 100000 bounds the scan; the bound is a constant the attacker's unknown pubkey always reaches, not something the input shrinks.
7. [server.go:671](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L671)
   The sphinx router's nodeKeyECDH is keychain.NewPubKeyECDH(*nodeKeyDesc, cc.KeyRing): nodeKeyDesc carries PubKey and Index 0, so every onion decryption (HTLC forward/receive, onion messages) goes through the same DerivePrivKey -> walletdb.Update path and queues behind the attacker's held writer lock.
8. [lnwallet/btcwallet/signer.go:179–198](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/btcwallet/signer.go#L179-L198)
   Commitment/HTLC/sweep signing resolves keys via fetchPrivKey -> deriveKeyByLocator -> wallet.DeriveFromKeyPathAddAccount on the same wallet database (a write transaction in btcwallet), so signing requests also queue behind the held writer lock.
9. [lnwallet/rpcwallet/rpcwallet.go:448–450](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/rpcwallet/rpcwallet.go#L448-L450)
   In remote-signing deployments the watch-only node legitimately sends exactly this request shape (raw_key_bytes with index 0), which is why the RPC layer cannot simply reject raw pubkeys; the signer's wallet.db is the one locked and the watch-only node's calls fail on the 5 s rpcTimeout (lncfg/remotesigner.go:11).

## Impact
Confidentiality: none, the ECDH fails and no key material is returned. Integrity: none counted — the only durable side effect (an account persisted for the chosen family) is already available to the same caller through SignMessage with any family, a sanctioned path. Availability: while each scan runs every wallet.db write in lnd waits — onion decryption for every HTLC (server.go:671 routes it through the same DerivePrivKey write transaction), the key derivations commitment/HTLC/sweep signing depends on, and the wallet's chain processing — and the attacker can keep requests queued for as long as it likes, so the node's HTLC pipeline and on-chain reaction are denied for the duration of the attack.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds a macaroon with signer:generate (the signer.macaroon, or the remote-signing custom macaroon) and reaches gRPC 10009 or REST 8080. They call DeriveSharedKey with ephemeral_pubkey = any valid point and key_desc{raw_key_bytes: any valid point not derived from the wallet, key_loc{key_family: F, key_index: 0}}. The handler accepts it, DerivePrivKey opens a write transaction and runs 100,000 derivations before failing. Repeating or pipelining the call keeps the wallet writer lock continuously contended. No configuration change or user interaction is needed, but signer:generate is a high privilege that is not handed to arbitrary users.

## Recommended fix
BtcWalletKeyRing.DerivePrivKey performs a 100,000-step linear key search inside an exclusive wallet write transaction whenever a descriptor carries a public key with index 0, and signrpc.DeriveSharedKey lets any signer:generate caller supply an arbitrary such public key and family. Fix criteria: A DeriveSharedKey request naming a public key the wallet does not know must fail without holding the wallet writer lock for the search: resolve the key through the wallet's address/key index or a read-only transaction, perform any scan outside the write transaction (opening a short write only to persist a key that was actually found), or otherwise bound the work done under the writer. Verify that a request with a random valid pubkey returns an error while concurrent wallet writes and onion decryptions proceed without waiting on it, and that the legitimate remote-signing shape (raw_key_bytes with index 0 for a real wallet key) still succeeds.

# ChainNotifier RPC accepts height_hint=1, letting read-only callers force full-chain block rescans

## Details
The ChainNotifier sub-server (chainrpc, compiled into release builds via RELEASE_TAGS) exposes RegisterConfirmationsNtfn and RegisterSpendNtfn under `onchain:read`, a permission in the default readonly.macaroon (rpcserver.go readPermissions) and in chainnotifier.macaroon. Both handlers pass the caller's `height_hint` unchanged to ChainNotifier.RegisterConfirmationsNtfn / RegisterSpendNtfn (lnrpc/chainrpc/chain_server.go:384-386, 506-508). The TxNotifier's only guard is `if heightHint == 0 { return ErrNoHeightHint }` (chainntnfs/txnotifier.go:588-590 and 1031-1033), commented 'to prevent scanning from the genesis block'; a hint of 1 passes. For a never-seen txid/script/outpoint there is no height-hint cache entry, so startHeight stays 1 (txnotifier.go:645-656, 1077-1088) and, unless 1 > currentHeight, a HistoricalConfDispatch/HistoricalSpendDispatch over [1, currentHeight] is returned (txnotifier.go:735-770, 1153-1183).

On the bitcoind backend the notifier dispatches each historical request in its own goroutine with no concurrency cap (chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:255-352). Script-only conf requests (zero txid, bitcoind.go:540) and script-only spend requests (zero outpoint, bitcoind.go:766-774) go straight to confDetailsManually (bitcoind.go:589-640) / historicalSpendDetails (bitcoind.go:865-918), which iterate every height from the tip down to 1, issuing GetBlockHash plus a full GetBlock to the backend for each block and deserializing it in lnd, matching every transaction. The btcd backend has the same loop for confirmations (chainntnfs/btcdnotify/btcd.go:647-700); neutrino drives a filter rescan from the same StartHeight (neutrinonotify/neutrino.go:985-1008). Txid-based conf requests also fall into the manual scan whenever the txindex lookup returns any error other than the exact not-found message matched in ConfDetailsFromTxIndex (bitcoind.go:551-565); whether a bitcoind without -txindex produces a non-matching message is an assumption about Bitcoin Core, not load-bearing here because the script-only path always scans manually.

Cancelling the RPC stream does not abort the scan: the handler's deferred Cancel() reaches TxNotifier.CancelConf/CancelSpend, which only close the client's channels and delete the ntfn from the set (txnotifier.go:777-816, 1188-1216); the rescan goroutine checks only b.quit. Each fresh script/outpoint is a new ConfRequest/SpendRequest with rescanStatus rescanNotStarted, so N ~100-byte requests start N independent, hours-long tip-to-genesis block walks running in parallel, each holding one full block (up to 4 MB) in memory while decoding. The bound on work is currentHeight - height_hint, which the attacker sets; the code fixes nothing.

The nearest sanctioned read-only path, ChainKit.GetBlock, returns one block per request to the caller (the caller pays the bandwidth) and RegisterBlockEpochNtfn's backlog fetches only hashes and 80-byte headers, so this path hands a read-only caller something neither concedes: unbounded full-block download, deserialization and matching work on the node and its chain backend, amplified from a tiny request and repeatable without limit. Impact is availability of a funds-critical component: lnd's own time-sensitive backend calls (GetBlock in handleBlockConnected, wallet RPCs, sendrawtransaction for sweeps/justice transactions) compete with the attacker's scans for the backend's RPC workers (Bitcoin Core's shallow default work queue is an assumption about the backend), and lnd's own CPU and memory scale with the number of concurrent scans the attacker chooses.

## Evidence
1. [lnrpc/chainrpc/chain\_server.go:384–386](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/chainrpc/chain_server.go#L384-L386)
   RegisterConfirmationsNtfn forwards the caller-supplied in.HeightHint to ChainNotifier.RegisterConfirmationsNtfn with no floor, no clamp to wallet birthday and no relation to the current tip; this is where an RPC-originated hint should be bounded.
2. [lnrpc/chainrpc/chain\_server.go:506–508](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/chainrpc/chain_server.go#L506-L508)
   RegisterSpendNtfn forwards in.HeightHint unvalidated for outpoint- or script-based spend registrations.
3. [lnrpc/chainrpc/chain\_server.go:62–69](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/chainrpc/chain_server.go#L62-L69)
   Both streaming RPCs require only onchain:read.
4. [rpcserver.go:105–108](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L105-L108)
   readPermissions, which defines the default readonly.macaroon, includes onchain:read, so the lowest-privilege standard macaroon reaches these RPCs.
5. [chainntnfs/txnotifier.go:586–590](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/txnotifier.go#L586-L590)
   The only guard against a genesis-to-tip scan rejects heightHint == 0 ('to prevent scanning from the genesis block'); a hint of 1 passes. The identical check for spends is at lines 1029-1034.
6. [chainntnfs/txnotifier.go:645–656](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/txnotifier.go#L645-L656)
   startHeight is the caller's hint unless the hint cache holds a higher value; an attacker-chosen never-seen script/txid has no cache entry, so startHeight stays 1 (same at 1077-1089 for spends).
7. [chainntnfs/txnotifier.go:735–770](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/txnotifier.go#L735-L770)
   Unless startHeight > currentHeight, a HistoricalConfDispatch over [startHeight, currentHeight] is returned and the set is marked rescanPending; a fresh request is always rescanNotStarted, so each distinct script yields a new dispatch (spend equivalent at 1153-1183).
8. [chainntnfs/txnotifier.go:777–816](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/txnotifier.go#L777-L816)
   CancelConf, invoked by the RPC handler's deferred Cancel() when the stream closes, only closes the client's channels and deletes the ntfn from the set; it does not signal the running historical rescan, so cancelling the stream leaves the scan running (CancelSpend at 1188-1216 is the same).
9. [chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:255–351](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go#L255-L351)
   Every HistoricalConfDispatch/HistoricalSpendDispatch is run in its own goroutine with no cap on concurrent rescans and only b.quit as an abort signal, so N requests yield N parallel full-chain walks.
10. [chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:540–565](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go#L540-L565)
   Script-only conf requests (zero txid) go straight to confDetailsManually; txid requests also fall back to it on any txindex lookup error other than the exact not-found message.
11. [chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:589–640](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go#L589-L640)
   confDetailsManually walks every height from currentHeight down to heightHint (1), issuing GetBlockHash and a full GetBlock per block and matching every transaction; the loop bound is the attacker's hint.
12. [chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:766–774](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go#L766-L774)
   Script-only spend requests are dispatched to the historical scan unconditionally, skipping the GetTxOut/txindex short-cuts available for outpoints.
13. [chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:865–918](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go#L865-L918)
   historicalSpendDetails is the equivalent tip-to-startHeight full-block walk for spend requests.
14. [chainntnfs/btcdnotify/btcd.go:647–700](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/btcdnotify/btcd.go#L647-L700)
   The btcd backend's confDetailsManually has the identical tip-to-startHeight full-block loop; neutrino dispatches a filter rescan from the same StartHeight (neutrinonotify/neutrino.go:985-1008).

## Impact
No data is disclosed or modified. Availability: each request forces an hours-long sequential download and deserialization of the whole chain (~900k blocks), and the number of concurrent scans is set by the attacker, so lnd's CPU and memory (one full block in flight per goroutine) and the chain backend's RPC capacity scale with the attack. lnd's time-critical backend calls (block fetch on new tips, wallet RPCs, broadcasting sweeps and justice transactions) compete with the scans; the threat model classes impairing the node's on-chain reaction as funds-relevant availability. The attacker can sustain this indefinitely from a read-only position, so availability is rated high; the degree to which the backend rejects lnd's own calls under load depends on the backend's RPC work-queue behaviour (Bitcoin Core / btcd), stated here as an assumption.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds any macaroon with onchain:read (the default readonly.macaroon handed to dashboards/monitoring, or chainnotifier.macaroon) and can reach the gRPC (10009) or REST (8080) listener, which the threat model treats as a network interface used by mobile apps and third parties. They call RegisterConfirmationsNtfn with a random valid P2WPKH script, zero txid, num_confs=1, height_hint=1 (or RegisterSpendNtfn with a random script and no outpoint). The notifier accepts the hint, finds no cache entry, and spawns a goroutine that fetches every block from tip to height 1. Repeating with fresh scripts spawns unlimited parallel scans; closing the stream does not stop them. No race, no special configuration, no user interaction; the chainrpc sub-server is compiled into release builds.

## Recommended fix
1. The RPC handlers and the TxNotifier treat any non-zero height_hint as acceptable, so the guard intended to prevent genesis-to-tip rescans is satisfied by a hint of 1 and a low-privilege RPC caller directly controls the size of the historical rescan window. Fix criteria: A caller-supplied height hint must not start a historical rescan earlier than a node-derived floor (for example the wallet birthday height or a bounded window below the current tip), or RPC-originated registrations must be rejected when they would scan more than a bounded number of blocks. Verify by registering with height_hint=1 for an unknown script and confirming no tip-to-genesis block walk is started.
2. Historical rescans spawned on behalf of RPC clients are unbounded in number and are not tied to the registering stream, so one client can run arbitrarily many concurrent full-chain scans that outlive its connections. Fix criteria: Concurrent RPC-originated historical rescans must be bounded (per client or globally) and a rescan whose only registrants have cancelled must stop. Verify by opening and closing many registrations and confirming the number of in-flight scan goroutines and backend block requests stays bounded.

# Channel announcement with >898 B feature vector is stored but unreadable, blocking lnd startup

## Details
The default (bbolt/kvdb) graph store writes a channel's feature vector without any size limit but reads it back with a hard 900-byte cap. putChanEdgeInfo (graph/db/kv_store.go:4969-4977) serialises edgeInfo.Features via lnwire.RawFeatureVector.Encode (uint16 length + base256 bits, sized by the highest set bit) and wraps it with wire.WriteVarBytes, which has no maximum; deserializeChanEdgeInfo (:5137-5146) reads it with wire.ReadVarBytes(r, 0, 900, "features"). Any stored vector of 901+ bytes - a feature bit at index >= 7184 - therefore yields an edge-index entry that can never be decoded again.

The feature vector of a remote ChannelAnnouncement1 is attacker-controlled and unbounded short of the 65533-byte wire frame: lnwire decodes it with a uint16 length (lnwire/features.go:661-671; channel_announcement.go:73-93), netann.validateChannelAnn1 verifies only the four signatures (netann/channel_announcement.go:96), the funding-output check (validateFundingTransaction) says nothing about features and is skipped under AssumeChannelValid (the neutrino default, config_builder.go:1741), and the gossiper stores ann.Features unchanged via models.WithFeatures (discovery/gossiper.go:2810) before Builder.AddEdge -> KVStore.AddChannelEdge -> putChanEdgeInfo. lnd's own announcements (funding/manager.go:4543) use an empty vector, so the legacy cap was never exercised by honest traffic; nothing in the write path enforces it.

Because fetchChanEdgeInfo/deserializeChanEdgeInfo is the first step of essentially every edge operation, one poisoned row has graph-wide, permanent effect:
- lnd cannot start in the default (non-AssumeChannelValid) mode: Builder.Start calls ChannelView (graph/builder.go:240-247), which aborts on the first undecodable edge (kv_store.go:4300-4305); server.go treats the Builder.Start error as fatal (lnd.go:771). This recurs on every restart.
- While running: DescribeGraph (forEachChannel), graph-cache population (ForEachChannelCacheable; async by default, so logged Critical and the cache marked failed, forcing DB fallback), FilterChannelRange for any query_channel_range covering that block, ChanUpdatesInHorizon/FetchChanInfos for that channel, and nodeTraversal for both endpoint nodes all fail.
- The edge cannot be removed: delChannelEdgeUnsafe (:3228-3231) returns the decode error, so DeleteChannelEdges, zombie pruning, PruneGraph for the block spending the funding output and DisconnectBlockAtHeight for that height all fail; in the builder's startup chain-sync path those are also fatal. No shipped RPC or tool repairs the row; the graph shares channel.db with channel state, so it cannot simply be discarded.

Dependency assumption: btcd v0.25.1-0.20260310163610 wire.ReadVarBytes returns a *MessageError when the varint count exceeds maxAllowed, and wire.WriteVarBytes imposes no maximum - the behaviour lnd relies on for every other capped field in this file.

## Evidence
1. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:4969–4976](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L4969-L4976)
   putChanEdgeInfo encodes edgeInfo.Features (uint16 length + bit vector, lnwire.RawFeatureVector.Encode) and persists it with wire.WriteVarBytes with no size bound; this is where the fix must bound (or reject) the vector so that every committed edge round-trips.
2. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:5137–5145](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L5137-L5145)
   deserializeChanEdgeInfo reads the same field with wire.ReadVarBytes(r, 0, 900, "features"); a stored blob of 901+ bytes (bit vector >= 899 bytes, i.e. any feature bit at index >= 7184) fails permanently with a btcd wire MessageError, so the edge-index value can never be decoded again.
3. [discovery/gossiper.go:2773–2810](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2773-L2810)
   handleChanAnnouncement validates only the four signatures (netann.ValidateChannelAnn -> validateChannelAnn1) and then builds the edge with models.WithFeatures(ann.Features) unmodified; the only other check before AddEdge (line 2957) is validateFundingTransaction, which is skipped entirely when AssumeChannelValid is set (the neutrino default, config_builder.go:1741).
4. [lnwire/features.go:661–670](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/features.go#L661-L670)
   RawFeatureVector.Decode accepts any uint16 length and sets a bit per set position, so a ChannelAnnouncement1 (bounded only by MaxMsgBody = 65533) can carry a feature bit at any index up to ~520k, far beyond the store's 898-byte reader limit.
5. [lnwire/channel\_announcement.go:73–92](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/channel_announcement.go#L73-L92)
   ChannelAnnouncement1.Decode reads Features via ReadElements (**RawFeatureVector case) with no additional bound; the features are covered by DataToSign so the announcer signs them with keys it controls.
6. [graph/builder.go:240–246](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/builder.go#L240-L246)
   Builder.Start (default, non-AssumeChannelValid mode) calls v1Graph.ChannelView and returns any error other than ErrGraphNoEdgesFound; server.go:2432-2436 propagates a Builder.Start error as startErr and lnd.go:771 exits with 'unable to start server', so lnd cannot start on any restart once the poisoned edge exists.
7. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:4300–4304](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L4300-L4304)
   ChannelView iterates the whole channel-point index and aborts on the first fetchChanEdgeInfo error, so a single undecodable edge-index value fails the whole call.
8. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:3228–3230](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L3228-L3230)
   delChannelEdgeUnsafe begins with fetchChanEdgeInfo and returns its error, so the poisoned edge can never be deleted: DeleteChannelEdges, zombie pruning, PruneGraph for the block spending its funding output and DisconnectBlockAtHeight for its height all fail (and are fatal in the builder's startup chain-sync path).
9. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:3786–3788](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L3786-L3788)
   nodeTraversal aborts on fetchChanEdgeInfo error, so every DB-path read of either endpoint node's channels (ForEachNodeChannel, GetNodeInfo, isPublic, DB-fallback pathfinding) fails.
10. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:2956–2958](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L2956-L2958)
   FilterChannelRange deserializes every edge in the requested height range and aborts on error, so every query_channel_range reply covering the poisoned channel's block fails.
11. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:459–475](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L459-L475)
   forEachChannel (DescribeGraph) and ForEachChannelCacheable (:498-545, graph-cache population) abort on the deserializeChanEdgeInfo error; with the default async cache load the population failure is logged Critical and the cache is marked failed, with the sync option it is a second fatal startup error.

## Impact
Availability: in the default mode lnd fails to start on every restart until the operator surgically edits channel.db (no shipped RPC or tool can delete the row, and the graph buckets share the file with channel state); while running, DescribeGraph, gossip range queries for that block, graph-cache population and DB reads of the two endpoint nodes fail. A node that cannot start cannot resolve HTLCs or punish breaches. Integrity: the graph permanently holds an edge that no supported path can update, prune or delete, and the block containing it cannot be pruned or reorged. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any remote party that can author a ChannelAnnouncement1 reaching the victim - directly over 9735 (post-brontide, no channel needed) or relayed by the gossip network. It signs with four keys it controls and sets one feature bit at index >= 7184. In default bitcoind/btcd mode it must also have confirmed one funding-style 2-of-2 output for those bitcoin keys (one on-chain tx, attacker cost only); under neutrino (AssumeChannelValid default) even that is skipped. Signature validation passes and the edge is committed deterministically; no victim configuration, privilege or interaction is involved. The victim's next restart fails.

## Recommended fix
1. putChanEdgeInfo persists feature vectors of any length while deserializeChanEdgeInfo caps the field at 900 bytes, so an accepted write can be unreadable. Fix criteria: Any edge info the store commits must round-trip through deserializeChanEdgeInfo: either the write path rejects (or the gossiper refuses) feature vectors the reader cannot decode, or the reader's bound matches the writer's. Verify by persisting an edge whose features set bit 65000 and reading it back via fetchChanEdgeInfo, ChannelView and FilterChannelRange without error (or confirming the announcement is rejected before storage).
2. ChannelView, forEachChannel, nodeTraversal, FilterChannelRange and delChannelEdgeUnsafe treat a single undecodable edge-index value as fatal for the whole operation, and the edge cannot be deleted, so one bad row disables startup and graph-wide reads. Fix criteria: An undecodable edge-index entry must not prevent lnd from starting or abort graph-wide reads, and must remain deletable/prunable. Verify by injecting an undecodable edge-index value and confirming Builder.Start, DescribeGraph, FilterChannelRange and DeleteChannelEdges still succeed (skipping or repairing the bad entry).

# Channel policy with 9993-10000 B extra data stored but unreadable, poisoning the graph store

## Details
The kv graph store's channel-policy serializer and deserializer disagree about the maximum size of the trailing opaque blob. serializeChanEdgePolicy (graph/db/kv_store.go:5470-5491) prepends the 8-byte max_htlc value to ExtraOpaqueData and writes both as a single VarBytes, enforcing only len(ExtraOpaqueData) <= MaxAllowedExtraOpaqueBytes (10000). deserializeChanEdgePolicyRaw (5566-5575) reads that same blob with wire.ReadVarBytes(..., 10000, ...). Because lnd requires message_flags bit 0 (max_htlc present) on every accepted channel_update (netann/channel_update.go:280-283, validateChannelUpdate1Fields), any policy whose ExtraOpaqueData is 9993..10000 bytes is written as a 10001..10008-byte blob and can never be read back: ReadVarBytes returns a wire MessageError, which the deserializer does not tolerate (only io.EOF/ErrUnexpectedEOF, ErrEdgePolicyOptionalFieldNotFound and ErrParsingExtraTLVBytes are).

Attack: any gossip participant that owns one public channel known to the victim (one side of a channel suffices; the signature only has to come from that node's key) sends a channel_update whose ExtraOpaqueData is a well-formed TLV stream of 9993..10000 bytes (e.g. one odd-type record; tlv P2P decoding caps individual records at 65535 bytes, tlv/stream.go:224). lnwire accepts it (ExtraOpaqueData.Decode is io.ReadAll, lnwire/extra_bytes.go; channel_update.go:164-184), the gossiper verifies the signature and calls Graph.UpdateEdge with ExtraOpaqueData unmodified (gossiper.go:3442-3450; models.ChanEdgePolicyFromWire copies it verbatim), builder.updateEdge adds no size check, UpdateEdgePolicy only checks ValidateTLV (kv_store.go:3400-3413), and the record is committed. The first update for a channel direction is not rate-limited. The kv store is the default graph backend (lncfg/db.go:132 UseNativeSQL=false).

Consequences, all persistent:
- The record is sticky: putChanEdgePolicy (5248-5270) must deserialize the previous policy and fails, so no later channel_update can replace it; delChannelEdgeUnsafe (3226-3246) fails via fetchChanEdgePolicies (5395-5417), so DeleteChannelEdges/zombie pruning cannot remove it either. Only manual DB surgery fixes it.
- Every full-graph read aborts: getChannelMap (285-300) propagates the error, breaking DescribeGraph (rpcserver.go:6253) and the in-memory graph-cache population (graph.go:218-276). With the default async population (graph/db/options.go:283) the error is Critical-logged, finishPopulation(false) marks the cache failed and never loaded (graph_cache_state.go:68-80), so all pathfinding falls back to the DB nodeTraversal path; with db.sync-graph-cache-load lnd fails to start (graph.go:131-135).
- nodeTraversal (3760-3806) fails for both endpoints of the channel, so DB-path pathfinding (now the only path) errors out whenever the search touches the attacker's node or its peer; an attacker who opens the channel to a popular hub breaks most payments.
- ChanUpdatesInHorizon fails whenever the horizon covers the entry (2344-2352): gossip_timestamp_range backlogs cannot be served and, once the update ages past ChannelPruneExpiry, pruneZombieChans (builder.go:650-668) fails every run (logged at builder.go:219-221, 799-801), permanently disabling zombie pruning.
- When the attacker later spends the funding output, PruneGraph (1575-1584) swallows the wrapped ErrEdgeNotFound from delChannelEdgeUnsafe and appends the nil edgeInfo to chansClosed; the downstream handling of that nil entry is filed separately as kvstore-prunegraph-nil-edgeinfo-deref-on-edge-not-found.

The maintainers' own tests exercise only ExtraOpaqueData well below the cap; nothing in discovery/, netann/ or graph/ bounds a channel_update's extra bytes before storage. Assumption on dependency: btcd v0.25.1-pre (go.mod) wire.ReadVarBytes rejects a count greater than maxAllowed with a *MessageError before reading the payload.

## Evidence
1. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:5470–5490](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L5470-L5490)
   serializeChanEdgePolicy builds one VarBytes blob = 8-byte MaxHTLC (always present: BOLT 7 message_flags bit 0 must be set) + ExtraOpaqueData. The only size check is len(ExtraOpaqueData) > 10000, so blobs of 10001..10008 bytes are written to disk.
2. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:5566–5574](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L5566-L5574)
   deserializeChanEdgePolicyRaw reads the same blob with wire.ReadVarBytes(r, 0, MaxAllowedExtraOpaqueBytes=10000, ...). A 10001..10008-byte count yields a wire MessageError, which is neither io.EOF nor io.ErrUnexpectedEOF, so the function returns (nil, err) and the policy can never be decoded again.
3. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:3400–3412](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L3400-L3412)
   UpdateEdgePolicy only runs ExtraOpaqueData.ValidateTLV() before persisting; a well-formed TLV stream of exactly 10000 bytes (one odd-type record) passes.
4. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:5248–5269](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L5248-L5269)
   putChanEdgePolicy must deserialize the *existing* policy to delete its update-index entry; only ErrEdgePolicyOptionalFieldNotFound/ErrParsingExtraTLVBytes are tolerated. The poisoned blob returns a different error, so every later channel_update for that direction fails: the record is sticky and cannot be repaired by the owner or anyone else.
5. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:5366–5416](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L5366-L5416)
   fetchChanEdgePolicy propagates the non-tolerated error; fetchChanEdgePolicies rewrites any policy error into ErrEdgeNotFound. Every caller that reads both policies (HasV1ChannelEdge, FetchChannelEdgesByID/ByOutpoint, fetchChanInfos, fetchNextChanUpdateBatch, delChannelEdgeUnsafe) therefore fails for this channel.
6. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:285–299](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L285-L299)
   getChannelMap (used by forEachChannel and ForEachChannelCacheable) aborts the whole iteration on any error other than the two tolerated ones, so one poisoned policy breaks every full-graph read: DescribeGraph and the in-memory graph cache population at startup.
7. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:3226–3245](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L3226-L3245)
   delChannelEdgeUnsafe calls fetchChanEdgePolicies before deleting anything and returns (nil, ErrEdgeNotFound-wrapped) on failure, so the poisoned channel can never be deleted or zombie-pruned: DeleteChannelEdges aborts the whole batch, and PruneGraph (1575-1584) swallows the error and appends the nil edgeInfo to chansClosed (downstream handling filed separately as kvstore-prunegraph-nil-edgeinfo-deref-on-edge-not-found).
8. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:3760–3771](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L3760-L3771)
   nodeTraversal (DB-path pathfinding via ForEachNodeDirectedChannel/GraphSession, ForEachNodeChannel for GetNodeInfo, isPublic for NodeUpdatesInHorizon) aborts when fetchChanEdgePolicy fails for either endpoint of the poisoned channel.
9. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:2344–2351](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L2344-L2351)
   fetchNextChanUpdateBatch returns the fetchChanEdgePolicies error, so ChanUpdatesInHorizon fails whenever the horizon covers the poisoned channel's update-index entry.
10. [graph/builder.go:650–667](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/builder.go#L650-L667)
   pruneZombieChans iterates ChanUpdatesInHorizon from epoch to now-ChannelPruneExpiry and returns on the first error, so once the poisoned update ages past the horizon, zombie pruning is permanently disabled for the whole graph.
11. [graph/db/graph.go:259–275](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/graph.go#L259-L275)
   populateCache returns the ForEachChannelCacheable error. With the default async population this is Critical-logged and the cache stays in the failed state, so all pathfinding falls back to the DB nodeTraversal path, which itself fails on the poisoned channel; with db.sync-graph-cache-load the error makes ChannelGraph.Start, and therefore lnd startup, fail.
12. [discovery/gossiper.go:3442–3449](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L3442-L3449)
   The gossiper builds the policy from the wire ChannelUpdate1 with ExtraOpaqueData unmodified and calls Graph.UpdateEdge; no size check exists upstream.
13. [lnwire/channel\_update.go:164–183](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/channel_update.go#L164-L183)
   ChannelUpdate1.Decode retains the complete remaining bytes as ExtraOpaqueData, bounded only by the 65535-byte wire message, so 10000 bytes of extra TLV data are accepted and signed over.
14. [rpcserver.go:6253–6256](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L6253-L6256)
   DescribeGraph is implemented with ForEachChannel and so returns an error for the whole graph once one policy is poisoned.

## Impact
Availability: DescribeGraph, graph-cache population, gossip horizon replies and zombie pruning fail persistently; DB-fallback pathfinding fails for searches touching the poisoned channel's endpoints; with sync cache load lnd cannot start. Integrity: the graph store permanently holds a record that cannot be updated or removed through any supported path and zombie pruning of the whole graph stops, degrading routing-table correctness. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any Lightning node that owns one public channel announced to the victim (a few thousand sats, no relationship to the victim). It signs and broadcasts a single channel_update with a 10000-byte TLV ExtraOpaqueData and max_htlc flag; the gossip network relays it, or the attacker connects directly to the victim's 9735 and sends it. No victim configuration, interaction or privilege is involved; the write is accepted deterministically. From then on full-graph reads, policy updates and deletion of that channel fail until the operator edits channel.db by hand.

## Recommended fix
1. serializeChanEdgePolicy enforces the 10000-byte limit on ExtraOpaqueData alone while writing ExtraOpaqueData plus the 8-byte max_htlc as one blob that the deserializer caps at 10000 bytes, so accepted writes can be unreadable. Fix criteria: The write-side bound and the read-side bound must apply to the same bytes: any policy that putChanEdgePolicy commits must round-trip through deserializeChanEdgePolicyRaw. Verify by persisting a policy with max_htlc set and ExtraOpaqueData of 10000 bytes and reading it back via fetchChanEdgePolicy, ForEachChannel and ChanUpdatesInHorizon without error (or by rejecting such an update before it is stored).
2. Full-graph readers (getChannelMap, nodeTraversal, fetchChanEdgePolicies, delChannelEdgeUnsafe, putChanEdgePolicy) treat one undecodable policy as fatal for the whole operation, and the record cannot be overwritten or deleted, so a single bad row poisons the store. Fix criteria: An undecodable stored policy must not abort graph-wide reads, must not prevent the channel from being updated or deleted, and should be surfaced/repaired (e.g. treated as unknown and cleaned up by a migration). Verify by injecting an undecodable policy value and confirming DescribeGraph, cache population, zombie pruning and DeleteChannelEdges still succeed.
