# Final taproot delay scripts unspendable when peer sets to_self_delay=0, burning local funds

## Details
The 'production' (final) variants of the simple-taproot-channel to_local delay leaf (TaprootLocalCommitDelayScript) and second-level HTLC delay leaf (TaprootSecondLevelTapLeaf) were rewritten to save one byte: `<key> OP_CHECKSIGVERIFY <to_self_delay> OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY`. Because OP_CSV does not consume its argument and there is no trailing OP_DROP/OP_1, the pushed to_self_delay value is what remains on the stack when the leaf finishes, and tapscript requires that single remaining element to be truthy. If to_self_delay is 0 the push is the empty vector (OP_0), OP_CSV succeeds (sequence >= 0 always), and the script evaluates to FALSE. The leaf is permanently unspendable; the only other leaf is the revocation leaf, which requires the per-commitment secret that is only ever revealed for *revoked* states. The staging scripts (`OP_CHECKSIG <csv> OP_CSV OP_DROP`) and all segwit v0 scripts leave the signature result on the stack and are unaffected.

to_self_delay for OUR to_local/second-level outputs is chosen by the counterparty (open_channel.to_self_delay when they initiate, accept_channel.to_self_delay when we initiate). lnd validates it only against an upper bound (lnwallet/reservation.go VerifyConstraints: `CsvDelay > maxLocalCSVDelay`), stores it as LocalChanCfg.CsvDelay (reservation.go:619) and feeds it unchanged into CommitScriptToSelf (lnwallet/commitment.go:979) and the second-level HTLC trees (lnwallet/channel.go:8205, commitment.go:1264) with WithProdScripts selected by chanType.IsTaprootFinal().

Attack: a remote peer whose node advertises bit 81 opens (or accepts) a final simple-taproot channel with us and sets to_self_delay = 0. Funding completes normally — nothing in lnwire, funding/manager.go, chanacceptor or lnwallet rejects 0. Every commitment transaction we hold from then on pays our balance to a to_local output whose only non-revocation spend path can never be satisfied, and every HTLC we would resolve on-chain via HTLC-success/HTLC-timeout lands in a second-level output with the same defect. The peer can then push the channel to a unilateral close at any time (go offline, stop responding to HTLC settlement, or simply let us force-close): our entire channel balance and any in-flight HTLC value becomes unrecoverable. The attacker's own outputs (to_remote: fixed `OP_1 OP_CSV`) are unaffected, so they lose nothing, and if we route payments through the channel they may also collect fees/pushed amounts before triggering the close. The sweeper will keep failing to broadcast (script fails validation), so there is no partial mitigation.

The same pattern also makes the prod received-HTLC timeout leaf (`... <cltv_expiry> OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY`) fail for cltv_expiry == 0, but that path belongs to the offering side and we never offer with expiry 0, so it is noted only as context.

This depends on --protocol.simple-taproot-chans being enabled on the victim (a documented, non-dev release option). Assumption: txscript.ScriptTemplate (btcd v0.25.1-pre) renders the int64 value 0 as a minimal push (OP_0); any other encoding of 0 (e.g. 0x01 0x00) is equally falsy, so the conclusion does not depend on it.

## Evidence
1. [input/script\_utils.go:2188–2205](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/input/script_utils.go#L2188-L2205)
   TaprootLocalCommitDelayScript with WithProdScripts emits `<key> OP_CHECKSIGVERIFY <csv> OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY`. OP_CSV leaves its argument on the stack as the script's sole final element, so the leaf evaluates to true only if <csv> is non-zero. With csvTimeout == 0 the number renders as an empty push, OP_CSV passes trivially, and the final stack item is the empty vector -> tapscript evaluation fails. The staging variant (`OP_CHECKSIG <csv> OP_CSV OP_DROP`) leaves the CHECKSIG result instead and is not affected.
2. [input/script\_utils.go:1533–1560](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/input/script_utils.go#L1533-L1560)
   TaprootSecondLevelTapLeaf prod variant has the same shape (`<delayKey> OP_CHECKSIGVERIFY <csv> OP_CSV`); with csvDelay == 0 every second-level HTLC-success/HTLC-timeout output on our commitment is likewise unspendable via the only non-revocation leaf.
3. [lnwallet/reservation.go:957–964](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/reservation.go#L957-L964)
   VerifyConstraints only enforces an upper bound (CsvDelay > maxLocalCSVDelay). There is no lower bound; a peer-supplied to_self_delay of 0 is accepted.
4. [lnwallet/reservation.go:619](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/reservation.go#L619)
   CommitConstraints copies the remote-dictated CsvDelay into ourContribution, i.e. LocalChanCfg.CsvDelay, which is the delay applied to our own to_local and second-level outputs.
5. [funding/manager.go:1756–1762](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L1756-L1762)
   handleFundingOpen takes msg.CsvDelay directly from the peer's open_channel and only runs CommitConstraints (same at 2126-2133 for accept_channel). No zero check anywhere in the funding flow for the delay the peer imposes on us.
6. [lnwallet/commitment.go:236–245](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/commitment.go#L236-L245)
   CommitScriptToSelf selects WithProdScripts whenever chanType.IsTaprootFinal(), and is called at line 977-981 with uint32(localChanCfg.CsvDelay) for our to_local output; genHtlcScript/SecondLevelHtlcTapscriptTree (lines 436-449, 1260-1266) do the same for second-level outputs using localChanCfg.CsvDelay (lnwallet/channel.go:8205).
7. [funding/commitment\_type\_negotiation.go:235–247](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/commitment_type_negotiation.go#L235-L247)
   CommitmentTypeSimpleTaprootFinal is negotiated from feature bit 80/81 (SimpleTaprootChannelsRequired/OptionalFinal), which lnd advertises in init and node_announcement whenever --protocol.simple-taproot-chans is set (feature/default_sets.go:103, server.go:750, lncfg/protocol.go:32 - not dev-gated). Reservation.go:459-460 sets channeldb.TaprootFinalBit for it.

## Impact
Direct, permanent loss of the victim's full channel balance plus any HTLC value it must claim on-chain: the funds are provably locked in outputs with no satisfiable spend path. That is a total integrity loss of the asset the node exists to protect (funds). No confidentiality impact. Availability of the node itself is not affected.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a Lightning peer (anyone who can connect on 9735) with a node that advertises SimpleTaprootChannels final bit 81. They send open_channel (or accept_channel when the victim initiates) with channel_type = simple-taproot-final and to_self_delay = 0. The victim must have --protocol.simple-taproot-chans enabled and its channel acceptor must allow the channel (default accepts). From then on every victim commitment is a trap; the attacker triggers a unilateral close by stopping cooperation. No race, no cryptographic work, no further user action.

## Recommended fix
1. The production taproot delay leaves rely on the CSV argument being the truthy final stack element, so a zero delay (which the counterparty controls) yields a script that always evaluates false. Fix criteria: Every to_local and second-level delay leaf generated for a final taproot channel must be spendable by the delay key for all to_self_delay values the funding code can accept, including 0; add tests that build the prod leaf with csv 0 and 1..16 and execute the sweep witness through txscript.NewEngine successfully (or make the leaf's truthiness independent of the delay value).
2. The funding flow accepts any remote-dictated to_self_delay with no lower bound, letting a counterparty impose a value that breaks the local commitment scripts. Fix criteria: open_channel/accept_channel with to_self_delay below a sane minimum (at least 1) must be rejected for every channel type, and existing final-taproot channels whose LocalChanCfg.CsvDelay is 0 must be detectable so operators can cooperatively close them; verify by attempting to open a final taproot channel with to_self_delay=0 against the fundee and observing a funding failure.

# Payee-crafted blinded path with real node keys crashes payer in newRoute index

## Details
A payee can craft a BOLT11 invoice with a blinded path whose 'blinded' hop public keys are the real public keys of nodes with announced channels. The only validation applied to the path (BlindedPayment.Validate, routing/blinding.go:333-366) rejects just the NUMS key and empty paths. lnd's pathfinder does not distinguish blinded hop vertices from graph vertices: in findPath (routing/pathfind.go:1061-1096) every pivot gets both its real graph channels (addGraphPolicies) and the payee's additional edges. The pathfinding target is the appended NUMS dummy, reachable only through the payee's last blinded edge, but the hops between the introduction node and that last blinded node can be real graph channels.

newRoute (routing/pathfind.go:354-380) then back-fills blinded data assuming a 1:1 mapping between route hops after the intro node and BlindedHops: it indexes blindedPath.BlindedHops[dataIndex] with an unbounded counter. If the route contains two or more extra cleartext hops after the intro node, the index exceeds len(BlindedHops) (3 real hops + 1 NUMS dummy = 4) and the goroutine panics with 'index out of range'.

Concrete path. Attacker runs public nodes R1, X, Y, R2 with announced channels R1-X, X-Y, Y-R2, R1 reachable from an intro node I (any public node; I may be honest). The invoice carries blinded path [I, R1, R2] with arbitrary encrypted_data and an aggregate fee at least as high as I's real fee to R1 (or no real I-R1 channel). Attempt 1: the direct zero-cost blinded edge R1->R2 (blinding.go:434-462) wins, route ...->I->R1->R2. The intro node cannot decrypt the garbage encrypted_data and returns invalid_onion_blinding (link.go:3722-3736); processPaymentOutcomeIntermediate's FailInvalidBlinding branch (result_interpretation.go:515-566) sets no final failure reason and calls failBlindedRoute, recording a failure for pair (R1,R2) at the attempted amount. Attempt 2 (automatic, same payment lifecycle): the apriori estimator returns ~1e-6 for (R1,R2) (probability_apriori.go:363-376), which processEdge prunes under MinProbability=0.01 (pathfind.go:886-893); since R2's only other channel is from Y, the search yields ...->I->R1->X->Y->R2->NUMS, with the I->R1 blinded hint (carrying the BlindedPayment) as the entry into the cluster. In newRoute the NUMS edge is stripped, hops after I are R1, X, Y, R2 and dataIndex reaches 4 against a 4-element BlindedHops slice: panic. The payment lifecycle runs in the goroutine started by SendPaymentAsync (router.go:929) with no recover, so lnd exits.

The same code is reached from QueryRoutes (router_backend.go:355-356) but there the RPC panic-recovery interceptor catches it; via SendPaymentV2/SendPayment it is a process crash, repeated on every payment to such an invoice. While down, the node cannot resolve HTLCs or react to breaches, which the threat model classes as funds-at-risk availability.

Related weakness, not separately counted: with exactly one extra hop the index lands on the NUMS dummy entry and a garbage (non-crashing) route is sent; and blinded hop keys equal to real nodes also let the search bypass the intro node entirely (then blindedPayment is nil and IntroNodeOnlyPath returns an error rather than panicking).

## Evidence
1. [routing/pathfind.go:354–379](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/pathfind.go#L354-L379)
   newRoute's blinded back-fill pass assumes every hop after the introduction node is one of the payee's blinded hops: it indexes blindedPath.BlindedHops[dataIndex] with a counter that increments once per route hop and never compares dataIndex to len(BlindedHops). A found path with more hops after the intro node than the blinded path has entries (real hops + the appended NUMS dummy) panics with index out of range. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [routing/pathfind.go:1061–1095](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/pathfind.go#L1061-L1095)
   For every pivot popped in the backward Dijkstra, findPath calls u.addGraphPolicies(g.graph) and then adds the payee's additional (blinded) edges. A pivot whose key is a 'blinded' hop key is treated like any graph vertex: if the payee chose it equal to a real announced node's key, that node's real public channels are expanded alongside the blinded edge, so cleartext graph hops can be spliced between the intro node and the blinded tail.
3. [routing/pathfind.go:886–892](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/pathfind.go#L886-L892)
   processEdge drops any edge whose cumulative route probability falls below cfg.MinProbability (DefaultMinRouteProbability = 0.01, pathfind.go:83). After the first attempt is failed as described, the apriori estimator (probability_apriori.go:363-376) returns nodeProbability*(1-2^(-age/halflife)) ~ 1e-6 for the freshly failed pair (R1,R2), so the direct blinded edge is pruned on the automatic retry and the search is forced onto the real-graph detour into R2.
4. [routing/result\_interpretation.go:515–565](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/result_interpretation.go#L515-L565)
   When the introduction node returns invalid_onion_blinding (an lnd intro node does so for any failure, incl. undecryptable payee-controlled encrypted_data, via link.go:3722-3736), this branch awards success to the pairs before the intro node, sets no final failure reason (so the payment lifecycle retries), and calls failBlindedRoute, which penalises the last pair of the blinded route (R1->R2) at the attempted amount (lines 872-886).
5. [routing/blinding.go:333–365](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/blinding.go#L333-L365)
   BlindedPayment.Validate is the only validation applied to a payee's blinded path (via BuildBlindedPathSet, lnrpc/routerrpc/router_backend.go:1310-1327). It rejects only an empty path and the NUMS key; nothing requires blinded hop keys to be unknown to the graph or binds the number of route hops after the intro node to the number of blinded hops.
6. [routing/blinding.go:398–461](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/blinding.go#L398-L461)
   toRouteHints builds the intro->first-hop edge with the aggregate policy and every inner blinded edge with zero fee, zero CLTV delta, MinHTLC 0 and no enforced MaxHTLC, carrying the BlindedPayment. On the first attempt the direct zero-cost inner edge always wins; the intro->R1 hint is what makes blindedPayment non-nil in newRoute on the retry (getEdgeNetwork keeps the highest-fee policy between a hint and a real channel, unified_edges.go:398-418, so the payee's aggregate fee lets the hint win even if a real I-R1 channel exists).
7. [routing/payment\_session.go:442–454](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/payment_session.go#L442-L454)
   RequestRoute calls newRoute on the found path with the payment's BlindedPathSet; this runs inside the payment lifecycle goroutine, not under an RPC handler.
8. [routing/router.go:921–934](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/router.go#L921-L934)
   SendPaymentAsync (called by routerrpc SendPaymentV2, router_server.go:406) runs sendPayment -> resumePayment in a plain go func() with no recover(); the rpcperms panic-recovery interceptors wrap only RPC handler goroutines. A panic in newRoute therefore terminates the whole lnd process.

## Impact
The lnd process terminates on an unrecovered panic in the payment goroutine. While offline the node cannot forward or resolve HTLCs, sweep or punish, and any in-flight payments stall; the crash recurs on every payment to such an invoice (automated payers such as exchanges processing withdrawals pay attacker-supplied invoices without review). No confidentiality or integrity impact beyond the stalled payment.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any payee: they hand the victim a BOLT11 invoice containing a blinded path whose blinded hop keys are real public node keys arranged (by the attacker's own cheap public nodes) so the only alternative route to the last hop has two extra graph hops. The victim pays once; the first attempt fails at the intro node with invalid_onion_blinding, mission control penalises the last blinded pair, and the automatic second attempt builds the detour route and panics in newRoute, killing the process. No defences stand in the way; the behaviour is deterministic given the topology.

## Recommended fix
1. newRoute's blinded back-fill assumes a one-to-one correspondence between route hops after the introduction node and the payee's BlindedHops and indexes the slice with an unchecked counter, violating the invariant that indices derived from a search result stay within payee-supplied data bounds. Fix criteria: newRoute must return an error (never panic) when the number of hops from the introduction node to the end of the route does not exactly match the number of real blinded hops, and must bounds-check every BlindedHops access. Verify with a path containing extra cleartext hops between the intro node and the blinded tail: RequestRoute/FindRoute return an error and the process stays up.
2. findPath treats payee-chosen blinded hop vertices like graph vertices, adding their real channels when a blinded key collides with a known node, so cleartext graph edges can be spliced into (or substituted for) the blinded segment. Fix criteria: During pathfinding to a blinded path set, vertices that are blinded hop keys (and the NUMS target) must only be expanded through their blinded additional edges, never through graph policies, or blinded paths whose hop keys match known graph nodes or the local node must be rejected up front. Verify that a blinded path with real-node keys and a penalised direct edge yields errNoPathFound rather than a route mixing graph hops into the blinded segment.

# Claude agent runs inside fork PR checkout, honouring attacker-controlled CLAUDE.md and .claude settings

## Details
claude.yml lets maintainers summon Claude on any PR by commenting `@claude`. Before launching the agent, the workflow runs `gh pr checkout "$PR_NUMBER"` (lines 33-43), so for a fork PR the agent's working directory becomes a tree entirely authored by an unprivileged account. The action is then started (line 47) with no `claude_args` restriction, holding CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and, via id-token: write, an OIDC-minted Claude GitHub App installation token with contents/pull-requests/issues write that the action configures into the origin remote URL (.git/config) so the agent can push.

Root cause: a privileged, secret-holding agent sources its project configuration and instructions from an untrusted control sphere. The repository tracks no CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json or .mcp.json (only .claude/commands/dedupe.md), so whatever the fork adds is the only project configuration Claude Code sees: CLAUDE.md is loaded as project instructions; .claude/settings.json may carry `hooks` (shell commands executed by the CLI) and `permissions.allow` rules; .mcp.json may declare MCP servers whose `command` is attacker shell. The repository's own claude-dedupe-issues.yml relies on the action loading `.claude/commands/dedupe.md` from the checkout, confirming project-scoped `.claude/` config in cwd is honoured.

The maintainers' sibling workflow pr-severity.yml (lines 4-6) states their own safety property - the agent is safe because no PR code is checked out or executed - which claude.yml does the opposite of. The scan's threat model names `claude.yml (checks out fork branches)` as an in-scope CI/supply-chain surface.

Dependency assumptions (anthropics/claude-code-action@v1, floating major tag, and the Claude Code CLI it installs): (1) CLAUDE.md in cwd is read as project memory (the action's documented behaviour); (2) default allowed tools include Read/Write/Edit and `Bash(git add|commit|push:*)` when `use_commit_signing` is unset; (3) the action sets the origin URL to `https://x-access-token:<app-token>@github.com/...` and exports CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN to the Claude process, so tool subprocesses inherit it; (4) in headless mode the CLI loads project `.claude/settings.json` hooks/permission rules and `.mcp.json` (with `enableAllProjectMcpServers`) without a trust prompt. Assumption (4) could not be verified in the checkout; if it fails, the CLAUDE.md-steering path (1)-(3) still yields the same credentials and writes.

## Evidence
1. [.github/workflows/claude.yml:33–43](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/claude.yml#L33-L43)
   For any @claude comment/review on a PR the workflow runs `gh pr checkout "$PR_NUMBER"` (line 43), which for a fork PR fetches refs/pull/N/head and replaces the trusted base checkout in the working directory with a tree authored by an unprivileged account. This is the step the fix must change.
2. [.github/workflows/claude.yml:45–61](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/claude.yml#L45-L61)
   anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 (floating major tag) is then started with cwd on that fork tree, holding CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; `claude_args` is commented out, so no --allowedTools / settings restriction is applied and the action's default tool set (Read/Write/Edit plus git add/commit/push via Bash when commit signing is off) governs.
3. [.github/workflows/claude.yml:21–26](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/claude.yml#L21-L26)
   id-token: write lets the action exchange OIDC for a Claude GitHub App installation token (contents/pull-requests/issues write) that it configures into the git remote URL for pushes; that token and the OAuth token are reachable from the agent's process tree.
4. [.github/workflows/claude.yml:15–18](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/claude.yml#L15-L18)
   Trigger is any comment/review containing @claude; the action's default actor gate only requires the commenter to have write access, so a maintainer reviewing a fork PR is the intended usage path - the PR author needs no privilege.
5. [.claude/commands/dedupe.md:1–3](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.claude/commands/dedupe.md#L1-L3)
   The repository's own tracked Claude project configuration; claude-dedupe-issues.yml invokes `/dedupe` which only resolves if the action's Claude Code loads `.claude/` from the checkout - the project's own usage establishes that project-scoped `.claude/` configuration in cwd is honoured. No CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json or .mcp.json is tracked, so a fork's copies are the only ones the agent sees.
6. [.github/workflows/pr-severity.yml:4–6](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/pr-severity.yml#L4-L6)
   Sibling workflow states the maintainers' own safety rule - the agent is only safe because no code from the PR is checked out or executed - which claude.yml violates for fork PRs.

## Impact
Confidentiality HIGH: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (long-lived Anthropic account credential) and the Claude GitHub App installation token are readable by attacker hooks or by the default Read tool from .git/config and surfaced in a public PR comment. Integrity HIGH: the App token has contents write on lightningnetwork/lnd, and `git push` is a default-allowed tool, so the attacker can push arbitrary branches/commits to the base repository and act under the Claude bot identity. Availability: none. Subsequent-system impact: The exfiltrated CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is a credential for the maintainers' Anthropic account outside GitHub: inference under that account (low confidentiality) and quota/billing consumption (low availability).

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any GitHub account that can open a fork PR; delivery: CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json, .mcp.json in the PR head. Trigger: a maintainer comments @claude on that PR (intended use, UI:A). Path A (if headless Claude Code honours project hooks/MCP - unverified dependency link): SessionStart/PreToolUse hook runs attacker shell with the OAuth token in env and the App token in .git/config. Path B (established): CLAUDE.md steers the agent to Read .git/config and post it, or to commit and `git push` attacker content to the base repo - this must defeat the model's injection resistance, hence AC:H.

## Recommended fix
1. The untrusted fork PR head is checked out into the agent's working directory (claude.yml:43) before an agent holding secrets and a write-capable App token starts, so fork-controlled CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json (hooks, permissions) and .mcp.json govern a privileged process. Fix criteria: The agent must never start with its working directory, settings, hooks, MCP config or CLAUDE.md sourced from a fork PR: skip the agent (or the checkout) when the PR head repository is not the base repository or the author lacks write access, or keep the agent's cwd and configuration on the trusted base checkout with fork project settings/hooks/MCP disabled. Verify by opening a fork PR adding a .claude/settings.json hook that writes a marker and a CLAUDE.md instruction; after @claude is invoked neither has any effect.
2. The agent's tool surface is unrestricted (claude_args unset), so default Read/Write/Edit and git push tools, plus any permission widening from project settings, let a steered agent read .git/config and push to the base repository. Fix criteria: On PRs from forks the agent's tools must be limited to read-only PR inspection and commenting (no git push, no file reads of .git), and project-level permission/hook/MCP settings must be ignored; verify that a CLAUDE.md instruction to push a branch or print .git/config cannot succeed.
3. CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and the write-capable App token are present in the environment and .git/config inherited by tool subprocesses and hooks, so any code execution inside the agent's process tree exfiltrates them. Fix criteria: Tool and hook subprocesses must not be able to read the OAuth token or a write-capable GitHub token from their environment, /proc or the git remote URL; verify that a shell spawned by the agent cannot recover either credential.

# PR severity bot: any PR author can prompt-inject agent holding OAuth and write tokens

## Details
pr-severity.yml runs anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 under pull_request_target (opened/synchronize) for every PR, including fork PRs from unprivileged accounts (allowed_non_write_users: "*" disables the action's write-access gate). The job grants pull-requests: write and issues: write for the whole repository, and hands the agent the long-lived CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN plus GITHUB_TOKEN (lines 37-38). The prompt directs the model to read the PR with `gh pr view N --json files,...` (attacker-chosen file paths are always returned) and the model will ordinarily also view the PR title/body - all authored by the PR author. The only containment is `--allowedTools "Bash(gh pr view:*)" "Bash(gh pr edit:*)" "Bash(gh pr comment:*)"` (line 47), which the comment at lines 40-46 says limits prompt-injection risk. The base-branch checkout brings no `.claude/settings.json` deny rules (the repo ships only `.claude/commands/dedupe.md`).

The allow-list is a command-prefix rule: it bounds neither the arguments nor the target PR, so an injected instruction is an *allowed* command.

1. Cross-PR writes and CI-gate bypass (needs no assumption beyond the allow-list and lines 10-13): `gh pr edit <own PR> --add-label no-itest` / `no-changelog` makes main.yml's check-label step (reads `github.event.pull_request.labels` on the attacker's next `pull_request` push) skip every integration-test matrix job (main.yml:295-300, 385, 455, 507) and the release-notes check (:576); `skip-severity-check` suppresses re-classification; `gh pr edit <any PR> --base/--title/--body/--add-label` and `gh pr comment <any PR>` act on any PR in the repository as github-actions[bot].

2. Secret exfiltration: `gh pr comment <n> --body-file /proc/self/environ` posts the gh process's environment to a public comment; `gh pr comment <n> --body "$CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN"` is equivalent if the Bash tool permits parameter expansion. That the gh process environment holds a write-capable GitHub token is established by the workflow itself: it sets no GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN env for gh, yet relies on `gh pr edit`/`gh pr comment` as its only write mechanism, so the action must export the token into the claude process environment, which Bash-tool children inherit. That CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is likewise present is an assumption on anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 / the Claude Code CLI (the env var is the CLI's documented CI auth mechanism). The OAuth token outlives the job and grants Claude Code inference on the maintainers' Anthropic account; the GITHUB_TOKEN is usable for the remaining job lifetime with repo-wide PR/issue write.

Attack: open a fork PR whose body/title/commit message/file path carries instructions. The workflow fires on `opened` with no maintainer action; the attacker retries on every push (`synchronize`) at no cost. Prompt-injection success is probabilistic but unlimited retries are free.

## Evidence
1. [.github/workflows/pr-severity.yml:43–47](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/pr-severity.yml#L43-L47)
   allowed_non_write_users: "*" lets the agent run for every PR author, and the only containment is three prefix rules Bash(gh pr view:*), Bash(gh pr edit:*), Bash(gh pr comment:*). A prefix rule admits any arguments after the prefix, so `gh pr comment <n> --body-file /proc/self/environ`, `gh pr comment <n> --body "$CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN"`, and `gh pr edit <any-other-PR> --base/--title/--body/--add-label` are all permitted commands.
2. [.github/workflows/pr-severity.yml:7–13](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/pr-severity.yml#L7-L13)
   pull_request_target on opened/synchronize runs with secrets for fork PRs, and the job token carries pull-requests: write and issues: write for the whole repository, not just the triggering PR.
3. [.github/workflows/pr-severity.yml:36–38](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/pr-severity.yml#L36-L38)
   CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (long-lived Anthropic account token) and GITHUB_TOKEN are handed to the action; the action exports them to the claude process, whose Bash tool children (gh) inherit them, so they are readable through /proc/self/environ or $VAR expansion inside an allowed gh command.
4. [.github/workflows/pr-severity.yml:133–150](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/pr-severity.yml#L133-L150)
   The prompt directs the model to run gh pr view on the PR, pulling attacker-authored title, body, comments, commit messages and file paths into the model context. Those fields are the injection carrier; the workflow comment at lines 4-6 assumes reading metadata is safe.
5. [.github/actions/check-label/action.yml:24–27](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/actions/check-label/action.yml#L24-L27)
   CI gating reads PR labels from the event payload. A hijacked agent can `gh pr edit <own PR> --add-label no-itest` (and no-changelog / skip-severity-check); on the attacker's next push main.yml skips integration tests and reports them auto-passed.
6. [.github/workflows/main.yml:295–299](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/main.yml#L295-L299)
   Consumer of the no-itest label: basic-integration-test, integration-test, windows and macOS itest jobs are all skipped when the label is present.

## Impact
Confidentiality HIGH: the repository's long-lived CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and the job's GITHUB_TOKEN are disclosed publicly. Integrity LOW: the agent's repo-wide pull-requests/issues write lets the attacker edit titles, bodies, base branches and labels of other PRs and post bot-identity comments, and the no-itest/no-changelog labels disable CI gates on the attacker's own PR; it cannot merge or push code. Availability: none. Subsequent-system impact: The stolen OAuth token is a credential for the maintainers' Anthropic account outside the GitHub boundary: the attacker can run Claude Code/API inference as that account (confidentiality of account identity/usage, low) and consume its quota or billing (availability, low).

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any GitHub account able to open a pull request against lightningnetwork/lnd; no privilege on the repository is needed. Delivery is the PR title/body/commit message/file path. The workflow runs automatically on `opened`/`synchronize` with secrets (pull_request_target, allowed_non_write_users "*"); no maintainer action is needed. The injected instruction is an allowed command (`gh pr comment N --body-file /proc/self/environ`, `gh pr edit M --add-label ...`), so no sandbox or permission mechanism has to be defeated (AC:L). Success depends on the model following the injected text, which is probabilistic and outside the attacker's control, so repeated attempts (free, on every push) may be required (AT:P).

## Recommended fix
1. An LLM agent that reads attacker-controlled PR metadata is run with secrets and a repo-wide write token for unprivileged fork PRs (pull_request_target + allowed_non_write_users "*"), so untrusted text can direct privileged actions. Fix criteria: Classification of untrusted PRs must not involve a model holding secrets or write tokens: either compute severity deterministically from the changed-file list in a script, or run the agent only for trusted authors / without CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and with a token scoped to the single PR. Verify by opening a fork PR whose body instructs the bot to comment with its environment and to relabel another PR: neither action can occur.
2. The tool allow-list is a command prefix, so `gh pr comment --body-file`, `$VAR` bodies and arbitrary PR numbers pass, and the agent's subprocess environment still contains the secrets. Fix criteria: If an agent is kept, its only write capability must be a wrapper that hard-codes the triggering PR number, accepts a validated label from a fixed set and a body argument (no --body-file, no other PR), and the claude process environment must not contain CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN or a write-capable GitHub token readable by tools. Verify that /proc/self/environ of a tool subprocess contains no secret and that any gh invocation naming another PR is rejected.

# Issue dedupe bot: any issue author can steer agent to post bot comments on arbitrary issues

## Details
claude-dedupe-issues.yml runs anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 on every `issues: opened` event for any author (allowed_non_write_users: "*") with a GITHUB_TOKEN carrying issues: write, exposed to the agent as GH_TOKEN. The /dedupe command (.claude/commands/dedupe.md) tells the agent to read the triggering issue with `gh issue view`, search for duplicates, and finally run `./scripts/comment-on-duplicates.sh --base-issue <n> --potential-duplicates <a> <b> <c>`, the only write-capable tool it is granted.

The root cause is that the write tool is not bound to the triggering context. The script validates that --base-issue and each duplicate are numeric, exist in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY and number at most three, but the base issue is whatever the agent passes; the triggering issue number appears only as text in the prompt, never as an environment variable or event-derived constant the script enforces. The issue body the agent must read is authored by the untrusted account that opened the issue, so instructions placed in it (prompt injection) can steer the agent to call the script with a different --base-issue and attacker-chosen --potential-duplicates. The result is a bot-identity (github-actions[bot]) 'Found possible duplicate issue(s)' comment on any issue in the repository - open or closed, including release-tracking or security-related issues - linking to issues of the attacker's choosing (for example attacker-created issues containing misleading content), repeatable at will by opening further issues.

The remaining allowed tools (gh issue view/list, gh search) are read-only and the script's validation prevents arbitrary comment text, other repositories, labels or closing, so impact is confined to misleading fixed-format bot comments on arbitrary issues. The workflow_dispatch input issue_number is dispatchable only by write users and is not part of this path.

Dependency assumptions (anthropics/claude-code-action@v1, floating major tag; Claude Code permission semantics as documented): allowed_non_write_users: "*" permits runs for non-collaborator actors; a slash-command prompt loads .claude/commands/dedupe.md and honours its allowed-tools frontmatter; Bash(cmd:*) is a prefix rule allowing any arguments to cmd.

## Evidence
1. [scripts/comment-on-duplicates.sh:16–18](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/scripts/comment-on-duplicates.sh#L16-L18)
   --base-issue is taken from the agent-supplied argument; nothing binds it to the issue that triggered the workflow (github.event.issue.number is never exported to the script), so an injected agent can target any issue in the repository.
2. [.github/workflows/claude-dedupe-issues.yml:3–5](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/claude-dedupe-issues.yml#L3-L5)
   Runs automatically for every newly opened issue; opening an issue on the public repository requires no privilege.
3. [.github/workflows/claude-dedupe-issues.yml:26–34](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/claude-dedupe-issues.yml#L26-L34)
   allowed_non_write_users: "*" lets claude-code-action run for non-collaborator authors; the prompt /dedupe <repo>/issues/<n> directs the agent to read the attacker's issue body with gh issue view, the prompt-injection carrier. GH_TOKEN is the repository GITHUB_TOKEN.
4. [.github/workflows/claude-dedupe-issues.yml:17–20](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.github/workflows/claude-dedupe-issues.yml#L17-L20)
   Job token has issues: write for the whole repository, so gh issue comment succeeds on any issue.
5. [.claude/commands/dedupe.md:2](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/.claude/commands/dedupe.md#L2)
   The command grants Bash(./scripts/comment-on-duplicates.sh:*) - the only write-capable tool - as a prefix rule, so any argument combination is permitted without binding to the triggering issue.
6. [scripts/comment-on-duplicates.sh:85–96](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/scripts/comment-on-duplicates.sh#L85-L96)
   Posts a fixed-format 'Found possible duplicate issue(s)' comment with the chosen same-repo issue links to the chosen base issue under the github-actions[bot] identity.

## Impact
Integrity LOW: the attacker can place misleading github-actions[bot] 'possible duplicate' comments, linking to same-repo issues of their choosing, on any issue in the repository, lending the project's bot identity to attacker-selected content; the fixed template and the script's numeric/same-repo/max-3 validation prevent arbitrary text, label changes, closing or cross-repository actions. No confidentiality impact (read tools reach only public data with a repo-scoped token) and no availability impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any GitHub account able to open an issue on the public repository; the issue body is the delivery vehicle and the workflow runs automatically with the repository's issues: write token for every new issue. The only write tool accepts any numeric same-repo issue numbers, so no control beyond the model's adherence to its instructions stands between the injected text and the cross-issue comment; failed attempts cost nothing and can be retried with new issues.

## Recommended fix
The agent's single write capability (comment-on-duplicates.sh) accepts any --base-issue, so an agent steered by untrusted issue content can post the bot's duplicate comment on issues other than the one that triggered the run, violating the integrity of the issue tracker under the bot identity. Fix criteria: The target of the bot's comment must be fixed to the triggering issue from the workflow event (for example supplied through the environment by the workflow and enforced by the script, with agent-supplied base-issue arguments rejected or ignored), so that an issue body instructing the bot to comment elsewhere results in no comment on any other issue. Verify by opening an issue containing such instructions and confirming only that issue can receive the bot's comment.

# DebugLevel trace logging plus GetDebugInfo log export leaks invoice preimages without invoices permission

## Details
The macaroon permission table keeps invoice data under the `invoices` entity: LookupInvoice, ListInvoices and SubscribeInvoices all require `invoices:read` (rpcserver.go:403-414) and `invoice.macaroon` is baked as a separate default macaroon (rpcserver.go:192-213). Two handlers in rpcserver.go together let a macaroon that lacks any `invoices` permission read invoice preimages anyway.

`DebugLevel` (rpcserver.go:7158-7200) is gated only by `info:write` (rpcserver.go:471-475). It hands the caller's `level_spec` to `build.ParseAndSetDebugLevels`, which accepts any valid level for any registered subsystem and applies it through the sub logger's handlerSet, whose SetLevel fans out to the file handler (build/handler_sets.go:97-103). In release builds LoggingType is LogTypeDefault and file logging is on by default (build/log_default.go, build/handlers.go:12-38, sample-lnd.conf:1073), so the on-disk `lnd.log` immediately starts receiving trace/debug lines. `GetDebugInfo` (rpcserver.go:3511-3540) is gated by `info:read + offchain:read + onchain:read + peers:read` (rpcserver.go:350-363) and, with `include_log=true`, reads the whole current `lnd.log` from `LogDir` and returns it unredacted.

Production log statements write funds-relevant secrets at those levels: lnrpc/invoicesrpc/addinvoice.go:622 spews every newly created invoice including `Terms.PaymentPreimage` at trace (IRPC; lntypes.Preimage.String renders hex); rpcserver.go:5950 spews the full invoice on every LookupInvoice at trace (RPCS); invoices/invoiceregistry.go:1404 logs the settle preimage of hodl invoices at debug (INVC); peer/brontide.go:2809-2821 renders `UpdateFulfillHTLC` preimages and `RevokeAndAck` revocation secrets in the debug summary that logWireMessage (2918-2951) emits for every wire message, with a full spew at trace (PEER).

Attack: a holder of a custom-baked macaroon (macaroons/README.md documents arbitrary entity subsets; no default macaroon has `info:write` without `invoices:read`, so this is an ops/monitoring macaroon granted `info:write` for `stop`/`debuglevel` plus the four read entities) calls `DebugLevel{level_spec:"IRPC=trace,RPCS=trace,INVC=debug,PEER=debug"}`, waits while the node creates invoices and exchanges HTLCs, then calls `GetDebugInfo{include_log:true}` and reads the preimages of invoices that have not yet been paid, together with every peer's revocation secrets and all invoice details. A pending-invoice preimage lets any party holding an HTLC for that hash (an intermediary on the payer's route, or the attacker's own routing node) settle it and take the payment. The level change persists in `r.cfg.DebugLevel` until another DebugLevel call or a restart. If the operator already runs at debug/trace (sample-lnd.conf's own example is `debuglevel=debug,PEER=info`), GetDebugInfo alone suffices.

This is not conceded to the position by any sanctioned path: `offchain:read` reveals preimages only after settlement (routerrpc SubscribeHtlcEvents SettleEvent) or for the node's own outgoing payments (ListPayments), never the preimage of a pending invoice or a counterparty's revocation secret. Root cause: the log is a sink for secrets belonging to the `invoices` and `peers` entities, DebugLevel lets an `info:write` holder decide that those secrets get written, and GetDebugInfo exports the sink under a permission set that omits those entities. Behavioural assumption: btclog/v2 v2.0.1-0.20250728225537 DefaultHandler.SetLevel takes effect immediately for subsequent records (the project's own ParseAndSetDebugLevels startup path relies on the same call).

## Evidence
1. [rpcserver.go:3511–3539](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L3511-L3539)
   GetDebugInfo with include_log=true does os.ReadFile on filepath.Join(r.cfg.LogDir, defaultLogFilename) (lnd.log, the same path the rotator writes at config.go:1610-1613) and returns every line unredacted. This is the export sink; the fix must either gate it on the entities whose secrets the log carries or redact the log.
2. [rpcserver.go:350–362](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L350-L362)
   GetDebugInfo's permission set is info:read + offchain:read + onchain:read + peers:read; invoices:read is not among them, while LookupInvoice/ListInvoices/SubscribeInvoices (lines 403-414) each require invoices:read.

   DebugLevel passes the caller's level_spec unchanged to build.ParseAndSetDebugLevels, which accepts any valid level (trace included) for any registered subsystem, and persists the new spec in r.cfg.DebugLevel. Nothing restricts which subsystems or levels an RPC caller may select.
4. [rpcserver.go:471–474](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L471-L474)
   DebugLevel is gated only by info:write, so a macaroon with no invoices or peers write rights can raise IRPC/RPCS/INVC/PEER to trace or debug at runtime.
5. [lnrpc/invoicesrpc/addinvoice.go:622–623](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/invoicesrpc/addinvoice.go#L622-L623)
   At trace level (IRPC) every newly created invoice is spewed in full before it is stored, including Terms.PaymentPreimage (*lntypes.Preimage, whose String() at lntypes/preimage.go:17 renders the hex preimage), i.e. the secret of a not-yet-paid invoice.

   LookupInvoice spews the complete invoice record (preimage included) at trace level under RPCS whenever any invoices:read holder looks an invoice up.

   SettleHodlInvoice (function at 1359) logs the preimage with which a hodl invoice was settled at debug level under INVC.

   messageSummary renders UpdateFulfillHTLC as preimage=%x and RevokeAndAck as rev=%x (the revocation secret), so these secrets appear in the PEER debug summary of every such message sent or received.
9. [peer/brontide.go:2918–2951](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L2918-L2951)
   logWireMessage emits the messageSummary at debug and a full spew of every wire message at trace for every message read from or written to a peer.
10. [build/handler\_sets.go:97–102](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/build/handler_sets.go#L97-L102)
   handlerSet.SetLevel fans the new level out to every handler in the set, so a sub logger's SetLevel (build/sub_logger.go:138-147) changes the level of the file handler as well as the console handler.
11. [build/handlers.go:12–37](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/build/handlers.go#L12-L37)
   In release builds LoggingType is LogTypeDefault (build/log_default.go), so NewDefaultLogHandlers adds the rotating lnd.log file handler unless logging.file.disable is set; sample-lnd.conf:1073 documents the default as false, and config.go:1578-1613 wires these handlers into cfg.SubLogMgr and the rotator.

## Impact
Confidentiality: the caller obtains the preimages of pending (unpaid) invoices, hodl-invoice settle preimages, preimages of every HTLC fulfilled through the node, revocation secrets exchanged with every peer, full invoice records, and the complete operational log - data its macaroon entities do not grant and that the invoices entity exists to protect; pending-invoice preimages are directly monetisable by any party on the payer's route, which makes the disclosed information a direct serious impact (VC:H). Integrity and availability of the node are not affected beyond the log-level change that info:write already concedes to the caller.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a network RPC client (gRPC 10009 / REST 8080) holding a non-admin, custom-baked macaroon carrying info:write plus info/offchain/onchain/peers read, but no invoices entity. Two ordinary unary calls: DebugLevel to raise IRPC/RPCS/INVC/PEER verbosity, then GetDebugInfo(include_log=true) once invoices have been created or HTLCs have flowed. The macaroon interceptor checks only the permission table entries shown; ParseAndSetDebugLevels imposes no subsystem or level restriction; file logging is the release default. No victim interaction and no race.

## Recommended fix
1. GetDebugInfo returns the raw lnd.log under a permission set (info/offchain/onchain/peers read) that does not cover the entities whose secrets appear in the log, breaking macaroon entity separation. Fix criteria: Exporting the log requires a privilege commensurate with everything the log can contain (at minimum invoices:read in addition to the current four, or admin-only), or the returned log is redacted of preimages, revocation secrets and other credentials. Verify by creating invoices at trace level and calling GetDebugInfo(include_log=true) with a macaroon lacking invoices:read: the call is denied or no 32-byte preimage/revocation hex appears in the returned lines.
2. DebugLevel is gated by info:write although it decides whether other entities' secrets are written to disk, and invoice/peer code logs preimages and revocation secrets in clear at trace/debug. Fix criteria: The secret-bearing log statements (addinvoice trace spew, LookupInvoice spew, SettleHodlInvoice debug line, peer messageSummary/spew of UpdateFulfillHTLC and RevokeAndAck) stop emitting raw preimages and revocation secrets at any level (log hashes or redacted forms instead), and/or DebugLevel requires a privilege commensurate with exposing all logged data. Verify that running at trace yields no preimage or revocation hex in lnd.log.

# Incoming contest resolver Launch settles exit-hop invoice at height 0, bypassing CLTV expiry gate

## Details
When a channel closes on chain, every non-dust incoming HTLC becomes an htlcIncomingContestResolver. Its Launch() calls findAndapplyPreimage(), which, for an exit-hop payload, invokes Registry.NotifyExitHopHtlc(rhash, amt, expiry, currentHeight=0, circuitKey, hodlChan=nil, ...). The comment says the call is only meant to read an existing settle resolution, but NotifyExitHopHtlc is a state-changing operation: for an OPEN invoice with no recorded HTLC it runs updateInvoice, and the only protection against settling an invoice whose HTLC cannot be safely claimed on chain is the expiry gate `ctx.expiry < currentHeight + finalCltvRejectDelta` / `+ inv.Terms.FinalCltvDelta` (invoices/update.go:293-298, 501-506). With currentHeight=0 this gate is vacuous, so an HTLC that is already expired, or expires within the next block, is accepted and, if it carries the invoice amount, the invoice is marked SETTLED, invoice subscribers are notified (notifyClients), and the preimage is handed to the success resolver.

The link's own call passes the real height (htlcswitch/link.go ~3520) and rejects such HTLCs with ResultExpiryTooSoon; crucially that rejection happens before the HTLC is recorded in the invoice, so there is no replay record for the later on-chain call to see. Resolve() does pass the real height (line 331) and does abandon expired HTLCs (line 239), but by then the invoice is already settled and nothing reverses it.

Attack: a channel counterparty who is also the payer (any peer; lnd accepts inbound channels by default) obtains an invoice from the victim, sends update_add_htlc with cltv_expiry = current height + 1..2 and an onion whose OutgoingCLTV equals that expiry (so hop.ValidateFinalHtlc passes), receives the victim's commitment_signed/htlc signatures, ignores the victim's update_fail_htlc and broadcasts their commitment. The chain watcher dispatches the close only after 3-6 confirmations (lnwallet/confscale_prod.go), by which time the HTLC has expired and the attacker's pre-signed HTLC-timeout transaction has reclaimed the output. The arbitrator then builds the contest resolver, Launch() settles the invoice at height 0, the sweep of an already-spent output fails, and Resolve() records the HTLC as failed. Net result: the victim's invoice database and invoice-subscription stream report the invoice as paid although no funds were received, which for a merchant acting on invoice settlement is payment without paying. A secondary effect is that partial MPP HTLCs accepted via this path are recorded with AcceptHeight 0.

Root cause: a state-changing registry call is made with a placeholder height that disables the registry's expiry safety check, and the on-chain path has no equivalent 'too close to expiry / already expired' check of its own before the invoice is settled.

## Evidence
1. [contractcourt/htlc\_incoming\_contest\_resolver.go:742–745](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/htlc_incoming_contest_resolver.go#L742-L745)
   findAndapplyPreimage calls Registry.NotifyExitHopHtlc with currentHeight=0 and hodlChan=nil. The comment claims the call is 'only interested in the settle resolution', but NotifyExitHopHtlc is state-changing: for an OPEN invoice with no recorded HTLC it runs updateInvoice, records the HTLC (AcceptHeight 0) and settles the invoice, and the zero height makes the registry's expiry gate vacuous. This is the line the fix must change.
2. [contractcourt/htlc\_incoming\_contest\_resolver.go:109–135](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/htlc_incoming_contest_resolver.go#L109-L135)
   Launch() runs findAndapplyPreimage; channel_arbitrator.resolveContracts calls launchResolvers (synchronously, before the Resolve goroutines start) and again on every blockbeat, so an HTLC paying an OPEN invoice is submitted to the registry at height 0 as soon as the close is dispatched; on a settle resolution it applies the preimage and launches the inner success resolver.
3. [invoices/update.go:293–298](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/invoices/update.go#L293-L298)
   updateMpp rejects an HTLC only when expiry < currentHeight + finalCltvRejectDelta (default 19) or < currentHeight + inv.Terms.FinalCltvDelta. With currentHeight=0 both are vacuous for any real absolute expiry, so an already-expired HTLC passes, is recorded, and (full amount, non-hodl) the invoice is marked SETTLED and notifyClients fires. The legacy path at lines 501-506 is identical. Because the check precedes the AddHtlcs record, a link-side ExpiryTooSoon rejection leaves no replay entry for the on-chain call to find.
4. [contractcourt/htlc\_incoming\_contest\_resolver.go:84–106](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/htlc_incoming_contest_resolver.go#L84-L106)
   invalidFinalHtlc, the only pre-check before the height-0 registry call, delegates to hop.ValidateFinalHtlc (htlcswitch/hop/forwarding_info.go:112-135), which checks amount, expiry >= onion OutgoingCLTV and 'expiry too far' only; it has no 'too soon / already expired' check, so a sender setting OutgoingCLTV == expiry passes even when expiry <= current height.
5. [contractcourt/htlc\_incoming\_contest\_resolver.go:239–261](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/htlc_incoming_contest_resolver.go#L239-L261)
   Resolve() later sees currentHeight >= htlcExpiry and abandons the HTLC (PutFinalHtlcOutcome false, ResolverOutcomeTimeout). Nothing in contractcourt reverts the invoice settlement performed at Launch (htlc_success_resolver.checkpointForeignSpend likewise only records the failed outcome), so the invoice stays SETTLED while the output is taken by the counterparty's HTLC-timeout spend.
6. [contractcourt/channel\_arbitrator.go:2047–2054](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/channel_arbitrator.go#L2047-L2054)
   Every non-dust incoming HTLC on the confirmed (remote or remote-pending) commitment becomes HtlcIncomingWatchAction → newIncomingContestResolver (line 2642); HtlcClaimAction is never assigned, so the counterparty's HTLC reaches Launch regardless of whether the link ever accepted it.
7. [invoices/invoiceregistry.go:926–939](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/invoices/invoiceregistry.go#L926-L939)
   NotifyExitHopHtlc copies the caller-supplied currentHeight straight into invoiceUpdateCtx; the registry has no independent view of chain height, so the resolver's 0 is what the expiry checks see.
8. [witness\_beacon.go:156–175](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/witness_beacon.go#L156-L175)
   The production WitnessBeacon's LookupPreimage consults only the witness cache (preimages learned from forwards/on-chain spends), not the invoice database, so for the node's own unsettled invoice findAndapplyPreimage's known-preimage branch is not taken and the height-0 registry call is reached.
9. [htlcswitch/link.go:3522–3525](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L3522-L3525)
   The link's off-chain exit-hop path passes the real heightNow to NotifyExitHopHtlc, so the same HTLC is failed ExpiryTooSoon off-chain; the on-chain Launch path bypasses this shipped control. Neither lnwallet.ReceiveHTLC (channel.go:6456) nor the link's add-receipt handler validates cltv_expiry against the chain height, so the victim signs a commitment carrying the near/already-expired HTLC.
10. [contractcourt/chain\_watcher.go:821–836](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/chain_watcher.go#L821-L836)
   The chain watcher dispatches a commitment spend only after requiredConfsForSpend (CloseConfsForCapacity, minimum 3) confirmations, so Launch runs at least 3 blocks after the counterparty's commitment confirmed; an HTLC whose expiry is at or below that confirmation height is reclaimable by the counterparty's pre-signed HTLC-timeout in the same or next block, long before the node's sweep.

## Impact
The node's invoice state is corrupted: an invoice is marked SETTLED and settlement notifications are emitted for an HTLC the node never collects, so downstream systems relying on lnd's invoice state release goods or credit without payment. Funds are not stolen from the node's balance, but the integrity of the payment-received record is fully defeated for that invoice. No confidentiality or availability impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a direct channel peer (anyone may open a channel) who also holds an invoice from the victim, e.g. as a customer. They add an HTLC paying the invoice with a near-immediate expiry, collect the victim's signatures, ignore the fail-back and force close. After the 3-6 confirmation dispatch delay the HTLC is expired and already reclaimed by the attacker's HTLC-timeout tx; the resolver's Launch nevertheless settles the invoice at height 0. No race or non-default configuration is needed beyond the victim accepting the inbound channel and issuing an invoice; the attacker controls expiry and timing.

## Recommended fix
1. findAndapplyPreimage passes currentHeight=0 to a state-changing NotifyExitHopHtlc call, which disables the registry's finalCltvRejectDelta / FinalCltvDelta expiry gate and lets an expired or imminently-expiring on-chain HTLC settle an OPEN invoice. Fix criteria: The Launch-time lookup must not change invoice state for HTLCs the registry would reject at the real chain height: either supply the actual best height (and let the registry fail ExpiryTooSoon HTLCs), or make the Launch path a pure read of an existing settle resolution that cannot accept or settle. Verify by force-closing with an incoming HTLC whose expiry has already passed at dispatch: the invoice must remain OPEN and no settle notification may be emitted.
2. The on-chain exit-hop path has no independent check that the HTLC is still claimable (expiry sufficiently far from the current height) before handing the preimage to the success resolver and settling the invoice. Fix criteria: Before any registry call that can settle, the resolver must compare htlcExpiry against the current best height with the same (or stricter) margin the link uses, and abandon the HTLC without settling if the margin is not met. Verify that an HTLC with expiry <= current height + finalCltvRejectDelta is abandoned with the invoice left untouched.

# ForwardingHistory, ListPayments and ListInvoices page size is caller-chosen with no upper bound

## Details
Three list endpoints in rpcserver.go let the caller choose the page size with no ceiling, so a single request forces lnd to load an entire table into memory under one read transaction, convert every record to protobuf, and serialise a response bounded only by grpc-go's default send limit.

`ForwardingHistory` (rpcserver.go:7587-7703, permission offchain:read at rpcserver.go:487) sets `numEvents = req.NumMaxEvents` and only substitutes 100 when the field is zero (7617-7620). The function's own doc comment (7577-7586) and the shipped `lncli fwdinghistory` help text (cmd/commands/cmd_payments.go:1552) both state that at most 50k events are returned per response, but no such clamp exists anywhere on the path. `channeldb.ForwardingLog.Query` (forwarding_log.go:331-407) walks the forwarding-log bucket inside one `kvdb.View` transaction from StartTime (default: Unix epoch) to EndTime (default: now), decoding and appending events until `uint32(len(resp.ForwardingEvents)) >= q.NumMaxEvents`; with `num_max_events = 4294967295` that exit never fires. On a routing node the forwarding log is the largest, ever-growing table (every forwarded HTLC, never pruned unless the operator runs DeleteForwardingHistory). The whole log is decoded into `[]ForwardingEvent`, re-marshalled into `[]*lnrpc.ForwardingEvent`, and, if `peer_alias_lookup` is set, a graph lookup is performed per distinct channel; the gRPC server sets only MaxRecvMsgSize (lnd.go:375-379), so the marshalled response is also fully built in memory. Millions of events translate into gigabytes of transient heap. miscDB is dbs.ChanStateDB (server.go:788), so the read transaction is held on channel.db itself.

`ListPayments` (rpcserver.go:7004-7016, offchain:read) and `ListInvoices` (5980-6006, invoices:read, reachable with the stock invoice.macaroon too) have the same shape: `MaxPayments`/`NumMaxInvoices` are uint64 request fields copied straight into the DB query with only the zero value defaulted. `channeldb.paginator.Query` (paginate.go:115-140) iterates until the caller's count is reached; `KVStore.QueryPayments` (payments/db/kv_store.go:1125-1135) fetches each payment with all of its HTLC attempts and route hops, `channeldb.DB.QueryInvoices` (channeldb/invoices.go:556-560) returns full invoice records including HTLC and AMP sets, and the SQL invoice store (invoices/sql_store.go:1141-1160) loops over pages until `NumMaxInvoices` is reached, so no backend bounds the result.

Impact: an RPC client holding only a read macaroon (the stock `readonly.macaroon` covers all three calls; `invoice.macaroon` covers ListInvoices) can drive lnd to out-of-memory with one request per endpoint, or pin a long-lived read transaction on channel.db. For a Lightning node a crash or stall is funds-relevant because it must stay live to resolve HTLCs and punish breaches. The code contradicts its own stated 50k contract, and the sibling endpoints share the defect. The paginated path the project sanctions bounds per-request memory to the page size; this path removes that bound.

Dependency assumptions: grpc v1.83.1 (go.mod:61) applies no server send-size limit unless MaxSendMsgSize is set (default math.MaxInt32) and marshals a unary response fully before writing it; bbolt v1.4.3 (go.mod:165) read transactions hold the mmap read lock, so a write transaction that must grow the file waits for the long read to finish.

## Evidence
1. [rpcserver.go:7617–7642](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L7617-L7642)
   ForwardingHistory (offchain:read, permission table rpcserver.go:487) sets numEvents = req.NumMaxEvents (uint32) and only substitutes 100 when the field is zero; the value is copied unchanged into channeldb.ForwardingEventQuery.NumMaxEvents. The doc comment at 7577-7586 states that 50k events per response is the cap used to stay under gRPC limits, but no clamp exists. This is the primary fix location.
2. [channeldb/forwarding\_log.go:331–406](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/forwarding_log.go#L331-L406)
   ForwardingLog.Query opens one kvdb.View read transaction, seeks to StartTime and iterates every key up to EndTime, decoding and appending a ForwardingEvent until uint32(len(resp.ForwardingEvents)) >= q.NumMaxEvents. With NumMaxEvents = 2^32-1 and the default StartTime = epoch / EndTime = now, that condition never fires and the entire log is materialised in memory under one read transaction.
3. [rpcserver.go:7004–7015](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L7004-L7015)
   ListPayments (offchain:read, rpcserver.go:459) copies req.MaxPayments (uint64) into paymentsdb.Query.MaxPayments; only the zero value is replaced by DefaultMaxPayments (100). The comment admits all payments are fetched into memory, yet no ceiling is applied to a caller-supplied value.
4. [rpcserver.go:5980–6005](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L5980-L6005)
   ListInvoices (invoices:read, rpcserver.go:407, reachable with the stock invoice.macaroon as well as readonly.macaroon) defaults req.NumMaxInvoices (uint64) from 0 to 100 and otherwise passes it unchanged into invoices.InvoiceQuery.NumMaxInvoices; every returned invoice is then converted with invoicesrpc.CreateRPCInvoice including its HTLC and AMP state.
5. [channeldb/paginate.go:115–139](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/paginate.go#L115-L139)
   paginator.Query loops over the index cursor until uint64(totalItems) >= p.totalItems or the cursor is exhausted; totalItems is the caller's MaxPayments / NumMaxInvoices, so a type-maximum value walks the whole index inside one read transaction.
6. [payments/db/kv\_store.go:1125–1134](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/payments/db/kv_store.go#L1125-L1134)
   KVStore.QueryPayments builds the paginator with query.MaxPayments and, per index entry, fetchPaymentWithSequenceNumber loads the full MPPayment including all HTLC attempts (routes, hops), appending each to resp.Payments.
7. [channeldb/invoices.go:556–559](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/invoices.go#L556-L559)
   channeldb.DB.QueryInvoices builds the paginator with q.NumMaxInvoices and fetchInvoice loads each full invoice record (HTLCs, AMP state) into resp.Invoices.
8. [invoices/sql\_store.go:1141–1159](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/invoices/sql_store.go#L1141-L1159)
   The SQL invoice store's paginationLimit only sizes each SQL batch; the outer for-loop keeps fetching pages and appending invoices until len(invoices) == int(q.NumMaxInvoices) or rows run out, so the SQL backends are equally unbounded.
9. [cmd/commands/cmd\_payments.go:1552–1553](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/cmd/commands/cmd_payments.go#L1552-L1553)
   The shipped lncli fwdinghistory help text tells operators 'The max number of events returned is 50k', confirming the 50k cap is the project's intended contract rather than an incidental comment; the server does not implement it.
10. [lnd.go:375–378](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnd.go#L375-L378)
   The gRPC server is configured only with MaxRecvMsgSize(200 MiB); no MaxSendMsgSize is set, so the response size is bounded only by grpc-go's default (math.MaxInt32 in grpc v1.83.1), and the full marshalled response is built in memory before transmission.
11. [server.go:788](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L788)
   miscDB (which serves ForwardingLog()) is dbs.ChanStateDB, i.e. channel.db, so the long-running read transaction in ForwardingLog.Query is held on the same bbolt database that stores commitment and HTLC state.

## Impact
A single request materialises a whole table (DB structs, protobuf structs and the marshalled response all resident at once) and can exhaust process memory, killing the daemon, or hold a long bbolt read transaction on channel.db that stalls state writes needing to grow the file. For lnd this is loss of availability of the whole node, which is funds-relevant. No confidentiality or integrity impact beyond what the read permission already grants.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a network RPC client (gRPC 10009 or REST 8080) authenticated with a limited macaroon: offchain:read reaches ForwardingHistory and ListPayments, invoices:read reaches ListInvoices, and both are in the stock readonly.macaroon (rpcserver.go:105-135) with invoices:read also in invoice.macaroon. One unary call per endpoint with the max field set to its type maximum; no defences, no interaction, no special configuration. The memory consumed is proportional to the table size the request unlocks, which on routing nodes is millions of forwarding events.

## Recommended fix
1. ForwardingHistory, ListPayments and ListInvoices forward caller-supplied page sizes to the database layer without an upper bound, so one request can materialise an entire table. Fix criteria: Each endpoint clamps the requested page size to a server-side maximum (the documented 50k for forwarding events, and comparable caps for payments and invoices) and returns pagination offsets so clients iterate. Verify that a request with the maximum field set to its type maximum returns at most the cap and that memory use stays proportional to the cap, not to table size.
2. channeldb.ForwardingLog.Query and the payments/invoices query paths accept an unbounded NumMaxEvents/MaxPayments/NumMaxInvoices and iterate until that count under one read transaction. Fix criteria: The storage-layer query functions enforce their own maximum batch size independent of the RPC layer so no caller can request an unbounded scan. Verify by calling Query with NumMaxEvents=MaxUint32 against a large log and confirming the returned slice is bounded.

# SubscribeChannelGraph spawns an unbounded goroutine per gossip update for a slow subscriber

## Details
`SubscribeChannelGraph` (rpcserver.go:6819-6871, gated by `info:read`, which the stock readonly macaroon carries via `readPermissions`) subscribes to `ChannelGraph.SubscribeTopology` and relays every `TopologyChange` to the gRPC stream (also exposed over REST/WebSocket at /v1/graph/subscribe). On the producer side, `ChannelGraph.notifyTopologyChange` (graph/db/notifications.go:158-198) delivers each change to each registered client by spawning a fresh goroutine that captures the `TopologyChange` and blocks on `t.ntfnChan <- topologyDiff` until the client reads it, the client is cancelled, or the graph quits. The per-client channel has a buffer of 10 and there is no cap on pending delivery goroutines, no coalescing, and no eviction of slow clients. The topology-update producer (graph/db/graph.go:172-177) also runs each update in its own goroutine, so nothing upstream slows down when a consumer stalls; the updates themselves originate from public gossip (discovery/gossiper.go -> graph/builder.go -> graphDB.AddNode/AddChannelEdge/UpdateEdgePolicy).

If the RPC consumer stops reading its stream (deliberately, or because it is a mobile/remote client on a poor link), `updateStream.Send` blocks once the HTTP/2 flow-control window is exhausted (grpc-go v1.83.1 `ServerStream.SendMsg` contract: blocks until there is sufficient flow control), the handler loop stops reading `client.TopologyChanges`, and from then on every node announcement, channel announcement, channel update and channel close the gossiper accepts adds a goroutine (kilobytes of stack) holding its `TopologyChange` (node addresses, features, policy data) to the heap. The stall is sustainable indefinitely: the client's HTTP/2 transport answers the server keepalive pings (default 1 min / 20 s, config.go:232-237) without the application reading, and the only release is stream termination, when the deferred `client.Cancel()` closes `exit` and the pending goroutines unwind. Memory grows linearly with gossip rate x stall time x number of stalled subscriptions; the rate is set by the public network's organic gossip volume (tens of thousands of updates per hour on mainnet), which the attacker need not control (per-peer inflation is throttled in discovery/, e.g. MaxChannelUpdateBurst, and requires the authoring node's signature).

An RPC client holding an info-read macaroon can open one or more SubscribeChannelGraph streams and never read them, driving lnd to memory exhaustion over hours; the same growth hits honest deployments whose subscriber is merely slow. Loss of node availability is funds-relevant for a Lightning node (missed HTLC/breach windows). The other in-tree consumers of SubscribeTopology (server.go:472 updatePersistentPeerAddrs, autopilot/manager.go:135) drain promptly and are not affected; the sibling RPC subscriptions (`SubscribeInvoices`, `SubscribeChannelBackups`) use an unbounded `queue.ConcurrentQueue` with the same shape but are fed by the node's own activity rather than public gossip.

## Evidence
1. [graph/db/notifications.go:158–198](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/notifications.go#L158-L198)
   notifyTopologyChange spawns one goroutine per registered topology client per TopologyChange (line 171); each goroutine captures topologyDiff and blocks on `t.ntfnChan <- topologyDiff` (buffer 10, SubscribeTopology line 112) until the consumer reads, the client is cancelled (exit closed in handleTopologySubscriptions) or the graph quits. No cap, coalescing or slow-client eviction exists, so a non-reading client accumulates one goroutine plus one TopologyChange per gossip update.
2. [rpcserver.go:6819–6871](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L6819-L6871)
   SubscribeChannelGraph (permission info:read, rpcserver.go:451, included in the stock readonly macaroon via readPermissions) registers a topology client and relays each change with updateStream.Send. When the gRPC/REST client stops reading, Send blocks on HTTP/2 flow control, the loop stops draining client.TopologyChanges, and the per-update goroutines accumulate until the stream ends and the deferred client.Cancel() closes exit.
3. [graph/db/graph.go:172–177](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/graph.go#L172-L177)
   handleTopologySubscriptions dispatches every topologyUpdate with `go c.handleTopologyUpdate`, so the producer (AddNode/AddChannelEdge/UpdateEdgePolicy at graph.go:385/414/648, fed by the gossiper via graph/builder.go:1121/1267 and discovery/gossiper.go:2199/2499/2957/3450) never experiences back-pressure from a stalled subscriber.

## Impact
Unbounded goroutine and heap growth inside the lnd process over hours of stall leads to OOM or severe GC pressure, i.e. loss of availability of the whole node, which must stay live to resolve HTLCs and punish breaches. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a network RPC client with info:read (stock readonly macaroon; the threat model names limited-macaroon callers as adversaries). It opens one or more SubscribeChannelGraph (or REST /v1/graph/subscribe) streams and stops reading while keeping the connection alive, which a stock grpc client does by simply not calling Recv. Memory then grows with the public gossip rate, which flows continuously on mainnet without attacker involvement. Default configuration, no defences (no per-client bound, no slow-subscriber eviction, no stream limit), no victim interaction. Assumes grpc-go v1.83.1's documented SendMsg flow-control blocking.

## Recommended fix
1. notifyTopologyChange allocates one blocking goroutine per client per update with no bound, so a stalled subscriber converts gossip volume into unbounded memory. Fix criteria: Delivery to a topology client is bounded: pending notifications per client are capped (drop/coalesce, or disconnect the slow client with an error) so that a non-reading subscriber cannot accumulate more than a fixed number of in-flight updates. Verify by holding a SubscribeChannelGraph stream without reading while gossip flows and confirming goroutine count and heap stay flat.
2. SubscribeChannelGraph has no per-subscriber back-pressure handling and the number of concurrent topology subscriptions per macaroon/connection is unlimited. Fix criteria: The RPC handler detects a consumer that cannot keep up (e.g. send deadline or bounded queue) and terminates the stream, and/or the number of simultaneous graph subscriptions is limited. Verify that a stalled client is disconnected rather than growing server memory.
