# Pre-auth gRPC/REST request decoding unbounded by auth: 200 MiB protobuf and unlimited REST bodies decoded before macaroon check

## Details
lnd's only RPC authentication is the rpcperms interceptor chain (rpcState -> macaroon -> middleware), attached to one grpc.Server that carries every service, including the deliberately macaroon-less WalletUnlocker/State. Interceptors run inside the generated method handler after `dec(in)` has fully unmarshalled the request (lnrpc/walletunlocker_grpc.pb.go:185-201, and every other `_Handler`), so request ingestion and protobuf decoding are pre-authentication work. That work is bounded only by `grpc.MaxRecvMsgSize(lnrpc.MaxGrpcMsgSize)` = 200 MiB (lnd.go:376), a ceiling chosen for large authenticated replies such as DescribeGraph (tls_manager.go:139-143); no MaxConcurrentStreams, InTapHandle or per-method limit exists anywhere in the tree.

Protobuf decoding amplifies attacker bytes: a 200 MiB body of `0x12 0x00` elements is ~105M zero-length entries of `repeated string cipher_seed_mnemonic` (walletunlocker.proto:117) and becomes ~105M 16-byte string headers (~1.7 GiB live, more during slice growth) on top of the 200 MiB raw buffer; `0x1a 0x00` elements of `repeated WatchOnlyAccount accounts` (:232) each become a heap-allocated message (~40x). Any lnd message with a repeated field works, on any method; the call is rejected for lacking a macaroon or wrong wallet state only after the allocation.

The REST listener (lnd.go:1046) is plain `http.Serve` with no `http.MaxBytesReader`; the generated grpc-gateway handlers (e.g. walletunlocker.pb.gw.go:74-78) read the entire body into memory via `utilities.IOReaderFactory` and JSON-decode it into the proto message in-process before forwarding on loopback. REST performs no authentication of its own (the macaroon header is only forwarded), so an unauthenticated client makes the process allocate an attacker-chosen, unbounded amount. By contrast the WebSocket proxy caps inbound frames at 4 MiB (websocket_proxy.go:45,156), the inbound ceiling the gRPC and plain-REST paths do not apply.

TLS is server-only (cert/tls.go:97-103), so no transport-layer credential is needed. Default listeners are loopback, but the project sanctions non-loopback binding with macaroons as the control (sample-lnd.conf `restlisten=0.0.0.0:8080`, docs/grpc/*.md LAN clients with `--tlsextraip`, config.go:1693-1711 refusing `--no-macaroons` only on non-private listeners); no documentation restricts the ports to trusted networks. For a Lightning node a remotely repeatable OOM kill is funds-relevant: the node must stay online to resolve HTLCs and punish revoked commitments.

Dependency behaviour assumed, not verifiable in the checkout: grpc-go v1.83.1 buffers a unary message up to MaxRecvMsgSize and unmarshals it before invoking the handler, and leaves concurrent streams unlimited when MaxConcurrentStreams is unset; grpc-gateway v2.16.0 `IOReaderFactory` is `io.ReadAll` and JSONPb decodes a whole JSON value; protobuf-go (replaced by lightninglabs/protobuf-go-hex-display v1.33.0-hex-display) appends repeated elements with slice growth.

## Evidence
1. [lnd.go:373–380](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnd.go#L373-L380)
   The single grpc.Server carrying every lnd service (Lightning, all subservers, WalletUnlocker, State) is created with grpc.MaxRecvMsgSize(lnrpc.MaxGrpcMsgSize) = 200 MiB. This is the only inbound bound; no MaxConcurrentStreams, InTapHandle or per-method limit exists anywhere in the tree. This is the primary fix location: pre-authentication ingestion inherits a ceiling sized for authenticated replies.
2. [lnrpc/walletunlocker\_grpc.pb.go:185–201](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/walletunlocker_grpc.pb.go#L185-L201)
   Generated unary handler (same shape for every lnd method): dec(in) fully unmarshals the request into a Go message BEFORE interceptor(ctx, in, info, handler) is invoked, so the rpcState and macaroon interceptors run only after the attacker-sized message has been received and protobuf-decoded.
3. [lnd.go:1044–1049](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnd.go#L1044-L1049)
   The REST listener serves the grpc-gateway/WebSocket/CORS handler chain via plain http.Serve: no http.Server limits and no http.MaxBytesReader anywhere in the tree, so the HTTP request body size is unbounded. REST performs no authentication of its own; the macaroon header is only forwarded to the loopback gRPC hop.
4. [lnrpc/walletunlocker.pb.gw.go:70–82](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/walletunlocker.pb.gw.go#L70-L82)
   Generated grpc-gateway handler for POST /v1/initwallet (same shape for every body:'*' route): utilities.IOReaderFactory(req.Body) reads the whole body into memory and marshaler.NewDecoder(...).Decode(&protoReq) JSON-decodes it into the proto message in-process, before client.InitWallet forwards it on loopback where the auth interceptors live. An unauthenticated client therefore sets the allocation size with no cap.
5. [rpcperms/interceptor.go:544–616](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcperms/interceptor.go#L544-L616)
   CreateServerOpts attaches only unary/stream interceptors (panic recovery, error log, rpcState, macaroon, middleware). These are the system's entire RPC authentication and by construction run after grpc-go has buffered and decoded the request; nothing here can reject or bound a message before decoding.
6. [lnrpc/walletunlocker.proto:117](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/walletunlocker.proto#L117)
   InitWalletRequest.cipher_seed_mnemonic is `repeated string` (and `accounts` at line 232 is a repeated message). A 200 MiB body of ~105M zero-length elements (2 wire bytes each) decodes into ~105M 16-byte string headers (~1.7 GiB live, higher during slice growth) or ~105M heap-allocated WatchOnlyAccount messages (~40x), i.e. 8-40x amplification over bytes sent. Any lnd message with a repeated field behaves the same.
7. [lnrpc/websocket\_proxy.go:42–45](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/websocket_proxy.go#L42-L45)
   The project's own WebSocket proxy caps inbound frames at MaxWsMsgSize = 4 MiB (applied via conn.SetReadLimit at line 156), with the comment that gRPC has 'a similar setting'. This shows the intended inbound ceiling; the gRPC server (200 MiB) and plain REST path (unbounded) do not apply it.
8. [cert/tls.go:97–103](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/cert/tls.go#L97-L103)
   The server TLS config sets only Certificates/CipherSuites/MinVersion, no ClientAuth: any network client can complete the TLS handshake and send request bodies without a credential at the transport layer.
9. [config.go:1693–1711](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config.go#L1693-L1711)
   EnforceSafeAuthentication refuses only the --no-macaroons combination on non-private listeners: the project sanctions binding gRPC/REST on non-loopback interfaces (sample-lnd.conf shows restlisten=0.0.0.0:8080, docs/grpc/*.md describe LAN clients with --tlsextraip) with TLS+macaroons as the sole control, so an unauthenticated remote client on these ports is an in-scope position and no documented fencing requirement excludes it.
10. [tls\_manager.go:138–156](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/tls_manager.go#L138-L156)
   The 200 MiB figure is explicitly motivated by large replies (DescribeGraph) for the REST->gRPC loopback client; the same constant is reused as the server's inbound receive ceiling, including for macaroon-less WalletUnlocker/State routes and every pre-auth request.

## Impact
Multi-GiB heap growth per unauthenticated request drives the lnd process to an OOM kill or swap thrash on typical node hardware (2-8 GiB), repeatable after every restart. Loss of lnd availability is funds-relevant per the threat model: missed HTLC timeout and breach-remedy windows. No confidentiality or integrity effect.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any client able to open a TLS connection to the gRPC (10009) or REST (8080) listener, with no macaroon and in any wallet state. gRPC: send a unary request to any method (e.g. /lnrpc.WalletUnlocker/InitWallet) whose ~200 MiB body is repeated zero-length elements; grpc-go buffers and protobuf-decodes it into multi-GiB heap before the interceptor rejects it; repeat on parallel HTTP/2 streams. REST: POST an arbitrarily large JSON {"cipher_seed_mnemonic":["",...]} to /v1/initwallet; the gateway reads and decodes it in-process with no cap. Remote reach needs the listener bound beyond the default loopback, a documented, sanctioned configuration.

## Recommended fix
1. The 200 MiB MaxRecvMsgSize (and the absence of any REST body limit) is applied to all inbound requests, including those from unauthenticated clients and to methods that will be rejected by the macaroon/state interceptors, so the attacker controls how much memory lnd allocates before any authorization decision is made. Fix criteria: Pre-authentication request ingestion must be bounded to a small size independent of the 200 MiB reply ceiling: e.g. a low per-message receive limit for unauthenticated connections/methods (WalletUnlocker/State and any call lacking a macaroon), with the large limit applied only after macaroon validation, and an http.MaxBytesReader (or equivalent) on the REST listener. Verify by sending a 200 MiB repeated-empty-element InitWalletRequest without a macaroon over gRPC and an oversize JSON body over REST: both must be rejected without materialising the decoded message, and lnd's RSS must not grow beyond the configured small bound.
2. No cap on concurrent HTTP/2 streams lets a single attacker multiply the per-request allocation. Fix criteria: Concurrent inbound streams per connection (grpc.MaxConcurrentStreams) and total in-flight pre-auth requests are bounded so that the worst-case aggregate pre-auth allocation is a fixed, documented amount; verify that N parallel oversize requests from one client cannot drive memory above that amount.

# Taproot channel MuSig2 signing sessions are never released, growing memory per state update

## Details
For simple-taproot (musig2) channels, every commitment state transition creates MuSig2 signing sessions in the signer's process-global MusigSessionManager (lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go:186, embedded in BtcWallet for the daemon's lifetime; lc.Signer at lnwallet/channel.go:10297) that are never freed.

Two sessions are created per round: (1) in SignNextCommitment, RemoteSession.SignCommit generates a JIT nonce, calls FinalizeSession -> MuSig2CreateSession (stored in the sync.Map at input/musig2_session_manager.go:140), then calls MuSig2Sign with cleanUp=false (lnwallet/musig_session.go:416-418). The remote party combines the signatures, so lnd never calls MuSig2CombineSig or MuSig2Cleanup on this session. (2) In ReceiveNewCommitment, LocalSession.VerifyCommitSig calls FinalizeSession -> MuSig2CreateSession (stored), verifies the remote partial signature in pure Go (MusigPartialSig.Verify, never touching the stored session), and the LightningChannel then replaces LocalSession with Refresh(); the stored MuSig2State is orphaned. The same happens to RemoteSession in ReceiveRevocation.

input/musig2_session_manager.go only deletes entries in MuSig2Sign when cleanUp is true (never for lnwallet), in MuSig2CombineSig once all partial sigs are present (never for commitment sessions), or via MuSig2Cleanup (no caller in lnwallet; the only callers are the signrpc server and the rpcwallet forwarder). The map (lnutils.SyncMap over sync.Map) has no bound, expiry or eviction.

Each leaked MuSig2State retains a musig2.Context (including a copy of the channel multisig private key and key set), a musig2.Session (public nonces, combined nonce, message, and, for the never-signed verification sessions, the 97-byte secret nonce), the session info and a map entry, on the order of 1-2 KB per session (structure of musig2.Context/Session assumed from btcd v0.25.1-pre as pinned in go.mod). A channel counterparty drives the number of state updates: on a taproot channel it can loop HTLC add/fail cycles (or, as initiator, update_fee) indefinitely at no cost, each full round adding two leaked sessions on our side; no per-channel update rate limit exists in htlcswitch or peer. Sustained at tens of rounds per second this grows the lnd heap by hundreds of KB/s until the daemon is OOM-killed, taking the node offline (and with it its ability to resolve HTLCs and respond to breaches). Honest traffic leaks at the same rate, so busy taproot routing nodes degrade without any attacker. In remote-signing deployments the leak occurs in the remote signer process instead, since rpcwallet forwards MuSig2CreateSession/MuSig2Sign with the same cleanUp=false flag.

Secondary hygiene issue: the orphaned sessions keep our shachain-derived secret nonces and multisig private key copies resident in memory for the lifetime of the process.

Condition under which it holds: the node must have at least one simple-taproot channel, which requires the operator to have enabled the non-default protocol.simple-taproot-chans option (documented in sample-lnd.conf as an experimental, but supported and shipped, channel type) and to have opened or accepted a taproot channel with the attacker. The attacker needs no privilege on the node beyond being that counterparty.

## Evidence
1. [lnwallet/musig\_session.go:416–418](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/musig_session.go#L416-L418)
   SignCommit calls m.signer.MuSig2Sign(sessionID, msg, false). The cleanUp flag is false, so the MuSig2State registered for this remote-commitment session stays in the signer's session map after the partial signature is produced. Nothing ever combines or cleans this session (the remote party combines), so one entry is leaked per commitment we sign.
2. [lnwallet/musig\_session.go:526–586](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/musig_session.go#L526-L586)
   VerifyCommitSig calls FinalizeSession (line 528), which calls MuSig2CreateSession (line 314) and stores a new MuSig2State holding our secret verification nonce. The session is only used for a pure-Go partialSig.Verify (line 560); MuSig2Sign/MuSig2CombineSig/MuSig2Cleanup are never invoked on it, so it is leaked once per commitment we receive.
3. [input/musig2\_session\_manager.go:134–142](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/input/musig2_session_manager.go#L134-L142)
   MuSig2CreateSession stores every session in the process-wide musig2Sessions SyncMap (a sync.Map wrapper) keyed by a fresh nonce-derived ID; there is no bound, expiry or eviction.
4. [input/musig2\_session\_manager.go:174–185](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/input/musig2_session_manager.go#L174-L185)
   MuSig2Sign only deletes the session when cleanUp is true; lnwallet always passes false. MuSig2CombineSig (lines 233-236) deletes only when all partial signatures are present, which never happens for commitment sessions; MuSig2Cleanup (lines 242-257) has no caller in lnwallet.
5. [lnwallet/channel.go:4274–4287](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L4274-L4287)
   SignNextCommitment signs every new remote commitment with lc.musigSessions.RemoteSession.SignCommit for taproot channels; this is the per-update entry point that leaks the remote-commitment session.
6. [lnwallet/channel.go:5490–5544](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L5490-L5544)
   ReceiveNewCommitment verifies every incoming taproot commit_sig via LocalSession.VerifyCommitSig and then replaces the session with LocalSession.Refresh, abandoning the finalized session object whose backing MuSig2State remains in the signer map. This is the per-update entry point that leaks the local-commitment session.
7. [lnwallet/channel.go:6079–6095](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L6079-L6095)
   ReceiveRevocation similarly replaces RemoteSession via Refresh after each revoke_and_ack without cleaning up the previously finalized session.
8. [lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go:186–188](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go#L186-L188)
   Production wiring: BtcWallet embeds a single input.MusigSessionManager created once at wallet construction, so the session map is process-global and lives for the daemon's lifetime; lc.Signer (lnwallet/channel.go:10297) is this wallet, so the leaked sessions accumulate in the lnd (or remote signer) process.

## Impact
Unbounded heap growth in the lnd daemon (or the remote signer) proportional to counterparty-driven state updates, never released until process restart, ending in OOM termination; the node must stay online to resolve HTLCs and punish breaches, so loss of availability is the direct impact. Per-session footprint (~1-2 KB: MuSig2State, musig2.Context with private key copy, musig2.Session with nonces, sync.Map entry) is an assumption from the structure of btcd v0.25.1-pre's musig2 package as pinned in go.mod. The retained secret nonces/private key copies are a hygiene concern only, not a confidentiality impact on their own.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the counterparty of a simple-taproot channel with the victim node, which requires the node to run with the non-default protocol.simple-taproot-chans option and to have opened/accepted such a channel (AT:P). The counterparty holds no credential or privilege on the node (PR:N): lnd accepts inbound channels and all subsequent channel updates from any peer. Over the P2P connection it repeatedly adds HTLCs that lnd fails (or, as initiator, alternates update_fee), forcing commit_sig/revoke_and_ack rounds. Each round makes lnd call SignCommit (leaks one session) and VerifyCommitSig (leaks one session); no per-channel update rate limit exists in htlcswitch/peer. No crypto or defense must be defeated; the leak is deterministic and linear in the number of updates the attacker chooses to drive.

## Recommended fix
1. MusigSession.SignCommit signs with cleanUp=false and no later call releases the remote-commitment session, so each signed commitment leaks a MuSig2State in the signer's session map. Fix criteria: After a partial signature is produced for a commitment that this node will not combine, the session must be removed from the MusigSessionManager (e.g. sign with cleanUp=true or explicitly call MuSig2Cleanup). Verify by driving N taproot state updates and asserting the session map size does not grow with N.
2. MusigSession.VerifyCommitSig finalizes a session (allocating a stored MuSig2State with the secret verification nonce) solely to verify in pure Go, and the LightningChannel then discards the MusigSession via Refresh without releasing the backing session. Fix criteria: Verification must not leave a stored signer session behind: either verify without creating a signer-side session, or release the session (MuSig2Cleanup) once verification completes or when Refresh replaces it. Verify that receiving N commit_sigs on a taproot channel leaves no additional entries in the session map and no retained secret nonces.

# Fundee accepts any funder feerate_per_kw, yielding unrelayable, unclosable commitment

## Details
BOLT 2 requires the fundee to fail an open_channel whose feerate_per_kw it considers too small for timely processing. lnd's fundee path has no such check: fundeeProcessOpenChannel (funding/manager.go:1440-1760) validates amount, push, channel type, reserve/dust/CSV bounds, but forwards msg.FeePerKiloWeight unchanged as InitFundingReserveMsg.CommitFeePerKw (:1693). lnwallet.NewChannelReservation (reservation.go:304-395) only verifies the funder's balance can cover the resulting fee and stores the rate into both commitments (:507,:513); CreateCommitmentTxns (wallet.go:1571-1620) runs only blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity. The default ChainedAcceptor has no acceptors unless an operator registers an RPC channel acceptor (lnd.go:616, rpcserver.go:8147). A remote funder can therefore open a channel with feerate_per_kw = 0 (or any value below chainfee.FeePerKwFloor = 253 sat/kw) and the fundee signs and persists a zero-fee initial commitment.

Consequences once the funding tx confirms: (1) lnd's own post-funding invariant rejects every later commitment below the floor (validateCommitmentSanity, channel.go:3942; createCommitmentTx effFeeRate check, channel.go:2940), so the fundee can neither accept nor originate an HTLC — ReceiveHTLC fails the link (link.go:4117-4120) — and only the initiator ever sends update_fee (link.go:3903). The channel is usable only if the attacker chooses to repair it with an update_fee. (2) The fundee cannot unilaterally exit: a force close publishes the zero-fee commitment, TestMempoolAccept/sendrawtransaction reject it below minrelaytxfee (mapped to lnwallet.ErrMempoolFee, btcwallet.go:1301-1305), the arbitrator tolerates that error and waits in StateCommitmentBroadcasted (channel_arbitrator.go:1162-1175) forever. For anchor channels the sweeper's anchor child cannot be accepted because the parent never entered the mempool; lnd performs no automatic package submission for force closes (SubmitPackage is only exposed via the walletrpc RPC, bitcoind >= 28 assumed). The non-anchor static_remote_key-only channel type is still accepted (commitment_type_negotiation.go:228-233) and has no CPFP path at all. (3) Any amount pushed to the fundee is unrecoverable without the funder's cooperation. The only operator remedy is AbandonChannel with the i_know_what_i_am_doing flag (rpcserver.go:3305).

The attacker pays the funding amount (>= MinChanSize, default 20k sat) plus mining fees and can later recover the funds by cooperative close, so this is deterministic griefing rather than theft: an unauthenticated peer can saddle an lnd node with channels it can neither use nor close, each with its arbitrator/chain-watcher and (for anchor channels) a share of the wallet's anchor reserve. Assumption: Bitcoin Core/btcd reject a zero-fee transaction submitted via RPC below minrelaytxfee and do not package-evaluate RPC submissions.

## Evidence
1. [funding/manager.go:1683–1704](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L1683-L1704)
   fundeeProcessOpenChannel copies msg.FeePerKiloWeight straight into InitFundingReserveMsg.CommitFeePerKw with no lower (or upper) bound; none of the preceding validation in the function (amount, push, channel type, reserve/dust/CSV) looks at the fee rate. This is where the fix belongs.
2. [lnwallet/reservation.go:304–394](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/reservation.go#L304-L394)
   NewChannelReservation only uses CommitFeePerKw to compute the funder's balance and rejects a negative or dust funder balance; a fee rate of 0 passes every check and is stored into both commitments' FeePerKw.
3. [lnwallet/wallet.go:1571–1619](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/wallet.go#L1571-L1619)
   CreateCommitmentTxns, invoked from handleSingleFunderSigs when funding_created arrives, builds the initial commitments and performs only blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity, which has no minimum-fee check; the zero-fee commitment is then signed and persisted.
4. [lnwallet/channel.go:3940–3944](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L3940-L3944)
   validateCommitmentSanity rejects any later commitment below chainfee.FeePerKwFloor, so a channel opened below the floor cannot accept or add a single HTLC until the funder raises the fee; this is also the invariant the initial-state path fails to enforce.
5. [htlcswitch/link.go:3903–3905](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L3903-L3905)
   handleUpdateFee returns immediately for the non-initiator: the fundee has no way to send update_fee and repair the channel itself.
6. [funding/commitment\_type\_negotiation.go:228–232](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/commitment_type_negotiation.go#L228-L232)
   The funder may still negotiate a static_remote_key-only (non-anchor) commitment type, for which the fundee has no anchor output to CPFP; its zero-fee commitment is then unbroadcastable by any means lnd offers.
7. [contractcourt/channel\_arbitrator.go:1162–1175](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/channel_arbitrator.go#L1162-L1175)
   On force close the arbitrator treats a mempool-fee rejection (lnwallet.ErrMempoolFee) as non-fatal and advances to StateCommitmentBroadcasted, relying on anchor CPFP that cannot work when the parent was never accepted; the channel stays unresolved indefinitely.

## Impact
No confidentiality impact. Integrity: the node is made to sign and persist a commitment it cannot broadcast; any balance pushed to it is unrecoverable without the funder's cooperation, and the channel's state can never be advanced by the victim — a limited integrity effect on channel state. Availability: the victim holds a channel it can neither use nor unilaterally close, consuming an arbitrator, chain watcher, link and (for anchor channels) wallet anchor reserve, removable only via the flagged AbandonChannel RPC; the node as a whole keeps running, so partial availability loss.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any Internet peer completes a brontide handshake to 9735 and sends open_channel with feerate_per_kw = 0 and a channel type both sides support (default anchors, or static_remote_key-only), then completes funding_created/funding_signed and broadcasts a real funding transaction of at least MinChanSize. The fundee accepts under default configuration with no RPC channel acceptor registered; no race or special state is required. The attacker's funds are recoverable later via cooperative close, so the cost is on-chain fees and locked capital.

## Recommended fix
The fundee trusts the funder-chosen initial commitment fee rate without checking it against the relay floor, so it signs and persists a commitment transaction it may be unable to broadcast, contrary to the floor lnd itself enforces on every later commitment. Fix criteria: fundeeProcessOpenChannel must reject an open_channel whose feerate_per_kw is below the node's current minimum relay fee rate (at least chainfee.FeePerKwFloor), and optionally above a sane maximum, returning a funding error to the peer before any reservation is created. Verify by sending open_channel with feerate_per_kw = 0 and = 100 and confirming an error reply with no reservation or pending channel persisted, while a feerate at or above the floor still opens.

# Inbound channel whose confirmed funding tx fails ValidateChannel stays pending indefinitely, defeating the 2016-block forget timer

## Details
A remote funder chooses the FundingPoint in funding_created; fundeeProcessFundingCreated -> CompleteReservationSingle -> handleSingleFunderSigs (lnwallet/wallet.go:2432) only checks the funder's signature over our commitment (which the funder can always produce for any outpoint) and persists the channel with IsPending=true. The outpoint is validated only once the referenced transaction confirms: handleFundingConfirmation (funding/manager.go:3383-3387) calls Wallet.ValidateChannel and, when it fails, returns an error annotated 'TODO(roasbeef): delete chan state?'. advancePendingChannelState (1410-1416) wraps the error and advanceFundingState (1096-1102) only logs it: the channel is never closed with FundingCanceled, NotifyFundingTimeout is never emitted and the peer is never sent an error. Because waitForFundingWithTimeout (2993-3030) already returned on the confirmation and closed cancelChan, the waitForTimeout goroutine that implements the BOLT-2 2016-block forget rule has exited, so no further cleanup can happen for the lifetime of the process.

Triggering it: the TxNotifier only dispatches a confirmation for a tx whose txid matches AND which carries an output paying the channel's funding pkScript (chainntnfs/txnotifier.go:212-229; ConfDetailsFromTxIndex applies the same MatchesTx check, chainntnfs/interface.go:762), and our multisig key is derived fresh per reservation (lnwallet/wallet.go:1411), so pointing at a pre-existing confirmed tx does not work. The attacker instead mines one cheap transaction with a dust (330 sat) P2WSH output paying the exact 2-of-2 funding script, and either sets FundingPoint.Index to a different output (chanvalidate Locate/ErrWrongPkScript), to an out-of-range index (Locate error), or leaves the correct index with a value != capacity (ErrInvalidSize; capacity >= MinChanSize 20000 sat by default). After NumConfsRequired confirmations the Confirmed event fires, ValidateChannel fails, and the channel is stuck. One transaction can carry one such output per bogus channel, for channels opened from many throw-away identities.

Consequences: fundeeProcessOpenChannel counts DB channels with IsPending=true toward the per-peer MaxPendingChannels (default 1) and the node-wide pendingChansLimit of 50 (funding/manager.go:1468-1506). The stuck entries therefore occupy those slots indefinitely, converting the 2016-block inbound-channel denial of service of the verified companion finding inbound-pending-channel-global-cap-sybil-exhaustion (same cap, never-confirming outpoints) into one that does not expire on its own: with 51 stuck entries every honest inbound open_channel fails with ErrMaxPendingChannels. Each entry also keeps a chainWatcher/ChannelArbitrator registered (WatchNewChannel at 2652; ChainArbitrator.loadOpenChannels uses FetchAllChannels, which includes pending channels) and keeps the attacker's key in persistentPeers (server.go:1680-1681), so the node keeps dialling it.

Recovery: a restart re-runs advanceFundingState for every pending channel (start(), 740-787). Within 2016 blocks of the recorded broadcast height the historical confirmation is re-dispatched and the channel sticks again. After 2016 blocks, waitForTimeout's RegisterBlockEpochNtfn(nil) receives the current tip immediately (bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:362, btcdnotify/btcd.go:416, neutrinonotify/neutrino.go:482) and will usually beat the backend round-trip of the historical confirmation lookup, so a restart two weeks later most likely cleans the entry via fundingTimeout, but nothing in the running process ever does; otherwise the operator must AbandonChannel each one with i_know_what_i_am_doing (rpcserver.go:3305-3310).

## Evidence
1. [funding/manager.go:3383–3387](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L3383-L3387)
   handleFundingConfirmation calls Wallet.ValidateChannel on the confirmed tx and, on failure, returns an error with the comment 'TODO(roasbeef): delete chan state?' — the pending channel record is neither closed (CloseChannel/FundingCanceled) nor announced as timed out; this is where the fix belongs.
2. [funding/manager.go:1346–1416](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L1346-L1416)
   advancePendingChannelState: only ErrConfirmationTimeout leads to fundingTimeout (1350-1351); the handleFundingConfirmation error at 1410-1416 is wrapped and returned, and advanceFundingState (1096-1102) merely logs it, leaving IsPending=true in channeldb.
3. [funding/manager.go:2993–3030](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L2993-L3030)
   waitForFundingWithTimeout closes cancelChan when a confirmation is delivered, which terminates the waitForTimeout goroutine; after the (invalid) confirmation the 2016-block forget rule can never fire for this channel while the process lives.
4. [funding/manager.go:1468–1505](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L1468-L1505)
   fundeeProcessOpenChannel counts channels with IsPending=true from the database toward the per-peer MaxPendingChannels and the node-wide pendingChansLimit (50); a stuck entry occupies these slots indefinitely and blocks honest inbound open_channel with ErrMaxPendingChannels.
5. [funding/manager.go:2531–2547](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L2531-L2547)
   fundeeProcessFundingCreated hands the remote-chosen FundingPoint to CompleteReservationSingle, which persists the pending channel; the only check is the funder's signature over our commitment, so the outpoint can reference any transaction the attacker likes.
6. [lnwallet/wallet.go:2646–2720](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/wallet.go#L2646-L2720)
   ValidateChannel builds the funding pkScript and calls chanvalidate.Validate with an OutPointChanLocator over the confirmed tx; it fails when the index is out of range, the output script differs, or the output value differs from the capacity.
7. [lnwallet/chanvalidate/validate.go:155–184](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chanvalidate/validate.go#L155-L184)
   Validate: Locate error (bad index), ErrWrongPkScript (output script mismatch) and ErrInvalidSize (value != capacity) are the three attacker-selectable failure modes.
8. [chainntnfs/txnotifier.go:212–229](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/txnotifier.go#L212-L229)
   ConfRequest.MatchesTx requires the txid to match AND some output to pay the funding pkScript; so the confirmation fires only for an attacker-mined tx that carries a dust output with the exact 2-of-2 funding script (wrong value or wrong index), not for an arbitrary pre-existing tx.
9. [funding/manager.go:3278–3306](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L3278-L3306)
   waitForTimeout registers RegisterBlockEpochNtfn(nil) and times out when the delivered height >= broadcastHeight + 2016; the notifiers dispatch the current tip immediately for a nil bestBlock, so a restart after 2016 blocks usually cleans the entry, but no restart within that window does and nothing in the running process ever does.

## Impact
No confidentiality or integrity impact on funds. Availability: stuck entries never expire while the process runs and re-stick on any restart within 2016 blocks; with 51 identities the node persistently refuses all inbound channel opens (ErrMaxPendingChannels), a core function for routing nodes/LSPs, until the operator abandons each channel or restarts after two weeks. Existing channels and payments keep working. Each entry also retains a chainWatcher/arbitrator and a persistent-peer reconnect loop.

## Reproduction steps
1. Anonymous peer on 9735 opens an inbound channel (open_channel/accept_channel), sends funding_created whose FundingPoint names a transaction it mines itself with a 330-sat P2WSH output paying the channel's funding script at the wrong index or with a value != capacity, plus a valid signature over our commitment. Fundee persists the pending channel; once the tx reaches NumConfsRequired confirmations the notifier dispatches it, ValidateChannel fails and the channel is never cleaned up. One cheap on-chain transaction can carry one such output per bogus channel; default configuration; no race.

## Recommended fix
A confirmed funding transaction that fails ValidateChannel is treated as a transient error: the pending channel record, arbitrator registration, persistent-peer entry and pending-slot accounting are never released, and the confirmation has already cancelled the 2016-block forget timer. Fix criteria: When the referenced funding transaction confirms but does not match the expected script/index/amount, the fundee must treat the channel as invalid and perform the same cleanup as fundingTimeout (CloseChannel with FundingCanceled, NotifyFundingTimeout, error to the peer), so it stops counting toward per-peer and global pending limits without a restart. Verify by confirming a tx with a mismatching output for an inbound pending channel and checking it disappears from FetchPendingChannels and that a new inbound open_channel from another peer is accepted.

# Anonymous peers exhaust global inbound pending-channel cap with unfunded channels for 2016 blocks

## Details
The fundee path of the funding manager counts every channel in the database with IsPending=true (f.cfg.ChannelDB.FetchPendingChannels) and refuses all further inbound open_channel messages once that count exceeds the hard-coded pendingChansLimit of 50 (funding/manager.go:1496-1505). The only per-adversary bound is MaxPendingChannels (default 1), keyed on the remote node's public key (funding/manager.go:1460-1494), which an anonymous peer can generate for free.

An attacker with 51 throw-away node identities does the following for each: connect over brontide to port 9735 (an accessman restricted slot suffices and is released again once the pending channel is recorded, accessman.go:245-263), send open_channel for an amount >= minchansize (default 20000 sat) with the default channel type, receive accept_channel, and send funding_created whose FundingPoint names a transaction that will never exist, plus a valid signature over our first commitment transaction. The attacker owns the funding key the signature must come from, so it can sign for any outpoint. fundeeProcessFundingCreated -> CompleteReservationSingle -> lnwallet handleSingleFunderSigs sets FundingOutpoint to the remote value, verifies only that commitment signature, and calls SyncPending (lnwallet/wallet.go:2576), persisting the channel as IsPending with FundingBroadcastHeight = current height before funding_signed is even sent. No on-chain funds, fee, mempool presence or confirmation are required. The attacker then disconnects.

Each such entry survives until waitForTimeout fires at BroadcastHeight + 2016 blocks (~14 days, lncfg.DefaultMaxWaitNumBlocksFundingConf; funding/manager.go:3285-3320) and fundingTimeout removes it. During that window len(pendingChans) > 50 and every inbound open_channel from any honest peer fails with ErrMaxPendingChannels. The attacker refreshes the set every two weeks for an indefinite lockout. Legitimate outbound pending channels also count toward the same cap, lowering the number of identities needed.

The project itself documents the primitive it hands the attacker here: docs/onion_message_rate_limiting.md:47-52 excludes pending channels from the onion-message gate because 'a pending channel is one where we have sent or received a funding transaction but the channel is not yet confirmed ... Pending channels are also cheap to open and, under adversarial conditions, easy to leave stuck. Counting them would hand the attacker the same free-identity primitive the gate exists to remove.' The funding manager's node-wide cap counts exactly those channels.

Side effects: each bogus channel is handed to the ChainArbitrator and the attacker identity is added to persistentPeers (server.go:1670-1686), so the node keeps dialling 51 attacker addresses for two weeks.

The operator has no configuration knob for the cap and can only recover early by abandoning each bogus channel via AbandonChannel with i_know_what_i_am_doing (rpcserver.go:3305-3310 refuses the call otherwise in release builds).

This is lnd-specific: BOLT 2 only asks the fundee to forget an unconfirmed channel after 2016 blocks; the node-wide 50-entry refusal that turns 51 unfunded entries into a lockout of all inbound channel opens is lnd's addition. Related but distinct: the candidate on confirmed-but-invalid funding transactions (funding/manager.go handleFundingConfirmation), which would make such entries permanent instead of two-week-bounded.

## Evidence
1. [funding/manager.go:1496–1505](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L1496-L1505)
   fundeeProcessOpenChannel fetches every channel in the DB with IsPending=true (FetchPendingChannels, channeldb/db.go:1178) and fails every inbound open_channel with ErrMaxPendingChannels once len(pendingChans) > pendingChansLimit (50), regardless of which peer created the pending entries or whether their funding tx was ever seen.
2. [funding/manager.go:1460–1494](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L1460-L1494)
   The only identity-scoped guard is MaxPendingChannels (lncfg.DefaultMaxPendingChannels = 1), counted per remote node pubkey via activeReservations[peerIDKey] and FetchOpenChannels(peerPubKey). Node pubkeys are free to generate, so 51 throw-away identities each get one pending channel.
3. [lnwallet/wallet.go:2501–2576](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/wallet.go#L2501-L2576)
   handleSingleFunderSigs (reached via CompleteReservationSingle from fundeeProcessFundingCreated) sets chanState.FundingOutpoint to the remote-supplied FundingPoint, verifies only the remote's signature over our commitment tx (verifyCommitSig, which the funder produces with its own funding key for any outpoint), then persists the channel with IsPending=true and FundingBroadcastHeight=bestHeight via SyncPending (2576). Nothing checks that the outpoint exists in the mempool or chain.
4. [funding/manager.go:2531–2547](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L2531-L2547)
   fundeeProcessFundingCreated passes the remote-chosen FundingPoint straight to CompleteReservationSingle; on success the channel is already in the DB as pending before funding_signed is sent, so the attacker can disconnect at this point and the entry survives.
5. [funding/manager.go:3285–3319](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L3285-L3319)
   waitForTimeout only cancels a non-initiated pending channel once the chain reaches BroadcastHeight + lncfg.DefaultMaxWaitNumBlocksFundingConf (2016 blocks, ~2 weeks) in release builds; fundingTimeout (2917-2945) then removes it. Until then each bogus entry occupies a slot in the global cap. waitForFundingWithTimeout (3006-3012) starts this timer only for non-initiator, non-zero-conf channels.
6. [funding/manager.go:106–109](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L106-L109)
   pendingChansLimit = 50 is a hard-coded, node-wide constant with no configuration knob.
7. [server.go:1670–1685](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L1670-L1685)
   WatchNewChannel, called for each bogus pending channel, marks the attacker identity as a persistent peer and hands the channel to the ChainArbitrator, so the node also keeps redialling the 51 attacker identities for the two-week window (side effect, not the primary impact).

## Impact
No confidentiality or integrity effect. Availability: the node can no longer accept any inbound channel from anyone for ~2 weeks per attack round, indefinitely renewable, and the condition persists after the attacker disconnects. Existing channels, forwarding and payments keep working and the node can still open outbound channels, so this is denial of one function; CVSS 4.0 rates an attacker who 'cannot disrupt existing connections, but can prevent new connections' as High availability impact, and for LSPs and routing nodes accepting inbound channels is a primary function. Secondary cost: 51 persistent-peer dial loops and 51 ChainArbitrator watchers for the window.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any Internet host that can complete a brontide handshake to port 9735 (the node pubkey is public). It generates 51 node keys and for each performs the open_channel/accept_channel/funding_created exchange with a fabricated funding outpoint and a commitment signature it can always produce with its own funding key; the pending entry is persisted before funding_signed, so it can disconnect immediately. No funds, mining, race or victim configuration beyond defaults (MaxPendingChannels=1, pendingChansLimit=50, no RPC channel acceptor) is needed; the node must merely be chain-synced, which any operating node is. Effect is deterministic, lasts 2016 blocks, and is repeatable.

## Recommended fix
A node-wide hard cap on pending channels is consumed by inbound channels whose funding transaction has never been seen, and the only per-adversary limit is keyed on a free-to-mint node identity, so an anonymous party fills the cap at zero cost and denies inbound channel opening to everyone for the 2016-block forget window. Fix criteria: After the fix, an unauthenticated peer must not be able to make the fundee reject inbound channels from unrelated peers by creating unconfirmed, unfunded inbound channels: for example the global cap must exclude non-initiated pending channels whose funding tx has not been observed, or be evaluated per identity/source bucket rather than node-wide, or non-initiated pending channels whose funding tx never appears in the mempool or chain must be forgotten after a short window instead of 2016 blocks, and the cap should be operator-configurable. Verify by creating 51 unfunded inbound pending channels from distinct node keys and confirming that a 52nd honest open_channel is still accepted.

# CheckMacaroonPermissions with empty permission list skips signature and caveat verification

## Details
The `/lnrpc.Lightning/CheckMacaroonPermissions` RPC is lnd's documented macaroon-validity oracle for third-party software (REST: POST /v1/macaroon/checkpermissions). Its proto contract states that when `permissions` is empty, the macaroon is still judged on "issuance authority and caveat validity" (i.e. was it signed by this node's root key, and are its time/IP/custom caveats satisfied) and that an empty list merely means "skip checking permissions".

The implementation does not deliver that. `rpcServer.CheckMacaroonPermissions` (rpcserver.go:8333-8383) forwards an empty `[]bakery.Op` to `macaroons.Service.CheckMacAuth` (service.go:207-254), which does `authChecker.Allow(ctx, requiredPermissions...)` and returns nil on success. In gopkg.in/macaroon-bakery.v2 (pinned v2.0.1) `AuthChecker.allowAny` first runs `init`, which calls `Oven.MacaroonOps`; a bad signature yields a `*VerificationError` that is appended to `initErrors` and *skipped*, not returned. It then iterates over the requested ops; with zero ops `numAuthed == len(ops)` holds trivially and the function returns `nil` before the branch that surfaces `initErrors` or evaluates `checkConditions` (caveats). The second `uri:` fallback `Allow` is never reached because `err == nil`.

Consequently, for an empty permission list, lnd answers `valid: true` for:
- a wholly forged macaroon (any bytes as signature) whose ID is `0x03 || protobuf(MacaroonId{storage_id:"0", ...})` — root key id "0" always exists so `RootKeyStorage.Get` succeeds and the signature failure is swallowed;
- a genuine macaroon that has expired (`time-before`), is locked to a different IP (`ipaddr`/`iprange`), or carries an unsupported custom caveat.

The only prerequisites are that the bytes unmarshal as a V2 macaroon with a Version3 ID prefix (service.go:212-234).

Attack path: an application that authenticates its own users by their lnd macaroon (the use case the proto documents, e.g. a web wallet/dashboard or LiT-style proxy that first asks lnd "is this macaroon genuine and unexpired?" and only later maps permissions) calls this RPC with `permissions=[]`. An attacker with no credential submits a forged or expired macaroon to that application; lnd returns `valid: true`; the application grants the session. lnd's own interceptor is not affected: every entry in the permission tables has at least one op (verified by searching all `*rpc` permission maps), so `checkMacaroon` never calls `Allow` with zero ops.

Assumption stated: behaviour of `gopkg.in/macaroon-bakery.v2 v2.0.1` `AuthChecker.init/allowAny` as described (verification errors deferred to `initErrors`, early nil return when all requested ops are authorized, including the vacuous zero-op case).

## Evidence
1. [macaroons/service.go:236–244](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/macaroons/service.go#L236-L244)
   CheckMacAuth calls authChecker.Allow(ctx, requiredPermissions...) and returns nil immediately when err == nil. With an empty requiredPermissions slice the bakery AuthChecker has zero operations to authorize; its allowAny loop trivially reaches numAuthed == len(ops) and returns nil before consulting the verification errors it collected during init, so neither the HMAC signature chain nor any first-party caveat (time-before, ipaddr, iprange, lnd-custom) is ever evaluated.
2. [rpcserver.go:8333–8382](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L8333-L8382)
   CheckMacaroonPermissions builds permissions from req.Permissions; when the caller sends an empty list and check_default_perms_from_full_method=false the sanity switch does not reject it, and an empty []bakery.Op is passed straight to r.macService.CheckMacAuth. A nil error becomes Valid: true.
3. [lnrpc/lightning.proto:5138–5145](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/lightning.proto#L5138-L5145)
   The documented contract for the permissions field: with an empty list the macaroon 'is considered valid only based on issuance authority and caveat validity' and the empty list is 'equivalent to saying skip checking permissions'. The implementation checks neither issuance authority (signature) nor caveats in this mode, so a relying application using this documented oracle mode is misled.
4. [macaroons/service.go:212–233](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/macaroons/service.go#L212-L233)
   The only checks that do run on the attacker-supplied bytes before Allow(): the macaroon must unmarshal, be version V2, and have an ID whose first byte is bakery.Version3. These are trivially satisfiable by a forger.
5. [macaroons/store.go:244–279](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/macaroons/store.go#L244-L279)
   RootKeyStorage.Get returns a generic fmt.Errorf (not bakery.ErrNotFound) for an unknown root key id, which makes bakery init fail hard; so the forger must embed an existing storage id in the macaroon ID. DefaultRootKeyID '0' always exists, so this is not an obstacle.

## Impact
lnd itself does not grant RPC access based on this oracle (its interceptor always checks at least one op), so the direct effect on lnd is a wrong validation verdict returned by one RPC: an integrity defect in the auth-oracle output, no disclosure or availability impact on lnd. Subsequent-system impact: A relying application that gates logins or sessions on lnd's verdict for the documented empty-permission mode accepts forged, expired or IP-locked-elsewhere macaroons as genuine, giving the forger whatever that application grants an authenticated macaroon holder (typically full read/write access to the wallet UI). Rated high for both confidentiality and integrity of that application's protected resources; no availability effect.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker position: anyone able to present a macaroon to a relying application that uses lnd's documented empty-permission validity mode of CheckMacaroonPermissions (gRPC or REST POST /v1/macaroon/checkpermissions). Delivery: a forged V2 macaroon with ID 0x03||MacaroonId{storage_id:"0", ops:[any one op]} and arbitrary signature, or any genuine macaroon whose time-before/ipaddr/iprange/lnd-custom caveat is unsatisfied. Root key "0" always exists because config_builder.go:534 bakes the admin macaroon with DefaultRootKeyID on every unlock path (stateless or not), so RootKeyStorage.Get succeeds and the signature failure is swallowed. The relying application calls the RPC with its own macaroon:read credential; lnd answers valid:true. Explicit dependency assumption: gopkg.in/macaroon-bakery.v2 v2.0.1 AuthChecker.init appends *VerificationError from Oven.MacaroonOps to initErrors and continues, and allowAny returns nil when numAuthed == len(ops) (vacuously true for zero ops) before any checkConditions call or initErrors surfacing; no in-tree test contradicts this. Requires a relying application to use the documented empty-list mode (AT:PRESENT); the attacker needs no credential at that application (PR:NONE).

## Recommended fix
CheckMacAuth relies on bakery Allow() to verify signature and caveats, but Allow() performs those checks only per requested operation; with zero operations it vacuously succeeds, so 'issuance authority and caveat validity' are never established for the empty-permission mode the RPC documents. Fix criteria: For an empty permission list, CheckMacaroonPermissions must still fail for (a) a macaroon whose signature does not verify under the node's root key for its embedded root key id, and (b) a correctly signed macaroon with any unsatisfied first-party caveat (expired time-before, non-matching ipaddr/iprange, unregistered lnd-custom). Verify by calling the RPC with permissions=[] using a forged macaroon with root key id 0 and with an expired admin macaroon; both must return an error, while a fresh valid macaroon still returns valid:true.

# IP-lock macaroon caveats bypassed via REST/WebSocket proxy using loopback peer address

## Details
lnd lets operators bind a macaroon to a client IP (`ipaddr <ip>`) or CIDR range (`iprange <cidr>`): `lncli bakemacaroon --ip_address`, `lncli --macaroonip`, and the library constraints `macaroons.IPLockConstraint` / `IPRangeLockConstraint` (the `--ip_range` flag is declared in cmd_macaroon.go:33 but is not registered on the bakemacaroon command, lines 95-116, so iprange caveats are produced via the library API or external tooling). The caveats are enforced server-side by `macaroons.IPLockChecker` / `IPRangeLockChecker` (constraints.go:133-186), registered on the production macaroon service (config_builder.go:493-497); both derive the client address solely from `peer.FromContext(ctx)`, i.e. the TCP peer of the gRPC connection carrying the request.

The REST and WebSocket interface (default port 8080) is a grpc-gateway proxy in the same process. `startRestProxy` (lnd.go:948-962) dials the node's own first gRPC listener, rewriting `0.0.0.0`/`[::]` to `127.0.0.1`/`[::1]`; `RegisterWithRestProxy` registers every service against that destination (lnd.go:999-1002, rpcserver.go:972-1015) and the WebSocket proxy forwards into the same mux (lnd.go:1008-1011). Every REST request is therefore re-originated from the node's own address (127.0.0.1 for the default `rpclisten=localhost:10009`, or the configured listener IP), and the interceptor chain (rpcperms/interceptor.go:579-586) runs the IP caveat checkers against that address. lnd never consults grpc-gateway's `x-forwarded-for` metadata (no reference in the tree), and the WebSocket path synthesizes a fresh `http.Request` with no `RemoteAddr`, forwarding only Origin, Referer and Grpc-Metadata-Macaroon (websocket_proxy.go:52-56, 169-181).

Effect: an `ipaddr 127.0.0.1` / `ipaddr ::1` / `iprange 127.0.0.0/8` caveat -- the natural way to make a macaroon 'local only' -- is satisfied for ANY REST/WebSocket client, wherever it connects from; likewise `ipaddr <listener-ip>` or an `iprange` containing the node's own `rpclisten` address. Over gRPC the same macaroon is rejected from a non-matching address (itest/lnd_macaroons_test.go:108-127 asserts 'different IP address'). The two RPC surfaces thus enforce the same caveat inconsistently, and the REST surface -- the one most third-party apps use -- gets no protection from it.

Attack path: an attacker obtains a copy of a node-locally IP-locked macaroon (e.g. an admin macaroon the operator locked to 127.0.0.1 before storing it on a less-trusted host, or that leaked from a backup) and issues `POST https://node:8080/v1/...` with `Grpc-Metadata-Macaroon: <hex>` from any host that can reach the REST listener. The gRPC-side peer is 127.0.0.1, the caveat passes, and the request executes with the macaroon's full permission set.

Conditions: the REST listener must be reachable from the attacker's position (`restlisten` defaults to localhost:8080; sample-lnd.conf:196 documents `restlisten=0.0.0.0:8080` as a supported configuration for remote clients), the macaroon must be locked to loopback or to an address/range that contains the node's own `rpclisten` address, and `rpclisten` must be a TCP address (with a unix-socket `rpclisten` the peer address has no host:port and the checker fails closed). docs/safety.md:139 and macaroons/README.md:87-89 present the IP restriction as a macaroon-theft mitigation with no disclosure that it is not enforced on the REST surface.

## Evidence
1. [macaroons/constraints.go:133–186](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/macaroons/constraints.go#L133-L186)
   IPLockChecker and IPRangeLockChecker derive the client address solely from peer.FromContext(ctx), the TCP peer of the gRPC connection on which the request arrived. For REST/WebSocket traffic that peer is lnd's own in-process gateway, so the caveat is compared against the node's address, not the client's. No forwarded-for metadata is consulted.
2. [lnd.go:948–962](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnd.go#L948-L962)
   The REST proxy's gRPC destination is the node's own first RPC listener, with wildcard addresses rewritten to 127.0.0.1 / [::1]. Every REST request reaches the gRPC server over a loopback (or node-local) TCP connection whose peer address is the proxy, not the HTTP client.
3. [lnd.go:999–1011](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnd.go#L999-L1011)
   All services are registered on the grpc-gateway mux against restProxyDest and the mux is wrapped by the WebSocket proxy; the full interceptor chain, including the ipaddr/iprange caveat checkers, runs on the gRPC side where the peer is the proxy.
4. [lnrpc/websocket\_proxy.go:169–180](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/websocket_proxy.go#L169-L180)
   For WebSocket calls a new http.Request is synthesized with no RemoteAddr, and only Origin, Referer and Grpc-Metadata-Macaroon are forwarded (defaultHeadersToForward, lines 52-56), so even grpc-gateway's x-forwarded-for metadata could not carry the true client address on this path.
5. [config\_builder.go:493–497](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config_builder.go#L493-L497)
   The production macaroon service registers IPLockChecker and IPRangeLockChecker, so the ipaddr/iprange caveats are a shipped, enforced control on the gRPC server that the REST path undermines.
6. [cmd/commands/cmd\_macaroon.go:29–36](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/cmd/commands/cmd_macaroon.go#L29-L36)
   The operator-facing promise: lncli bakemacaroon --ip_address describes the macaroon as 'bound to' an IP address with no qualification that the binding is not enforced for REST clients. (The --ip_range flag is declared here but not registered on the command's Flags at lines 95-116; iprange caveats come from the library constraint instead.)

## Impact
The bypass yields the full permission set of the locked macaroon from a network position the caveat was meant to exclude. IP locking is typically applied to admin macaroons to limit the damage of theft; with the lock defeated a stolen admin macaroon lets the attacker read all wallet/channel data, move funds (SendCoins, SendPayment, CloseChannel) and stop the daemon. Impact is bounded by the macaroon's own permissions, so the worst realistic case is rated.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds a copy of a macaroon whose ipaddr/iprange caveat names loopback or an address/range containing the node's own rpclisten address (a leaked 'local-only' admin or custom macaroon). They send ordinary REST or WebSocket requests to the node's 8080 listener from any host that can reach it; the proxy re-dials gRPC from the node's own address, the checker compares the caveat against that address and accepts. No defence to evade and no user interaction. Attack requirements: the REST listener must be reachable from the attacker's position and the caveat must name a node-local address (AT:PRESENT). Possession of the restricted credential is modelled as low privilege (PR:LOW).

## Recommended fix
1. The ipaddr/iprange checkers identify the caller by the gRPC transport peer, but for REST/WebSocket traffic that peer is lnd's own in-process proxy, so the caveat is compared against the node's address instead of the client's. Fix criteria: An IP-locked macaroon presented over REST or WebSocket must be evaluated against the real HTTP client's address, established only from a source the gateway controls (never from a client-supplied header), or the proxied path must reject IP-locked macaroons outright when that address cannot be established. Verify: bake an admin macaroon with ipaddr 127.0.0.1, call GET /v1/getinfo on an exposed REST listener from a non-loopback host -- must fail; the same call from loopback must succeed; gRPC behaviour unchanged. The WebSocket path must not lose the client address when synthesizing the forwarded request.
2. Operator documentation and lncli help present --ip_address/--macaroonip as binding the macaroon to a client address without disclosing that the binding is not enforced for the REST surface, so operators rely on an ineffective control. Fix criteria: Until enforcement is fixed, bakemacaroon help text, macaroons/README.md and docs/safety.md state that IP caveats are only enforced for direct gRPC connections, so a correct deployment does not depend on them for REST clients.

# Interceptor ExpiryTooSoon failure leaks private alias channel's real SCID in channel_update

## Details
lnd's option_scid_alias support exists so that a private channel's confirmed short channel ID (which identifies its on-chain funding UTXO) is never disclosed to third parties: invoice route hints carry only the alias (lnrpc/invoicesrpc/addinvoice.go:900-910), and both Switch.failAliasUpdate and link.createFailureWithUpdate substitute an alias before embedding a channel_update in a BOLT 4 failure for an incoming alias channel.

The InterceptableSwitch sits in front of the Switch for every forwarded HTLC (peer/brontide.go:1580 wires link.ForwardPackets to InterceptSwitch.ForwardPackets; the run loop passes every packet through interceptForward). In interceptForward, handleExpired is called for every forwarded UpdateAddHTLC before and regardless of whether an HtlcInterceptor RPC client is connected or RequireInterceptor is enabled. If the incoming HTLC's cltv_expiry is below currentHeight + cltvInterceptDelta (lncfg.DefaultCltvInterceptDelta = 22), handleExpired fails the HTLC with FailWithCode(lnwire.CodeExpiryTooSoon).

The CodeExpiryTooSoon branch of interceptedForward.FailWithCode (htlcswitch/interceptable_switch.go:949-956) calls f.htlcSwitch.cfg.FetchLastChannelUpdate(f.packet.incomingChanID) directly and embeds the result in FailExpiryTooSoon. incomingChanID is the incoming link's ShortChanID() (link.go:3268), i.e. channeldb.OpenChannel.ShortChannelID: for a non-zero-conf option_scid_alias channel that is the confirmed SCID (and for a zero-conf channel it becomes the confirmed SCID after confirmation). The private channel's graph edge is stored under that same confirmed SCID (funding/manager.go handleChannelReadyReceived -> addToGraph), so the lookup succeeds and netann.UnsignedChannelUpdateFromEdge returns our signed update with ShortChannelID = the real SCID. The adjacent CodeTemporaryChannelFailure branch (lines 932-947) correctly calls failAliasUpdate(incomingChanID, true) first; the ExpiryTooSoon branch does not. The failure is encrypted with EncryptFirstHop for the payment origin and relayed back.

Attack: an attacker who knows an alias of one of our private scid-alias channels with peer P (any payer receives it in a route hint of an invoice we issue) builds an onion ... -> P -> us (via the alias) -> one of our public channels -> ..., and chooses CLTVs so that our incoming expiry is in (height+3, height+22). P forwards normally (an lnd P's only lower bound on the outgoing expiry is canSendHtlc's heightNow+DefaultOutgoingCltvRejectDelta=3, link.go:2629). Our interceptable switch deterministically fails the HTLC with ExpiryTooSoon containing our signed channel_update for the real SCID, which the attacker decrypts as the payment origin. The attacker learns the funding outpoint of the private channel, defeating the feature's purpose (channel/UTXO deanonymisation, linking on-chain funds to our node and to P). Had the packet reached the regular Switch, the outgoing link's CheckHtlcForward/canSendHtlc would have failed it with the public outgoing channel's update, or any incoming-side failure would have gone through createFailureWithUpdate -> FailAliasUpdate; the interceptor path runs first and short-circuits both.

Conditions: the node has option_scid_alias enabled (protocol.option-scid-alias, off by default per sample-lnd.conf) and at least one private channel negotiated with that feature (or a confirmed zero-conf channel). No HtlcInterceptor needs to be registered; this is default forwarding behaviour of every release node with such a channel.

## Evidence
1. [htlcswitch/interceptable\_switch.go:949–956](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/interceptable_switch.go#L949-L956)
   FailWithCode(CodeExpiryTooSoon) calls f.htlcSwitch.cfg.FetchLastChannelUpdate(f.packet.incomingChanID) directly and embeds the result unmodified in lnwire.NewExpiryTooSoon. Unlike the CodeTemporaryChannelFailure branch immediately above (lines 932-947) it never calls htlcSwitch.failAliasUpdate(incomingChanID, true), so for an incoming option_scid_alias channel whose link SCID is the confirmed one, the embedded channel_update.short_channel_id is the real funding SCID. The failure is then EncryptFirstHop-encrypted for the payment origin.
2. [htlcswitch/interceptable\_switch.go:743–789](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/interceptable_switch.go#L743-L789)
   handleExpired fails every forwarded add whose incomingTimeout < currentHeight + cltvInterceptDelta (server.go:931 sets lncfg.DefaultCltvInterceptDelta = 22) with FailWithCode(CodeExpiryTooSoon). The incoming expiry is a field of the sender's UpdateAddHTLC, chosen by the upstream payer.
3. [htlcswitch/interceptable\_switch.go:587–629](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/interceptable_switch.go#L587-L629)
   interceptForward calls handleExpired for every non-local UpdateAddHTLC before any check of whether an HtlcInterceptor client is registered or requireInterceptor is set (forwardOffChain, where those checks live, runs only after handleExpired returns not-handled). The run loop (lines ~300-330) dispatches every packet from ForwardPackets through interceptForward and only forwards the non-intercepted ones to the real Switch, so this path pre-empts the Switch/link checks on every default-configured node.
4. [peer/brontide.go:1580](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L1580)
   Every channel link's ForwardPackets is wired to InterceptSwitch.ForwardPackets, so all forwarded adds pass through interceptForward before reaching the Switch.
5. [htlcswitch/link.go:3268](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L3268)
   The forwarded htlcPacket's incomingChanID is l.ShortChanID() = channeldb.OpenChannel.ShortChannelID, which for a non-zero-conf option_scid_alias channel is the confirmed SCID from funding confirmation (funding/manager.go handleFundingConfirmation -> handleChannelReadyReceived -> addToGraph with the same confirmed scid), and for a zero-conf channel becomes the confirmed SCID once confirmed.
6. [htlcswitch/switch.go:2770–2899](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/switch.go#L2770-L2899)
   failAliasUpdate is the shipped control for incoming failures on alias channels; its comment states the incoming case must replace the real SCID with an alias 'to ensure no privacy leak occurs... if a private non-zero-conf option-scid-alias feature-bit channel leaked its UTXO here rather than supplying an alias'. The interceptor's ExpiryTooSoon path bypasses it.
7. [htlcswitch/link.go:885–906](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L885-L906)
   Sibling implementation: the link's createFailureWithUpdate always routes channel_update construction through FailAliasUpdate first, demonstrating the intended protection the interceptor path omits.
8. [server.go:5436–5449](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L5436-L5449)
   FetchLastChannelUpdate looks the channel up in the local graph by SCID (graph/builder.go GetChannelByID -> FetchChannelEdgesByID) and returns our signed ChannelUpdate1; netann.ExtractChannelUpdate / UnsignedChannelUpdateFromEdge (netann/channel_update.go:143) sets ShortChannelID from policy.ChannelID, i.e. the confirmed SCID under which the private channel's edge is stored.
9. [lncfg/config.go:32–75](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lncfg/config.go#L32-L75)
   Defines the window: DefaultIncomingBroadcastDelta=16, DefaultFinalCltvRejectDelta=19, DefaultCltvInterceptDelta=22 (used by the interceptable switch), while DefaultOutgoingCltvRejectDelta=3 is the only lower bound an lnd upstream peer applies to the expiry it offers us (htlcswitch/link.go:2629 canSendHtlc). Any incoming expiry in (height+3, height+22) is forwarded by the peer and failed by us with ExpiryTooSoon.
10. [lnrpc/invoicesrpc/addinvoice.go:900–910](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/invoicesrpc/addinvoice.go#L900-L910)
   For private option_scid_alias channels, invoice route hints carry the peer alias in place of the real SCID: this is how the project discloses the alias to arbitrary payers while deliberately withholding the confirmed SCID, and it is what lets a third party route an HTLC into the channel via the peer.

## Impact
Discloses the confirmed SCID (block height / tx index / output index = funding UTXO) of a private option_scid_alias channel, the single datum the feature exists to hide: on-chain funds become linkable to the node and its peer, and the channel's capacity and both endpoints are deanonymised. Limited to one channel's identifier per probe; no integrity or availability impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is any remote payer who holds an alias for one of our private scid-alias channels (invoice route hints disclose exactly that). They craft a multi-hop payment via the channel peer P into our node with an incoming CLTV between height+4 and height+21 (P's canSendHtlc only rejects <= height+3; our handleExpired fails < height+22). Our node deterministically fails it via the interceptable switch's handleExpired -> FailWithCode(ExpiryTooSoon) and returns our signed channel_update carrying the confirmed SCID, decryptable only by the attacker as the payment origin. Requires only that the node runs with option_scid_alias and has such a private channel; no RPC access, no registered interceptor, no user interaction, no race.

## Recommended fix
interceptedForward.FailWithCode builds the ExpiryTooSoon channel_update from FetchLastChannelUpdate(incomingChanID) without the alias substitution that Switch.failAliasUpdate(scid, true) performs for incoming failures, so the confirmed SCID of a private option_scid_alias channel is embedded in a failure returned to the payment origin. Fix criteria: Every channel_update embedded in a failure generated for an incoming option_scid_alias channel by the interceptable switch (ExpiryTooSoon included, and any future code in FailWithCode) must carry an alias rather than the confirmed SCID, i.e. go through the same alias-aware construction as the TemporaryChannelFailure branch and link.createFailureWithUpdate, with FetchLastChannelUpdate used only as the fallback when failAliasUpdate returns nil for a non-alias channel. Verify by forwarding an HTLC with an incoming expiry below height+CltvInterceptDelta over a private scid-alias channel and decrypting the returned ExpiryTooSoon: its channel_update.short_channel_id must be an alias.
