# RBF coop-close ErrorReporter forwards raw wallet/signer/DB error text to the channel counterparty

## Details
The RBF cooperative-close state machine (protofsm) hands every transition error, unmodified, to `chanErrorReporter.ReportError` (protofsm/state_machine.go:698 -> peer/brontide.go:4151). `ReportError` replaces only `ErrInvalidStateTransition` with a fixed string; every other error is sent to the counterparty verbatim as `lnwire.Error.Data` (`errMsg = []byte(chanErr.Error())`, brontide.go:4155-4165), and `lnwire.Error.Encode` writes `Data` as-is.

The transitions in lnwallet/chancloser/rbf_coop_transitions.go return or `%w`-wrap internal subsystem errors without classifying them: `env.NewDeliveryScript` -> `Brontide.genDeliveryScript` -> btcwallet `NewAddress` (rbf_coop_transitions.go:255-260, :320-325; brontide.go:3287-3306, wired at :4340-4342); `ChanObserver.DisableChannel`/`MarkShutdownSent` (:105-130, chan status manager and channeldb kvdb writes); `MarkCoopBroadcasted` (:1613-1616, :2113-2116, channeldb write); and `CloseSigner.CreateCloseProposal`/`CompleteCooperativeClose` (:1202-1209, :1594-1601, :1686-1692 via `createLocalCloseeSignature`, :2066-2084), which for non-taproot channels calls `Signer.SignOutputRaw` (lnwallet/channel.go:8805) and for taproot channels `MuSig2Sign`. In a remote-signing deployment (docs/remote-signing.md) those are `RPCKeyRing.SignOutputRaw` -> `remoteSign` -> `walletClient.SignPsbt` (rpcwallet.go:1228-1234, `error signing PSBT in remote signer instance: %v`) and `MuSig2Sign` (rpcwallet.go:887-891); `considerShutdown` only logs, so the wrapped gRPC status text propagates to the peer. Assumption (grpc v1.83.1): a fail-fast RPC against a ClientConn in TRANSIENT_FAILURE fails with `codes.Unavailable` whose description embeds the transport dial error (`dial tcp <signer host:port>: connect: ...` or `lookup <hostname>: ...`), so the signer's internal address/hostname is what reaches the counterparty. Channel-DB backend errors (bbolt/sqlite/postgres/etcd text) and wallet address-manager errors are disclosed the same way.

The counterparty controls when these subsystems are exercised: a `shutdown` makes the victim call `NewAddress`, `RequestDisable` and `MarkShutdownSent` (ShutdownReceived :307-335); a `closing_complete` makes it sign via the signer and write the DB (RemoteCloseStart :2066-2116); after an error `ReportError` re-initialises the FSM (brontide.go:4176-4196), so the attempt can be repeated, and RBF rounds let further `closing_complete` messages re-exercise the signer. The counterparty cannot induce the wallet, signer or DB fault itself; it obtains the text whenever such a fault exists when it sends the message (e.g. a remote-signer outage, which it can also detect from stalled commitment signing). The legacy close path deliberately replaces exactly these failures with fixed strings (`close addr unavailable`, `unable to estimate fee`, brontide.go:3509-3528), so the RBF path diverges from the maintainers' own policy. Reachable only when the victim has enabled `protocol.rbf-coop-close` (default false, sample-lnd.conf:1472) or `protocol.simple-taproot-chans`, which force-enables it (server.go:733-736), and the peer negotiated the feature (brontide.go:1139-1140). Impact is limited information exposure (internal infrastructure addresses, backend type, fault state) to a channel counterparty. Resolves lead lead-brontide-4109-2c03.

## Evidence
1. [peer/brontide.go:4151–4170](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L4151-L4170)
   ReportError sanitises only ErrInvalidStateTransition; every other FSM error is sent verbatim to the counterparty as lnwire.Error.Data (errMsg = []byte(chanErr.Error())) via SendMessageLazy. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [protofsm/state\_machine.go:698](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/protofsm/state_machine.go#L698)
   The state-machine driver passes the raw applyEvents error straight to cfg.ErrorReporter.ReportError, so every transition error text reaches the reporter unfiltered.
3. [lnwallet/chancloser/rbf\_coop\_transitions.go:318–325](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/rbf_coop_transitions.go#L318-L325)
   ShutdownReceived (remote shutdown): env.NewDeliveryScript (wallet NewAddress) failure is returned unwrapped and reaches the peer; SendShutdown does the same at :255-260.
4. [lnwallet/chancloser/rbf\_coop\_transitions.go:1686–1692](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/rbf_coop_transitions.go#L1686-L1692)
   createLocalCloseeSignature wraps CreateCloseProposal (signer) errors with %w; RemoteCloseStart calls it on a remote closing_complete (:2066-2073) and wraps again, so signer error text propagates to ReportError. Same pattern at :1202-1209 (LocalCloseStart) and :1594-1601, :2076-2084 (CompleteCooperativeClose).
5. [lnwallet/chancloser/rbf\_coop\_transitions.go:105–130](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/rbf_coop_transitions.go#L105-L130)
   sendShutdownEvents wraps ChanObserver.DisableChannel (chan status manager) and MarkShutdownSent (channeldb write) errors with %w; MarkCoopBroadcasted errors are returned raw at :1613-1616 and :2113-2116, so DB backend error text is forwarded.
6. [peer/brontide.go:3287–3305](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L3287-L3305)
   genDeliveryScript returns the btcwallet NewAddress error unmodified; it is wired as env.NewDeliveryScript for the RBF closer at :4340-4342, so wallet-internal error strings become the FSM error.
7. [lnwallet/rpcwallet/rpcwallet.go:1228–1233](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/rpcwallet/rpcwallet.go#L1228-L1233)
   remoteSign (reached from SignOutputRaw :605-611, which lnwallet CreateCloseProposal calls at channel.go:8805) embeds the gRPC error with %v after considerShutdown merely logs; MuSig2Sign does the same at :887-891 for taproot channels. When the signer is unreachable the Unavailable status text carries the transport dial error with the signer's host:port (grpc v1.83.1 behaviour, assumed).
8. [peer/brontide.go:3509–3528](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L3509-L3528)
   Contrast: the legacy createChanCloser path logs the wallet/fee-estimator error locally and returns fixed strings ('close addr unavailable', 'unable to estimate fee') to the peer, showing the sanitisation policy the RBF path does not follow.

## Impact
Confidentiality LOW: internal error strings are disclosed to an untrusted channel counterparty - in remote-signing deployments the signer's dial address/hostname and connection state, otherwise channel-DB backend type and failure text and wallet address-manager state. No key material, balances beyond what the peer already knows, or preimages are exposed. No integrity or availability impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A channel counterparty whose peer negotiated RBF coop close (victim opted in via protocol.rbf-coop-close or simple-taproot-chans: AT:P) sends shutdown or closing_complete over the authenticated-but-unauthorised P2P link (PR:N, UI:N, AV:N). Each message makes the victim exercise its wallet, chan-status/DB and signer; any failure's raw text is returned in lnwire.Error, and the FSM is re-initialised so the attempt can be repeated. The attacker cannot cause the wallet/signer/DB fault; it must coincide with an existing fault (AT:P), which it can time (e.g. a stalled signer observable from commitment signing). No security control has to be evaded (AC:L).

## Recommended fix
chanErrorReporter.ReportError forwards arbitrary FSM error text to the peer, and the RBF transitions wrap wallet, chan-status, DB and signer errors with %w or return them raw without classifying them as internal. Fix criteria: A remote peer never receives wallet, signer, RPC/gRPC or database error strings: only protocol-level errors (invalid shutdown script, upfront-shutdown mismatch, thaw height, cannot pay fee, bad signature/nonce, invalid state transition) are echoed, each with fixed wording, and every other error is logged locally and replaced by a generic message, mirroring the legacy close path's 'close addr unavailable' handling.

# Legacy taproot coop-close responder accepts arbitrary fee, persists unbroadcastable close tx before publish

## Details
For simple-taproot channels closed through the legacy closing_signed negotiation (the default: protocol.rbf-coop-close is off, and the remote can decline the RBF feature bit anyway), the non-initiator deliberately accepts the initiator's first fee offer because of musig2 nonce constraints (`case isTaproot && !isInitiator`, lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:928-943). `msg.FeeSatoshis` flows verbatim into `proposeCloseSigned` and `CompleteCooperativeClose`; the v0 path's `calcCompromiseFee`/`feeInAcceptableRange`/`maxFee` controls are never consulted.

The wire decoder casts the uint64 fee to the signed `btcutil.Amount` (lnwire/lnwire.go:532-538, read at closing_signed.go:72), so a remote initiator can deliver a negative fee. `CoopCloseBalance` (lnwallet/commitment.go:1089-1104) subtracts it from the remote (payer) balance, inflating the remote output; only negative balances are rejected. `CreateCloseProposal`/`CompleteCooperativeClose` (lnwallet/channel.go:8783-8789 and its twin check) apply only `blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity`, which never compares outputs with the funding input. The node therefore produces a partial signature over a consensus-invalid (outputs > input) close, combines it with the attacker's matching partial signature, and at chancloser.go:1076-1082 `MarkCoopBroadcasted` durably sets `ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted` and stores the tx before `BroadcastTx` at :1097. `BtcWallet.PublishTransaction` (lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go:1316-1397) runs TestMempoolAccept, which rejects the tx, and the error is returned; a positive fee below the min relay fee ends identically (mapped to ErrMempoolFee).

`negotiateCloseErrHandler` (peer/brontide.go:5582-5603) resets the in-memory channel, deletes the closer and disconnects, but nothing reverts the persisted status. On every reconnect `loadActiveChannels` (brontide.go:1294-1335) withholds the channel from the switch and `restartCoopClose` (:3733-3749) returns without re-driving negotiation because a close tx exists and RBF is not allowed; the chain arbitrator re-publishes the invalid tx and only logs the failure (contractcourt/chain_arbitrator.go:880-947, 1406); `PendingChannels` reports the bogus txid as waiting-close; RPC `CloseChannel` without force is refused because the link is not in the switch (rpcserver.go:2905-2920). The only exit is a local force close (lnwallet `ForceClose` guards only LocalDataLoss). Funds are not stolen (the local output is unchanged), but one message converts a cooperative close into a permanent bogus waiting-close that the victim must resolve unilaterally. This is the legacy sibling of the verified rbf-closee-unvalidated-remote-fee-locktime; the persist-before-publish ordering is the one the 0.21.3 notes patched for the 'no tx yet' case.

## Evidence
1. [lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:920–943](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go#L920-L943)
   ReceiveClosingSigned, case isTaproot && !isInitiator: the remote initiator's FeeSatoshis is accepted verbatim ('accept the very first offer') and signed via proposeCloseSigned with no sign, range or relay-fee check; the calcCompromiseFee/maxFee logic of the v0 branch is never reached.
2. [lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:1067–1099](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go#L1067-L1099)
   The fully signed tx is built with the remote fee; MarkCoopBroadcasted persists ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted plus the tx (:1076-1082) BEFORE BroadcastTx (:1097); a broadcast failure returns an error but the persisted status stays.
3. [lnwire/lnwire.go:532–537](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/lnwire.go#L532-L537)
   FeeSatoshis is decoded by casting uint64 to int64 (btcutil.Amount), so a negative fee is representable off the wire.
4. [lnwallet/commitment.go:1089–1103](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/commitment.go#L1089-L1103)
   CoopCloseBalance subtracts the (negative) fee from the remote payer's balance, inflating their output; only negative balances are rejected, so outputs can exceed the funding input.
5. [lnwallet/channel.go:8783–8788](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L8783-L8788)
   Only blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity is applied to the proposed close; there is no inputs-vs-outputs check, so the consensus-invalid tx is partially signed (CompleteCooperativeClose repeats the same check).
6. [peer/brontide.go:5582–5603](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L5582-L5603)
   negotiateCloseErrHandler handles the BroadcastTx failure by resetting the in-memory channel, deleting the closer and disconnecting; nothing undoes the persisted ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted.
7. [peer/brontide.go:3733–3749](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L3733-L3749)
   restartCoopClose: on every reconnect a non-RBF channel with a stored close tx is treated as 'all we can do is wait for it to confirm', so the channel is never re-negotiated.
8. [lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go:1316–1397](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go#L1316-L1397)
   PublishTransaction runs TestMempoolAccept and returns the mapped rejection (consensus failure or ErrMempoolFee) as an error, so the persisted-but-unbroadcast state is the deterministic outcome.
9. [rpcserver.go:2905–2920](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L2905-L2920)
   CloseChannel without force is refused when the link is absent from the switch and no RBF closer exists, so the operator's only remaining exit is a force close.

## Impact
No confidentiality impact. Integrity LOW: the node signs a consensus-invalid close and channel.db durably records it as the cooperative close; the local output amount is unchanged so no funds move. Availability LOW: the channel is parked permanently in waiting-close with a bogus txid, never re-negotiated by the legacy restart logic, not coop-closable via RPC, and must be force-closed by the operator (CSV delay on the victim's funds, sweep fees); force close itself remains possible. Scope is one channel per attacker-funded taproot channel.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the funding initiator of a simple-taproot channel with the victim, which requires the victim to have opted in with --protocol.simple-taproot-chans (default off, AT:P). Legacy close is the default path (rbf-coop-close off) and the attacker can decline the RBF bit regardless. It sends shutdown with its nonce, receives the victim's shutdown, then one closing_signed carrying fee_satoshis >= 2^63 (negative) or a sub-relay fee plus a valid musig2 partial signature over the resulting tx. The victim deterministically co-signs, persists ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted and fails broadcast. No credentials, no user interaction, no defense to defeat.

## Recommended fix
1. The taproot responder path accepts the initiator's fee without any validation of sign or minimum. Fix criteria: Before signing in the isTaproot && !isInitiator branch, reject fees that are negative, zero or below the minimum relay fee for the transaction weight (and optionally above a sanity maximum); such closing_signed messages must result in a protocol error with no signature and no persisted state.
2. CoopCloseBalance treats a negative fee as a credit and the close-tx builders never compare outputs against the funding input. Fix criteria: Reject negative coop close fees in CoopCloseBalance and verify sum(outputs)+fee equals the funding output value in CreateCloseProposal/CompleteCooperativeClose so no over-spending close tx can be signed.
3. ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted and the close tx are persisted before the broadcast is attempted, and a broadcast failure does not revert it; restartCoopClose then treats the channel as permanently closing. Fix criteria: A broadcast rejection of a freshly agreed close must not leave the channel in a state where legacy restart logic refuses to re-drive negotiation: either persist only after a successful (or at least mempool-accepted) publish, or clear/mark the status on failure so the channel can be re-negotiated or at least clearly reported as failed.

# EstimateRouteFee probe goroutine sends on closed channel: unrecovered panic crashes lnd

## Details
`Server.sendProbePayment` (lnrpc/routerrpc/router_server.go:975-1038), reached from `EstimateRouteFee` whenever a `payment_request` is supplied, runs `SendPaymentV2` in a bare helper goroutine against an in-memory `probePaymentStream` whose ctx is the RPC request context, while the handler goroutine consumes payment updates from the stream. Two lifetime bugs exist between the two goroutines.

1. **Send on closed channel -> unrecovered panic -> lnd exits.** The handler does `defer close(errChan)` (line 980) and returns as soon as it receives a terminal `Payment` (FAILED/SUCCEEDED). The producer goroutine is still inside `trackPaymentStream` at that moment. When the request carries a client deadline (gRPC `grpc-timeout`, or REST `Grpc-Timeout` forwarded by the gateway) that fires in the window between the producer taking the terminal update off `Updates()` and its next `select` (the control tower closes the subscriber queue right after the terminal event, routing/control_tower.go:412-426, so `Updates()` and `ctx.Done()` are both ready and Go's `select` picks pseudo-randomly), `trackPaymentStream` returns `context.DeadlineExceeded`, which `trackPayment` does not swallow (only `context.Canceled` is mapped to nil, lines 1565-1569). `SendPaymentV2` therefore returns an error and the goroutine executes `select { case errChan <- err: ... case <-ctx.Done(): }` with `errChan` already closed; a send case on a closed channel is eligible in `select` and panics when chosen. The panic is raised in a `go func()` that the gRPC panic-recovery interceptor (rpcperms/interceptor.go:683-700) does not cover, so the Go runtime terminates the whole `lnd` process. The window is narrow (microseconds around the terminal update, times the random select outcomes), but the caller controls both the deadline (sub-millisecond granularity) and the probe's completion time: a `payment_request` for a pubkey absent from the graph fails locally with NO_ROUTE within milliseconds, costs nothing, and can be repeated at an arbitrary rate with deadlines swept around the measured completion latency until the race is won. Note: if the deadline fires *before* the terminal update, the producer wakes on `ctx.Done()` while `errChan` is still open, so that case cannot panic (it either returns the error to the handler or leaks it, see 2).

2. **Permanent handler goroutine leak (deterministic on cancel).** If the client cancels or disconnects while the probe is in flight, `trackPaymentStream` returns `context.Canceled`, `trackPayment` maps it to nil, `SendPaymentV2` returns nil, and the producer exits *without* writing to `errChan`. The handler loop selects only on the stream, `errChan` and `s.quit` (never `ctx.Done()`), so it blocks forever: one leaked handler goroutine (plus its gRPC handler slot) per cancelled call, unbounded. The same leak happens with probability ~1/2 when a deadline fires mid-probe and the producer's final `select` chooses `ctx.Done()` over the send. The probe payment itself keeps running under `context.Background()` because probe requests leave `Cancelable` unset (router_server.go:400-406; router.proto documents that cancelling the call does not cancel the payment loop).

Attacker: any RPC client holding a macaroon with `offchain:read` (readonly.macaroon; dashboards, monitoring agents). Input: an `EstimateRouteFee` request with a `payment_request` (any invoice, including one for a non-existent node) plus a client deadline, or a cancelled call. Impact: whole-node crash (channels offline, HTLC timeouts and breach remedies unmonitored until an operator restarts) and unbounded goroutine growth, from a read-only credential.

Dependency assumptions (not verifiable in this checkout): grpc-go v1.83.1 derives the handler ctx from the client's `grpc-timeout` via `context.WithTimeout` (so `ctx.Err()` is `DeadlineExceeded` when the timer fires first) and cancels the stream ctx with `Canceled` once the handler returns (which is why the panic path needs the deadline to fire first); grpc-gateway v2.16.0 forwards the REST `Grpc-Timeout` header as the gRPC deadline and cancels on HTTP client disconnect.

## Evidence
1. [lnrpc/routerrpc/router\_server.go:975–1037](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/routerrpc/router_server.go#L975-L1037)
   sendProbePayment: `defer close(errChan)` (980) runs as soon as the handler returns on a terminal Payment (1003-1032) while the producer goroutine (986-996) is still inside SendPaymentV2 and may still execute `errChan <- err`; the receive loop (998-1037) never selects on ctx.Done(), so a producer that exits without sending leaves the handler parked forever.
2. [lnrpc/routerrpc/router\_server.go:1611–1663](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/routerrpc/router_server.go#L1611-L1663)
   trackPaymentStream returns context.Err() from `case <-context.Done()`. After the terminal update has been handed to the handler, the next iteration has Updates() (closed by the control tower) and an expired ctx both ready; choosing ctx yields context.DeadlineExceeded.
3. [lnrpc/routerrpc/router\_server.go:1556–1580](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/routerrpc/router_server.go#L1556-L1580)
   trackPayment maps only context.Canceled to nil. DeadlineExceeded is returned as a real error (panic path: the producer then sends on the closed errChan); Canceled becomes nil (leak path: the producer exits without signalling and the handler never returns).
4. [lnrpc/routerrpc/router\_server.go:954–962](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/routerrpc/router_server.go#L954-L962)
   probePaymentStream.Send races delivery to the handler against ctx.Done(); with an expired deadline both are ready and select picks pseudo-randomly, so the terminal update can still reach the handler after the deadline has passed.
5. [lnrpc/routerrpc/router\_server.go:400–406](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/routerrpc/router_server.go#L400-L406)
   Probe requests never set Cancelable, so the payment lifecycle runs under context.Background(); a client cancel or deadline affects only the RPC-side ctx, which is why the leaked handler is permanent and the probe keeps running.
6. [routing/control\_tower.go:412–425](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/control_tower.go#L412-L425)
   After delivering a terminal event the control tower closes the subscriber's queue input, so Updates() closes within microseconds of the terminal update. This bounds the panic window (the deadline must fire in that window) but does not prevent it; it is why the race is narrow rather than the ~1/8 the original record claimed for any early deadline.
7. [lnrpc/routerrpc/router\_server.go:107–109](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/routerrpc/router_server.go#L107-L109)
   EstimateRouteFee requires only offchain:read.
8. [rpcserver.go:105–113](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L105-L113)
   readPermissions includes offchain:read; lnd.go:859 bakes readonly.macaroon from readPermissions, so the lowest-privilege standard macaroon reaches this code.
9. [rpcperms/interceptor.go:683–699](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcperms/interceptor.go#L683-L699)
   The panic-recovery interceptor recovers only panics raised synchronously in the handler goroutine. The producer runs in a separate `go func()`, so its panic is unrecovered and terminates the lnd process.

## Impact
An unrecovered panic in a non-handler goroutine terminates the entire lnd process: all channels go offline and HTLC timeouts and breach remedies are unmonitored until an operator restarts the node. The deterministic handler leak additionally lets a read-only caller grow goroutines and gRPC handler slots without bound. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker holds any macaroon with offchain:read (e.g. readonly.macaroon) and can reach the gRPC (10009) or REST (8080) listener. For the crash they send EstimateRouteFee with a payment_request and a client deadline tuned to the probe's completion time; a payment_request for a pubkey absent from the graph completes locally with NO_ROUTE in milliseconds at no cost, so attempts can be repeated at an unlimited rate with deadlines swept around the observed latency. Each attempt wins only if the deadline fires in the microsecond window around the terminal update and the pseudo-random selects fall the wrong way, so this is a race that must be won (AT:P) but needs no special conditions beyond that (AC:L). The handler leak needs no race: every cancelled in-flight call leaks one handler goroutine deterministically.

## Recommended fix
1. errChan is closed by the handler while the producer goroutine may still send on it; the producer selects between the send and ctx.Done() with no guarantee the channel is still open, so a late error (DeadlineExceeded, server shutdown) panics the process. Fix criteria: The producer goroutine must never be able to send on a closed channel: either never close errChan (let it be garbage collected), or guarantee by synchronisation that the handler waits for the producer to finish before closing. Verify that EstimateRouteFee with an already-expired deadline, repeated many times, never terminates the process.
2. The handler's receive loop does not observe the request context, and the producer may exit (on context.Canceled) without signalling, so the handler goroutine blocks forever after a client cancellation. Fix criteria: sendProbePayment must return promptly whenever the request context is done or the producer goroutine has exited, regardless of whether an error was produced. Verify that cancelling or disconnecting an in-flight EstimateRouteFee call does not leave a blocked handler goroutine behind.

# RBF coop-close closee signs and persists remote close tx with unvalidated fee and locktime

## Details
In the RBF cooperative-close flow (negotiated when --protocol.rbf-coop-close is set, or implied by --protocol.simple-taproot-chans, server.go:732-735; default off, sample-lnd.conf:1472), when the counterparty acts as closer it sends `closing_complete` carrying `fee_satoshis` and `locktime`. The closee side (`RemoteCloseStart.ProcessEvent`, lnwallet/chancloser/rbf_coop_transitions.go:1997-2152) validates the fee solely with `RemoteCanPayFees` (`RemoteBalance >= fee`, rbf_coop_states.go:729) and copies `locktime` into the transaction unchecked via `WithCustomLockTime` (:2016). lnd's own closer sets locktime to the current block height (:1274), but the closee never checks the remote's value.

`lnwire` decodes the protocol's unsigned `fee_satoshis` as `btcutil.Amount(int64(uint64))` (lnwire/lnwire.go:537), so a wire value >= 2^63 — which in protocol terms is a fee larger than any balance and must be rejected — becomes a negative fee that passes `RemoteCanPayFees`. `CoopCloseBalance` (lnwallet/commitment.go:1089-1104) then subtracts the negative fee from the remote's output, inflating it, and only rejects negative balances. `CreateCloseProposal`/`CompleteCooperativeClose` (lnwallet/channel.go:8783-8789, 8905) run only `blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity` (per-output and total <= MaxSatoshi; no inputs-vs-outputs check) and the script engine (signature validity only). The node therefore signs a transaction whose outputs exceed the funding input, verifies the remote's valid signature over that same tx, persists it as the channel's cooperative close with `ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted` (`MarkCoopBroadcasted`, :2113; channeldb/channel.go:2195-2201), replies with `closing_sig`, and emits `BroadcastTxn`; the mempool rejects it but protofsm only logs the failure (protofsm/state_machine.go:474-479) and the FSM advances to `ClosePending(Remote)`. A fee of 0/1 sat (below min relay fee) or an arbitrary far-future `locktime` (e.g. 0xFFFFFFFF) yields the same outcome with a non-relayable or non-final transaction.

What the counterparty gains beyond simply stalling the close: the channel DB durably records a consensus-invalid (or unrelayable/non-final) transaction as the broadcast cooperative close; `PendingChannels` reports a waiting-close with that bogus txid (rpcserver.go:4339); the `CloseChannel` stream reports `ClosePending` with it (peer/brontide.go:4019ff, rpcserver.go:3213), telling the operator a close is in flight when nothing can confirm; and `ChainArbitrator.rebroadcast` re-publishes and fails on every restart (contractcourt/chain_arbitrator.go:896-956). Funds are not at risk: only the remote's own output is inflated, and force close remains available (rpcserver.go:2833 is gated only by Restored/LocalDataLoss status). The defect is that lnd signs and durably records a counterparty-supplied closing transaction without checking that it is consensus-valid, relayable, or final. Ledger lead lead-rbf-coop-transitions-1997-bc27 is resolved by this record; the legacy taproot-responder sibling is filed separately (legacy-taproot-responder-accepts-arbitrary-fee-persists-close).

## Evidence
1. [lnwallet/chancloser/rbf\_coop\_transitions.go:1997–2002](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/rbf_coop_transitions.go#L1997-L2002)
   RemoteCloseStart.ProcessEvent: the only check on the remote's ClosingComplete.FeeSatoshis is RemoteCanPayFees (RemoteBalance >= fee). A negative or zero fee passes; no minimum-fee or sign check exists.
2. [lnwallet/chancloser/rbf\_coop\_transitions.go:2014–2018](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/rbf_coop_transitions.go#L2014-L2018)
   The remote's LockTime is copied verbatim into the close transaction via WithCustomLockTime; no finality/plausibility check (ErrNonFinalSequence is declared but never used).
3. [lnwallet/chancloser/rbf\_coop\_transitions.go:2065–2130](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/rbf_coop_transitions.go#L2065-L2130)
   With the remote fee/locktime, the node signs (createLocalCloseeSignature), finalises (CompleteCooperativeClose), persists ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted with this tx (MarkCoopBroadcasted) and emits a BroadcastTxn, then moves to ClosePending(Remote).
4. [lnwallet/chancloser/rbf\_coop\_states.go:728–730](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/rbf_coop_states.go#L728-L730)
   RemoteCanPayFees is a plain >= on a signed btcutil.Amount; negative fees are 'payable'.
5. [lnwire/lnwire.go:532–537](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/lnwire.go#L532-L537)
   Wire decoding of btcutil.Amount casts the uint64 to int64, so a remote can present a negative FeeSatoshis (values >= 2^63).
6. [lnwallet/commitment.go:1089–1103](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/commitment.go#L1089-L1103)
   CoopCloseBalance subtracts the (negative) fee from the payer, inflating the remote output; it only rejects negative balances, so outputs can exceed the funding input.
7. [lnwallet/channel.go:8783–8788](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L8783-L8788)
   CreateCloseProposal/CompleteCooperativeClose only run blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity, which has no input-vs-output value check, so the consensus-invalid tx is signed.
8. [protofsm/state\_machine.go:470–481](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/protofsm/state_machine.go#L470-L481)
   BroadcastTxn failures (mempool rejection of the invalid/non-final tx) are only logged; the FSM still records the state transition to ClosePending.

## Impact
No confidentiality impact. Integrity LOW: channel state durably records (and the node signs and attempts to broadcast) a consensus-invalid, unrelayable or non-final transaction as the cooperative close, and PendingChannels/CloseChannel misreport a pending close txid to the operator and RPC clients; the misrecorded tx is republished on every restart. Availability NONE: the channel was already quiesced for shutdown, a stalling counterparty leaves it equally unusable, and force close remains available (rpcserver.go:2833 ungated by ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted); the node itself keeps running. No funds are lost since only the remote's own output is affected.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a channel counterparty — permissionless to become one, but a funded channel with the RBF close feature negotiated (opt-in on the victim) and both shutdowns exchanged are required (AT:P). After channel flush it sends one closing_complete with fee_satoshis >= 2^63 (decoded negative), or fee 0, or locktime 0xFFFFFFFF, plus a signature over the resulting transaction, which it can compute since it knows every tx field. No defence has to be defeated: the only check is RemoteCanPayFees, and the node signs, persists and tries to broadcast deterministically. Assumes btcd v0.25.1-pre blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity performs no input-vs-output value check (that lives in CheckTransactionInputs).

## Recommended fix
1. The closee accepts any fee that is <= the remote balance as signed int64, including negative and sub-relay values, and any locktime, then signs and persists the resulting transaction. Fix criteria: Before signing in RemoteCloseStart, reject fee_satoshis that is negative, zero, or below the minimum relay fee for the transaction size, and reject locktime values that make the transaction non-final at the current height (and implausibly far in the future). A closing_complete with fee >= 2^63 or locktime 0xFFFFFFFF must produce a protocol error with no signature, no MarkCoopBroadcasted and no broadcast attempt.
2. CoopCloseBalance treats a negative coopCloseFee as a credit, and CreateCloseProposal/CompleteCooperativeClose only run CheckTransactionSanity, so a transaction whose outputs exceed the funding input can be signed. Fix criteria: CoopCloseBalance (or its callers) must reject negative fees, and the close-tx construction must verify sum(outputs)+fee == funding value so that no cooperative close transaction with outputs exceeding the input can be signed regardless of caller.
3. The state machine records ClosePending and persists ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted even when the broadcast attempt fails. Fix criteria: A failed BroadcastTxn for a freshly signed close should surface as an error/CloseErr state rather than a successful ClosePending, or the persisted close tx should be marked as unpublished, so operators and the RPC stream are not told a close is pending when the mempool rejected it.

# Legacy coop close accepts empty remote shutdown script, signing a non-standard close transaction

## Details
In the legacy `shutdown`/`closing_signed` flow, the remote's shutdown `scriptpubkey` is validated by `validateShutdownScript` (chancloser.go:647-680). The well-formedness check (`lnwallet.ValidateUpfrontShutdown`) is only applied `if len(peerScript) != 0`, and when the remote set no upfront shutdown script (lnd's default) the function returns nil for an empty script. `ReceiveShutdown` therefore accepts a `shutdown` with a zero-length scriptpubkey and stores it as `remoteDeliveryScript` (:745, :795). BOLT 2 requires the shutdown script to be one of the standard forms and requires failing the channel otherwise; the RBF flow in the same package enforces this (`validateRemoteDeliveryScript`, rbf_coop_transitions.go:218-229), the legacy flow does not.

Fee negotiation then proceeds normally. `CreateCooperativeCloseTx` (channel.go:9740-9756) emits the remote's output with an empty `PkScript`; `CheckTransactionSanity` has no standardness check, so `CreateCloseProposal` signs it, the remote's signature over the same tx verifies, and `ReceiveClosingSigned` persists it with `MarkCoopBroadcasted` (:1079) and calls `BroadcastTx` (:1097). bitcoind/btcd reject an output with an empty scriptPubKey as non-standard (TestMempoolAccept 'scriptpubkey'), so the publish fails; `negotiateCloseErrHandler` disconnects but the persisted `ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted` remains, and for non-RBF channels `restartCoopClose` (brontide.go:3746-3748) will forever 'wait for it to confirm'. The channel is stuck in waiting-close and must be force-closed. If a miner were to include the transaction directly, the remote's output would be anyone-can-spend; that is the remote's own loss, so the impact on the local node is the persisted unrelayable close and forced unilateral close, the same class as legacy-taproot-responder-accepts-arbitrary-fee-persists-close. Preconditions: an open channel, and the remote did not commit to an upfront shutdown script (default).

## Evidence
1. [lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:647–679](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go#L647-L679)
   validateShutdownScript runs lnwallet.ValidateUpfrontShutdown on the peer script only when len(peerScript) != 0 (:658) and, with no upfront script on record (lnd default: enable-upfront-shutdown=false), returns nil for a zero-length remote scriptpubkey.
2. [lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:732–799](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go#L732-L799)
   ReceiveShutdown (closeIdle :735-745 and closeShutdownInitiated :785-796) stores the unvalidated empty msg.Address as remoteDeliveryScript and proceeds to fee negotiation; peer/brontide.go handleCloseMsg performs no validation of its own before calling it.
3. [lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:1067–1099](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go#L1067-L1099)
   On fee agreement the empty script is passed to CompleteCooperativeClose; the tx is signed, persisted with MarkCoopBroadcasted (:1079) before BroadcastTx (:1097); a broadcast failure is returned to negotiateCloseErrHandler (disconnect) while ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted and the tx stay on disk.
4. [lnwallet/channel.go:9739–9756](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L9739-L9756)
   CreateCooperativeCloseTx emits the remote output with PkScript = empty slice whenever their balance is above dust. CreateCloseProposal/CompleteCooperativeClose only apply blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity (consensus shape) and execute the funding input's script; output script standardness is never checked, so the remote signature over the identical tx verifies.
5. [lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go:1316–1367](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/btcwallet/btcwallet.go#L1316-L1367)
   PublishTransaction runs TestMempoolAccept first; a non-standard output ('scriptpubkey' reject) is not one of the ignored reasons and mapRpcclientError returns it as a plain error, so the close is never published yet remains persisted.
6. [peer/brontide.go:3742–3748](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L3742-L3748)
   restartCoopClose: when a coop close tx is on record and the channel is not RBF-capable it returns nil,nil ('all we can do is wait for it to confirm'); loadActiveChannels (:1290-1296) refuses to start a non-default-status channel, so the channel is parked in waiting-close until the operator force-closes (rpcserver.go:2791 permits that).
7. [lnwallet/chancloser/rbf\_coop\_transitions.go:213–228](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/rbf_coop_transitions.go#L213-L228)
   The RBF flow's validateRemoteDeliveryScript explicitly rejects a zero-length script ('An absent script is rejected here rather than treated as nothing to check'), showing the maintainers consider it invalid; the legacy path lacks the check.
8. [lnwire/lnwire.go:777–794](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/lnwire.go#L777-L794)
   DeliveryAddress decoding enforces only an upper bound (deliveryAddressMaxSize); a zero-length scriptpubkey in Shutdown is accepted off the wire.

## Impact
No confidentiality impact. Integrity LOW: the node signs and durably records a non-standard, unrelayable transaction as the channel's cooperative close, violating its own and BOLT 2's script policy. Availability LOW: the legacy channel is parked in waiting-close with no automatic recovery (restartCoopClose waits forever, republishClosingTxs fails every restart), the operator must notice and manually force-close (rpcserver.go:2791 allows it), and the victim's funds are then subject to the attacker-chosen to_self_delay plus sweep fees instead of an immediate cooperative payout. Local funds are not at risk; an anyone-can-spend output would be the remote's own loss.

## Reproduction steps
1. A channel counterparty (channel required: AT:P) that committed no upfront shutdown script sends a legacy shutdown with a zero-length scriptpubkey (or sends it in reply to the victim's shutdown), completes legacy fee negotiation and signs the resulting tx, which it can since it knows all fields. The victim signs, persists ChanStatusCoopBroadcasted and fails to broadcast, deterministically; no shipped control is in the way (the peer layer does no validation and validateShutdownScript skips empty scripts). The attacker simply does not negotiate the RBF coop-close feature so the legacy path is used. Assumptions on pinned dependencies: btcd v0.25.1-pre blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity does not check output script form, and bitcoind/btcd testmempoolaccept rejects an empty scriptPubKey output as non-standard ('scriptpubkey').

## Recommended fix
validateShutdownScript treats an empty remote scriptpubkey as 'nothing to validate' instead of as an invalid script. Fix criteria: A shutdown whose scriptpubkey is empty (or otherwise fails ValidateUpfrontShutdown) must be rejected with ErrInvalidShutdownScript in the legacy path exactly as in the RBF path, so no close transaction is ever constructed or signed with an empty remote output script.

# Spontaneous AMP creates persistent invoice per HTLC before validation; unpaid partials accumulate

## Details
Reachable only when the node runs with --accept-amp (default false, sample-lnd.conf:548). With it enabled, NotifyExitHopHtlc (invoices/invoiceregistry.go:942-955) calls processAMP for every exit-hop HTLC carrying an AMP record, before the registry lock and before any of the amount/set validation in updateMpp. processAMP (:844-901) unconditionally persists a new invoice via i.AddInvoice keyed by the HTLC's child hash, indexed by the sender-chosen payment_addr, with Value = the sender-chosen total_msat and Terms.Expiry = 0; the only pre-check is the CLTV expiry. AddInvoice writes the invoice, hash index, pay-addr index and add-index entry, and dispatches an 'invoice added' event to every SubscribeInvoices client.

A remote sender therefore creates an unbounded number of persistent invoice records at zero monetary cost: for each HTLC it picks a fresh random payment_addr and set_id and sends a single AMP HTLC whose amount is below its declared total_msat. processAMP creates the invoice; updateMpp (invoices/update.go:315-319) records the HTLC (with any attacker-supplied onion/wire custom records persisted in HtlcAcceptDesc.CustomRecords) and returns resultPartialAccepted, starting the 120 s auto-release timer; the event loop (:348-354) then calls cancelSingleHtlc with ResultMppTimeout, which the link turns into FailMPPTimeout (htlcswitch/link.go:1558), refunding the sender. The invoice remains Open on disk, sits in the in-memory expiry queue for the 1 h default expiry (invoice_expiry_watcher.go:223-242), is then moved to Canceled, and is retained forever unless the operator opted into gc-canceled-invoices-on-startup / -on-the-fly (both default false; :1529-1551). It is also returned by InvoicesAddedSince to every reconnecting subscriber. No limit bounds the number of such records; the rate is bounded only by the attacker's HTLC slots (max_accepted_htlcs per channel per 120 s hold). A legitimate spontaneous AMP payment leaves one settled invoice that the sender paid for; the defect is persisting an invoice for sets that never complete, which is free for the sender.

## Evidence
1. [invoices/invoiceregistry.go:844–900](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/invoices/invoiceregistry.go#L844-L900)
   processAMP builds an invoice from sender-chosen values (Value = mpp.TotalMsat(), PaymentAddr = mpp.PaymentAddr(), Terms.Expiry left 0) and persists it with i.AddInvoice (DB write + add-index + pay-addr index + 'invoice added' notification) after only a CLTV pre-check; this is the write the fix must defer until the set completes, or pair with deletion when it never does.
2. [invoices/invoiceregistry.go:942–954](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/invoices/invoiceregistry.go#L942-L954)
   With cfg.AcceptAMP set, every exit-hop HTLC carrying an AMP record reaches processAMP before the registry lock and before notifyExitHopHtlcLocked/updateMpp inspect amounts or set state.
3. [invoices/update.go:315–318](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/invoices/update.go#L315-L318)
   If the HTLC amount is below the sender-declared total, the HTLC is recorded on the new invoice (plus its AMP set-id index entry) and returned as resultPartialAccepted, which starts the auto-release timer.
4. [invoices/invoiceregistry.go:348–353](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/invoices/invoiceregistry.go#L348-L353)
   After HtlcHoldDuration (120 s) the event loop calls cancelSingleHtlc with ResultMppTimeout: the HTLC is failed back to the sender (link maps it to FailMPPTimeout, refunding the funds) while the invoice stays Open in the DB.
5. [invoices/invoice\_expiry\_watcher.go:223–241](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/invoices/invoice_expiry_watcher.go#L223-L241)
   Terms.Expiry of 0 maps to zpay32.DefaultInvoiceExpiry (1 h); the record is held in the in-memory expiry queue and then canceled, not deleted.
6. [invoices/invoiceregistry.go:1529–1550](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/invoices/invoiceregistry.go#L1529-L1550)
   Canceled invoices are deleted only when GcCanceledInvoicesOnTheFly is set (default false, sample-lnd.conf:554; startup GC likewise default false), so each attacker-created record persists indefinitely.

## Impact
Unbounded, attacker-paced growth of the invoice DB and its hash/pay-addr/set-id/add indexes, of the in-memory expiry queue (1 h window), and of the subscriber notification stream and InvoicesAddedSince backlog, at zero cost to the attacker; degrades invoice listing/lookup, startup FetchPendingInvoices and subscriber catch-up and consumes disk over time. No confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Any Lightning node with a channel or route to the victim sends AMP HTLCs with random payment_addr/set_id and amount below total_msat; no authentication, invoice or payment is needed and each HTLC is refunded after the 120 s hold. The attack requirement is the attacker's need to hold a channel/route with enough liquidity to keep HTLCs in flight (each occupies one of max_accepted_htlcs slots for 120 s), which bounds the rate but not the total.

## Recommended fix
processAMP persists a spontaneous AMP invoice as soon as the first HTLC of a set arrives, before the set is validated or complete, and nothing removes invoices whose sets never complete. Fix criteria: Spontaneous AMP HTLCs that never complete a set must not leave a persistent invoice behind (create the invoice only on set completion, or guarantee deletion when the partial set is released/expired). Verify by sending N partial AMP HTLCs with distinct payment addresses and confirming the invoice count does not grow by N after they time out.

# Inbound canned-shim channel ignores registered shim outpoint, amount and remote key

## Details
lnd lets an operator pre-register an externally constructed funding output for an *inbound* channel via FundingStateStep{ShimRegister{ChanPointShim{amt, chan_point, local_key, remote_key, pending_chan_id, thaw_height}}} (rpcserver.go:8406-8438; used by Lightning Pool and similar external-funding protocols). The lnrpc contract (lnrpc/lightning.proto:2537-2574) describes chan_point as "the target channel point to reference in created commitment transactions" and amt as "the size of the pre-crafted output", and FundingStateStep as registering "specific parameters" for an expected pending channel ID. On the responder side the wallet enforces none of chan_point, amt or remote_key.

In handleFundingReserveRequest (lnwallet/wallet.go:957-1061) a registered ShimIntent is looked up by req.PendingChanID (971-973) and the whole `!ok` provisioning block is skipped, including the only lines that read the intent's amounts (1051-1052). localFundingAmt/remoteFundingAmt therefore remain req.LocalFundingAmt (0) and req.RemoteFundingAmt, which funding/manager.go sets from the peer's open_channel funding_satoshis; capacity (1105) is whatever the peer claims. The only shim properties applied are the local multisig key via shimKeyRing and the thaw height (1071-1081, 2813-2824). handleSingleContribution (2112) stores the peer's funding_pubkey verbatim as theirContribution.MultiSigKey. handleSingleFunderSigs (2431-2433) stores the peer's funding_created FundingPoint verbatim as chanState.FundingOutpoint, builds both commitments over it, and signs the peer's commitment against a 2-of-2 script made from the peer's key and the peer-chosen capacity (2513-2533). ShimIntent.ChanPoint() is only called on the initiator path (1677/1746) and ShimIntent.remoteKey is never compared to anything; CannedAssembler.ProvisionChannel's amount sanity check (canned_assembler.go:296-304) runs at registration time against the shim's own Amt (rpcserver.go:8420-8422) and is vacuous. The only shim-vs-wire comparison in funding/manager.go is the LeaseExpiry equality for script-enforced-lease channels (1798-1818).

Attack: the external-funding counterparty, who knows the pending_chan_id by design, sends open_channel with that ID and an arbitrary funding_satoshis / funding_pubkey (within min/max chan size and whatever channel acceptor is installed), then funding_created with an arbitrary FundingPoint and a valid signature over the resulting commitment. The victim signs the peer's commitment, persists the channel as pending with the shim's ThawHeight, and consumes the per-peer MaxPendingChannels exemption granted to shim reservations (funding/manager.go:1455-1461, 1480-1485) because "the user has registered the shim and therefore expects this channel to arrive". The registered output (e.g. the real batch-transaction output carrying the paid-for capacity and the victim's shim key) is bound to no commitment. The shim is one-shot (deleted at wallet.go:2591-2593 on completion and 1528-1533 on cancel), so the limit bypass is one slot per registration. PendingChannels does not expose pending_chan_id, so the operator can only detect the substitution by comparing channel points/thaw heights themselves. A never-confirming bogus outpoint is still forgotten after 2016 blocks (manager.go:3006-3008, zero-conf rejected by default); variants that keep the real outpoint but alter amount or key fail ValidateChannel at confirmation and stay pending (see invalid-confirmed-funding-tx-leaves-channel-pending-forever).

Impact: integrity of the operator's channel bookkeeping and of any external protocol that relies on lnd honouring the registered shim (a different, smaller or never-confirming channel labelled as the registered lease channel, plus one extra pending slot). The responder contributes no funds to a shim-funded inbound channel, so there is no direct loss of the victim's on-chain funds. Reachable whenever the operator has registered a ChanPointShim for an inbound channel.

## Evidence
1. [lnwallet/wallet.go:957–1061](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/wallet.go#L957-L1061)
   handleFundingReserveRequest: a ShimIntent registered for req.PendingChanID (lookup 971-973) makes the whole `!ok` block skip, so localFundingAmt/remoteFundingAmt stay req.LocalFundingAmt (0) / req.RemoteFundingAmt (the peer's open_channel funding_satoshis); the only reads of the intent's amounts (1051-1052) are inside the skipped block, so capacity (1105) is peer-chosen.
2. [lnwallet/wallet.go:2431–2433](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/wallet.go#L2431-L2433)
   handleSingleFunderSigs stores the peer's funding_created FundingPoint verbatim as chanState.FundingOutpoint and builds both commitments over it; ShimIntent.ChanPoint() is only consulted on the initiator path (1677/1746).
3. [lnwallet/wallet.go:2513–2533](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/wallet.go#L2513-L2533)
   The funding script the responder signs against is derived from theirContribution.MultiSigKey (the peer's funding_pubkey, stored verbatim at 2112) and the peer-chosen Capacity, never from the shim's remoteKey/amount; ShimIntent.FundingOutput()/MultiSigKeys().RemoteKey are never used on this path.
4. [lnwallet/wallet.go:1071–1081](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/wallet.go#L1071-L1081)
   The only shim properties the responder path applies: the local multisig key (shimKeyRing, 2813-2824) and the thaw height, which marks the resulting channel Frozen/Lease and exempts it from the per-peer pending-channel limit.
5. [lnwallet/wallet.go:2112](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/wallet.go#L2112)
   handleSingleContribution records the peer's contribution (including MultiSigKey = open_channel funding_pubkey) verbatim with no comparison to the registered shim's remoteKey.
6. [funding/manager.go:1455–1461](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L1455-L1461)
   Reservations backed by a canned shim are excluded from the per-peer MaxPendingChannels count on the assumption that the operator expects this specific channel; an arbitrary channel opened under the registered pending ID receives the same exemption.
7. [funding/manager.go:1798–1818](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L1798-L1818)
   The only shim-vs-wire comparison in the fundee flow is the LeaseExpiry equality for script-enforced-lease channels; funding amount, funding key and funding outpoint are never compared against the registered shim.
8. [lnwallet/chanfunding/canned\_assembler.go:264–308](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chanfunding/canned_assembler.go#L264-L308)
   CannedAssembler.ProvisionChannel's only sanity check (LocalAmt+RemoteAmt == fundingAmt) runs at shim registration against the shim's own Amt (rpcserver.go passes RemoteAmt = rpcShimIntent.Amt), so it cannot catch a later mismatch with the peer's open_channel.
9. [rpcserver.go:8406–8438](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L8406-L8438)
   FundingStateStep ShimRegister: the operator registers Amt, ChanPoint, RemoteKey, PendingChanId and ThawHeight; the pending ID is shared with the counterparty so it can reference it in open_channel.
10. [lnrpc/lightning.proto:2537–2574](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/lightning.proto#L2537-L2574)
   The documented ChanPointShim contract: chan_point is "the target channel point to reference in created commitment transactions" and amt "the size of the pre-crafted output"; the responder path does not honour either.

## Impact
No confidentiality impact. Integrity: lnd signs for, records and reports (with the shim's thaw height) a channel that does not match the registered external funding output in capacity, outpoint or funding key, defeating the guarantee the shim API documents and granting the peer the shim's pending-limit exemption; the responder's own funds are not placed in the channel. Availability: one extra pending slot per registration and a possibly stuck pending channel (via the separate confirmed-invalid path); negligible.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the remote peer designated as external funder; it knows the registered pending_chan_id (shared out-of-band by design, lightning.proto:2554-2557). It sends open_channel reusing that ID with a different funding_satoshis/funding_pubkey (within min/max chan size and any installed channel acceptor), then funding_created with any outpoint and a valid signature over the resulting commitment. No wallet or funding-manager check compares these to the shim; no race. Requires that the victim has registered a ChanPointShim for an inbound channel (the feature under attack, not a disabled control).

## Recommended fix
On the responder path the wallet accepts the peer's funding amount, funding key and funding outpoint without comparing them to the ShimIntent registered for the same pending channel ID, so the shim constrains nothing but the local key and thaw height. Fix criteria: When a registered ShimIntent is matched in handleFundingReserveRequest, the reservation capacity must be taken from (or checked equal to) the intent's funding amount; the remote funding key accepted in handleSingleContribution must equal the shim's remoteKey; and the FundingPoint supplied in funding_created must equal ShimIntent.ChanPoint() before handleSingleFunderSigs signs anything. Any mismatch fails the funding flow (and should cancel/retain the shim per operator expectation). Verify by registering a shim and sending open_channel/funding_created with differing amount, key or outpoint and confirming rejection before SyncPending.

# Justice transaction abandoned when aggregate fee exceeds breached value; no fallback or retry

## Details
BreachArbitrator.exactRetribution builds the justice transaction once the revoked commitment confirms by calling createJusticeTx (breach_arbitrator.go:737). createJusticeTx first builds the spend-all variant via createSweepTx(allInputs...) and, if that fails, returns immediately without building the commit-only, HTLC-only or second-level variants (1483-1486). exactRetribution then logs and returns (739-741): the goroutine exits, nothing is rescheduled, and the retribution is only revisited by start() after a full process restart.

sweepSpendableOutputsTxn computes txFee = EstimateFeePerKW(2) x weight(all inputs) and sweepAmt = totalAmt - txFee (1622-1641) with no per-input economy check, no fee cap (sweep.MaxFeeRate is not applied here) and no budget. When txFee >= totalAmt the sole output is negative and blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity rejects it (1677), so the whole retribution is abandoned. When txFee is just below totalAmt the output is dust: the tx is signed, PublishTransaction fails, and only the identical-fee-rate split variants are republished after four blocks.

The weight is controlled by the counterparty: every non-dust HTLC on the revoked commitment adds ~414 WU (InputSize*4 + AcceptedHtlcPenaltyWitnessSize) and lnd accepts up to 483 inbound HTLCs by default (input.MaxHTLCNumber/2, config.go:1817). A revoked state carrying 483 HTLCs produces a ~200 kWU justice tx: at 12,500 sat/kw (50 sat/vB) its fee is ~2.5M sat, at 5,000 sat/kw (20 sat/vB) ~1M sat. Any channel whose total breached value is below that figure cannot be punished at all, even though the counterparty's to_local alone could be swept by a 2-input (~600 WU) transaction for a few thousand sat.

Attack: the inbound-channel counterparty builds a state with many small HTLCs to the victim and a large to_local for itself; the HTLCs settle (state revoked); it then pays its balance to the victim and, during a high-fee period, broadcasts the old commitment. The victim's node logs 'Unable to create justice tx' and does nothing further. After RemoteChanCfg.CsvDelay (144-2016 blocks by default, server.go:1640-1666) the attacker sweeps the revoked to_local and, after the CLTVs, times out the HTLC outputs with the pre-signed HTLC-timeout transactions. The victim only recovers if it happens to restart lnd while fees are lower, inside the CSV window. Even when construction succeeds, a high fee silently burns most of the breached value because uneconomical inputs are never pruned.

Related weakness in the same function (answers ledger item L-OC-001): the fee is estimated exactly once per construction; the only way back to justiceTxBroadcast is a detected counterparty spend (847), so a justice tx stuck because the one-time 2-block estimate became insufficient is never RBF/CPFP-bumped, and the epoch branch (851-915) only rebroadcasts the same pre-signed variants. The estimator (bitcoind/btcd or the web fee API) is floored at 253 sat/kw but has no ceiling, so an over-estimate from the fee source has the same effect as counterparty-inflated weight.

## Evidence
1. [contractcourt/breach\_arbitrator.go:737–741](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/breach_arbitrator.go#L737-L741)
   exactRetribution calls createJusticeTx once the breach tx confirms; on any error it logs 'Unable to create justice tx' and returns, terminating the retribution goroutine before waitForSpendEvent or the block-epoch loop is even entered. No timer or epoch re-attempts construction; the retribution stays in the Store and is only revisited by start() (lines ~299-311) after a full process restart.
2. [contractcourt/breach\_arbitrator.go:1483–1486](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/breach_arbitrator.go#L1483-L1486)
   createJusticeTx builds the spend-all variant first and returns the error immediately if it fails, so the commit-only, HTLC-only and per-second-level variants (which tolerate their own failures, 1488-1515) are never constructed even when they would be economical.
3. [contractcourt/breach\_arbitrator.go:1618–1641](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/breach_arbitrator.go#L1618-L1641)
   sweepSpendableOutputsTxn sets txFee = EstimateFeePerKW(2) x weight(all inputs) and sweepAmt = totalAmt - txFee. There is no per-input economy check, no fee-rate ceiling (the Estimator wired in server.go:1351 is cc.FeeEstimator, not the sweeper's MaxFeeRate-capped path) and no budget, so a large input set in a high-fee environment yields a negative or dust sole output.
4. [contractcourt/breach\_arbitrator.go:1677–1679](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/breach_arbitrator.go#L1677-L1679)
   blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity (btcd v0.25.1-pre) rejects the negative-value output; the error propagates and aborts createJusticeTx and exactRetribution.
5. [contractcourt/breach\_arbitrator.go:843–847](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/breach_arbitrator.go#L843-L847)
   The only path back to justiceTxBroadcast (and a fresh fee estimate) is a detected counterparty spend of a breached output; there is no retry on construction failure or on a stuck transaction.
6. [contractcourt/breach\_arbitrator.go:851–915](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/breach_arbitrator.go#L851-L915)
   The block-epoch branch only rebroadcasts the pre-signed split variants built with the same one-time fee rate; it never re-estimates, RBF-bumps or CPFPs the justice tx.
7. [config.go:185](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config.go#L185)
   defaultRemoteMaxHtlcs = 483; applied via server.go RequiredRemoteMaxHTLCs (1715-1723) to every channel lnd opens or accepts, so the counterparty may place up to 483 non-dust HTLC outputs on the commitment it later breaches with.
8. [lnwallet/commitment.go:514–516](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/commitment.go#L514-L516)
   For the default zero-fee-HTLC anchor channel type HtlcTimeoutFee is 0, so HtlcIsDust (lnwallet/channel.go:2742-2778) only requires each HTLC to reach the dust limit (~354 sat). Each such output adds ~414 WU to the justice tx while contributing as little as ~354 sat, so above roughly 3.4 sat/vB every HTLC input is a net loss and 483 of them push the aggregate fee past the whole breached value at ordinary fee rates.
9. [input/size.go:458](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/input/size.go#L458)
   Each accepted-HTLC penalty input costs InputSize*4 + 250 = 414 WU (offered-HTLC penalty is similar), so 483 HTLCs put the justice tx at roughly 200 kWU.

## Impact
The counterparty recovers its revoked to_local and HTLC outputs, i.e. funds that belong to the victim under the current channel state: direct loss of funds (integrity of balances). The retribution goroutine terminates, leaving the breach remedy unavailable for that channel until restart (minor availability). No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a channel counterparty (any node the victim opened or accepted a channel with). It accumulates a revoked state carrying hundreds of minimum-value (dust-limit) HTLCs plus a large own balance, later pays that balance to the victim, then broadcasts and confirms the old commitment when the victim's 2-block fee estimate times ~200 kWU exceeds the breached value. createSweepTx(allInputs) then yields a negative sole output, CheckTransactionSanity fails, exactRetribution returns and nothing retries until lnd restarts; after the attacker-side CSV delay the victim imposed (144-2016 blocks, funding.MinBtcRemoteDelay/MaxBtcRemoteDelay) the attacker sweeps its revoked to_local and times out the HTLC outputs. The attacker pays to confirm an ~80 kWU commitment at the same fee rate, so net gain is positive only when the breached value is below ~200 kWU x feerate (roughly 0.5M sat at 10 sat/vB, 2.5M sat at 50 sat/vB), which bounds the loss per channel. Requires timing a high-fee period relative to channel size (AT:P), no user interaction, and defeats no shipped control. Assumption: btcd v0.25.1-pre blockchain.CheckTransactionSanity rejects a transaction whose output value is negative (ErrBadTxOutValue).

## Recommended fix
1. createJusticeTx/sweepSpendableOutputsTxn price the whole input set at one fee rate and fail as a unit when the aggregate fee exceeds the aggregate value, instead of pruning uneconomical inputs or falling back to the cheaper variants. Fix criteria: Justice construction must succeed whenever at least one breached output is economical: inputs whose fee share exceeds their value are dropped (or deferred), and failure of the spend-all variant must not prevent building and publishing the commit-only, HTLC-only and second-level variants. Verify with a retribution of 483 HTLCs at a fee rate where fee(all) > total: the commit outputs are still swept.
2. exactRetribution returns on construction error and only re-enters justiceTxBroadcast on a counterparty spend, so a transient or fee-dependent failure permanently abandons the breach remedy until process restart, and a stuck justice tx is never fee-bumped. Fix criteria: A construction or publication failure must be retried on a schedule (e.g. every block) with a fresh fee estimate until the outputs are spent or the retribution is cleaned up, and an unconfirmed justice tx must be fee-bumped (RBF/CPFP) or handed to the sweeper's budget-based machinery before the remote CSV delay expires. Verify that after a failed createJusticeTx the retribution is re-attempted on the next block without restarting lnd.
