# Any non-spent GetUtxo error is treated as 'channel spent' and permanently blacklists a live SCID

## Details
validateFundingTransaction (discovery/gossiper.go:4025-4039) performs the final spent-ness check for a ChannelAnnouncement1 via d.cfg.ChainIO.GetUtxo. Its error handling tests btcwallet.ErrOutputSpent only to add a zombie mark; the return statement unconditionally wraps *every* error as ErrChannelSpent. The caller handleChanAnnouncement (gossiper.go:2876-2898) treats ErrChannelSpent as proof the channel is closed: it adds a recentRejects entry, calls ScidCloser.PutClosedScid(ctx, scid) to persist the SCID in the closed-channel index, and then (gossiper.go:2928-2935) increments the relaying peer's ban score.

BtcWallet.GetUtxo (lnwallet/btcwallet/blockchain.go:40-129) returns the raw backend error for btcd/bitcoind gettxout failures (HTTP/RPC transport errors, backend overload or restart, connection resets) and, for neutrino, any rescan error plus ErrOutputNotFound when no spend report is produced. None of these indicate the funding output was spent, yet all lead to PutClosedScid. The project's own code acknowledges this class of failure: the sibling FetchFundingTx branch in the same function (gossiper.go:3956-3984) string-matches backend errors precisely 'to ensure we don't erroneously mark a channel as a zombie due to an RPC failure', and lnd's neutrino notifier (chainntnfs/neutrinonotify/neutrino.go:886-889) treats a 'not found' GetUtxo result as non-fatal and not a spend. The GetUtxo branch has no such distinction.

The closed-SCID index is insert-only in both stores (graph/db/kv_store.go:4540-4579 has only Put/Is; sqldb/sqlc/queries/graph.sql:1323-1344 has only INSERT/SELECT) and is consulted before signature or funding validation (gossiper.go:2736-2765). So a single transient backend failure while validating a valid, newly announced channel permanently prevents this node from ever adding that channel to its graph: every later honest ChannelAnnouncement1 for it is rejected as 'ignoring closed channel', and each honest peer relaying it accrues ban score (non-channel peers are disconnected and refused for 48h at score 100). Unlike the zombie index, which processZombieUpdate (gossiper.go:2314-2370) can clear on a fresh signed channel_update, nothing clears closed-SCID entries; only manual database surgery repairs it. The effect is cumulative over the node's lifetime.

Attacker reachability: the failure condition is a chain-backend error during gossip validation. It occurs spontaneously under backend restarts or RPC saturation, and an anonymous remote peer (any node that completes the brontide handshake) can raise its frequency: self-signed fake ChannelAnnouncement1s pass netann.ValidateChannelAnn and each forces a getblockhash+getblock on the backend before failing chanvalidate, with up to 1000 such validations running concurrently (gossiper.go:606); the ban manager only disconnects the sender after 100 completed rejections and is keyed by pubkey, so fresh identities (or a channel peer, which is never disconnected) sustain the flood. Honest announcements validated while the backend is saturated then fail at GetTxOut and are permanently marked closed. The attacker cannot deterministically choose which honest SCID is affected and must coincide with its processing (AT:PRESENT).

Explicit assumptions (dependency behaviour not verifiable in this checkout): that btcd rpcclient v0.25.1-pre in HTTP POST mode surfaces bitcoind overload/transport failures (e.g. the default rpcworkqueue=16 'Work queue depth exceeded' response) as errors from GetTxOut rather than queueing indefinitely, and that neutrino's GetUtxo returns errors or a nil spend report under peer/network trouble. The remote-triggered variant holds to the extent these hold; the permanent misclassification on any transient backend error holds from lnd's code alone.

## Evidence
1. [discovery/gossiper.go:4025–4039](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L4025-L4039)
   validateFundingTransaction: the GetUtxo error branch distinguishes btcwallet.ErrOutputSpent only to add a zombie mark; the return statement wraps every non-nil error (RPC transport/HTTP failures, backend overload responses, neutrino rescan errors, ErrOutputNotFound) as ErrChannelSpent. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [discovery/gossiper.go:2876–2898](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2876-L2898)
   handleChanAnnouncement treats ErrChannelSpent as an authoritative 'already closed' verdict: it adds a recentRejects entry and calls ScidCloser.PutClosedScid(ctx, scid), persisting the SCID in the graph's closed-channel index.
3. [discovery/gossiper.go:2928–2935](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2928-L2935)
   After the ErrChannelSpent case the relaying peer is treated as misbehaving: handleBadPeer increments its ban score (and disconnects non-channel peers at the threshold), so an honest peer relaying a valid new channel during a backend error is penalised.
4. [discovery/gossiper.go:2736–2765](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2736-L2765)
   On every later announcement for that SCID, IsClosedScid returns true before signature or funding validation; the announcement is rejected with 'ignoring closed channel' and the relaying peer's ban score is incremented again. The node can never learn the channel.
5. [lnwallet/btcwallet/blockchain.go:40–129](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/btcwallet/blockchain.go#L40-L129)
   BtcWallet.GetUtxo returns the raw error from gettxout for the btcd (RPCClient) and bitcoind (BitcoindClient) backends and from the neutrino rescan, and returns ErrOutputNotFound when the neutrino rescan yields no spend report. Only a nil txout / populated SpendingTx yields ErrOutputSpent; every other error is not spend evidence.
6. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:4540–4579](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L4540-L4579)
   The kvdb closed-SCID bucket has only PutClosedScid and IsClosedScid; no code path in the tree deletes an entry, so a misclassification persists for the lifetime of the database.
7. [sqldb/sqlc/queries/graph.sql:1323–1344](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/sqlc/queries/graph.sql#L1323-L1344)
   The SQL store's graph_closed_scids queries are INSERT and SELECT only (InsertClosedChannel, IsClosedChannel); there is no delete query, so the native-SQL graph store is equally write-only.
8. [discovery/gossiper.go:3956–3984](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L3956-L3984)
   The project's own standard for this function: the sibling FetchFundingTx error branch string-matches 'not found'/'out of range' explicitly 'to ensure we don't erroneously mark a channel as a zombie due to an RPC failure', returning a transient ErrNoFundingTransaction for anything else. The GetUtxo branch a few lines below omits the equivalent distinction and persists the result.
9. [chainntnfs/neutrinonotify/neutrino.go:886–889](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/neutrinonotify/neutrino.go#L886-L889)
   lnd's own neutrino spend notifier treats a 'not found' result from the same neutrino GetUtxo as non-fatal and not a spend, confirming that the project does not regard a not-found/error result as evidence the output was spent.
10. [discovery/gossiper.go:606](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L606)
   The validation barrier admits up to 1000 concurrent gossip validation jobs; each self-signed fake ChannelAnnouncement1 from a remote peer passes signature validation and costs the backend a getblockhash+getblock, which is the remote peer's lever for raising the backend error rate while honest announcements are being validated.

## Impact
Integrity: live channels are permanently and incorrectly recorded as closed in the node's graph database (kvdb or SQL) and can never be learned without manual database surgery; the effect is cumulative. Availability: the node cannot route through affected channels for the life of the database, and honest peers relaying those announcements accrue ban score, with non-channel peers disconnected and refused for 48h at the threshold. Per-event scope is one channel and no funds or secrets are exposed, so integrity and availability are LOW, confidentiality NONE.

## Reproduction steps
1. The sink is reached by every remote ChannelAnnouncement1 (anonymous peer, in-scope adversary). The trigger is any non-spent GetUtxo error while an honest announcement is validated; it arises spontaneously under backend restarts or RPC saturation and a remote unauthenticated peer can raise its frequency by flooding cheap self-signed fake announcements that each cost the victim a backend block fetch, with 1000 concurrent validation slots and a ban manager that only acts after 100 completed rejections per pubkey. The attacker cannot pick which honest SCID is hit and must coincide with its processing, so the attack depends on runtime state (AT:PRESENT); no privileges or user interaction are needed. The link from the flood to backend errors rests on btcd rpcclient v0.25.1-pre / bitcoind default queue behaviour that could not be verified in the checkout, which caps the rating.

## Recommended fix
1. validateFundingTransaction collapses every GetUtxo failure, including transient transport/RPC errors and neutrino 'not found', into ErrChannelSpent, which the caller treats as an authoritative, permanent 'channel closed' verdict. Fix criteria: Only a positive spent determination (btcwallet.ErrOutputSpent or an equivalent typed error) may lead to PutClosedScid or a zombie mark; any other GetUtxo error must be treated as a transient validation failure (rejected for now, not persisted, no ban-score increment for the relaying peer). Verify: inject an RPC error from GetUtxo while validating a valid announcement, then confirm a subsequent honest announcement for the same SCID is validated and added, and the closed-SCID index has no entry for it.
2. The closed-SCID index is write-only and consulted before validation, so a wrong entry can never be corrected by later evidence. Fix criteria: Provide a correction path for closed-SCID entries (e.g. remove the entry when a later funding-output check succeeds, or expire entries) so that a single misclassification is not permanent. Verify: an SCID present in the closed index whose funding output is later confirmed unspent becomes addable to the graph.

# Unauthenticated peer zombie-marks real channel SCIDs with a self-signed fake announcement

## Details
handleChanAnnouncement validates a remote ChannelAnnouncement1 in this order: chain hash, alias, premature, IsKnownEdge, IsClosedScid, ValidateChannelAnn, then validateFundingTransaction. ValidateChannelAnn (netann.validateChannelAnn1) only verifies the four signatures against the NodeID/BitcoinKey fields carried in the same message, so a message signed with attacker-held keys passes for any SCID. In validateFundingTransaction, if the funding transaction at the SCID exists but its output script differs from the 2-of-2 script built from the announcement's BitcoinKey1/BitcoinKey2, chanvalidate.Validate returns ErrWrongPkScript and the gossiper calls Graph.MarkZombieEdge(scid) (gossiper.go:4013), which writes the SCID into the zombie index with zero node keys (builder.go:962-977).

The mismatch is driven entirely by attacker-chosen keys and says nothing about the real channel at that SCID; the code nevertheless persists a negative verdict keyed on the SCID alone. Consequences while the entry stands:
- IsKnownEdge returns exists||isZombie (builder.go:1394-1399), so handleChanAnnouncement drops the honest ChannelAnnouncement1 for that SCID unprocessed, with a nil result (gossiper.go:2729-2732). The check is not conditioned on isRemote, so the node's own announcement for its own freshly confirmed channel (funding/manager.go addToGraph) is dropped the same way.
- handleChanUpdate maps the SCID to ErrZombieEdge and calls processZombieUpdate (gossiper.go:3258-3264); with zero stored keys pubKey is nil and every update, honest remote or the node's own, is rejected with 'incorrect pubkey to resurrect zombie' (gossiper.go:2338-2345). For an own channel this makes addToGraph return 'error sending channel update', so the channel never reaches the addedToGraph state, is never announced and is absent from the graph that pathfinding reads the source node's edges from.

The only un-zombie path left is VersionedGraph.FilterKnownChanIDs (graph/db/graph.go:785-806): during a channel-range sync a zombie whose reply timestamps are fresh is MarkEdgeLive'd without inspecting the stored keys. lnd runs a historical range sync with a random peer every DefaultHistoricalSyncInterval (1h) with timestamp queries on by default, so a poisoned public SCID is normally resurrected within about an hour and queried on a later sync, after which the attacker can re-poison it from a fresh identity. An own channel that was never announced does not appear in peers' replies and is not resurrected this way.

The attacker's only cost is +1 ban score per message (threshold 100, in-memory, keyed by pubkey, disconnects only non-channel peers) and a recentRejects entry keyed by (scid, sender pubkey); both are bypassed by rotating the ephemeral identity used for the brontide handshake. BOLT 7 requires a receiver to ignore an announcement whose funding output does not match; lnd instead stores an SCID-wide blacklist entry derived from unverifiable third-party data.

## Evidence
1. [discovery/gossiper.go:4001–4019](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L4001-L4019)
   validateFundingTransaction: when chanvalidate.Validate reports the on-chain output script does not match the script derived from the announcement's BitcoinKey1/BitcoinKey2 (ErrWrongPkScript), the SCID is written to the zombie index via MarkZombieEdge before ErrInvalidFundingOutput is returned. The keys that failed to match are attacker-chosen, so the mismatch proves nothing about the real channel at that SCID. This is the line the fix must change.
2. [discovery/gossiper.go:2773–2791](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2773-L2791)
   The only authentication before the funding check is ValidateChannelAnn, which for ChannelAnnouncement1 verifies the four signatures against the NodeID/BitcoinKey fields carried in the same message; an attacker signing with its own keys passes for any SCID.
3. [discovery/gossiper.go:2729–2732](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2729-L2732)
   Once the SCID is in the zombie index, IsKnownEdge returns true and any ChannelAnnouncement1 for the same SCID, remote or the node's own (the check is not gated on isRemote), is dropped with a nil result and never validated.
4. [graph/builder.go:962–977](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/builder.go#L962-L977)
   MarkZombieEdge stores the zero key for both nodes 'so this edge can't be resurrected', so ChannelUpdate-based resurrection cannot undo the poisoning.
5. [discovery/gossiper.go:2318–2344](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L2318-L2344)
   processZombieUpdate: with zero keys stored, pubKey is nil and every ChannelUpdate1 for the poisoned SCID (honest remote or local) is rejected with 'incorrect pubkey to resurrect zombie'.
6. [discovery/gossiper.go:3258–3269](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L3258-L3269)
   handleChanUpdate routes the ErrZombieEdge result of GetChannelByID into processZombieUpdate, so a poisoned SCID's updates reach the zero-key rejection above.
7. [graph/builder.go:1394–1399](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/builder.go#L1394-L1399)
   IsKnownEdge treats zombie entries as known, which is what causes the honest announcement to be skipped.
8. [funding/manager.go:3727–3748](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L3727-L3748)
   addToGraph sends the node's own ChannelAnnouncement1 (silently dropped by IsKnownEdge when the SCID was poisoned) and then its own ChannelUpdate (rejected by processZombieUpdate), so it returns an error and the own channel never reaches the addedToGraph state.
9. [graph/db/graph.go:785–805](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/graph.go#L785-L805)
   The only remaining un-zombie path: during a channel-range sync, zombies whose reply timestamps are fresh are MarkEdgeLive'd without checking the stored keys. This bounds the poisoning of public SCIDs to roughly the historical-sync interval (DefaultHistoricalSyncInterval = 1h), after which the attacker can re-poison.

## Impact
Integrity: the attacker selectively controls which real channels are absent from the victim's graph database via zombie entries created from forged data, degrading or steering path finding; for the victim's own newly confirmed channel the poisoned entry blocks addToGraph so the channel is never announced nor usable for outbound routing until the entry is cleared. Availability: payments needing suppressed channels fail to find routes for the suppression window. No confidentiality impact. Public-SCID poisoning is bounded by the hourly range sync, so both impacts are rated LOW.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: any node completing a brontide handshake with the victim (an inbound restricted slot or being dialled); no channel, funds or interaction required, since peer/brontide.go forwards all gossip to the gossiper. Delivery: one ChannelAnnouncement1 per target SCID signed with attacker-held keys. The victim fetches the block, the script mismatch triggers MarkZombieEdge. The target SCID must not yet be in the victim's graph (a freshly confirmed channel, a node mid-initial-sync, or the victim's own channel between funding confirmation and addToGraph), which is a runtime-state requirement. Identity rotation every <100 messages defeats the in-memory ban and reject cache. Default configuration (AssumeChannelValid false).

## Recommended fix
1. validateFundingTransaction persists an SCID-wide negative verdict (zero-key zombie mark) when the mismatch is between the real funding output and keys the announcement's author chose; the verdict says nothing about the real channel yet blocks its honest announcement via IsKnownEdge. Fix criteria: A funding-script mismatch for a remote announcement must not create a zombie entry that blocks later announcements for the same SCID from other sources; e.g. record the rejection only in the per-peer reject cache, or key the negative cache on (SCID, announced key set) rather than SCID alone. Verify: after a self-signed fake announcement for a real SCID is rejected, an honest ChannelAnnouncement1 for that SCID from another peer, and the node's own announcement for its own channel at that SCID, are still validated and added to the graph.
2. IsKnownEdge treats zero-key zombie entries as fully known and handleChanAnnouncement skips all processing for them (local and remote alike), so an attacker-created entry can only be cleared by the timestamp-based range sync. Fix criteria: A ChannelAnnouncement1 for a zombie SCID whose stored keys are zero (or do not match the announced keys) should be re-validated rather than dropped. Verify: with a zero-key zombie entry present, an honest announcement for that SCID passes validation and replaces the zombie entry.

# Non-strict forwarding: failMailboxUpdate fallback embeds the actually-used private channel's channel_update (real SCID) in the failure returned to the sender

## Details
lnd forwards non-strictly. handlePacketAdd resolves the onion's outgoing SCID B to a link via getLinkByMapping (which records pkt.originalOutgoingChanID = B), then takes interfaceLinks = getLinks(peer): every link to that peer, including unannounced (private) channels (switch.go:2996-3006). Each candidate is filtered with CheckHtlcForward, one is chosen at random, packet.outgoingChanID is overwritten with the chosen link's SCID and the packet is handed to that link's mailbox (switch.go:3127-3181). The design intent is that failures are attributed to the channel the sender asked for: in the pre-selection failure path only linkErrs[requested SCID] is returned (switch.go:3131-3146), and node-ID (blinded) hops get a generic unknown_next_peer with an explicit comment that a per-candidate channel_update 'could leak a private channel' (switch.go:3119-3129; mailbox.go:706-712).

That intent is broken after selection. When the chosen link A cannot add the HTLC, link.handleDownstreamUpdateAdd calls mailBox.FailAdd(pkt) (link.go:1639-1661; also on flush/quiescence and fee-exposure, and on the 1-minute mailbox delivery timeout, mailbox.go:542). FailAdd builds the failure with failMailboxUpdate(pkt.originalOutgoingChanID = B, m.cfg.shortChanID = A) (mailbox.go:713-715; the mailbox's shortChanID is the link's own SCID, switch.go:2141-2142). failMailboxUpdate first tries failAliasUpdate(B, false), which returns nil whenever B is not an alias and B is not a key of baseIndex (switch.go:2770-2800, 2840-2845). baseIndex is populated only for links whose channel is zero-conf or has NegotiatedAliasFeature() (updateLinkAliases, switch.go:2210-2263), i.e. channels where the option_scid_alias feature bit was negotiated. lnd does not signal that bit unless the operator sets protocol.option-scid-alias (default false, sample-lnd.conf:1441; server.go:746 sets NoOptionScidAlias = !ScidAlias(), and feature/manager.go:191-193 then unsets ScidAliasOptional/Required). In the default configuration, therefore, baseIndex is empty, failAliasUpdate always returns nil, and failMailboxUpdate falls back to s.cfg.FetchLastChannelUpdate(mailboxScid) (switch.go:2756) — our latest signed channel_update for A, the link that actually carried the add, not the channel the sender requested. Private channels are in the local graph (funding addToGraph is run for every channel, manager.go:4405), so the fetch succeeds and lnwire.NewTemporaryChannelFailure(update_A) is encrypted back to the sender with pkt.obfuscator (mailbox.go:729-737). The comment on failMailboxUpdate ('mailboxScid ... is always the confirmed SCID') assumes mailboxScid is the requested channel; with non-strict forwarding it can be a different, unannounced channel.

Triggering an add failure after selection is in the sender's hands. CheckHtlcForward/canSendHtlc (link.go:2613-2704) checks only the forwarding policy (min/max HTLC), CLTV bounds and a Bandwidth() snapshot; it does not model the remote's max_accepted_htlcs or max_htlc_value_in_flight, which lnwallet enforces only in AddHTLC (channel.go:4063-4072). So (a) an attacker who routes HTLCs over B and holds downstream the ones that landed on A fills A's HTLC slots; the next HTLC landing on A passes the switch check and fails AddHTLC with ErrMaxHTLCNumber; or (b) a burst of adds delivered in one commitment is dispatched by the switch's single plex loop (switch.go:1670-1671) against the same stale balance snapshot before A's link goroutine (link.go:1426-1427) has run AddHTLC for the first, so all but the first fail with insufficient balance/reserve. Either way the sender decrypts a channel_update it never asked for: A's real SCID (funding UTXO), the existence of an unannounced channel between us and P, A's forwarding policy (capacity bound) and a balance bound. Repeating enumerates all private channels we have with P.

Scope note: if protocol.option-scid-alias is enabled and the peer also signals it, loadActiveChannels (peer/brontide.go:1194-1251) retroactively assigns an alias to and marks every channel with that peer, so B is in baseIndex, failAliasUpdate(B,false) returns B's own update and the fallback is not reached. The defect is therefore specific to channels without the alias feature — lnd's default — and the leaked private channel is a legacy (real-SCID) unannounced channel, not an alias channel.

Root cause: failMailboxUpdate's fallback discloses the SCID of the link that actually carried the add (mailboxScid) instead of attributing the failure to the sender-requested SCID (or returning a channel_update-free failure) when the two differ.

## Evidence
1. [htlcswitch/switch.go:2746–2765](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/switch.go#L2746-L2765)
   failMailboxUpdate: failAliasUpdate(outgoingScid=requested B, false) returns nil for any channel without the alias feature (lnd default), then falls back to FetchLastChannelUpdate(mailboxScid) — the SCID of the link that actually received the add, which under non-strict forwarding may be an unannounced channel the sender never named. The comment assumes mailboxScid is the requested channel.
2. [htlcswitch/switch.go:2770–2799](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/switch.go#L2770-L2799)
   failAliasUpdate returns nil when the SCID is neither an alias nor a key in baseIndex (continues to :2845), which is the condition that reaches the leaking fallback.
3. [htlcswitch/switch.go:2210–2263](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/switch.go#L2210-L2263)
   updateLinkAliases populates baseIndex only for zero-conf links or links whose channel NegotiatedAliasFeature(); legacy channels (no option_scid_alias feature negotiated) never enter baseIndex, so failAliasUpdate is nil for them.
4. [server.go:746](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L746)
   NoOptionScidAlias = !cfg.ProtocolOptions.ScidAlias(): unless the operator enables protocol.option-scid-alias, lnd drops the option_scid_alias feature bit, so no channel gets ScidAliasFeatureBit and baseIndex stays empty.
5. [feature/manager.go:191–193](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/feature/manager.go#L191-L193)
   With NoOptionScidAlias set, ScidAliasOptional/Required are removed from the advertised feature vectors.
6. [sample-lnd.conf:1441](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sample-lnd.conf#L1441)
   Documented default: protocol.option-scid-alias=false. The leaking fallback is therefore the default code path, not an edge case.
7. [peer/brontide.go:1194–1251](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L1194-L1251)
   Bounds the condition: when the feature bit IS negotiated with a peer, every channel with that peer is retroactively aliased and marked ScidAliasNegotiated, so the requested public channel is in baseIndex and failAliasUpdate returns its own update — the fallback is only reached for channels without the alias feature.
8. [htlcswitch/switch.go:2996–3005](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/switch.go#L2996-L3005)
   handlePacketAdd resolves the requested SCID to a peer and takes getLinks(targetPeer): every channel to that peer, including unannounced ones, becomes a forwarding candidate.
9. [htlcswitch/switch.go:3127–3180](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/switch.go#L3127-L3180)
   A random candidate that passed CheckHtlcForward is chosen; packet.outgoingChanID is overwritten with the chosen link's SCID while originalOutgoingChanID (set in getLinkByMapping, :2357) keeps the sender's requested SCID; the packet is handed to the chosen link's mailbox.
10. [htlcswitch/mailbox.go:689–759](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/mailbox.go#L689-L759)
   FailAdd builds the failure via failMailboxUpdate(pkt.originalOutgoingChanID, m.cfg.shortChanID) — the mailbox's own (chosen link's) SCID — and encrypts it back to the sender with pkt.obfuscator. The adjacent node-ID branch (:706-712) shows the project treats a per-candidate channel_update as a private-channel leak.
11. [htlcswitch/link.go:1639–1660](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L1639-L1660)
   handleDownstreamUpdateAdd calls mailBox.FailAdd(pkt) whenever channel.AddHTLC fails (insufficient balance/reserve, max HTLC count, max in-flight), which the upstream sender can bring about after the switch-side check passed.
12. [htlcswitch/link.go:2613–2705](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L2613-L2705)
   canSendHtlc (the switch-time CheckHtlcForward) checks only policy min/max, CLTV bounds and a Bandwidth() snapshot; it does not model the remote's max_accepted_htlcs or max_htlc_value_in_flight, and the snapshot excludes adds already dispatched but not yet processed by the link.
13. [lnwallet/channel.go:4063–4072](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L4063-L4072)
   validateCommitmentSanity (run by AddHTLC) rejects with ErrMaxPendingAmount / ErrMaxHTLCNumber — constraints absent from the switch-side check, giving the sender a deterministic way to make the chosen link's AddHTLC fail (fill the private channel's HTLC slots with held HTLCs).
14. [htlcswitch/switch.go:1670–1671](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/switch.go#L1670-L1671)
   The switch dispatches forwarded adds sequentially in its plex loop; each is checked against the destination link's current Bandwidth() before the link goroutine (link.go:1426-1427, pkt := <-l.downstream) has run AddHTLC for the previous one — a burst of adds therefore all pass and all but the first fail in AddHTLC.
15. [funding/manager.go:4405–4408](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L4405-L4408)
   addToGraph is invoked for every channel, public or private, so FetchLastChannelUpdate(privateScid) succeeds and returns a signed channel_update carrying the private channel's real SCID.

## Impact
Discloses to an arbitrary third-party sender the existence, real SCID (funding UTXO), forwarding policy (capacity bound) and a balance bound of an unannounced channel it did not request and that neither we nor the peer published — information lnd's own forwarding code elsewhere deliberately withholds (requested-link-only attribution, generic failure for node-ID hops). Confidentiality of channel-privacy data only; no integrity or availability impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. The triggering input is authored by an anonymous upstream sender/routing peer who builds the onion (requested outgoing SCID B) and chooses HTLC amounts and batching; the P2P boundary authorizes nothing. Preconditions on the target: it has both an announced channel B and an unannounced channel A to the same peer P (a common routing-node/LSP topology), and the channels lack the option_scid_alias feature — lnd's default, since protocol.option-scid-alias=false drops the feature bit (server.go:746, feature/manager.go:191). Attack: route HTLCs over B; non-strict forwarding places ~1/n of them on A; make A's AddHTLC fail after the switch check passed, either deterministically by holding downstream the HTLCs that landed on A until A's max_accepted_htlcs/max_htlc_value_in_flight (checked only in AddHTLC) is reached, or probabilistically with a burst of adds in one commitment whose sum exceeds A's available balance (all checked against the same stale Bandwidth() snapshot). The sender then decrypts our signed channel_update for A. No privileges or user interaction; repetition enumerates all private channels with P.

## Recommended fix
1. failMailboxUpdate falls back to FetchLastChannelUpdate(mailboxScid) — the SCID of the link that actually carried the add — when the requested SCID has no alias mapping, so a non-strictly selected unannounced channel's real SCID is embedded in the TemporaryChannelFailure returned to the sender. Fix criteria: A failure generated for an HTLC redirected by non-strict forwarding must never embed a channel_update whose short_channel_id differs from the SCID the sender requested (or an alias of it): when mailboxScid != requested SCID, use the requested channel's update or a channel_update-free failure. Verify by forcing an AddHTLC failure (e.g. HTLC-count exhaustion) on an unannounced parallel channel to the same peer with protocol.option-scid-alias at its default and decrypting the returned failure: only the requested SCID (or its alias) may appear.
2. handlePacketAdd admits unannounced parallel channels into the non-strict candidate set while later failure paths (mailbox FailAdd on AddHTLC error, flush/quiescence, fee exposure, delivery timeout) do not treat them as hidden. Fix criteria: Either exclude unannounced links from the non-strict candidate set when the requested link is announced, or guarantee that every post-selection failure path attributes the failure to the requested SCID only; tests must cover both the alias-feature and the no-alias-feature (default) configurations.

# Blinded-route HTLC failure retransmitted on reestablish with real reason instead of invalid_onion_blinding

## Details
When lnd is a hop inside a blinded route (BOLT 4 route blinding) and must fail an incoming HTLC, the link is supposed to hide the real reason: a relaying node must return update_fail_malformed_htlc with invalid_onion_blinding, and an introduction node must return an encrypted invalid_onion_blinding error. The link does this on the wire in sendIncomingHTLCFailureMsg (htlcswitch/link.go:3684-3761), but the state it persists is different.

In sendHTLCError (link.go:3622-3641) the link first encrypts the real failure message (e.g. lnwire.NewTemporaryChannelFailure(upd) containing our channel_update for the outgoing channel, FeeInsufficient, IncorrectCltvExpiry, ExpiryTooSoon, InvalidOnionPayload, FinalIncorrectHtlcAmount...) and records it with l.channel.FailHTLC(add.ID, reason, ...) as a Fail entry whose FailReason is that real encrypted failure. The same happens in processLocalUpdateFailHTLC (link.go:4713-4770) for failures returned from downstream through the switch. Only then is the blinded replacement sent to the peer.

lnwallet turns a Fail entry into lnwire.UpdateFailHTLC{Reason: pd.FailReason} (payment_descriptor.go:275-281), persists it in CommitDiff.LogUpdates when the fail is signed into the remote commitment (channel.go:3644), and on channel_reestablish re-sends those LogUpdates verbatim when the peer reports it did not receive our last commit_sig (channel.go:4724-4732). The retransmission therefore delivers update_fail_htlc with the real reason - the exact information route blinding exists to withhold - and, for a relaying node, a different message type than originally sent.

Attack: the attacker is the payer and also our direct upstream peer on the incoming channel (the usual case when we are the recipient's introduction node and the payer is connected to it, or when the attacker is the hop before us inside the blinded path). They send a probe HTLC into a blinded path that will fail at or after our hop (wrong amount/CLTV, or let the downstream fail). We send the blinded replacement plus commit_sig. The attacker simply does not send revoke_and_ack and drops the connection. On reconnect they report next_commitment_number equal to our previous height, which is consistent with our state (LastWasRevoke/remoteTipHeight checks pass), so ProcessChanSyncMsg re-sends LogUpdates: update_fail_htlc with the real encrypted failure. As the payer, the attacker holds the shared secret for our hop and decrypts it. A TemporaryChannelFailure/FeeInsufficient/IncorrectCltvExpiry failure contains our channel_update for the outgoing channel, i.e. the SCID of the next blinded hop (the recipient's channel if we are the last hop), together with its fee/CLTV policy; a wrapped downstream error reveals which blinded hop failed and why. This defeats the recipient-privacy guarantee of blinded paths and is detectable by neither the recipient nor the other hops. No funds are at risk and channel state remains consistent (both messages remove the same HTLC), so the impact is confidentiality only.

## Evidence
1. [htlcswitch/link.go:3684–3760](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L3684-L3760)
   sendIncomingHTLCFailureMsg swaps the wire message for blinded hops: an introduction node encrypts a fresh FailInvalidBlinding and sends it as update_fail_htlc; a relaying node sends update_fail_malformed_htlc{CodeInvalidBlinding}. Neither of these replacements is what the caller already recorded in the channel update log, so the persisted state diverges from what was sent on the wire.
2. [htlcswitch/link.go:3622–3640](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L3622-L3640)
   sendHTLCError first encrypts the REAL failure (e.g. TemporaryChannelFailure carrying our channel_update for the next blinded channel, FeeInsufficient, IncorrectCltvExpiry, InvalidOnionPayload) with EncryptFirstHop and stores that reason in the update log via l.channel.FailHTLC(add.ID, reason, ...). Only afterwards does it call sendIncomingHTLCFailureMsg, which sends the blinded replacement instead.
3. [htlcswitch/link.go:4713–4769](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L4713-L4769)
   processLocalUpdateFailHTLC has the same pattern for failures coming back from downstream through the switch: l.channel.FailHTLC(pkt.incomingHTLCID, htlc.Reason, ...) records the downstream (IntermediateEncrypt-wrapped) reason as a Fail entry, then sendIncomingHTLCFailureMsg sends the invalid_onion_blinding replacement on the wire.
4. [lnwallet/payment\_descriptor.go:275–280](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/payment_descriptor.go#L275-L280)
   toLogUpdate maps a Fail entry to lnwire.UpdateFailHTLC{Reason: pd.FailReason}. There is no record that the entry was sent as a malformed/blinded replacement, so the stored real reason becomes the retransmitted wire message.
5. [lnwallet/channel.go:3644](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L3644)
   createCommitDiff persists pd.toLogUpdate() for every local update signed into the pending remote commitment (CommitDiff.LogUpdates).
6. [lnwallet/channel.go:4724–4731](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L4724-L4731)
   ProcessChanSyncMsg, when the peer's channel_reestablish says it did not receive our last commit_sig, re-sends every CommitDiff.LogUpdates UpdateMsg verbatim followed by the CommitSig. For the blinded case this emits update_fail_htlc carrying the real encrypted failure that the link deliberately withheld.

## Impact
Discloses the real failure the node intentionally withheld: failure code and, for policy failures, our channel_update for the next blinded channel (SCID, fees, CLTV delta), or the wrapped downstream error identifying which blinded hop failed. No integrity or availability impact: both the real and replacement messages remove the same HTLC, so commitment state stays consistent. Subsequent-system impact: The leaked next-hop SCID/policy identifies the recipient's blinded path internals (potentially the recipient's own channel when we are the final hop), defeating the privacy the recipient relied on when publishing the blinded path; the recipient cannot detect or prevent this.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is an anonymous channel counterparty who is also the payer (no credentials on our node). Precondition: our node is an introduction or relaying hop in a blinded path and the attacker is our upstream peer on that HTLC. Steps: send a probe HTLC that fails at/after us; receive our blinded replacement and commit_sig; withhold revoke_and_ack and disconnect; reconnect with next_commitment_number = our last height; receive update_fail_htlc with the real reason via ProcessChanSyncMsg retransmission; decrypt with the sender's shared secret. All steps are under the attacker's control and deterministic.

## Recommended fix
The update-log entry recorded for a blinded-route failure (Fail with the real encrypted reason) does not match the message sent to the peer (update_fail_malformed_htlc{invalid_onion_blinding} or an encrypted invalid_onion_blinding update_fail_htlc), so channel_reestablish retransmission, which replays the stored LogUpdates verbatim, emits the withheld real reason. Fix criteria: The persisted update-log entry and CommitDiff.LogUpdates for a blinded failure must be exactly what was sent on the wire: a MalformedFail entry with CodeInvalidBlinding for relaying hops, and a Fail entry whose reason is the encrypted invalid_onion_blinding for introduction hops. Verify by failing an HTLC as a blinded relaying/introduction hop, signing it into a commitment, reconnecting with the peer claiming not to have received the commit_sig, and asserting the retransmitted message type and reason equal the originals and never decrypt to the real failure.

# Channel peer fills persistent waiting-proof store via orphan announcement_signatures with arbitrary SCIDs

## Details
handleAnnSig handles a remote AnnounceSignatures1 whose ShortChannelID is unknown to the graph (discovery/gossiper.go:3606-3634) as an 'orphan' proof for a channel still being opened. The only authorization is FindChannel(peer, ann.ChannelID) (server.go:3514-3529), which succeeds if the sender has any channel with us whose funding outpoint hashes to ann.ChannelID; FetchOpenChannels/fetchNodeChannels (channeldb/db.go) returns pending channels as well, and a fundee persists a pending channel via SyncPending when it processes funding_created (lnwallet/wallet.go:2576, funding/manager.go:2527-2533), so a never-funded inbound channel also satisfies the check. The message's ShortChannelID is not compared with that channel's SCID or aliases, no signature is verified, and the proof is persisted with WaitingProofStore.Add.

WaitingProof.Key is (type, ShortChannelID, isRemote) (channeldb/waitingproof.go:390-400), so each distinct SCID the peer picks creates a new durable record in channel.db and a new entry in the store's in-memory cache map (waitingproof.go:61-93). The isPremature gate only requires scid.BlockHeight+5 <= bestHeight, leaving every past block height x 2^24 tx indexes x 2^16 outputs as usable keys. The stored value is the whole wire message: AnnounceSignatures1.Decode reads ExtraOpaqueData to EOF (lnwire/announcement_signatures.go:62-70) and Encode writes it back (line 93), so each record can be up to ~65.5 KB (MaxMsgBody 65533 minus 168 bytes of fixed fields). Nothing ever deletes these records: the sole Remove (gossiper.go:3828) targets the opposite half of a real, successfully assembled proof; channel close does not touch the bucket; only a one-off migration (migration35) reads it. NewWaitingProofStore reloads and decodes every record at each startup (waitingproof.go:43-58).

The peer forwards AnnounceSignatures1 to the gossiper stream with no rate limiter or channel-membership check (peer/brontide.go:2465-2478; only Ping and OnionMessage have limiters), and the gossiper has no per-peer gate before handleAnnSig. A counterparty can therefore stream AnnounceSignatures1{ChannelID: <real>, ShortChannelID: <fresh>, ExtraOpaqueData: <~65 KB>} and grow channel.db by tens of kilobytes per message, each costing a synchronous kvdb write transaction on the serialized networkHandler path, plus unbounded growth of the in-memory key map. The result is permanent, unreclaimable garbage in the channel-state database (whose integrity and performance the node's funds depend on), slower startup, memory growth, and eventual disk exhaustion, with no supported cleanup. The growth bound is set by the attacker's input (distinct SCIDs), not by the code, so this is unbounded allocation keyed by an unvalidated field rather than volumetric load.

## Evidence
1. [discovery/gossiper.go:3606–3633](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L3606-L3633)
   Orphan branch of handleAnnSig: when Graph.GetChannelByID(ann.ShortChannelID) fails, the only gate is FindChannel(nMsg.source, ann.ChannelID); on success the unverified message is persisted via WaitingProofStore.Add under a key derived from the attacker-chosen ShortChannelID, with no comparison to the channel's SCID and no cap. This is the code the fix must change.
2. [server.go:3514–3528](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L3514-L3528)
   findChannel matches only the 32-byte ChannelID (funding outpoint hash) against FetchOpenChannels(node) — which includes pending channels — and never compares the message's ShortChannelID with the channel's SCID.
3. [channeldb/waitingproof.go:390–399](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/waitingproof.go#L390-L399)
   WaitingProof.Key is type || SCID || side, so every distinct attacker-chosen SCID produces a new persistent record rather than overwriting an existing one.
4. [channeldb/waitingproof.go:61–92](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/waitingproof.go#L61-L92)
   Add encodes the whole message and Puts it in the channel.db 'waitingproofs' bucket in its own write transaction, then inserts the key into an in-memory map that is never pruned; NewWaitingProofStore (lines 43-58) decodes every record into that map at startup.
5. [lnwire/announcement\_signatures.go:62–69](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwire/announcement_signatures.go#L62-L69)
   Decode reads ExtraOpaqueData to EOF (lnwire/extra_bytes.go:46-64), so a remote peer controls up to ~65 KB of opaque payload per message; Encode (line 93) writes it back, so each persisted waiting-proof record is up to ~65.5 KB rather than a few hundred bytes.
6. [peer/brontide.go:2465–2478](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L2465-L2478)
   readHandler routes AnnounceSignatures1 straight into the gossiper message stream; unlike Ping and OnionMessage there is no rate limiter, and unlike LinkUpdater messages there is no hasChannel check, so delivery is bounded only by connection throughput.
7. [discovery/gossiper.go:3828–3835](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/discovery/gossiper.go#L3828-L3835)
   The only Remove call deletes the opposite half of a successfully assembled proof for the real SCID; records stored under bogus SCIDs are never deleted, and no channel-close path touches the bucket.

## Impact
Availability: unbounded growth of channel.db (up to ~65.5 KB per message, one synchronous write transaction each on the serialized gossiper loop) and of a never-pruned in-memory map, with every record decoded again at each startup; sustained abuse degrades the node and can fill the disk over hours to days, but the node keeps operating meanwhile and disk exhaustion is operator-visible, so LOW. Integrity: the channel-state database is polluted with permanent attacker-authored records that no supported path removes, LOW. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker: a remote peer that has an open channel with the victim, or merely a pending one (a fundee persists the pending channel on funding_created before any confirmation, and FetchOpenChannels returns it), so no on-chain spend is strictly required; the victim must accept inbound channels, which is lnd's default (maxpendingchannels=1 suffices). Delivery: send AnnounceSignatures1 over the existing peer connection with the real ChannelID, a fresh ShortChannelID each time, and an arbitrary ~65 KB ExtraOpaqueData tail; no signature or on-chain data needs to be valid. No rate limit, cap or SCID validation stands in the way. The channel relationship with the victim is a condition of the vulnerable system's state (AT:PRESENT); the attacker holds no privilege on the victim's RPC (PR:NONE); no user interaction.

## Recommended fix
1. The orphan branch of handleAnnSig authorizes on ChannelID alone and persists a record keyed by an attacker-chosen ShortChannelID (and containing attacker-chosen opaque bytes), so one channel grants unlimited distinct persistent writes. Fix criteria: An orphan AnnounceSignatures1 is stored only if its ShortChannelID corresponds to the channel identified by ChannelID (the open channel's confirmed SCID or a known alias), and at most one remote half-proof per channel is retained (e.g. keyed or deduplicated by ChannelID). Verify: a channel peer sending AnnounceSignatures1 with the real ChannelID but a mismatched or varying SCID is rejected and nothing new is written to the waiting-proof store.
2. Waiting-proof records have no lifecycle: nothing removes them when the channel closes or when they turn out to be bogus, and the store's in-memory cache mirrors every record forever. Fix criteria: Waiting proofs are removed when the associated channel is closed or after a bounded lifetime, so the store is bounded by the number of channels currently awaiting announcement. Verify: records for channels no longer open are pruned on close or at startup, and the store cannot grow beyond that bound.
3. Inbound announcement_signatures are accepted from a peer without any per-peer rate limit, so the per-message write cost can be driven at line rate. Fix criteria: Inbound AnnounceSignatures1 from a peer are rate-limited or capped per channel, so a peer cannot force an unbounded number of persistent writes. Verify: a peer exceeding the limit has further messages dropped without a database write.

# Unbounded incoming HTLC cltv_expiry makes sphinx replay-log entries never garbage-collected

## Details
The sphinx replay-protection log (htlcswitch.DecayedLog, backing sphinxreplay.db) is designed to be self-cleaning: each processed onion's shared-secret hash prefix is stored together with the HTLC's cltv_expiry, and a block-epoch garbage collector deletes entries once the chain height passes that cltv. The cltv used as the eviction height is, however, the raw `cltv_expiry` from the counterparty's `update_add_htlc`, which lnd never bounds before the onion batch is committed.

Path: a channel counterparty sends `update_add_htlc` with `cltv_expiry = 0xFFFFFFFF` (or any height far past the tip) and a well-formed onion it built itself. `lnwire.UpdateAddHTLC.Decode` reads Expiry as a plain uint32; `processRemoteUpdateAddHTLC` (link.go:4054) checks only flushing state, blinding-point policy and fee exposure; `LightningChannel.ReceiveHTLC` (lnwallet/channel.go:6456) stores the add with no expiry check (validateCommitmentSanity covers dust, HTLC count, pending amount and fee only). When the add locks in, `processRemoteAdds` builds a `DecodeHopIteratorRequest` with `IncomingCltv: msg.Expiry` (link.go:3023). `OnionProcessor.DecodeHopIterators` passes that value to `tx.ProcessOnionPacket` (iterator.go:818-820) and `tx.Commit()` (iterator.go:863) persists `(sha256(sharedSecret)[:20] -> cltv)` via `DecayedLog.PutBatch` (decayedlog.go:342-353). Only afterwards do `CheckHtlcForward`/`canSendHtlc` (`timeout > MaxOutgoingCltvExpiry+height`, link.go:2643; `incomingDelta > MaxOutgoingCltvExpiry`, link.go:2577) or `hop.ValidateFinalHtlc` (`FinalHtlcExpiryTooFar`) reject the HTLC; rejection fails it back but leaves the entry. `gcExpiredHashes` (decayedlog.go:216) removes an entry only when `cltv < height`, so these entries live for the lifetime of the node. No production code path calls `DecayedLog.Delete`, and the optional channeldb migration34 only drops the obsolete `batch-replay` bucket, never `shared-hash` entries.

For legitimate traffic the design bounds an entry's life to roughly height + 2*MaxOutgoingCltvExpiry (~4032 blocks) because the forward/final-hop checks would otherwise fail the HTLC; the attacker's value removes that bound entirely. Each attempt costs the attacker nothing but a failed HTLC (no fees paid; the slot is freed when the fail is acked); every new onion ephemeral key yields a new 20-byte key, so the `shared-hash` bucket grows without bound at the attacker's HTLC rate, and because `gcExpiredHashes` does a full `ForEach` over the bucket inside a kvdb.Batch on every block, GC work per block grows linearly with the poisoned entry count. An introduction-node or relaying position is not required; any peer with a channel to the node suffices, and by default lnd accepts inbound channel opens.

This is outside protocol-inherent limits: the BOLT 2 rule (fail the channel if cltv_expiry >= 500000000) is not implemented anywhere in lnwire, lnwallet, htlcswitch or peer, and even it would not help, since 499999999 is still millennia past the tip; the stored eviction height should be derived from the chain tip plus the node's own maximum accepted delta rather than trusted from the wire.

Dependency assumption: lightning-onion v1.3.0 (go.mod) `Tx.ProcessOnionPacket(seqNum, pkt, assocData, incomingCltv, ...)` records `incomingCltv` as the batch entry's value and `Tx.Commit()` hands the batch to `ReplayLog.PutBatch`; lnd's `PutBatch` stores whatever `b.ForEach` yields verbatim, so the persisted value is the wire cltv lnd supplied.

## Evidence
1. [htlcswitch/hop/iterator.go:818–820](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/hop/iterator.go#L818-L820)
   DecodeHopIterators hands the wire-supplied req.IncomingCltv unchanged to tx.ProcessOnionPacket; this value becomes the eviction height stored for the onion's shared-secret hash in the replay log.
2. [htlcswitch/hop/iterator.go:863](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/hop/iterator.go#L863)
   tx.Commit() persists every entry of the batch to the replay log before any forwarding/exit-hop expiry policy is evaluated on the HTLC (those checks happen later in link.go), so a later rejection does not remove the entry.
3. [htlcswitch/link.go:3020–3026](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L3020-L3026)
   IncomingCltv is populated directly from msg.Expiry of the counterparty's update_add_htlc with no upper bound applied.
4. [htlcswitch/decayedlog.go:342–353](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/decayedlog.go#L342-L353)
   PutBatch stores the attacker-chosen cltv verbatim as the value for the 20-byte shared-secret hash prefix key.
5. [htlcswitch/decayedlog.go:212–222](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/decayedlog.go#L212-L222)
   gcExpiredHashes only deletes entries whose stored cltv < current height (full ForEach over the bucket every block); an entry with cltv = 0xFFFFFFFF (or any height far beyond the chain tip) is never evicted. No production code calls DecayedLog.Delete, and channeldb/migration34 only deletes the obsolete batch-replay bucket, not shared-hash entries.
6. [lnwallet/channel.go:6456–6504](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L6456-L6504)
   ReceiveHTLC accepts the remote update_add_htlc into the update log without any check on htlc.Expiry (BOLT 2's 'cltv_expiry >= 500000000' rule is not implemented anywhere in lnwallet, htlcswitch or peer).
7. [server.go:683–686](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L683-L686)
   The production sphinx router is constructed with DecayedLog as its ReplayLog, so this is the deployed path.
8. [htlcswitch/link.go:2642–2649](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L2642-L2649)
   The only 'expiry too far' bound on forwards (MaxOutgoingCltvExpiry) runs in CheckHtlcForward from the switch, after the replay-log commit, and fails the HTLC back without touching the stored entry.

## Impact
Impact is confined to availability: unbounded persistent growth of sphinxreplay.db and linearly increasing per-block GC work on the node, slow rather than immediate (tens of bytes per HTLC plus bbolt overhead). No confidentiality or integrity impact; funds and channel state are not affected directly.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a channel counterparty (anyone who opens or accepts a channel with the node). They repeatedly send update_add_htlc with a huge cltv_expiry and a fresh valid onion; each add is locked in, onion-processed and committed to the replay log before any expiry policy runs, then fails back. No defences stand in the way and the behaviour is deterministic; only the normal commitment-update rate limits the growth.

## Recommended fix
1. The eviction height stored in the replay log is the untrusted cltv_expiry from the counterparty's update_add_htlc, so a far-future value disables the decaying log's garbage collection for that entry. Fix criteria: The height at which a replay-log entry is evicted must be bounded by a node-controlled value (e.g. current height plus the maximum CLTV delta the node would ever accept for a forward or final hop), independent of the wire cltv_expiry; an HTLC with cltv_expiry = 0xFFFFFFFF must leave no entry that survives beyond that bound. Verify by processing such an HTLC and confirming gcExpiredHashes removes its entry once the bound passes.
2. Incoming HTLCs with absurd cltv_expiry are accepted into the channel update log and onion-processed before any expiry sanity check runs. Fix criteria: An incoming update_add_htlc whose cltv_expiry exceeds a sane upper bound (at minimum the BOLT 2 limit of 500000000, preferably the node's maximum accepted delta above the current height) must be rejected before onion processing commits any state. Verify that such an add does not reach DecayedLog.PutBatch.

# Remote Shutdown/ClosingSigned derives a new wallet address before validation, repeatable per reconnect

## Details
When a channel counterparty sends a `shutdown` or `closing_signed` for a confirmed channel that has no cooperative-close state machine yet, `readHandler` (peer/brontide.go:2411-2420) forwards the message to `handleCloseMsg` unvalidated, which first calls `fetchActiveChanCloser`. For a channel without a local upfront shutdown script (lnd default: `enable-upfront-shutdown=false`) that function eagerly calls `genDeliveryScript()` -> `p.cfg.Wallet.NewAddress(addrType, false, DefaultAccountName)` (a new external address on the default account, persisted by the wallet and handed to the chain backend as a watched address — btcwallet behaviour, see assessment), queries the fee estimator and `GetBestBlock`, constructs a `ChanCloser` and stores it. Only afterwards is the remote message validated by `ReceiveShutdown`/`ReceiveClosingSigned`. If validation fails, `negotiateCloseErrHandler` deletes the closer (abandoning the fresh address) and disconnects the peer.

Trivial inputs reach that error path: a `closing_signed` sent without a preceding `shutdown` hits the `default` branch of `ReceiveClosingSigned` (closer still in `closeIdle`) and returns `ErrInvalidState`; a `shutdown` whose `scriptpubkey` is not a witness program fails `validateShutdownScript` with `ErrInvalidShutdownScript`. Nothing is persisted for the channel: `MarkShutdownSent` is reached only from `initChanShutdown`, i.e. after `ReceiveShutdown` has accepted the message. On the next connection `loadActiveChannels` finds no `ShutdownInfo`, builds no closer, stores the channel as active again, and the counterparty can repeat the message and force another derivation. `checkIncomingConnBanScore` accepts a peer with a channel unconditionally (protected) and `InboundPeerConnected` has no per-pubkey reconnect throttle, so the loop runs at handshake speed (many derivations per second from one counterparty).

What the project concedes: on a *valid* remote shutdown lnd intentionally derives one fresh address (TestPeerChannelClosureAcceptFeeResponder), but that address is persisted in `ShutdownInfo` and reused on every reconnect, so the honest flow is bounded to one address per channel. The failure path removes that bound. Consequences for the victim: unbounded growth of wallet.db and the in-memory address manager, an ever-larger watched-address set pushed to the chain backend (neutrino filter matching / bitcoind-btcd watch lists), and an arbitrarily large run of unused external addresses in the default account. Because `lncli create` uses a default recovery window of 2500 consecutive unused addresses (cmd/commands/commands.go:41), a later legitimate payout landing at an address derived after such a gap would not be found by a default seed restore. The attack requires a confirmed channel with the victim; it needs no other precondition beyond lnd's defaults.

## Evidence
1. [peer/brontide.go:3484–3553](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L3484-L3553)
   fetchActiveChanCloser: when a close message arrives for an active channel with no closer, it calls p.genDeliveryScript() (Wallet.NewAddress -> persisted external address), EstimateFeePerKW and createChanCloser, then stores the closer — all before any field of the remote message is validated. This is the ordering the fix must change.
2. [peer/brontide.go:5376–5499](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L5376-L5499)
   handleCloseMsg calls fetchActiveChanCloser first, then ReceiveShutdown / ReceiveClosingSigned; on error it invokes the negotiateCloseErrHandler closure, discarding the closer (and the freshly derived address) and disconnecting the peer.
3. [peer/brontide.go:5581–5603](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L5581-L5603)
   negotiateCloseErrHandler deletes the closer from activeChanCloses and calls p.Disconnect; nothing is persisted for the channel, so the next connection repeats the derivation.
4. [peer/brontide.go:2411–2420](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L2411-L2420)
   readHandler forwards every Shutdown and ClosingSigned straight to chanCloseMsgs with no validation of the message or its channel state.
5. [peer/brontide.go:3290–3310](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L3290-L3310)
   genDeliveryScript calls p.cfg.Wallet.NewAddress(addrType, false, DefaultAccountName) on every invocation; no caching or reuse of an unused address.
6. [lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:1120–1123](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go#L1120-L1123)
   ReceiveClosingSigned in closeIdle (no Shutdown seen) falls to the default branch and returns ErrInvalidState, so a bare closing_signed suffices to reach the error path after the address was derived.
7. [lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:732–740](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go#L732-L740)
   ReceiveShutdown rejects a non-witness delivery script via validateShutdownScript (ErrInvalidShutdownScript): a second cheap trigger of the error path after derivation.
8. [lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go:531–541](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chancloser/chancloser.go#L531-L541)
   initChanShutdown persists the local delivery script via MarkShutdownSent only after ReceiveShutdown accepted the remote message; this is what bounds the honest path to one address per channel and what the failure path never reaches.
9. [peer/brontide.go:1409–1469](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L1409-L1469)
   loadActiveChannels rebuilds the closer from persisted ShutdownInfo (reusing the stored delivery script) on reconnect; absent ShutdownInfo no closer exists, so a repeated close message derives again.
10. [accessman.go:507–513](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/accessman.go#L507-L513)
   checkIncomingConnBanScore accepts an inbound connection unconditionally when the peer has a channel (peerChanInfo), so the counterparty is re-admitted on every reconnect.
11. [server.go:4134–4214](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L4134-L4214)
   InboundPeerConnected applies no per-pubkey reconnect throttling; a stale connection from the same pubkey is dropped in favour of the new one, so the cycle repeats as fast as the handshake completes.

## Impact
No confidentiality impact. Integrity LOW: the default account's external address chain is advanced by an attacker-chosen count of unused derivations, a persistent change to wallet state the operator did not make, which leaves a gap larger than the default 2500-address recovery window and so endangers a later default seed restore. Availability LOW: wallet.db, the in-memory address manager and the watched-address set handed to the chain backend grow without bound (one entry per message, never reclaimed), and each cycle disconnects the channel peer. The honest flow concedes one address per channel; this path removes that bound.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a channel counterparty; opening a channel is permissionless but requires funding a confirmed channel (AT:P). After the brontide handshake it sends one bare closing_signed (or a shutdown with a non-witness script) for the channel; the victim derives and persists a new external wallet address, fails validation, disconnects. The attacker reconnects (accepted unconditionally as a protected peer) and repeats. No shipped control has to be defeated and lnd's defaults (enable-upfront-shutdown=false) suffice. Assumption on btcwallet v0.16.20-0.20260915140118-f2c79d772865: wallet.NewAddress derives the next external address of the key scope, persists it in waddrmgr and notifies the chain client to watch it.

## Recommended fix
fetchActiveChanCloser performs the side-effecting wallet derivation (and fee estimation) before the remote close message has been validated, and the failure path discards the derived address without persisting anything. Fix criteria: A remote shutdown/closing_signed that fails validation (wrong state, invalid script, upfront mismatch, frozen channel) must not cause a new wallet address to be derived or persisted: validate the message (state, script, channel) before creating the closer, or choose the delivery script lazily once the message is accepted, or reuse/persist a single unused address per channel so repeated failed attempts across reconnects do not advance the external address index.
