# Counterparty commit_sig during zero-conf confirmation erases the real SCID on disk, making the announced channel unroutable

## Details
A zero-conf channel exists as two independent channeldb.OpenChannel instances once it is active: the link's instance (processChannelReady fetches it with f.cfg.FindChannel, funding/manager.go:4181, and hands it to peer.AddNewChannel at 4358; peer.addActiveChannel wraps that same pointer in lnwallet.NewLightningChannel, peer/brontide.go:5793) and the funding manager's instance (advanceFundingState's `channel`, from the reservation's completeChan or FetchAllChannels on restart). Only the funding manager learns the confirmed SCID: waitForZeroConfChannel (funding/manager.go:3909-3961) calls c.MarkRealScid, which read-modify-writes the record on disk and sets confirmedScid on its own instance (channeldb/channel.go:1754-1784), then ReportShortChanID -> Switch.UpdateShortChanID -> link.UpdateShortChanID -> State().Refresh() to pull it into the link's instance.

The link's instance, however, writes its chanInfo record wholesale: every commitment revocation (lnwallet RevokeCurrentCommitment, lnwallet/channel.go:5833 -> OpenChannel.UpdateCommitment, channeldb/channel.go:2544) calls putChanInfo(chanBucket, c) with the link's in-memory fields, and extractTlvData (1344-1349) includes confirmedScid (TLV 4) and ConfirmationHeight (TLV 8). UpdateCommitment and Refresh serialize on the link instance's mutex but nothing orders them against MarkRealScid, which locks a different instance. If UpdateCommitment's bbolt transaction commits after MarkRealScid's and before Refresh's read transaction begins (including the case where UpdateCommitment already holds the link instance's lock when MarkRealScid commits, so Refresh waits behind the stale write), confirmedScid on disk is reset to 0. Refresh then reads 0, Switch.UpdateShortChanID (switch.go:2545-2560) records aliasToReal[alias]=0 and baseIndex[0]=alias, and the real SCID is never indexed.

The counterparty chooses when this write happens: it sends commitment_signed (after update_fee if it is the funder, or an add/fail HTLC cycle from either side), and it can see on-chain when the funding transaction reaches 6 confirmations - the moment waitForFundingConfirmation (numConfs forced to 6 for zero-conf) fires. A stream of commitment round trips across that block keeps the link inside UpdateCommitment (an fsync'd bbolt write each) for much of the time, making the collision likely; honest busy channels can also hit it by accident. The erased ConfirmationHeight (first conf, window of ~5 blocks) is cosmetic; the erased confirmedScid is not.

Consequences, traced:
- stateStep (addedToGraph, funding/manager.go:1242-1272) takes the confirmed SCID from the funding manager's in-memory instance (1255) and annAfterSixConfs announces the channel to the network with it (announceChannel, 3888) - the graph and all remote nodes route to the real SCID - then deletes the opening state (1270). Every HTLC that arrives for the real SCID hits getLinkByMapping (switch.go:2347-2420): IsAlias(real)=false, baseIndex[real] absent, forwardingIndex[real] absent (the forwarding index is keyed by the link's alias SCID) -> ErrChannelLinkNotFound -> FailUnknownNextPeer. Payments we originate over the channel fail the same way in getLocalLink (switch.go:904-934), which also falls back to baseIndex for the real SCID. The public channel is permanently unusable in both directions for anything routed by SCID; only HTLCs the peer pushes to us by ChannelID work.
- After a restart: the link is rebuilt from disk with confirmedScid=0, updateLinkAliases (switch.go:2207-2235) indexes only aliases, advanceFundingState returns at once because the opening state was deleted (ErrChannelNotFound, 1134-1145), and MarkRealScid has no other caller in the tree - the corruption is permanent.
- UpdateChannelPolicy (routing/localchans/manager.go:319-324) builds updates for the alias instead of the real SCID, so the announced edge's fees/flags can never be changed or disabled by the operator (only an on-chain close, keyed by outpoint, removes it).
- Channel backups (chanbackup/single.go:280-293) record the alias instead of the real SCID.
- lncli listchannels reports zero_conf_confirmed_scid=0.

Preconditions: a zero-conf channel with the attacker that is public (announced) - the operator accepted zero-conf from this peer via a channel acceptor (funding/manager.go:1614) or opened a zero-conf public channel to it. For private zero-conf channels (the LSP case) the real SCID is not used for routing, so the impact there is limited to the backup/RPC fields.

The root cause is the lost-update pattern: UpdateCommitment persists fields it does not own (confirmedScid, ConfirmationHeight) from a possibly stale in-memory copy, while the only writer of those fields uses a different instance and the only refresh of the link's copy is a single, unsynchronized Refresh.

## Evidence
1. [channeldb/channel.go:2511–2545](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/channel.go#L2511-L2545)
   UpdateCommitment (reached from lnwallet RevokeCurrentCommitment, i.e. every time the peer sends commitment_signed and we revoke) calls putChanInfo(chanBucket, c) with the link's own in-memory OpenChannel, writing confirmedScid and ConfirmationHeight wholesale from that instance rather than read-modify-write from disk.
2. [channeldb/channel.go:1333–1349](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/channel.go#L1333-L1349)
   extractTlvData puts c.confirmedScid (TLV 4) and c.ConfirmationHeight (TLV 8) into the chanInfo record that putChanInfo overwrites, so a stale instance resets both to zero on disk.
3. [funding/manager.go:3909–3960](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L3909-L3960)
   waitForZeroConfChannel operates on advanceFundingState's own OpenChannel instance (never the link's): c.Refresh(), then c.MarkRealScid(confChan.shortChanID) (read-modify-write to disk), then ReportShortChanID to make the link refresh. Between the MarkRealScid commit and the link's Refresh there is no synchronization with the link's writes.
4. [channeldb/channel.go:1754–1783](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/channel.go#L1754-L1783)
   MarkRealScid updates only the funding manager's instance in memory; the link's instance still has confirmedScid == 0 until it refreshes.
5. [htlcswitch/switch.go:2532–2561](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/switch.go#L2532-L2561)
   UpdateShortChanID refreshes the link from disk and then populates aliasToReal[alias] = link.confirmedScid() and baseIndex[confirmedScid] = linkScid using whatever is on disk at that moment. If the link's UpdateCommitment landed after MarkRealScid, confirmedScid is 0: the maps get alias->0 / 0->alias and the real SCID is never indexed.
6. [htlcswitch/link.go:2136–2149](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L2136-L2149)
   link.UpdateShortChanID only does State().Refresh() from disk; this is the sole point at which the link's instance learns the confirmed SCID.
7. [htlcswitch/switch.go:2347–2419](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/switch.go#L2347-L2419)
   getLinkByMapping: for a non-alias SCID it requires baseIndex[realScid] or forwardingIndex[realScid]; with the real SCID never indexed every forward addressed to the announced SCID fails with ErrChannelLinkNotFound (FailUnknownNextPeer). getLocalLink (904-934) has the same dependency for payments we originate.
8. [htlcswitch/switch.go:2207–2234](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/switch.go#L2207-L2234)
   updateLinkAliases at link (re)creation populates the real-SCID mappings only if link.zeroConfConfirmed() is true, i.e. only from the on-disk confirmedScid. After a restart with confirmedScid == 0 on disk the channel is treated as unconfirmed zero-conf forever.
9. [funding/manager.go:1242–1271](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L1242-L1271)
   stateStep (addedToGraph) takes the confirmed SCID from the funding manager's in-memory instance (1255) and annAfterSixConfs announces the channel with it (announceChannel, 3888), then deleteChannelOpeningState (1270); on restart advanceFundingState returns at ErrChannelNotFound (1134-1145), so MarkRealScid is never re-run and the zero on disk is permanent. MarkRealScid has no other caller in the tree.
10. [lnwallet/channel.go:5805–5837](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L5805-L5837)
   RevokeCurrentCommitment -> channelState.UpdateCommitment: the write is triggered by the counterparty's commitment_signed, so the peer controls its timing and frequency (e.g. a stream of update_fee/add+fail HTLC round trips).
11. [routing/localchans/manager.go:319–323](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/localchans/manager.go#L319-L323)
   UpdateChannelPolicy for a public zero-conf channel uses ZeroConfRealScid() only if ZeroConfConfirmed(); with the erased value our later policy updates are built for the alias SCID, which the network does not know, so the announced edge's policy can no longer be changed.
12. [chanbackup/single.go:280–292](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chanbackup/single.go#L280-L292)
   The SCB written after the erasure records the alias (with broadcast height, zeroed tx index) instead of the real SCID for a confirmed channel.
13. [funding/manager.go:3128–3144](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L3128-L3144)
   waitForFundingConfirmation sets ConfirmationHeight on the funding manager's instance at the first confirmation; the link's instance keeps writing 0 for the ~5 following blocks, so ConfirmationHeight is routinely lost too (cosmetic: only rpcserver calcRemainingConfs reads it).

## Impact
Integrity: a persisted field of the channel record (confirmedScid, plus ConfirmationHeight) is overwritten with a wrong value that survives restarts and propagates into channel backups and the switch's forwarding tables (bounded scope: LOW). Availability: the announced public channel can no longer carry any HTLC addressed by its SCID — all forwards into it and all payments we send over it fail — and the operator cannot correct or disable its announced policy; the node itself keeps running (LOW). No confidentiality impact; funds are not at risk since on-chain resolution keys off the funding outpoint.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the counterparty of a public zero-conf channel (PR:LOW — the node granted it a channel; zero-conf acceptance requires an acceptor, so this is an LSP/partner-style peer). It watches the chain for the 6th confirmation of the funding tx and keeps the channel's commitment state machine cycling (update_fee or add/fail HTLC with commitment_signed) around that block; each revocation writes stale confirmedScid=0. Success requires the write to land in the small window between MarkRealScid and the link's Refresh, i.e. a race that must be won (AT:P); the attacker gets one natural attempt per channel but can raise the collision probability arbitrarily by write frequency, and the same race fires accidentally on busy channels.

## Recommended fix
1. OpenChannel.UpdateCommitment (and putChanInfo generally) persists the whole chanInfo record from the caller's in-memory instance, including confirmedScid and ConfirmationHeight that are owned and written by a different in-memory instance in the funding manager, so a stale instance can roll those fields back on disk. Fix criteria: A commitment update must never change the persisted confirmed SCID or confirmation height: either those fields are stored outside the record that UpdateCommitment writes, or UpdateCommitment merges them from the on-disk record (read-modify-write) rather than from memory. Verify by issuing MarkRealScid on one instance and UpdateCommitment on another stale instance and confirming the on-disk confirmedScid still equals the real SCID.
2. The zero-conf confirmation flow updates the funding manager's copy and relies on a single unsynchronized Refresh of the link's copy, with no retry or consistency check, and nothing re-derives the real SCID after the opening state is deleted. Fix criteria: After confirmation the switch/link must end up indexing the real SCID regardless of concurrent commitment traffic (e.g. UpdateShortChanID is handed the confirmed SCID explicitly and verifies it after refresh, or the link's state is refreshed under the same lock that serializes commitment writes), and a restart must recompute the real SCID for a zero-conf channel whose funding tx is confirmed even if the opening state is gone. Verify by racing commitment_signed traffic against the 6th confirmation and checking that HTLCs addressed to the real SCID are forwarded and that listchannels shows the real SCID after restart.

# Onion message SCID forwarding resolves real SCIDs of unannounced channels, enabling private-channel probing

## Details
lnd forwards BOLT 4 onion messages (enabled and advertised by default: lncfg/protocol.go NoOnionMessagesOption default false, feature/default_sets.go OnionMessagesOptional in init and node_announcement). When the attacker-authored encrypted_data_tlv for our hop carries short_channel_id instead of next_node_id (onionmessage/hop.go:136-147), GraphNodeResolver.RemotePubFromSCID (onionmessage/resolver.go:84-100) performs a raw FetchChannelEdgesByID on the local graph and returns the other endpoint whenever our key is party to the edge (OtherNodeKeyBytes). Nothing checks that the channel is announced, and the alias manager is not consulted. The local graph holds every channel we have: for a confirmed (non-zero-conf) channel the funding manager saves the confirmed SCID as the opening state (funding/manager.go:3410), handleChannelReadyReceived -> addToGraph is run for private channels too (manager.go:4405), and the gossiper adds the resulting proof-less edge via Graph.AddEdge (discovery/gossiper.go:2957); such edges have AuthProof == nil and the gossiper deliberately never retransmits them 'to not leak its existence' (gossiper.go:1852-1858). By contrast, the HTLC path refuses to forward on the confirmed SCID of an unadvertised channel that negotiated option_scid_alias (htlcswitch/switch.go:2415-2423, 'the real SCID was used to forward over it'); the onion-message resolver accepts that same confirmed SCID and relays the message to the private counterparty via server.SendToPeer (server.go:5549, any connected peer, no further check).

Attack. A is any peer with one active channel to victim V (the default ingress gate, peer/onion_ratelimit.go:46; with protocol.onion-msg-relay-all any connected node). A wants to know whether V has an unannounced channel X (a candidate funding UTXO) with node P, or which P a candidate X belongs to. A builds a 3-hop onion message V -> P -> A' where V's payload says short_channel_id = X and P's payload says next_node_id = A' (a node A controls and has connected to P; P's outgoing SendToPeer has no channel requirement). V resolves X: if X is any channel V holds with P, V forwards to P (actor.go:236); P admits the message because V has a channel with P and forwards to A'. Arrival at A' confirms (X, P). If X is not V's channel, or belongs to a different peer than the guessed P, nothing arrives (P fails the sphinx HMAC). The loop-back variant V -> P -> V -> A does not work because P's same-peer cycle check (actor.go:191-215) drops a forward back to V, so a relay node A' reachable from P is required. Each probe is a single small onion message with no HTLC, fee or commitment-update cost. With a fixed target P, A enumerates candidate X over plausible unspent P2WSH/P2TR outputs; with a fixed candidate X, A enumerates P over the publicly known node IDs.

What is disclosed: the existence of an unannounced channel between V and P, its counterparty, and its real SCID, i.e. the funding outpoint and therefore capacity and on-chain linkage of V's and P's funds. For channels that negotiated option_scid_alias (opt-in via protocol.option-scid-alias) this is exactly the information the alias design exists to hide and that lnd's HTLC forwarding refuses to reveal; the onion-message path is an unguarded sibling of that protection, so the attack works whether or not the HTLC-side protection is in force. For legacy unannounced channels (default configuration), the HTLC path also forwards on the real SCID (spec-accepted limitation), but the onion path lowers the cost of enumeration by orders of magnitude. Private zero-conf channels stay under our alias in the graph (manager.go:3963-3990 re-keys only public ones), which the peer already knows, so those are not newly exposed.

Assumptions (not verifiable in this checkout): (1) lightning-onion v1.3.0 ProcessOnionPacket fails on HMAC mismatch for a hop whose node key differs from the one the sender encrypted to (standard sphinx), so a wrong P guess yields silence; (2) lightning-onion v1.3.0 decodes variable-length onion_message packets (lnd builds them with WithMaxPayloadSize and lnwire.OnionMessage carries a uint16-prefixed blob), so a 3-hop probe is a few hundred bytes and the default 512 kbps per-peer limiter (onionmessage.DefaultPeerOnionMsgKbps) admits on the order of a few hundred probes per second per channel; if packets were fixed at 1300-byte routing info the rate would be roughly 45/s, still far cheaper than HTLC probing; (3) BOLT 4's onion-message reader requirement is recalled as forwarding by short_channel_id only when it 'corresponds to an announced short_channel_id or a local alias for a channel', in which case lnd's behaviour is also beyond what the spec allows.

The recorded findings interceptor-expiry-too-soon-leaks-private-scid and nonstrict-forward-mailbox-fail-leaks-private-channel-scid establish that the project treats disclosure of unannounced channels' real SCIDs to third parties as a defect; this is a different source (onion message encrypted_data short_channel_id), a different sink (RemotePubFromSCID -> SendToPeer) and a different observer (the next-hop relay), not a duplicate.

## Evidence
1. [onionmessage/resolver.go:84–99](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/onionmessage/resolver.go#L84-L99)
   RemotePubFromSCID looks the peer-supplied SCID up directly in the full local graph (FetchChannelEdgesByID) and, provided our key is one endpoint (OtherNodeKeyBytes), returns the counterparty. There is no check that the channel is announced, no alias-vs-real-SCID distinction (cf. Switch.getLinkByMapping), and no restriction to SCIDs the sender could legitimately know.
2. [onionmessage/hop.go:136–161](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/onionmessage/hop.go#L136-L161)
   createRoutingAction takes short_channel_id from the attacker-authored encrypted_data_tlv (decrypted with our node key, so any peer can author it for us) and turns the resolved counterparty into a forwardAction.
3. [onionmessage/actor.go:191–243](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/onionmessage/actor.go#L191-L243)
   The only policy applied before SendToPeer is the same-peer cycle check; the message is then relayed to the resolved counterparty P, which is the observable side effect the prober relies on.
4. [htlcswitch/switch.go:2387–2428](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/switch.go#L2387-L2428)
   Sibling implementation for HTLCs: when a forward names the confirmed (real) SCID of a channel that negotiated option_scid_alias and is unadvertised, getLinkByMapping refuses with ErrChannelLinkNotFound ('the real SCID was used to forward over it'). The onion-message resolver omits this rule, so the real SCID that the HTLC path deliberately hides is accepted on the onion-message path.
5. [funding/manager.go:4405–4408](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L4405-L4408)
   addToGraph runs for every channel, public or private, at channel_ready, keyed by the confirmed SCID passed in; for non-zero-conf private channels (legacy or option_scid_alias) the local graph edge therefore exists under the real funding-UTXO SCID that FetchChannelEdgesByID will resolve.
6. [funding/manager.go:3389–3400](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L3389-L3400)
   For non-zero-conf option_scid_alias channels the local alias is stored only in the alias manager (AddLocalAlias alias->confirmed SCID); the graph edge keeps the confirmed SCID. The onion resolver consults neither GetAliases nor FindBaseSCID, so the alias does not resolve but the real SCID does.
7. [funding/manager.go:3963–3989](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/funding/manager.go#L3963-L3989)
   For zero-conf channels the edge is re-keyed to the confirmed SCID only if the channel is public; private zero-conf channels stay under our alias, so for them only the (already peer-disclosed) alias resolves. The real-SCID exposure is therefore specific to confirmed, non-zero-conf unannounced channels.
8. [peer/brontide.go:2480–2530](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/brontide.go#L2480-L2530)
   Ingress: any peer with at least one active channel (public or private, p.hasActiveChannels()) is admitted, subject only to the byte-rate limiter; the message is handed to the per-peer actor.
9. [peer/onion\_ratelimit.go:39–50](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/peer/onion_ratelimit.go#L39-L50)
   allowOnionMessage: the channel-presence gate is the only admission control; with onion-msg-relay-all it is skipped entirely so any connected node can probe.
10. [lncfg/protocol.go:74–107](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lncfg/protocol.go#L74-L107)
   Onion messaging is enabled unless --protocol.no-onion-messages is set (default enabled); per-peer limit 512 kbps default allows several hundred minimum-size onion messages per second per peer; relay-all is off by default.
11. [feature/default\_sets.go:122–124](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/feature/default_sets.go#L122-L124)
   OnionMessagesOptional is advertised in init and node announcement by default, so peers spawn the onion actor and this path is live on default-configured release nodes.
12. [server.go:2481–2487](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L2481-L2487)
   The resolver is constructed over the full s.graphDB (which holds our unannounced channels) and our identity key; server.SendToPeer forwards to any connected peer by pubkey with no further check.
13. [graph/db/kv\_store.go:4128–4164](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/graph/db/kv_store.go#L4128-L4164)
   fetchChannelEdgesByID returns any stored edge by SCID; private edges are stored identically to public ones (AuthProof nil), no privacy filter.

## Impact
Confidentiality: discloses existence, counterparty and real SCID (funding UTXO, capacity, on-chain linkage) of unannounced channels the node never published, including option_scid_alias channels whose real SCID the HTLC path deliberately withholds; one channel per confirmed guess, enumerable at tens to hundreds of probes per second. No integrity or availability impact on the victim.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a remote peer holding one active channel with the victim (the default onion ingress gate at peer/onion_ratelimit.go:46; no channel is needed if the operator enabled onion-msg-relay-all) plus a second node of its own connected to the guessed counterparty P so the forwarded message can be observed. It authors onion messages whose encrypted_data for our hop names a candidate short_channel_id and whose next hop instructs the resolved counterparty to relay to the attacker node; arrival confirms the guess. No security mechanism must be defeated; the per-peer byte limiter only bounds the probe rate (tens to hundreds per second depending on the lightning-onion packet-size assumption stated in the description). The exploit is deterministic. AT:PRESENT because the strongest consequence (bypass of the real-SCID protection) requires the victim to hold option_scid_alias private channels (protocol.option-scid-alias is opt-in) and the observer requires P to be reachable by an attacker node; legacy private channels are exposed on default configuration but the same existence fact is obtainable, at much higher cost, via the spec-accepted HTLC path.

## Recommended fix
1. RemotePubFromSCID resolves any SCID present in the local graph for which we are an endpoint, without the announced/alias-only rule the HTLC switch applies to unannounced option_scid_alias channels, so a peer-authored short_channel_id acts as an oracle over our unannounced channels. Fix criteria: Onion-message SCID forwarding must never act on the confirmed SCID of an unannounced channel that negotiated option_scid_alias (only its aliases may resolve), matching Switch.getLinkByMapping; the resolver should go through the alias manager (FindBaseSCID/GetAliases) rather than the raw graph. Verify: with option_scid_alias enabled and a private channel to P, an onion message naming the channel's confirmed SCID must not be forwarded to P, while one naming the alias is.
2. Forwarding by SCID over any unannounced channel lets a peer confirm channel existence/counterparty cheaply, far below the cost of equivalent HTLC probing. Fix criteria: Consider restricting SCID-based onion forwarding to announced channels plus aliases of unannounced ones (the only identifiers a legitimate blinded-path builder would use), or at minimum rate-limiting/logging unresolved-SCID lookups per peer. Verify by confirming that a probe naming a legacy private channel's real SCID from a third-party peer is not forwarded.

# Payee-crafted blinded path with empty intro-hop cipher text aborts KV-to-SQL payment migration

## Details
When a node enables `db.use-native-sql`, the payments migration runs MigratePaymentsKVToSQL over every stored payment, including in-flight ones (migratePayment handles StatusInFlight). In migrateRouteHop (payments/db/migration1/sql_migration.go:844-851) a route hop that has a BlindingPoint but zero-length EncryptedData is treated as corruption and the whole migration returns an error; the error propagates through migrateHTLCAttempt/migratePayment/migrateIndexEntry, ApplyAllMigrations fails, BuildDatabase returns the error and lnd exits (lnd.go:474-477). The migration comment asserts that 'internally built blinded routes also always contain both' fields; the invoice path does not guarantee that.

That hop shape is producible by a remote payee. A BOLT11 invoice's blinded path (`b` field) is decoded by zpay32.DecodeBlindedHop, which accepts a zero-length encrypted_recipient_data (only a 535-byte upper bound is enforced) and returns a non-nil empty CipherText. routing.BlindedPayment.Validate, the only check applied to invoice paths (routerrpc.BuildBlindedPathSet), checks hop count, HTLC bounds and the NUMS key but never requires non-empty cipher text. NewBlindedPaymentPathSet.deepCopy preserves the empty, non-nil slice. During path finding, newRoute (routing/pathfind.go:357-369) assigns the path's BlindingPoint to the introduction hop and copies the empty CipherText into hop.EncryptedData.

Two variants reach the KV store:
(1) Single-hop path (payee is the introduction node, the default-config variant): the intro hop is also the final hop. verifyAttempt (payments/db/payment.go:745) derives isBlinded from len(FinalHop().EncryptedData) != 0, so it classifies the attempt as non-blinded; with no payment address in the invoice there is no MPP record and a full-amount first attempt passes every check. RegisterAttempt persists the hop before sendAttempt. The onion still builds (PackHopPayload treats a non-nil empty slice as blinded, final hop keeps amount/cltv, nextChanID is zero) and the HTLC is delivered to the payee's own node, which can hold it for the whole CLTV window (bounded by the payer's cltv limit, default 2016 blocks). While the HTLC is held the payment is in flight, cannot be deleted by the operator (KVStore.DeletePayment refuses via removable()), and every start of lnd with native SQL enabled fails with 'invalid blinded hop ... blinding point requires encrypted recipient data'.
(2) Multi-hop path with an empty intro-hop cipher text and a non-empty final hop: verifyAttempt sees a blinded final hop with TotalAmtMsat set and passes; the intro node fails the HTLC, and the failed attempt stays in KV only if the node runs with `--keep-failed-payment-attempts` (otherwise DeleteFailedAttempts removes it when the payment terminates), in which case the migration is blocked until the operator deletes the payment.

The KV serializer (payments/db/kv_store.go:1757-1766) writes a zero-length encrypted-data record for a non-nil empty slice plus the blinding point record; the frozen reader used by the migration (payments/db/migration1/kv_store.go:1899-1914) returns EncryptedData with length 0 alongside the parsed blinding point, exactly the shape migrateRouteHop rejects. The explicit RPC guard 'encrypted data should be present if blinding point is provided' (router_backend.go:781) covers only hops supplied through SendToRoute. The live SQL store's insertRouteHops (payments/db/sql_store.go:1386) skips only nil EncryptedData and otherwise accepts the hop, so the rejection is specific to the upgrade path. The SQL transaction rolls back, so no stored data is corrupted; the operator's recourse is to run without native SQL until the HTLC resolves, or to use `db.skip-native-sql-migration`, which discards the payment history.

This is distinct from blinded-path-newroute-cipher-index-panic (a panic in newRoute itself); here the route is built successfully and the defect is the migration's rejection of a payee-producible stored hop.

## Evidence
1. [payments/db/migration1/sql\_migration.go:844–850](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/payments/db/migration1/sql_migration.go#L844-L850)
   migrateRouteHop treats a hop with BlindingPoint != nil and len(EncryptedData)==0 as malformed and returns an error that propagates through migrateHTLCAttempt/migratePayment/migrateIndexEntry to MigratePaymentsKVToSQL, aborting the whole payment migration. The comment asserts internally built blinded routes always carry both fields, which the invoice path does not guarantee.
2. [routing/pathfind.go:357–369](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/pathfind.go#L357-L369)
   newRoute sets hop.BlindingPoint on the introduction hop and copies blindedPath.BlindedHops[dataIndex].CipherText into hop.EncryptedData verbatim; a zero-length payee cipher text yields a hop with a blinding point and an empty, non-nil EncryptedData slice.
3. [zpay32/blinded\_path.go:218–239](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/zpay32/blinded_path.go#L218-L239)
   DecodeBlindedHop accepts dataLen == 0 (only the 535-byte upper bound is enforced) and returns CipherText = make([]byte, 0). This is the payee-controlled BOLT11 'b' field entry point.
4. [routing/blinding.go:332–365](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/blinding.go#L332-L365)
   BlindedPayment.Validate is the only validation applied to invoice blinded paths (via routerrpc.BuildBlindedPathSet). It checks hop count, HTLC bounds and the NUMS key but never requires a non-empty CipherText per hop.
5. [lnrpc/routerrpc/router\_backend.go:1313–1326](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/routerrpc/router_backend.go#L1313-L1326)
   BuildBlindedPathSet converts zpay32 blinded paths from a payment request into routing.BlindedPayment and only calls Validate. The guard 'encrypted data should be present if blinding point is provided' exists only for SendToRoute-style RPC hops (lines 781-784), not for invoice-supplied paths.
6. [payments/db/payment.go:745–759](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/payments/db/payment.go#L745-L759)
   verifyAttempt, the only attempt-level check before persistence, derives isBlinded from len(FinalHop().EncryptedData) != 0. For a single-hop blinded path with empty cipher text it classifies the attempt as non-blinded and a full-amount attempt without an MPP record passes; for a multi-hop path it only inspects the final hop, which the payee leaves non-empty.
7. [routing/payment\_lifecycle.go:618–632](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/routing/payment_lifecycle.go#L618-L632)
   registerAttempt persists the attempt via Control.RegisterAttempt before sendAttempt dispatches the HTLC, so the malformed hop reaches the KV store regardless of how the attempt later resolves.
8. [payments/db/kv\_store.go:1757–1766](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/payments/db/kv_store.go#L1757-L1766)
   The live KV serializer writes the encrypted-data record whenever EncryptedData != nil (so an empty non-nil slice becomes a zero-length record) and writes the blinding point record separately.
9. [payments/db/migration1/kv\_store.go:1899–1914](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/payments/db/migration1/kv_store.go#L1899-L1914)
   The frozen deserializeHop used by the migration reads the records back as EncryptedData with length 0 and BlindingPoint = parsed key, exactly the shape migrateRouteHop rejects.
10. [payments/db/kv\_store.go:1272–1299](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/payments/db/kv_store.go#L1272-L1299)
   KVStore.DeletePayment refuses to delete a payment with in-flight HTLCs (paymentStatus.removable()), so while the payee holds the HTLC the operator cannot remove the offending attempt from KV before migrating.
11. [payments/db/sql\_store.go:1386–1410](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/payments/db/sql_store.go#L1386-L1410)
   The live SQL write path (insertRouteHops) skips only hop.EncryptedData == nil and otherwise inserts the blinded row with whatever blinding point is present, so it accepts the same hop the migration rejects; the rejection is specific to the upgrade path.
12. [config\_builder.go:1187–1199](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config_builder.go#L1187-L1199)
   The migration error is returned from the payments MigrationFn; ApplyAllMigrations fails and BuildDatabase returns an error (lines 1240-1247), so lnd exits at startup while db.use-native-sql is set.

## Impact
The node cannot complete the KV-to-SQL payments migration and exits at startup while native SQL is enabled; the SQL transaction rolls back so nothing is corrupted, and the operator can revert to the KV backend or wait for the held HTLC to resolve. Availability impact is partial (blocked upgrade/startup until manual intervention), with no confidentiality or integrity impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A remote payee publishes a BOLT11 invoice whose blinded path has an introduction hop with zero-length encrypted_recipient_data. The victim node pays the invoice in the normal course of business; the attempt is persisted to KV with BlindingPoint set and empty EncryptedData before the HTLC is sent. In the default configuration the payee uses a single-hop path (payee = introduction node), the onion still builds, and the payee's own node holds the HTLC for up to the payer's cltv limit (default 2016 blocks); the in-flight payment cannot be deleted by the operator and the migration aborts deterministically if native SQL is enabled in that window. With --keep-failed-payment-attempts a multi-hop variant leaves a failed attempt in KV permanently. The attack therefore requires the operator to run the documented KV-to-native-SQL upgrade while the hop is present (attack requirements present) and the victim to pay the attacker's invoice (passive user interaction).

## Recommended fix
1. migrateRouteHop treats a payee-producible hop shape (blinding point with empty encrypted data) as unrecoverable corruption and aborts the entire migration instead of migrating or normalising the hop, violating the expectation that the upgrade path tolerates every state the live KV store can legitimately hold. Fix criteria: The migration must complete for KV payments containing a hop with a blinding point and empty encrypted data (e.g. persist the hop as the live SQL store does, or drop the orphaned blinding point with a warning as is done for orphaned total amounts), and the deep-compare normalisation must mirror that choice. Verify by migrating a KV payment built from an invoice blinded path with a zero-length introduction-hop cipher text and confirming MigratePaymentsKVToSQL succeeds and the payment reads back.
2. Invoice-supplied blinded paths are not validated for non-empty per-hop cipher text, while the equivalent RPC hop path is, so payee input shapes stored route data in a way the rest of the system does not expect. Fix criteria: Blinded paths decoded from a payment request should be rejected (or the hop treated as invalid) when any hop's encrypted_recipient_data is empty, consistent with the RPC guard, so that no attempt with a blinding point and empty encrypted data is ever registered. Verify by attempting to pay such an invoice and confirming the payment is rejected before RegisterAttempt.

# Postgres DSN password masking fails for re-encoded passwords, logging the credential

## Details
`sqldb.NewPostgresStore` (sqldb/postgres.go:97-102), reached from lncfg/db.go:483-486 whenever lnd runs with `db.backend=postgres` and `db.use-native-sql=true`, logs the configured Postgres DSN at Info level (default-enabled file logger, ~/.lnd/logs/<chain>/<net>/lnd.log) after passing it through `replacePasswordInDSN`, whose stated purpose is to replace the password with `***`.

`replacePasswordInDSN` parses the DSN with `url.Parse`, builds the needle `u.User.String()+"@"` and runs `strings.Replace(dsn, needle, username+":***@", 1)`. `url.Parse` accepts `!`, `*`, `'`, `(`, `)` and `%XX` raw in the userinfo (validUserinfo) and unescapes the password; `url.Userinfo.String()` then re-encodes it with Go's encodeUserPassword rules, which percent-escape every character outside unreserved/`$&+,;=` and canonicalise percent-escapes to upper-case hex and decoded unreserved characters. Any of the following therefore makes the needle differ from the raw text and the replacement a no-op:
- a raw sub-delimiter that Go escapes: `!`, `*`, `'`, `(`, `)` (e.g. `postgres://lnd:S3cr3t!@host/lnd` -> needle `lnd:S3cr3t%21@`);
- percent-encoding that Go canonicalises differently: lower-case hex (`%2f` -> `%2F`) or encoded unreserved characters (`%41` -> `A`).

In those cases `replacePasswordInDSN` returns the original DSN and `Using SQL database 'postgres://lnd:S3cr3t!@host:5432/lnd?sslmode=require'` is written to lnd.log on every start. A libpq keyword/value connection string (`host=... user=lnd password=secret dbname=lnd`), which pgx v5.11.0 also accepts (dependency assumption), parses with `u.User == nil` and is likewise logged verbatim, password included.

Passwords containing `!` or `*` are common, and lnd's own bug-report template (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml:104) asks users to upload lnd.log; the log file is created by jrick/logrotate v1.1.2 with umask-default 0644 (dependency assumption) inside the 0700 log directory lnd creates (build/logrotator.go:38). The masking failure thus discloses the database credential protecting the kvdb-emulated channel state and wallet tables plus the native SQL tables to anyone who reads or receives the log. The same code is duplicated in the published `sqldb/v2` module (sqldb/v2/postgres.go:56-80, :144), not yet imported by lnd. A robust fix rebuilds the DSN from the parsed URL with `url.UserPassword(username, "***")` / `u.Redacted()` rather than text substitution, and omits userinfo or the whole string for non-URL DSNs.

## Evidence
1. [sqldb/postgres.go:48–72](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/postgres.go#L48-L72)
   replacePasswordInDSN rebuilds the userinfo via u.User.String()+"@" and does a literal strings.Replace against the raw DSN. url.Userinfo.String() re-escapes the parsed password with encodeUserPassword rules ('!' -> %21, '*' -> %2A, lower-case %2f -> %2F, %41 -> 'A'), so whenever the operator's DSN spells the password differently from Go's canonical escaping the needle is not found and the DSN is returned unmodified, password included. A keyword/value DSN has no userinfo and is returned verbatim too.
2. [sqldb/postgres.go:98–102](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/postgres.go#L98-L102)
   NewPostgresStore logs the 'sanitized' DSN at Info level on every start-up, so the unmasked password lands in lnd.log whenever the masking misses.
3. [lncfg/db.go:483–486](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lncfg/db.go#L483-L486)
   Production caller: lnd invokes sqldb.NewPostgresStore(db.Postgres) with the operator's DSN whenever db.backend=postgres and db.use-native-sql=true, so the logging path runs on every start of such a deployment.
4. [sqldb/v2/postgres.go:56–80](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sqldb/v2/postgres.go#L56-L80)
   The published sqldb/v2 module carries the identical replacement logic and logs the result at :144; lnd does not import it yet, but its exported NewPostgresStore exposes the same defect to consumers.

## Impact
Discloses the Postgres credential protecting lnd's database (channel state and wallet KV tables and native SQL tables when postgres is the backend). Disclosure alone; the logging itself changes no integrity or availability. Rated LOW because the same secret is already present in lnd.conf on the same host and using it still needs network reach to the Postgres server, so the marginal exposure is to log readers and log recipients.

## Reproduction steps
1. No attacker action triggers it: whenever a postgres + native-SQL deployment's password contains a character Go escapes differently (`!*'()` raw, or non-canonical percent-encoding) or uses a keyword/value DSN, lnd writes the full DSN to lnd.log at Info level on every start. Anyone who can read the log (a local account with access to the log directory, log aggregation, or recipients of logs shared for support as lnd's bug-report template requests) obtains the database credential. Requires the postgres/native-SQL deployment and such a password (attack requirements), and local log access or log sharing.

## Recommended fix
Password masking is implemented as a literal text substitution whose needle is produced by re-escaping the parsed password, so any DSN whose password spelling differs from Go's canonical escaping — or any DSN that is not a URL with userinfo — is logged unmasked. Fix criteria: The logged DSN must never contain the password regardless of how it is spelled in the configured DSN. Verify with URL DSNs whose passwords contain `!`, `*`, `(`, lower-case percent-escapes and `%41`-style encodings, and with a libpq keyword/value connection string containing `password=`: the log line must show `***` (or omit userinfo / the credential entirely) in every case, in both sqldb and sqldb/v2.

# uint16 count in serializeLogUpdates silently drops persisted counterparty updates beyond 65535

## Details
channeldb persists the remote party's acked-but-unsigned updates (unsignedAckedUpdatesKey) and the local updates the peer has not yet signed for (remoteUnsignedLocalUpdatesKey) through serializeLogUpdates, which encodes the element count as uint16 while writing all elements. deserializeLogUpdates reads only `count` elements and ignores the rest. If a list ever holds >= 65536 entries the persisted count wraps (n mod 65536) and every entry past that is silently dropped the next time the key is read (UnsignedAckedUpdates at startup, AdvanceCommitChainTail on the next remote revocation).

The remote-controlled list is unsignedAckedUpdates. While the counterparty withholds revoke_and_ack for our pending commitment, lnwallet.SignNextCommitment returns ErrNoWindow (hasUnackedCommitment), so nothing we do can shrink the list; yet we still accept and revoke the counterparty's commitment_signed messages (link processRemoteCommitSig -> ReceiveNewCommitment -> RevokeCurrentCommitment -> UpdateCommitment). A counterparty that is the channel funder may send update_fee at will: lnwallet.ReceiveUpdateFee only checks we are not the initiator and requires no fee change, link.processRemoteUpdateFee only checks the fee-exposure threshold, and validateCommitmentSanity only requires the fee to be >= the 253 sat/kw floor and affordable by the initiator. Alternating between two valid fee rates, each followed by commitment_signed, appends one entry per round and rewrites the entire list to disk (quadratic write amplification: ~48 B x n per revoke, ~100 GB total to reach n=65536, each in its own fsynced transaction). The only guard, PendingCommitTicker (default 1 min), causes a non-permanent disconnect; the list is persisted and survives reconnects, and channel_reestablish simply retransmits (or confirms) our pending commitment_signed while the remote continues the loop.

After the victim restarts with n >= 65536, restorePendingRemoteUpdates rebuilds the remote log from only n mod 65536 entries (0 entries if n is an exact multiple). Because the remote log index is seeded from the local commitment's RemoteLogIndex, the surviving prefix passes the sanity check and no error is raised. The next remote commitment we sign (fetchCommitmentView) applies the stale fee / lacks remote settles and fails the peer already has, so our signature does not match the state the peer expects; an honest peer fails the channel and force-closes it, or a malicious one keeps the victim stuck. The victim's channel state on disk is corrupted independently of the counterparty's later behaviour. No funds are stolen: the fee is paid by the initiator and lost settles/fails leave HTLCs resolvable on chain.

Root cause is in channeldb: an untyped length field that cannot represent the list it serializes, with the reader trusting the count. The absence of any cap on counterparty updates accumulated while revoke_and_ack is withheld (lnwallet/htlcswitch) makes the wrap reachable and also makes per-revoke DB write cost grow without bound.

## Evidence
1. [channeldb/channel.go:3108–3140](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/channel.go#L3108-L3140)
   serializeLogUpdates writes numUpdates := uint16(len(logUpdates)) and then every element; deserializeLogUpdates allocates and reads exactly numUpdates elements and ignores the trailing bytes. For len >= 65536 the stored count is len mod 65536 and the newest entries are silently dropped on every read.
2. [channeldb/channel.go:2559–2567](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/channel.go#L2559-L2567)
   UpdateCommitment (run on every revoke_and_ack we send) re-serializes the full in-memory unsignedAckedUpdates list under unsignedAckedUpdatesKey; the write is O(n) per revoke and succeeds silently after the count wraps.
3. [lnwallet/channel.go:9512–9532](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L9512-L9532)
   ReceiveUpdateFee only checks we are not the initiator; it appends a FeeUpdate to the remote log unconditionally (no cap, no requirement that the fee differ from the current one).
4. [htlcswitch/link.go:4584–4619](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L4584-L4619)
   processRemoteUpdateFee only checks the fee-exposure threshold before calling ReceiveUpdateFee; alternating between two affordable fee rates passes every check.
5. [lnwallet/channel.go:4166–4174](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L4166-L4174)
   SignNextCommitment returns ErrNoWindow while the remote's revoke_and_ack for our pending commitment is outstanding, so nothing we do can move entries out of the acked-but-unsigned set; the remote's own commitment_signed messages are still accepted and revoked.
6. [lnwallet/channel.go:3721–3755](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L3721-L3755)
   getUnsignedAckedUpdates returns every remote log entry between the remote chain tail's and the local chain tail's remote message index with no cap, so each accepted update_fee round adds one persisted entry.
7. [htlcswitch/link.go:1413–1420](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L1413-L1420)
   The only guard, PendingCommitTicker (default 1 min, config.go:204), fails the link with LinkFailureDisconnect and no PermanentFailure; the peer is merely disconnected, the persisted list survives, and channel_reestablish lets the remote continue the loop.
8. [lnwallet/channel.go:1582–1599](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L1582-L1599)
   On restart restoreCommitState feeds UnsignedAckedUpdates() (already truncated) into restorePendingRemoteUpdates; because the remote log index is seeded from localCommit.RemoteLogIndex (NewLightningChannel:972-974) the surviving prefix passes the log_index sanity check and the loss is silent.
9. [channeldb/channel.go:3583–3621](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/channel.go#L3583-L3621)
   AdvanceCommitChainTail re-reads the key with deserializeLogUpdates (truncated) and re-serializes with the same uint16 count; no path detects or repairs the loss.

## Impact
Persisted channel state is silently corrupted (newest counterparty updates dropped) so after a restart the node can no longer produce a commitment the peer accepts; the channel must be force closed and the victim bears sweep costs and loses the channel. No funds are stolen (fees are paid by the initiator; lost settles/fails leave HTLCs claimable on chain) and no secrets are exposed. Reaching the wrap also forces the victim to write on the order of 100 GB to its channel database in ~65k fsynced transactions, degrading the node while the attack runs; the per-revoke write and in-memory log keep growing past the wrap.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a channel counterparty that funded the channel (any peer may open an inbound channel; the fundee cannot refuse update_fee). It withholds revoke_and_ack for our pending commitment and loops update_fee (alternating two valid rates) + commitment_signed; each round is accepted (processRemoteUpdateFee -> ReceiveUpdateFee, ReceiveNewCommitment), revoked, and persisted via UpdateCommitment, growing unsignedAckedUpdates without bound across reconnects because SignNextCommitment returns ErrNoWindow. ~65536 rounds are needed (hours; each costs the victim an O(n) fsynced DB write). The data loss takes effect when the victim restarts (routine), after which the rebuilt remote log lacks the newest updates and the next commitment we sign is rejected by the peer. The only defense is a 1-minute non-permanent disconnect that does not reset the persisted list.

## Recommended fix
1. serializeLogUpdates/deserializeLogUpdates encode the list length as uint16 while writing an unbounded number of elements, so the reader silently stops early after a wrap. Fix criteria: Serialization must either refuse (return an error) when len(logUpdates) exceeds the representable count, or use a width that can represent any list the callers can produce; deserialization must fail loudly if bytes remain after the counted elements. Verify: a list of 65536+ LogUpdates round-trips exactly or produces an error at write time, never a shorter list.
2. No bound on counterparty updates accumulated (and re-persisted on every revoke) while the counterparty withholds revoke_and_ack for our pending commitment. Fix criteria: The channel state machine or link must cap the number of remote updates accepted while a remote commitment is unacked (e.g. fail the channel/disconnect past a sane limit, or reject update_fee that does not change the fee), so unsignedAckedUpdates cannot grow without bound. Verify: a peer looping update_fee+commitment_signed without revoking is cut off well before the list reaches thousands of entries.

# AdvanceCommitChainTail skips persisting peer-unsigned local updates when no acked-updates key exists

## Details
AdvanceCommitChainTail is the atomic step run when the counterparty revokes a commitment we signed. Besides swapping the remote commitment and writing the revocation log, it must persist `updates` -- our local non-add updates (settle/fail/update_fee) now locked into the remote commitment but not yet in our local commitment -- under remoteUnsignedLocalUpdatesKey so lnwallet can rebuild the local update log after a restart (restorePeerLocalUpdates). The function first reads unsignedAckedUpdatesKey and, if the key is absent, returns success without writing remoteUnsignedLocalUpdatesKey at all. The comment claims this "shouldn't normally happen", but unsignedAckedUpdatesKey is only created by UpdateCommitment, i.e. the first time *we* send revoke_and_ack. A channel on which the peer has never sent commitment_signed therefore has no such key, and every revocation we receive on it takes the early-return path.

Concrete path: we are the channel funder (only the funder sends update_fee). The link's updateFeeTimer (10-60 min) fires and shouldAdjustCommitFee is true, so handleUpdateFee -> updateChannelFee sends update_fee + commitment_signed; this is our first state transition on the channel. The peer sends revoke_and_ack (lnwallet.ReceiveRevocation -> AdvanceCommitChainTail) and then simply never sends its own commitment_signed. The fee update now exists only in the in-memory local log; on disk neither unsignedAckedUpdatesKey nor remoteUnsignedLocalUpdatesKey exists (the CommitDiff that carried it was deleted in the same transaction). There is no timer for an owed commitment_signed (PendingCommitTicker is only resumed on ErrNoWindow and only disconnects), so this window stays open until the victim restarts. After restart, restorePeerLocalUpdates receives nil, the local log lacks the FeeUpdate, and lc.updateLogs.Local.logIndex is seeded from RemoteCommitment.LocalLogIndex (which already counts it), so channel_reestablish is clean and nothing is re-sent. When the peer reconnects and sends the owed commitment_signed covering the fee update, ReceiveNewCommitment builds our local commitment via fetchCommitmentView/computeView with FeePerKw seeded from the local chain tip (old rate) and no FeeUpdate in the view to override it; the signature does not verify, and processRemoteCommitSig fails the link with ErrInvalidCommitment / LinkFailureForceClose (htlcswitch/link.go:4359-4365): the victim unilaterally closes its own funded channel, paying the commitment fee and waiting out its CSV delay, while the counterparty's balance is immediately spendable.

The counterparty needs no special position beyond being the fundee and withholding one message; the trigger (a victim restart) is routine. Adds are not affected because they are rebuilt from the remote commitment's HTLC set, and settles/fails cannot occur before our first revoke, so the lost update type on this path is update_fee. The same loss occurs with an honest peer if the victim crashes between receiving revoke_and_ack and the peer's commitment_signed.

Root cause: a defensive early return conflates "no acked remote updates persisted yet" with "nothing to persist", dropping an unrelated piece of required state.

## Evidence
1. [channeldb/channel.go:3583–3590](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/channel.go#L3583-L3590)
   If unsignedAckedUpdatesKey is absent, AdvanceCommitChainTail returns nil immediately. The `updates` argument (our local non-add updates the peer has acked by revoking but not yet signed for) is never written under remoteUnsignedLocalUpdatesKey on this path. This is the code the fix must change: a missing key must be treated as an empty list, not as a reason to skip the rest of the transaction.
2. [channeldb/channel.go:3622–3633](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/channel.go#L3622-L3633)
   The write of remoteUnsignedLocalUpdatesKey happens only after the early-return check, so it is skipped entirely for the same revocation.
3. [channeldb/channel.go:2559–2567](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/channeldb/channel.go#L2559-L2567)
   UpdateCommitment (called from RevokeCurrentCommitment, i.e. when we send revoke_and_ack) is the only writer that creates unsignedAckedUpdatesKey; the only other Put is inside AdvanceCommitChainTail after the key already exists. A channel on which the peer has never sent commitment_signed therefore has no key, and every revocation we receive on it takes the early-return path.
4. [lnwallet/channel.go:6103–6109](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L6103-L6109)
   ReceiveRevocation passes localPeerUpdates (from unsignedLocalUpdates: our settle/fail/fee updates that are on the remote commitment but not on ours) as `updates`; these are what the early return discards. Adds are excluded because they are rebuilt from the remote commitment's HTLC set.
5. [lnwallet/channel.go:1588–1599](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L1588-L1599)
   On restart restoreCommitState reads RemoteUnsignedLocalUpdates() and restoreStateLogs/restorePeerLocalUpdates restore FeeUpdate entries from it into the local log; with nothing persisted the local fee update is gone.
6. [lnwallet/channel.go:969–970](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L969-L970)
   NewLightningChannel seeds the local update log's logIndex from RemoteCommitment.LocalLogIndex, which already counts the lost fee update, so the restored log has a gap rather than a pending entry and nothing prompts a re-send.
7. [lnwallet/channel.go:4870](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/channel.go#L4870)
   computeView initialises the view's FeePerKw from the local chain tip (the on-disk LocalCommitment, old fee) and only overrides it if a FeeUpdate entry is found in the log. With the entry lost, the local commitment rebuilt in ReceiveNewCommitment uses the old fee rate while the peer signed with the new one, so the signature does not verify.
8. [htlcswitch/link.go:4359–4364](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/htlcswitch/link.go#L4359-L4364)
   processRemoteCommitSig turns the ReceiveNewCommitment error into ErrInvalidCommitment with FailureAction LinkFailureForceClose: the victim unilaterally closes its own funded channel on receipt of the peer's valid commitment_signed.

## Impact
Persisted channel state is incomplete, causing the node to reject a valid commitment and unilaterally close a channel it funded: loss of that channel's availability, commitment and sweep fees paid by the victim, funds time-locked for the CSV delay while the counterparty's output is immediately spendable. No funds stolen, no secrets exposed, node itself stays up.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is the fundee of a channel the victim opened (an in-scope channel counterparty). It stays passive (never sends commitment_signed, so the victim never revokes and unsignedAckedUpdatesKey is never created), waits for the victim's link to issue update_fee + commitment_signed on its fee timer, replies with revoke_and_ack and withholds commitment_signed. The victim's AdvanceCommitChainTail takes the early return and the fee update is never persisted. On the victim's next restart the local log is rebuilt without it; when the attacker reconnects and sends the owed commitment_signed the victim rejects its own correct state and force closes. Deterministic once the preconditions hold; requires the victim to restart while the window is open and to have sent update_fee before any inbound commitment_signed (both routine over a channel's lifetime).

## Recommended fix
AdvanceCommitChainTail returns early when unsignedAckedUpdatesKey is missing and thereby never writes the independent remoteUnsignedLocalUpdatesKey for that revocation. Fix criteria: remoteUnsignedLocalUpdatesKey must be written with `updates` on every successful AdvanceCommitChainTail regardless of whether unsignedAckedUpdatesKey exists (treat a missing key as an empty list rather than returning). Verify: on a fresh channel where the local node signs first and the peer revokes, RemoteUnsignedLocalUpdates() returns the local fee/settle/fail updates after a restart and the subsequent inbound commitment_signed is accepted.

# Immature-locktime and other unexpected errors on the initial sweep broadcast are classified TxFatal, silently abandoning deadline-bound HTLC inputs

## Details
TxPublisher.handleInitialTxError (sweep/fee_bumper.go:1148-1155) classifies every error from initializeTx that is not one of the enumerated fee/budget/dust/missing-input errors as TxFatal. The sweeper handles TxFatal by marking every input of the set Fatal and deleting it (sweep/sweeper.go:1805-1855, 1540-1550); nothing re-offers the inputs until the node restarts. The same errors on a later replacement attempt are mapped to TxFailed and retried (fee_bumper.go:1860-1896), so the initial-path classification is an inconsistency, not an invariant.

A deterministic, counterparty-steerable way to hit the default branch is ErrLocktimeImmature from a one-block height disagreement between sweeper and publisher. Blockbeat consumers are notified sequentially chainArb -> sweeper -> txPublisher (server.go:2014-2019, chainio/dispatcher.go:285-297). The sweeper handles block H synchronously in its collector, calling sweepPendingInputs before NotifyBlockProcessed (sweeper.go:716-734), while the publisher only stores H when its own monitor loop receives the beat afterwards (fee_bumper.go:938-947). The sweeper's isMature admits an input whose CLTV locktime equals H (sweeper.go:233). If the resulting set is Immediate, Broadcast runs handleInitialBroadcast synchronously in the sweeper's goroutine (fee_bumper.go:437-439) -> createSweepTx -> prepareSweepTx with t.currentHeight.Load() == H-1 (fee_bumper.go:1504-1508), which rejects locktime H > H-1 (fee_bumper.go:1735-1740). The error reaches the default branch and every input in the set is abandoned.

A set is Immediate when any input carries params.Immediate (tx_input_set.go:477-487). In production that flag is set permanently on every input that survives a TxUnknownSpend (sweeper.go:2011) and by the BumpFee RPC (sweeper.go:1173); it is never cleared. Survivors are put back to PublishFailed with a raised StartingFeeRate and re-swept at once; if that attempt fails with a retriable TxFailed (ErrZeroFeeRateDelta, ErrMaxPosition, ErrNotEnoughBudget, a mempool publish error), or a later replacement fails (handleReplacementTxError -> TxFailed -> markInputsPublishFailed), the input sits in PublishFailed with Immediate=true and is re-clustered on every block (sweeper.go:1570-1580). The aggregator groups by DeadlineHeight and merges no-locktime inputs into a locktime group (aggregator.go:329-380), so such an Immediate input shares a set with a CLTV-locked HTLC timeout input of the same deadline the block that input matures; the whole set is then broadcast synchronously against the lagging height and marked Fatal.

The counterparty controls the levers: HTLC CLTV expiries set the locktimes and deadlines; a competing spend of one input of a batched sweep (e.g. a preimage claim racing our timeout sweep) produces the TxUnknownSpend that flips siblings to Immediate; mempool competition makes the immediate retry fail. HTLC resolvers discard the SweepInput result channel (htlc_timeout_resolver.go:580, :513; htlc_success_resolver.go:745, :791, :896) and block in watchHtlcSpend, so the Fatal result is observed by nothing: the timeout input is never claimed, and once the upstream HTLC has timed out the downstream peer may claim the output with the preimage; an abandoned success input is timed out by the counterparty after we already paid downstream. Commit-sweep/anchor resolvers return the error and their goroutine exits (channel_arbitrator.go:2759-2768). Recovery requires an operator restart; no alert is raised. The same default branch also turns a transient signer/CraftInputScript or prevout-fetcher error during createSweepTx (fee_bumper.go:1577-1600) into permanent abandonment of the set; that variant is environment-induced rather than attacker-authored.

   updateSweeperInputs re-queues PublishFailed inputs every block (and skips immature ones), so an Immediate input that failed its retry is re-clustered on each block until the collision happens.

   handleBumpEventTxFatal -> markInputsFatal marks every input of the set Fatal; updateSweeperInputs then deletes them, so they are never retried until restart.

   HTLC resolvers discard the SweepInput result channel and block waiting for a spend, so the Fatal result is observed by nobody and the deadline-bound output is never claimed.
16. [sweep/fee\_bumper.go:1860–1896](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sweep/fee_bumper.go#L1860-L1896)
   handleReplacementTxError maps the same unexpected errors to TxFailed (retry), showing the initial-path TxFatal classification is an inconsistency rather than a deliberate invariant.

## Impact
Every input of the affected set is dropped from the sweeper with no notification and no retry until an operator restart. For an HTLC timeout input this hands the downstream peer the option to claim the output with the preimage after the upstream HTLC has timed out; for an HTLC success input the counterparty times out an HTLC we already paid downstream. The loss is bounded to the HTLCs in one batch and the outputs are recoverable by restarting before the counterparty acts, so integrity and availability are rated LOW; the node keeps running.

## Reproduction steps
1. The triggering state is authored by channel counterparties and routing peers: HTLC CLTV expiries fix the locktimes and deadlines that place a timeout input in a cluster at block H; a competing on-chain spend of one input of a batched sweep (a normal preimage-vs-timeout race) flips the sibling inputs to Immediate; mempool competition makes the immediate retry fail so the sibling stays PublishFailed+Immediate. Once that state exists the fatal classification is deterministic on the block the CLTV input matures. The attacker steers but cannot dictate the exact coincidence (an Immediate input still retriable in the same deadline cluster), hence AT:PRESENT; no user interaction; the peer position is an ordinary authenticated channel counterparty (PR:LOW).

## Recommended fix
1. handleInitialTxError defaults unknown errors, including an immature locktime and transient signing/prevout errors, to TxFatal, converting conditions that clear on a later block into permanent abandonment of every input in the set. Fix criteria: Only errors that are provably permanent for the inputs may be classified fatal; an immature locktime, signer/RPC failure or other transient construction error on the first broadcast must leave the inputs retriable (TxFailed semantics), consistent with the replacement path. Verify that an ErrLocktimeImmature or signer error on the initial broadcast leaves the inputs in PublishFailed and that they are swept at the next block.
2. The publisher judges locktime maturity with its own block height, which lags the sweeper's by one block during a synchronous Immediate broadcast, so the two components disagree about an input the sweeper has already selected as mature. Fix criteria: Maturity must be decided from a single height shared between sweeper and publisher or carried in the BumpRequest, so an input the sweeper considers mature is never rejected as immature by the publisher. Verify by sweeping an Immediate set containing an input whose locktime equals the current block height from inside the sweeper's block handler.
3. HTLC resolvers discard the SweepInput result channel, so a fatal sweep result for a deadline-bound input is observed by nothing and the input is silently never claimed. Fix criteria: A fatal result for a resolver-offered input must be surfaced to the resolver (or re-offered automatically) so the HTLC is retried or the operator is alerted before the deadline passes. Verify that a TxFatal for an HTLC timeout input produces a visible error or a re-offer rather than an indefinite wait.

# Sweeper borrows wallet UTXOs without leasing them, so deadline-bound sweeps double-spend each other and the loser is silently starved

## Details
BudgetInputSet.AddWalletInputs (sweep/tx_input_set.go:350-401) borrows confirmed wallet UTXOs for sets that cannot pay their own fee: anchor CPFP (budget far above the 330-sat anchor) and second-level HTLC inputs with RequiredTxOut. It runs under Wallet.WithCoinSelectLock, lists the wallet's unspent coins, sorts them smallest-first and appends them, but never calls LeaseOutput. UtxoSweeper.sweep (sweeper.go:855-866) only hands a BumpRequest to the TxPublisher with Immediate = set.Immediate(); no contractcourt producer sets Immediate (only the operator's WalletKit.BumpFee path does), so TxPublisher.Broadcast (fee_bumper.go:426-443) merely stores the record. When the lock is released no transaction exists and the wallet still reports the coin as unspent.

Two sets in one sweepPendingInputs pass (sweeper.go:1584-1626) therefore select the same coin: every anchor is an ExclusiveGroup input placed in its own set (aggregator.go:86-93), and HTLC timeout/success second-level inputs are clustered by deadline height, so two channels force-closed in one block, or one channel with HTLCs at two different CLTVs, yields two wallet-input sets that both list the identical UTXO snapshot. The blockbeat queue runs chainArb -> sweeper -> txPublisher (server.go:2013-2019), so processRecords runs the initial broadcasts of both records sequentially within the same beat: the first record publishes; the second record's createAndCheckTx hits a mempool conflict with its sibling, which TestMempoolAccept reports as insufficient fee (the project's own test at lnwallet/test/test_interface.go:1919 asserts chain.ErrInsufficientFee for an under-paying RBF conflict); createRBFCompliantTx (fee_bumper.go:543-614) increments the fee until the second tx replaces the first and publishes it. Wallet inputs carry sequence 0 (BlocksToMaturity of a BaseInput), so the sweep signals RBF.

The first record is never told. Spend notifications are only dispatched for confirmed spends (chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:496-517 routes mempool spends to the separate mempool notifier), so getSpentInputs/isUnknownSpent cannot see the sibling's replacement. At the next block its fee bump either replaces the sibling (if its deadline-driven fee now exceeds the sibling's absolute fee plus relay) or fails with ErrInsufficientFee, which createAndPublishTx and handleReplacementTxError swallow and retry next block (fee_bumper.go:1340-1347, 1843-1848). The two records then alternate evicting each other, and the one whose absolute fee cannot exceed the sibling's within its budget (e.g. a small HTLC timeout tx against a CPFP that must pay for a large commitment parent, weight_estimator.go:130-133) is kept out of the mempool entirely until the sibling confirms on chain. Only then does TxUnknownSpend fire and the sweeper re-cluster the loser with fresh coins (sweeper.go:1971-2032). A channel counterparty can arrange this by holding HTLCs with two different CLTVs (or two channels) and stalling so the victim must go on chain, making the victim's own high-budget sweep starve its time-critical one past the incoming HTLC's expiry, which is the window the deadline-aware sweeper exists to protect.

Secondary consequence: channel funding leases its coins (wallet_assembler.go:530) but cannot see the sweeper's selection, so a funding flow that selects coins in the seconds between the sweeper's pass and the publisher's broadcast in the same beat builds a funding transaction the sweep later replaces (an initiator's pending channel never times out). This window is short and not attacker-timed.

Assumptions about btcwallet v0.16.20-pre: ListUnspent excludes outputs that are leased or spent by an unmined wallet transaction (which is why leasing would close the window), and PublishTransaction of a replacement removes the conflicting unmined wallet tx from the store.

## Evidence

   AddWalletInputs lists confirmed wallet UTXOs under the coin-select lock, sorts them smallest-first and appends them to the set, but never calls LeaseOutput; the coins are reserved only for the duration of the closure.

   sweepPendingInputs runs AddWalletInputs and s.sweep for each set under the coin-select lock; for non-Immediate sets nothing is created or published inside the lock, so the next set lists the identical UTXO snapshot and picks the same coin.

   sweep builds the BumpRequest with Immediate = set.Immediate(); no contractcourt producer sets Immediate, so the publisher only stores the record.

   Broadcast stores the record and returns unless req.Immediate; the tx is created in processRecords -> handleInitialBroadcast.
5. [server.go:2013–2019](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L2013-L2019)
   The blockbeat queue is chainArb -> sweeper -> txPublisher, so both records are registered before either initial broadcast, which then run sequentially in the same beat.
6. [sweep/fee\_bumper.go:543–614](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sweep/fee_bumper.go#L543-L614)
   createRBFCompliantTx treats ErrInsufficientFee from TestMempoolAccept as a reason to increment the fee and retry, so the second record's tx replaces its sibling that is already in the mempool.
7. [chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go:496–516](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind.go#L496-L516)
   Spend notifications registered via RegisterSpendNtfn are dispatched only for confirmed spends; mempool spends go to the separate mempool notifier, so the losing record's getSpentInputs/isUnknownSpent never learns its tx was replaced.
8. [sweep/fee\_bumper.go:1340–1347](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sweep/fee_bumper.go#L1340-L1347)
