   The publisher's own TODO acknowledges that wallet UTXOs are not locked and that the same wallet UTXO can be used by different sweeping transactions.
11. [sweep/aggregator.go:86–93](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sweep/aggregator.go#L86-L93)
   Every anchor (ExclusiveGroup) is placed in its own set, so two force-closed channels in one block yield two anchor CPFP sets that each need wallet inputs.
12. [contractcourt/htlc\_timeout\_resolver.go:512–522](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/contractcourt/htlc_timeout_resolver.go#L512-L522)
   Second-level HTLC timeout inputs (RequiredTxOut) are offered with a counterparty-chosen deadline and no Immediate flag; HTLCs at different CLTVs land in different clusters and each needs wallet inputs.
13. [sweep/walletsweep.go:282–294](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/sweep/walletsweep.go#L282-L294)
   The sibling path CraftSweepAllTx leases every selected UTXO under the same lock, showing the intended discipline that AddWalletInputs omits.
14. [lnwallet/chanfunding/wallet\_assembler.go:526–537](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnwallet/chanfunding/wallet_assembler.go#L526-L537)
   Channel funding selects coins under WithCoinSelectLock and leases them; it cannot see a coin the sweeper merely listed and can select the same coin before the sweep is published.

## Impact
The losing deadline-bound sweep is out of the mempool for every block in which its sibling leads and the sweeper does not know; where the sibling's absolute fee exceeds the loser's budget, the loser is starved until the sibling confirms, which in an engineered case pushes the HTLC timeout past the incoming HTLC's expiry (funds at risk). The common outcome is delay followed by recovery via TxUnknownSpend; a concurrently crafted funding transaction can be replaced, leaving a pending-open channel. No confidentiality impact.

## Reproduction steps
1. A channel counterparty triggers the condition without operator involvement: it holds HTLCs at two different CLTVs (or two channels) and stalls so the victim must resolve on chain, producing two deadline-bound sets that both need wallet inputs in the same sweeper pass. Whether the loser can later out-bid the winner depends on wallet UTXO shape, budgets and the fee market, hence AT:PRESENT. Requires an open channel with the victim (PR:LOW).

## Recommended fix
1. AddWalletInputs reserves wallet UTXOs only for the duration of the coin-select lock; the selection is not persisted via LeaseOutput, so later sets in the same pass and funding flows can select the same coin before the sweep transaction exists. Fix criteria: A wallet UTXO selected for a sweep set must be unavailable to any other coin selection (sweeper sets, funding, PSBT funding) from the moment it is chosen until the sweep confirms or is abandoned, with release on failure. Verify by registering two wallet-input sets in one pass and confirming they select disjoint coins, and by starting a funding flow right after such a selection and confirming the funding transaction does not conflict with the sweep.
2. The fee bumper treats ErrInsufficientFee on a replacement as a transient condition to retry silently, and spend monitoring is confirmed-only, so a record whose transaction was evicted from the mempool by a sibling never learns it is no longer live. Fix criteria: A monitored transaction that has been replaced in the mempool by a conflicting transaction must be detected and surfaced to the sweeper so the inputs can be re-clustered with other coins, rather than assumed live. Verify that after a sibling replacement the losing inputs are retried with fresh wallet inputs within one block.

# Tor-mode address parsing falls back to system DNS on resolution failure, leaking hostnames and node IP

## Details
With `tor.active=1` and without `tor.skip-proxy-for-clearnet-targets`, lnd installs `tor.ProxyNet` as `cfg.net` (config.go:1323) so hostname resolution goes through Tor's SOCKS5 RESOLVE (`ProxyNet.ResolveTCPAddr` -> `tor.ResolveTCPAddr` -> `tor.LookupHost` -> btcd `connmgr.TorLookupIP`, tor/tor.go:137-138, 204-224). `lncfg.ParseAddressString` (lncfg/address.go:264-280) calls that resolver for every host that is not an IP literal, .onion, loopback, IPv6 or unspecified, but when it fails with an error whose text contains 'tor host is unreachable' it silently retries the same name with `net.ResolveTCPAddr`, the operating-system resolver (hosts file, then the configured recursive DNS over clearnet).

The comment frames the retry as support for names that exist only in /etc/hosts, but the matched string is not specific to that case: it is btcd connmgr's rendering of SOCKS5 reply status 0x04 (HOST_UNREACHABLE), and Tor's SOCKS5 RESOLVE returns 0x04 for every unsuccessful resolution (NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, exit-side timeout). Two dependency assumptions are stated rather than verified in this checkout: btcd v0.25.1-pre `connmgr.TorLookupIP` maps status 0x04 to the text 'tor host is unreachable' (lnd's own match at address.go:272 is written against it), and Tor's `connection_ap_handshake_socks_resolved` answers any non-success RESOLVE with SOCKS5_HOST_UNREACHABLE. Consequently any hostname Tor cannot resolve is immediately re-queried through the node's system DNS, outside Tor, with no operator opt-in. The code fails open from the Tor resolver to the clearnet one.

The leak is the clearnet DNS query itself: it carries the hostname lnd is about to contact, originates from the node's real IP towards its recursive resolver, and reaches the name's authoritative server from that resolver's IP (or the node's own, with a local resolver or EDNS Client Subnet). The zone operator has seen it whether or not the fallback then succeeds. The subsequent connection is still dialed via Tor (`Dial: cfg.net.Dial`, server.go:1889), so the same party sees a Tor exit connect seconds after a clearnet lookup for its name, which ties the two together.

Reachable paths under tor.active:
- `WatchtowerClient.AddTower` / `RemoveTower` (lnrpc/wtclientrpc/wtclient.go:206-212, 244-252) parse the tower address with `c.cfg.Resolver` = `r.cfg.net.ResolveTCPAddr` (rpcserver.go:800, subrpcserver_config.go:336-338). The field's comment (lnrpc/wtclientrpc/config.go:22-25) says the resolver exists 'to ensure we don't leak any information when running over non-clear networks, e.g. Tor'. wtclientrpc has no build tag and ships in every release binary.
- `netann.HostAnnouncer` (server.go:1911-1916) re-resolves each `externalhosts` entry every 5 minutes through the same parser; lower value, since that name is the node's own advertised address.
- Startup parsing of `listen`, `externalip`, `rpclisten`, `restlisten`, `tor.socks/dns/control` (config.go:1260-1290, 1654-1740): operator-controlled, typically local, lowest value.

`parseAddr` in server.go (ConnectPeer) has no such fallback; peer connections are unaffected. The defect is the error discriminator in `ParseAddressString`: a generic Tor failure is taken as proof the name is local, defeating the Tor-only promise lnd logs at startup (lnd.go:526-529).

## Evidence
1. [lncfg/address.go:264–280](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lncfg/address.go#L264-L280)
   Primary location / fix point. After tcpResolver (under tor.active: Tor SOCKS5 RESOLVE) fails, ParseAddressString matches the error text 'tor host is unreachable' and retries the same hostname with net.ResolveTCPAddr, the operating-system resolver. The comment intends this only for names that exist solely in /etc/hosts, but the matched string is btcd connmgr's rendering of the generic SOCKS5 status 0x04 that Tor returns for every failed RESOLVE (NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, timeout), so every name Tor cannot resolve is re-queried over clearnet DNS with no operator opt-in.
2. [lnrpc/wtclientrpc/wtclient.go:206–212](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/wtclientrpc/wtclient.go#L206-L212)
   AddTower parses the operator-entered tower address (pubkey@hostname published by a third-party tower operator) with ParseAddressString and c.cfg.Resolver; RemoveTower does the same at 244-252. Runtime RPC path, no build tag, shipped in every release binary. This is the path on which a hostile tower operator who controls the name's DNS zone triggers the fallback.
3. [rpcserver.go:800](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/rpcserver.go#L800)
   PopulateDependencies hands r.cfg.net.ResolveTCPAddr to the sub-servers; subrpcserver_config.go:336-338 stores it as wtclientrpc Config.Resolver. Under tor.active this is tor.ProxyNet.ResolveTCPAddr.
4. [config.go:1323–1328](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/config.go#L1323-L1328)
   With tor.active, cfg.net becomes tor.ProxyNet so that, per the preceding comment, Tor-specific functions are used 'in order to avoid leaking our real information'. ParseAddressString's fallback bypasses this for any name Tor fails to resolve.
5. [tor/tor.go:137–145](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/tor/tor.go#L137-L145)
   tor.LookupHost (reached from ProxyNet.ResolveTCPAddr -> tor.ResolveTCPAddr at 204-224) calls btcd connmgr.TorLookupIP, whose failure error for SOCKS5 reply 0x04 is the string ParseAddressString matches on. Dependency assumption: btcd v0.25.1-pre connmgr maps status 0x04 to 'tor host is unreachable'; Tor's SOCKS5 RESOLVE answers every unsuccessful resolution with 0x04 HOST_UNREACHABLE.
6. [lnrpc/wtclientrpc/config.go:22–24](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnrpc/wtclientrpc/config.go#L22-L24)
   States the maintainers' guarantee: the Resolver exists 'to ensure we don't leak any information when running over non-clear networks, e.g. Tor'. The fallback inside ParseAddressString defeats exactly this guarantee.
7. [server.go:1889](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L1889)
   The tower client dials with cfg.net.Dial, i.e. through Tor's SOCKS proxy. The connection itself is therefore anonymised; the clearnet DNS query that immediately precedes it is the only exposure, and its timing lets the tower operator link the Tor-exit connection to the resolver/IP seen at their nameserver.
8. [server.go:1911–1916](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/server.go#L1911-L1916)
   Secondary path: netann.HostAnnouncer re-resolves every externalhosts entry through the same parser on a 5-minute ticker (netann/host_ann.go:95), so a Tor resolution failure sends the lookup to the system resolver repeatedly. Lower value, since that hostname is the node's own advertised address.
9. [lnd.go:526–529](https://github.com/Halbarevi/lqwd1/blob/17c16878a0246420e1dec11ce46ce92fba9065d5/lnd.go#L526-L529)
   lnd logs 'Proxying all network traffic via Tor!' when tor.active is set without skip-proxy-for-clearnet-targets; the system-DNS fallback contradicts that promise without any operator opt-in.

## Impact
Confidentiality only: the node's clearnet network location (its IP, or its recursive resolver's IP and hence ISP/geography) and the hostname it is about to contact are disclosed to the zone operator and to on-path observers of the DNS query, breaking the location privacy Tor mode exists to provide and that the Resolver field promises. No keys, funds or channel state are touched; the leak is a single datum, not full system confidentiality.

## Reproduction steps
1. Attacker is a watchtower operator who publishes pubkey@tower.example and runs that name's authoritative DNS. They answer NXDOMAIN (to everyone, or only to Tor-exit resolvers) and log queries. When the victim's operator runs `lncli wtclient add` on a tor.active node, Tor's RESOLVE fails with status 0x04, ParseAddressString falls back to the system resolver, and the attacker's nameserver records the victim's resolver/IP and the lookup time, which it matches to the Tor-exit connection that follows. No privileges on the node; requires Tor mode (non-default) and the operator entering the hostname.

## Recommended fix
ParseAddressString treats Tor's generic SOCKS5 'host unreachable' resolution failure as proof that the name is local-only and re-resolves it with the system resolver, failing open from Tor-proxied to clearnet DNS and sending the hostname and the node's clearnet identity outside Tor. Fix criteria: When resolution is configured to go through Tor, a hostname Tor cannot resolve must not be sent to the system resolver unless the operator has explicitly opted into clearnet lookups (e.g. tor.skip-proxy-for-clearnet-targets) or the name is resolved without any network query (loopback/unspecified/private literal, or a hosts-file-only lookup that does not fall through to DNS). All callers of ParseAddressString under tor.active (wtclientrpc AddTower/RemoveTower, HostAnnouncer, startup config) must inherit this behaviour. Verify by adding a tower at a non-resolvable hostname under tor.active and confirming no DNS query leaves via the system resolver.
